  3. Build a sidebar window that slides in from the right and stays mapped until its slide-out finishes.
Part III · Qt Quick: Drawing Things

Effects: Shadows, Blur, Masks, Tints

Shadows give depth, blur gives glass, masks give rounded images, tints make monochrome icons match your theme. Qt 6 provides all of this through MultiEffect. Quickshell adds ClippingRectangle for cheap rounded clipping and BackgroundEffect for compositor blur.

ClippingRectangle: rounded clipping, the easy way#

clip: true only clips to a rectangle. To clip children to rounded corners (album art, avatars, wallpaper thumbnails), use Quickshell's ClippingRectangle:

import Quickshell.Widgets

ClippingRectangle {
    width: 120; height: 120
    radius: 24                       // children are clipped to this rounded shape
    color: "#313244"                 // background behind the children
    Image {
        anchors.fill: parent
        source: "file:///home/me/.face"
        fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectCrop
    }
}

Its sibling ClippingWrapperRectangle also sizes itself around a single child with margins.

MultiEffect#

import QtQuick.Effects. MultiEffect takes a source item and draws it with effects applied. The usual pattern: hide the original (visible: false) and draw the effect in its place.

Drop shadow#

import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Effects

Item {
    width: 300; height: 200

    Rectangle {
        id: card
        anchors.centerIn: parent
        width: 220; height: 120; radius: 18
        color: "#1e1e2e"
        visible: false                         // drawn by the effect below
    }
    MultiEffect {
        source: card
        anchors.fill: card
        shadowEnabled: true
        shadowColor: "#000000"
        shadowOpacity: 0.55
        shadowBlur: 0.9                        // 0..1
        shadowVerticalOffset: 6
        shadowHorizontalOffset: 0
        autoPaddingEnabled: true               // allow the shadow to extend outside the item
    }
}
Shadows near window edges

A shadow is drawn inside your window. If your card touches the window's edge, the shadow is cut off. Leave margins around shadowed items, and make the window bigger than the visible card.

Blur (of your own content)#

Image { id: wall; anchors.fill: parent; source: "file:///…/wall.jpg"; fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectCrop; visible: false }
MultiEffect {
    source: wall
    anchors.fill: wall
    blurEnabled: true
    blur: 1.0             // amount 0..1
    blurMax: 64           // maximum radius in px (affects quality and cost)
    brightness: -0.2      // darken a bit for readable text on top
    saturation: 0.2
}

That's the lock screen look: a blurred, dimmed wallpaper.

Colorize (tint icons)#

Image { id: icon; source: "icons/logo.svg"; sourceSize: Qt.size(32, 32); visible: false }
MultiEffect {
    source: icon; anchors.fill: icon
    colorization: 1.0                 // 0 = original, 1 = fully tinted
    colorizationColor: "#cba6f7"
}

Mask (shape one item by another)#

Image { id: photo; width: 200; height: 120; source: "…"; fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectCrop; visible: false }
Rectangle { id: shape; width: 200; height: 120; radius: 30; visible: false; layer.enabled: true }
MultiEffect {
    source: photo; anchors.fill: photo
    maskEnabled: true
    maskSource: shape                 // where the mask is opaque, the photo shows
    maskThresholdMin: 0.5
    maskSpreadAtMin: 1.0
}

The mask source must be rendered offscreen, which is why it has layer.enabled: true. For plain rounded corners, ClippingRectangle is simpler and cheaper; use masks for arbitrary shapes (a circle with a notch, text-shaped holes).

MultiEffect property reference#

Group Properties
Source source, autoPaddingEnabled, paddingRect
Brightness/contrast brightness (-1..1), contrast (-1..1), saturation (-1..1)
Colorize colorization (0..1), colorizationColor
Blur blurEnabled, blur (0..1), blurMax (px), blurMultiplier
Shadow shadowEnabled, shadowColor, shadowOpacity, shadowBlur, shadowHorizontalOffset, shadowVerticalOffset, shadowScale
Mask maskEnabled, maskSource, maskInverted, maskThresholdMin/Max, maskSpreadAtMin/Max

layer: render an item offscreen#

Any item can be rendered into an offscreen texture with layer.enabled: true, and an effect can be applied with layer.effect:

Rectangle {
    width: 200; height: 100; radius: 16; color: "#1e1e2e"
    layer.enabled: true
    layer.effect: MultiEffect {
        shadowEnabled: true
        shadowBlur: 0.8
        shadowVerticalOffset: 4
    }
}

This is more compact than a separate MultiEffect, and the item stays interactive. It's also how you make a group of items fade as one (otherwise overlapping children show through each other at partial opacity): layer.enabled: true; opacity: 0.5.

Layers cost memory and GPU time

Each layer is a full texture. Don't enable layers on dozens of items, and don't put them on things that change every frame unless needed. Turn them off while hidden: layer.enabled: visible.

Blur behind your window (glass)#

MultiEffect only blurs your own content. To blur the windows and wallpaper behind a panel, the compositor must do it.

Hyprland: layer rules#

hyprland.conflayerrule = blur, quickshell:bar          # namespace from WlrLayershell.namespace
layerrule = ignorealpha 0.2, quickshell:bar   # don't blur nearly transparent pixels (e.g. shadows)

Give your window a namespace and a translucent background:

PanelWindow {
    WlrLayershell.namespace: "quickshell:bar"
    color: "transparent"
    Rectangle { anchors.fill: parent; radius: 14; color: "#b31e1e2e" }   // 70% opaque
}

The Wayland background-effect protocol: BackgroundEffect#

Newer Quickshell versions include BackgroundEffect (module Quickshell.Wayland), which asks the compositor to blur behind specific regions of your window through a Wayland protocol, where the compositor supports it. Check its reference page for the exact properties and compositor support.

Qt5Compat.GraphicalEffects (legacy)#

Older configs use import Qt5Compat.GraphicalEffects with DropShadow, OpacityMask, ColorOverlay, FastBlur, GaussianBlur. They still work if qt6-5compat is installed, but MultiEffect is the modern replacement:

Old New
DropShadow MultiEffect { shadowEnabled: true }
OpacityMask MultiEffect { maskEnabled: true } or ClippingRectangle
ColorOverlay MultiEffect { colorization: 1 }
FastBlur / GaussianBlur MultiEffect { blurEnabled: true }

Custom shaders (advanced)#

ShaderEffect runs your own GLSL fragment shader, compiled to .qsb with Qt's qsb tool. It's used for animated gradients, noise and wave effects. That's out of scope for beginners, but know it exists when you see .frag.qsb files in advanced rices.

Exercises
  1. Make a floating card with a soft shadow, leaving enough margin in its window for the shadow.
  2. Show your wallpaper blurred and darkened behind a big clock.
  3. Tint a white SVG icon with your accent color using colorization.
  4. On Hyprland, add a layerrule = blur for your bar's namespace and make the bar 70% opaque.
Part III · Qt Quick: Drawing Things

Shapes and Canvas

Rectangles can't do everything. Inverted "screen corners", panels that curve smoothly into the bar, circular progress rings, wavy separators, sparkline graphs: these need Shape (GPU vector paths) or Canvas (a JavaScript 2D drawing API).

Shape basics#

import QtQuick.Shapes. A Shape contains one or more ShapePaths. Each path starts at startX/startY and is built from path elements.

import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Shapes

Shape {
    width: 200; height: 100
    preferredRendererType: Shape.CurveRenderer     // smooth anti-aliased curves (Qt 6.6+)

    ShapePath {
        fillColor: "#cba6f7"
        strokeColor: "#1e1e2e"
        strokeWidth: 2                             // -1 = no stroke
        startX: 0; startY: 100
        PathLine { x: 100; y: 0 }                  // straight line to (100, 0)
        PathLine { x: 200; y: 100 }
        PathLine { x: 0; y: 100 }                  // back to start: a triangle
    }
}

Path elements#

Element Draws Key properties
PathLine straight line x, y (or relativeX/Y)
PathArc circular/elliptical arc x, y, radiusX, radiusY, direction (PathArc.Clockwise/Counterclockwise), useLargeArc
PathAngleArc arc by center and angles (rings!) centerX, centerY, radiusX, radiusY, startAngle, sweepAngle, moveToStart
PathQuad quadratic curve x, y, controlX, controlY
PathCubic cubic Bézier x, y, control1X/Y, control2X/Y
PathMove jump without drawing x, y
PathSvg SVG path data path: "M 0 0 L 10 10 …"
PathRectangle (6.8+) rectangle with radius x y width height radius

ShapePath properties#

Property Meaning
fillColor inside color ("transparent" for outline only)
fillGradient LinearGradient, RadialGradient, ConicalGradient
strokeColor, strokeWidth outline
strokeStyle, dashPattern ShapePath.SolidLine / DashLine
capStyle ShapePath.FlatCap, SquareCap, RoundCap
joinStyle MiterJoin, BevelJoin, RoundJoin
fillRule ShapePath.OddEvenFill / WindingFill

Recipe: inverted corner (screen corners)#

The black rounded corners many rices draw at the screen corners, or where a panel meets the bar, are squares with a quarter circle removed:

Shape {
    id: corner
    property int r: 20
    property color c: "#000000"
    width: r; height: r
    preferredRendererType: Shape.CurveRenderer
    ShapePath {
        fillColor: corner.c
        strokeWidth: -1
        startX: 0; startY: 0
        PathLine { x: corner.r; y: 0 }                                     // along the top
        PathArc  { x: 0; y: corner.r; radiusX: corner.r; radiusY: corner.r
                   direction: PathArc.Counterclockwise }                    // curve back to the left edge
        PathLine { x: 0; y: 0 }
    }
}

Rotate it 90°, 180° or 270° for the other corners. Project: Desktop Widgets and Screen Corners places four of them in a click-through overlay window.

Recipe: circular progress ring#

Shape {
    id: ring
    property real value: 0.72          // 0..1
    property real thickness: 5
    property color trackColor: "#313244"
    property color fillColor: "#a6e3a1"
    width: 48; height: 48
    preferredRendererType: Shape.CurveRenderer

    ShapePath {                        // background track
        fillColor: "transparent"
        strokeColor: ring.trackColor
        strokeWidth: ring.thickness
        capStyle: ShapePath.RoundCap
        PathAngleArc {
            centerX: ring.width / 2; centerY: ring.height / 2
            radiusX: ring.width / 2 - ring.thickness; radiusY: radiusX
            startAngle: 0; sweepAngle: 360
        }
    }
    ShapePath {                        // value arc, starting at 12 o'clock
        fillColor: "transparent"
        strokeColor: ring.fillColor
        strokeWidth: ring.thickness
        capStyle: ShapePath.RoundCap
        PathAngleArc {
            centerX: ring.width / 2; centerY: ring.height / 2
            radiusX: ring.width / 2 - ring.thickness; radiusY: radiusX
            startAngle: -90
            sweepAngle: 360 * ring.value
        }
    }
    Behavior on value { NumberAnimation { duration: 400; easing.type: Easing.OutCubic } }
}

Put a percentage Text in the middle and you have a CPU, RAM or battery gauge.

Recipe: a panel that melts into the bar#

Caelestia's drawers and end-4's corners connect panels to the bar with concave curves. Draw the panel's outline as a single path: straight sides, convex rounded bottom corners, and concave "flares" at the top where it meets the bar:

Shape {
    id: drawer
    property real w: 300
    property real h: 200
    property real r: 18                // corner radius
    width: w + 2 * r; height: h
    preferredRendererType: Shape.CurveRenderer
    ShapePath {
        fillColor: "#1e1e2e"; strokeWidth: -1
        startX: 0; startY: 0
        // concave flare top-left
        PathArc { x: drawer.r; y: drawer.r; radiusX: drawer.r; radiusY: drawer.r }
        PathLine { x: drawer.r; y: drawer.h - drawer.r }
        // convex bottom-left
        PathArc { x: drawer.r * 2; y: drawer.h; radiusX: drawer.r; radiusY: drawer.r; direction: PathArc.Counterclockwise }
        PathLine { x: drawer.w; y: drawer.h }
        // convex bottom-right
        PathArc { x: drawer.w + drawer.r; y: drawer.h - drawer.r; radiusX: drawer.r; radiusY: drawer.r; direction: PathArc.Counterclockwise }
        PathLine { x: drawer.w + drawer.r; y: drawer.r }
        // concave flare top-right
        PathArc { x: drawer.w + 2 * drawer.r; y: 0; radiusX: drawer.r; radiusY: drawer.r }
        PathLine { x: 0; y: 0 }
    }
    Behavior on h { NumberAnimation { duration: 350; easing.type: Easing.OutCubic } }
}

Animate h from 0 to its full height and the panel "grows" out of the bar. Project: Edge Drawers (Caelestia Style) builds a full drawer system on this.

Canvas: draw with JavaScript#

Canvas gives you an HTML5-style 2D context. It's great for graphs, waveforms and anything data-driven. It's slower than Shape (it rasterizes on the CPU by default), so redraw only when data changes.

Canvas {
    id: graph
    property var samples: []           // values 0..1
    width: 220; height: 50

    onSamplesChanged: requestPaint()   // redraw only on change
    onPaint: {
        const ctx = getContext("2d")
        ctx.reset()
        if (samples.length < 2) return
        const step = width / (samples.length - 1)

        // filled area
        ctx.beginPath()
        ctx.moveTo(0, height)
        samples.forEach((v, i) => ctx.lineTo(i * step, height - v * height))
        ctx.lineTo(width, height)
        ctx.closePath()
        const g = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, height)
        g.addColorStop(0, "#80cba6f7"); g.addColorStop(1, "#00cba6f7")
        ctx.fillStyle = g
        ctx.fill()

        // line on top
        ctx.beginPath()
        samples.forEach((v, i) => i ? ctx.lineTo(i * step, height - v * height) : ctx.moveTo(0, height - v * height))
        ctx.strokeStyle = "#cba6f7"; ctx.lineWidth = 2; ctx.lineJoin = "round"
        ctx.stroke()
    }

    Timer {                            // demo data: push a random sample every second
        interval: 1000; running: true; repeat: true
        onTriggered: graph.samples = [...graph.samples.slice(-29), Math.random()]
    }
}

Context methods you'll use: reset, clearRect, fillRect, strokeRect, beginPath, moveTo, lineTo, arc, quadraticCurveTo, bezierCurveTo, closePath, fill, stroke, fillText, createLinearGradient, createRadialGradient, save, restore, translate, rotate, scale. Properties: fillStyle, strokeStyle, lineWidth, lineCap, lineJoin, font, globalAlpha.

Set renderTarget: Canvas.FramebufferObject and renderStrategy: Canvas.Cooperative for GPU-backed drawing on supported setups.

Shape or Canvas?#

Shape Canvas
Rendering GPU, resolution-independent CPU bitmap (by default)
Animating animate properties, smooth must repaint each frame
Best for static or animated geometry: corners, rings, outlines data-driven drawings: graphs, visualizers
Exercises
  1. Draw all four inverted screen corners in a 200×200 test item.
  2. Build a battery ring gauge with the percentage text in the middle.
  3. Make a Canvas CPU graph fed with random values, then (after Running Commands with Process) with real /proc/stat data.
Part III · Qt Quick: Drawing Things

Fonts and Icons

Typography and icons carry most of a rice's personality. This chapter covers using installed fonts, bundling fonts, icon fonts (Material Symbols, Nerd Fonts), icon themes for app icons, and Quickshell's IconImage.

Using installed fonts#

Text {
    font.family: "Inter"               // exact family name from `fc-list : family`
    font.pixelSize: 14
    font.weight: Font.Medium
}

Find family names:

fc-list : family | sort -u | grep -i -E "inter|jetbrains|material"

If the family isn't found, Qt silently falls back to a default font. If your text looks "wrong", check the name.

Font properties#

Property Values
family family name
pixelSize size in logical pixels (use this in shells)
pointSize size in points (DPI-dependent)
weight Font.Thin (100), ExtraLight, Light, Normal (400), Medium, DemiBold, Bold (700), ExtraBold, Black (900), or a number
bold, italic, underline, strikeout bools
letterSpacing, wordSpacing px
capitalization Font.MixedCase, AllUppercase, AllLowercase, SmallCaps, Capitalize
hintingPreference Font.PreferFullHinting etc.
features OpenType features: ({ "tnum": 1 }) for tabular numbers
variableAxes variable-font axes (Qt 6.7+): ({ "wght": 650, "FILL": 1 })
Tabular numbers for clocks

In proportional fonts, "1" is narrower than "0", so a ticking clock or percentage jiggles. Enable tabular figures with font.features: ({ "tnum": 1 }) or use a monospace font for numbers.

Bundling a font with your config#

FontLoader {
    id: rubik
    source: Qt.resolvedUrl("assets/fonts/Rubik-Variable.ttf")
}
Text { font.family: rubik.name; text: "bundled font" }

FontLoader has source, name (the loaded family name) and status. This makes your rice self-contained, so others don't need the font installed.

Icon fonts#

An icon font is a font whose glyphs are icons. Change the color and size like text, and they stay sharp at any size.

Material Symbols (recommended)#

Google's icon set, used by end-4, Caelestia and most M3-styled rices. It uses ligatures: you write the icon's name as text.

Text {
    font.family: "Material Symbols Rounded"      // also: Outlined, Sharp
    font.pixelSize: 22
    color: "#cdd6f4"
    text: "battery_charging_full"                // the icon NAME
}

Browse names at fonts.google.com/icons. Common shell icons:

Area Names
Audio volume_up volume_down volume_mute volume_off mic mic_off headphones
Network wifi wifi_off wifi_1_bar wifi_2_bar signal_wifi_4_bar lan airplanemode_active
Bluetooth bluetooth bluetooth_connected bluetooth_disabled
Battery battery_full battery_0_bar…battery_6_bar battery_charging_full battery_alert
Power power_settings_new restart_alt logout lock bedtime
Media play_arrow pause skip_next skip_previous shuffle repeat music_note
Misc notifications notifications_off do_not_disturb_on light_mode dark_mode settings apps search close coffee screenshot keyboard

Variable axes: filled icons and weight

Material Symbols Variable has axes: FILL (0–1), wght (100–700), GRAD (-25–200) and opsz (20–48). With Qt 6.7+:

Text {
    font.family: "Material Symbols Rounded"
    font.pixelSize: 22
    font.variableAxes: ({ "FILL": active ? 1 : 0, "wght": 500, "opsz": 24 })
    text: "favorite"
}

Animating FILL from 0 to 1 on hover or toggle is the "icon fills in" effect seen in M3 rices.

Nerd Fonts#

Patched programming fonts with thousands of icons (Font Awesome, Devicons, Codicons…). You write glyphs by codepoint rather than by name:

Text {
    font.family: "JetBrainsMono Nerd Font"
    text: ""        // nf-fa-wifi
}

Look up codepoints at nerdfonts.com/cheat-sheet. Nerd Fonts are popular in terminal-style and minimal rices.

App icons: icon themes#

App icons in launchers, docks, trays and notifications come from icon themes (Papirus, Adwaita…) by name, like firefox or org.gnome.Nautilus.

Quickshell.iconPath()#

Resolve a name to an image URL with Quickshell.iconPath():

Image { source: Quickshell.iconPath("firefox") }                       // URL in the current theme
Image { source: Quickshell.iconPath(entry.icon, "application-x-executable") }   // with fallback name
Image { source: Quickshell.iconPath(name, true) }                      // "" if not found (check=true)

There's also Quickshell.hasThemeIcon() to test existence, and the raw image://icon/<name> URL scheme.

Choosing the theme#

Set the icon theme with a pragma at the top of shell.qml:

//@ pragma IconTheme Papirus-Dark

IconImage#

IconImage (from Quickshell.Widgets) is an Image specialized for icons: always square, sized with one implicitSize, crisp scaling:

import Quickshell.Widgets

IconImage {
    implicitSize: 32
    source: Quickshell.iconPath(modelData.icon, "application-x-executable")
    asynchronous: true
}

Use it for every app or tray icon.

Finding the right icon for a window#

A window's app id (kitty, firefox, org.gnome.Nautilus) usually matches its .desktop file. Look it up with DesktopEntries.heuristicLookup(), then use the entry's icon:

IconImage {
    implicitSize: 24
    source: Quickshell.iconPath(DesktopEntries.heuristicLookup(toplevel.appId)?.icon ?? toplevel.appId,
                                "application-x-executable")
}

SVG icons of your own#

Keep custom icons in assets/icons/. Use white or black SVGs and tint them with MultiEffect colorization (Effects: Shadows, Blur, Masks, Tints). Always set sourceSize for crispness.

A reusable MaterialIcon component#

widgets/MaterialIcon.qmlimport QtQuick

Text {
    id: root
    property string icon: ""
    property real fill: 0                   // 0 outline … 1 filled
    property int size: 20

    text: icon
    font.family: "Material Symbols Rounded"
    font.pixelSize: size
    font.variableAxes: ({ "FILL": fill, "opsz": Math.min(48, Math.max(20, size)) })
    color: "#cdd6f4"
    verticalAlignment: Text.AlignVCenter
    horizontalAlignment: Text.AlignHCenter

    Behavior on fill { NumberAnimation { duration: 180 } }
}
MaterialIcon { icon: "wifi"; fill: connected ? 1 : 0; size: 18 }
Exercises
  1. Show volume_up, wifi and battery_full Material Symbols in a row at 20 px.
  2. Build MaterialIcon.qml and make an icon fill in on hover.
  3. List 10 apps from DesktopEntries.applications with their icons using IconImage.
Part III · Qt Quick: Drawing Things

Timers, Dates and Time

Clocks, auto-hiding OSDs, polling a command, debouncing input, countdowns. This chapter covers Timer, Quickshell's SystemClock and ElapsedTimer, and formatting dates.

Timer#

Timer {
    id: t
    interval: 1000            // milliseconds
    running: true             // start immediately (bindable)
    repeat: true              // false = fire once
    triggeredOnStart: false   // true = also fire immediately when started
    onTriggered: console.log("tick")
}
Member Meaning
interval delay in ms
running active? Set or bind it
repeat repeat or one-shot
triggeredOnStart fire once right away on start
start(), stop(), restart() control
onTriggered the signal

Patterns#

Auto-hide after inactivity (OSDs, popups):

Timer { id: hideTimer; interval: 1500; onTriggered: osd.visible = false }
function poke() { osd.visible = true; hideTimer.restart() }     // every poke resets the countdown

Polling (re-run a command every N seconds):

Timer { interval: 2000; running: true; repeat: true; triggeredOnStart: true; onTriggered: cpuProc.running = true }

Poll only while visible (saves power):

Timer { interval: 1000; repeat: true; running: dashboard.visible; onTriggered: refresh() }

Debounce (wait until typing pauses before an expensive search):

TextField { onTextChanged: debounce.restart() }
Timer { id: debounce; interval: 200; onTriggered: runSearch() }

Delay once, e.g. ignore startup events:

property bool armed: false
Timer { interval: 2000; running: true; onTriggered: root.armed = true }

SystemClock: the right way to show time#

A Timer with interval: 1000 drifts and fires at arbitrary offsets, so a clock can visibly lag up to a second behind real minutes. SystemClock updates exactly on second, minute or hour boundaries, and only as often as you need:

import Quickshell

SystemClock {
    id: clock
    precision: SystemClock.Minutes      // Seconds | Minutes | Hours
}

Text { text: Qt.formatDateTime(clock.date, "hh:mm") }

It provides date, hours, minutes, seconds and enabled (set false to pause updates). See its reference page for every member.

Battery-friendly clocks

precision: SystemClock.Minutes wakes your shell 60 times less often than seconds precision. Use Seconds only if you actually display seconds, and switch dynamically: precision: showSeconds ? SystemClock.Seconds : SystemClock.Minutes.

Formatting dates and times#

Qt.formatDateTime(date, format), Qt.formatDate(date, format), Qt.formatTime(date, format).

Code Meaning Example
h / hh hour (0–23 or 1–12 with AP) / zero-padded 9 / 09
H / HH hour, always 24h 21
m / mm minute 5 / 05
s / ss second 7 / 07
AP / ap AM/PM marker; makes h 12-hour PM
d / dd day of month 1 / 01
ddd / dddd day name short / long Fri / Friday
M / MM month number 3 / 03
MMM / MMMM month name short / long Nov / November
yy / yyyy year 26 / 2026
'text' literal text in quotes 'Week' 
Qt.formatDateTime(clock.date, "ddd d MMM  hh:mm")     // Fri 21 Nov  14:05
Qt.formatDateTime(clock.date, "h:mm AP")             // 2:05 PM
Qt.formatDateTime(clock.date, "dddd, d MMMM yyyy")   // Friday, 21 November 2026

Names follow the system locale. For a specific locale: clock.date.toLocaleString(Qt.locale("de_DE"), "dddd").

Date arithmetic#

const d = new Date(clock.date)
const tomorrow = new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate() + 1)
const daysInMonth = new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth() + 1, 0).getDate()
const firstWeekday = new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), 1).getDay()   // 0 = Sunday
const mondayFirst = (firstWeekday + 6) % 7
const diffMs = target - d                       // subtract dates → milliseconds
const minutesLeft = Math.ceil(diffMs / 60000)

These are the building blocks of the calendar popup in Project: Clock and Calendar Popup.

Durations ("1:23:45", "3 min left")#

function fmtDuration(totalSec: int): string {
    const h = Math.floor(totalSec / 3600)
    const m = Math.floor((totalSec % 3600) / 60)
    const s = totalSec % 60
    const pad = n => String(n).padStart(2, "0")
    return h > 0 ? `${h}:${pad(m)}:${pad(s)}` : `${m}:${pad(s)}`
}

Used for media position and length (MPRIS gives seconds) and battery time-to-empty.

ElapsedTimer: measuring time#

ElapsedTimer measures time precisely, without the overhead of Date:

ElapsedTimer { id: stopwatch }
// stopwatch.restart() → later: stopwatch.elapsed() (seconds), elapsedMs(), elapsedNs()

Useful for stopwatches, "pressed for how long", or measuring how long a command took.

A countdown / pomodoro widget#

Item {
    id: pomo
    property int remaining: 25 * 60
    property bool running: false

    Timer {
        interval: 1000; repeat: true; running: pomo.running && pomo.remaining > 0
        onTriggered: {
            pomo.remaining--
            if (pomo.remaining === 0)
                Quickshell.execDetached(["notify-send", "Pomodoro", "Time for a break!"])
        }
    }
    Text {
        text: Math.floor(pomo.remaining / 60) + ":" + String(pomo.remaining % 60).padStart(2, "0")
        font.features: ({ "tnum": 1 })
        color: pomo.running ? "#a6e3a1" : "#cdd6f4"
        TapHandler { onTapped: pomo.running = !pomo.running }
        TapHandler { acceptedButtons: Qt.RightButton; onTapped: { pomo.running = false; pomo.remaining = 25 * 60 } }
    }
}
Exercises
  1. Replace the Timer-based clock from Chapter 4 with SystemClock (minutes precision).
  2. Show "Good morning / afternoon / evening" based on clock.hours.
  3. Make an OSD-style box that appears for 1.5 s each time you click a button, resetting the countdown on each click.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Shell Structure, Pragmas and Reloading

From here on we use Quickshell's own types. This chapter covers how a config is organized at the top level: the root object, the special //@ pragma lines, and what happens when Quickshell reloads.

The entry point: shell.qml#

Quickshell loads shell.qml from your config folder. Its root object can be:

  • a window (fine for a single bar, as in Your First Shell and the Dev Loop),
  • a Scope: a non-visual container for many windows and objects,
  • a ShellRoot: like Scope, plus an inline settings group.

Real configs use ShellRoot or Scope:

shell.qmlimport Quickshell
import QtQuick

ShellRoot {
    Bar {}                 // Bar.qml, a Scope with one PanelWindow per screen
    Notifications {}       // Notifications.qml
    Launcher {}            // Launcher.qml
}

Each child is usually its own file. shell.qml stays short: it's the table of contents of your shell.

Scope: grouping non-visual things#

Windows aren't Items, so they can't be children of a Rectangle or Item. A Scope is the container for anything that isn't drawn inside another window: windows, services, timers, IPC handlers, Variants.

Bar.qmlimport Quickshell
import QtQuick

Scope {
    // several windows can live in one Scope
    PanelWindow { anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true } implicitHeight: 32 }
    PanelWindow { anchors { bottom: true; left: true; right: true } implicitHeight: 24 }
    Timer { /* … */ }
}

Scopes also take part in reloading: when your config reloads, Quickshell matches old and new objects inside scopes to reuse windows and avoid flicker.

ShellRoot and settings#

ShellRoot exposes QuickshellSettings through settings:

ShellRoot {
    settings.watchFiles: true            // reload on file save (default true)
    settings.workingDirectory: Quickshell.env("HOME")
}

The same options are available at runtime on the Quickshell singleton: Quickshell.watchFiles, Quickshell.workingDirectory.

Pragmas#

Lines starting with //@ pragma at the top of shell.qml configure Quickshell before it loads anything:

shell.qml//@ pragma UseQApplication
//@ pragma IconTheme Papirus-Dark
//@ pragma Env QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE=Basic
//@ pragma Env QS_NO_RELOAD_POPUP=1
//@ pragma ShellId myshell
import Quickshell
Pragma Effect
UseQApplication Run as a full QApplication instead of a QGuiApplication. Needed by some Qt Widgets-based features (some Controls styles, native platform menus in some setups).
IconTheme <name> Icon theme for Quickshell.iconPath() and image://icon/
Env NAME=value Set an environment variable for the Quickshell process (and child processes)
ShellId <id> Stable shell ID, used for the data, state and cache dirs and to identify the instance
AppId <id> Desktop application ID (default org.quickshell)
DataDir <path> / StateDir <path> / CacheDir <path> Override Quickshell.dataDir, Quickshell.stateDir, Quickshell.cacheDir
DefaultEnv NAME=value Like Env, but only if the variable isn't already set
NativeTextRendering Use native (hinted) text rendering everywhere
RespectSystemStyle Don't force Quickshell's default Qt Quick Controls style
IgnoreSystemSettings Ignore desktop settings (system fonts, palette) when starting Qt
DropExpensiveFonts Skip font types that are expensive to load (saves startup time and memory)

Useful environment variables to set with Env:

Variable Meaning
QS_NO_RELOAD_POPUP=1 Don't show the "config reloaded" popup
QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE=Basic Controls style that's easiest to restyle
QT_QUICK_FLICKABLE_WHEEL_DECELERATION=… Tune scroll feel
QT_SCALE_FACTOR=1 Force a scale factor
Pragmas only in shell.qml, above the imports

Pragmas are read from the entry file before QML loads, and reading stops at the first import line. Put them at the very top. In other files they're just comments. An unknown pragma prints Unrecognized pragma in the log.

Hot reloading in detail#

When you save any file in your config folder:

  1. Quickshell parses the whole config again.
  2. If there's an error, it keeps the current version running and reports the error.
  3. If parsing succeeds, it creates the new object tree, matches windows and reloadable objects from the old tree to reuse them, then destroys the old tree.

What survives a reload:

Survives Doesn't survive
Windows (reused when matched, so no flicker) Plain property values (reset to defaults)
PersistentProperties values JS variables, Timer progress
NotificationServer notifications (with keepOnReload) Process state (processes restart)
Files you wrote with FileView Animations in progress

Matching objects across reloads: reloadableId#

Quickshell matches reloadable objects by position in the tree. If you reorder things, they may not match. Give important ones a stable Reloadable.reloadableId:

PersistentProperties {
    id: persist
    reloadableId: "sidebar-state"
    property bool open: false
    property int tab: 0
}

Reacting to reloads#

Connections {
    target: Quickshell
    function onReloadCompleted() { Quickshell.inhibitReloadPopup(); console.log("reloaded") }
    function onReloadFailed(error) { console.warn("reload failed:", error) }
}

Trigger a reload from code with Quickshell.reload(false) (soft: reuse windows) or Quickshell.reload(true) (hard: recreate everything).

Version checks#

Shells that others install may need to run on several Quickshell versions:

Component.onCompleted: {
    if (!Quickshell.hasVersion(0, 2)) console.warn("This shell needs Quickshell 0.2+")
}

Quickshell.hasVersion() and Quickshell.hasQtVersion() let you gate features.

Multiple instances#

You can run several configs at once (qs -c bar and qs -c widgets). Each is independent. Most people run one config that contains everything, which makes sharing state trivial. Some setups (like JaKooLit's) run small single-purpose configs alongside other tools.

Exercises
  1. Convert your playground shell.qml into a ShellRoot that contains a Bar {} from Bar.qml.
  2. Add //@ pragma IconTheme Papirus-Dark and //@ pragma Env QS_NO_RELOAD_POPUP=1.
  3. Add a PersistentProperties with a property int counter, increment it with a click, save the file, and see the counter survive the reload.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Windows: PanelWindow, Layers and Exclusive Zones

Everything Quickshell shows lives in a window. There are three kinds:

Type What it is Use for
PanelWindow A layer-shell surface glued to screen edges bars, docks, OSDs, launchers, notifications, overlays, desktop widgets, wallpapers
FloatingWindow A normal app window the compositor manages settings apps, debug panels
PopupWindow A popup positioned relative to another window dropdown menus, calendars, tooltips

All three share the base type QsWindow: visible, implicitWidth/implicitHeight, color, screen, mask, devicePixelRatio, and helpers like itemRect().

PanelWindow in depth#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    id: bar

    // ---- which screen ----
    screen: Quickshell.screens[0]

    // ---- placement ----
    anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }   // edges to attach to
    margins { top: 6; left: 8; right: 8 }            // distance from those edges
    implicitHeight: 36

    // ---- space reservation ----
    exclusiveZone: 36 + 6          // pixels reserved; tiled windows won't overlap
    // exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Auto   (default) reserve the window's size
    // exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore don't reserve, and ignore other panels' zones
    // exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Normal reserve nothing, but respect others

    // ---- stacking & input ----
    aboveWindows: true             // Top layer (false = Bottom layer)
    focusable: false               // take keyboard focus?

    // ---- look ----
    color: "transparent"           // window background (default WHITE!)
    visible: true

    // ---- layer-shell specifics ----
    WlrLayershell.namespace: "quickshell:bar"
    WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Top
    WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.None
}

anchors: attaching to screen edges#

anchors has four booleans. The combination decides the shape:

Anchors set Result You must set
none centered on screen implicitWidth and implicitHeight
top centered along the top edge both
top, left, right full-width top bar implicitHeight
bottom, left, right full-width bottom bar implicitHeight
left, top, bottom full-height left bar implicitWidth
top, right top-right corner (notifications) both
all four covers the whole screen nothing

margins#

Distance from each anchored edge. Margins on un-anchored edges do nothing. Use them for floating "island" bars and for placing popups below the bar.

exclusiveZone and exclusionMode#

  • exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Auto (default): reserve exactly the window's height or width plus margin.
  • Setting exclusiveZone: N switches to manual mode and reserves N pixels.
  • ExclusionMode.Ignore: reserve nothing and ignore other panels' reservations. Use it for overlays, fullscreen click-through windows, OSDs and launchers.
  • ExclusionMode.Normal: reserve nothing but stay out of other panels' zones.
Autohide bars

To hide a bar without windows jumping around, switch exclusiveZone between the bar height and 0 at the same time as animating the bar's content.

Layers#

WlrLayershell.layer picks one of four layers, via WlrLayer:

Layer Above Use
WlrLayer.Background nothing wallpaper
WlrLayer.Bottom wallpaper desktop widgets, desktop clock
WlrLayer.Top normal windows bars, docks (hidden by fullscreen windows)
WlrLayer.Overlay everything, including fullscreen launchers, OSDs, notifications, power menu

aboveWindows: true/false is a shortcut for Top/Bottom.

Namespace#

WlrLayershell.namespace names the surface for compositor rules. Pick a scheme like quickshell:<component>:

hyprland.conflayerrule = blur, quickshell:bar
layerrule = ignorealpha 0.3, quickshell:.*
layerrule = animation slide top, quickshell:notifications
layerrule = noanim, quickshell:osd

The namespace can't change after the window is created.

Keyboard focus#

WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus uses WlrKeyboardFocus:

Mode Behavior Use
None (default) never receives keys bars, widgets
OnDemand receives keys when clicked or focused normally sidebars with search boxes
Exclusive grabs all keyboard input while mapped launchers, power menus, lock-like UIs

focusable: true on PanelWindow is a portable shortcut (roughly OnDemand).

color, transparency and surface format#

The window's color defaults to white. For rounded, floating or translucent designs, set color: "transparent" and draw your own background inside. Translucency requires an alpha surface, which Quickshell picks automatically when the color isn't opaque at creation. QsWindow.surfaceFormat lets you force opaque for performance on opaque windows.

FloatingWindow#

FloatingWindow {
    title: "My Shell Settings"
    implicitWidth: 700; implicitHeight: 500
    minimumSize: Qt.size(400, 300)
    visible: GlobalStates.settingsOpen
    color: "#1e1e2e"
    onClosed: GlobalStates.settingsOpen = false     // user closed it via the compositor
}

It's managed like any app window: tiled, floated or fullscreened by the compositor. Members include title, minimumSize, maximumSize, minimized, maximized, fullscreen, parentWindow, startSystemMove() and startSystemResize(edges). Match it in compositor rules by title or app id.

Which screen? screen#

Every window has screen (ShellScreen). If you don't set it, the compositor picks one (usually the focused monitor). Multiple Monitors with Variants shows how to make one window per screen with Variants.

Useful QsWindow members#

Member Use
visible show/hide (window is unmapped when false)
backingWindowVisible whether it's actually mapped right now
contentItem root Item holding your children
devicePixelRatio the screen's scale factor
mask click-through region (Masks, Regions and Click-Through)
itemPosition(item) / itemRect(item) where an item is within the window (to anchor popups)
mapFromItem(item, …) coordinate mapping
updatesEnabled pause rendering of a hidden-but-mapped window
closed() signal the compositor closed the window
windowConnected() signal the window got its platform surface

From inside any item, the attached QsWindow.window gives you the containing window:

Rectangle {
    // deep inside a bar component:
    TapHandler { onTapped: console.log("I'm in", QsWindow.window, "on", QsWindow.window.screen.name) }
}

Common window recipes#

// 1. centered launcher (no anchors), above everything, grabs keys
PanelWindow {
    implicitWidth: 600; implicitHeight: 420
    exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
    color: "transparent"
    WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay
    WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive
}

// 2. click-through fullscreen overlay (decorations, screen corners)
PanelWindow {
    anchors { top: true; bottom: true; left: true; right: true }
    exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
    color: "transparent"
    mask: Region {}                       // empty region = no input at all
    WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay
}

// 3. desktop widget on the Bottom layer
PanelWindow {
    anchors { top: true; left: true }
    margins { top: 80; left: 80 }
    implicitWidth: 400; implicitHeight: 200
    exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
    color: "transparent"
    WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Bottom
}

// 4. OSD at bottom center
PanelWindow {
    anchors.bottom: true
    margins.bottom: 80
    implicitWidth: 300; implicitHeight: 56
    exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
    color: "transparent"
    WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay
}
Exercises
  1. Make a 44 px left vertical bar that reserves space.
  2. Make a centered 500×300 overlay window that closes on Esc (keyboard focus Exclusive + Keys.onEscapePressed).
  3. Make a desktop clock on the Bottom layer and confirm windows cover it.
  4. Add a blur layerrule for your bar's namespace (Hyprland).
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Multiple Monitors with Variants

A single PanelWindow appears on one screen. Most people want a bar on every monitor, and they want it to appear and disappear as monitors are plugged in. Quickshell's Variants does exactly that.

Screens#

Quickshell.screens is the list of connected monitors, each a ShellScreen:

ShellScreen property Example
name "eDP-1", "DP-2", "HDMI-A-1"
model "DELL U2720Q"
serialNumber
x, y position in the global layout
width, height logical size
devicePixelRatio scale factor (1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0…)
physicalPixelDensity, logicalPixelDensity pixels per mm
orientation, primaryOrientation rotation 
Component.onCompleted: Quickshell.screens.forEach(s => console.log(s.name, s.width + "x" + s.height, "@" + s.devicePixelRatio))

Variants: one copy per model entry#

Bar.qmlimport Quickshell
import QtQuick

Scope {
    Variants {
        model: Quickshell.screens          // one entry per monitor

        PanelWindow {                      // the delegate: created once per screen
            required property ShellScreen modelData
            screen: modelData              // put this copy on that screen

            anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }
            implicitHeight: 32

            Text {
                anchors.centerIn: parent
                text: modelData.name + "  ·  " + modelData.width + "×" + modelData.height
            }
        }
    }
}

When you plug in a monitor, Quickshell.screens changes and Variants creates a new bar. Unplug it and that bar is destroyed.

Variants vs Repeater#

Variants Repeater
Creates any objects, including windows Items inside a parent item
Lives in a Scope (non-visual) an Item
Typical model Quickshell.screens lists of data to draw

Variants' members: model, delegate, instances (the created objects). The delegate receives modelData; declare it as required property.

Only some monitors#

Variants {
    model: Quickshell.screens.filter(s => s.name !== "HDMI-A-1")   // skip the TV
}

Better: make it configurable (Files, Watching and JSON Config):

model: Config.bar.screens.length
       ? Quickshell.screens.filter(s => Config.bar.screens.includes(s.name))
       : Quickshell.screens

Per-monitor differences#

Inside the delegate, modelData tells you which screen you're on:

PanelWindow {
    required property ShellScreen modelData
    screen: modelData
    readonly property bool isLaptop: modelData.name.startsWith("eDP")
    implicitHeight: isLaptop ? 30 : 36
    // show the tray only on the main monitor:
    Loader { active: modelData.name === Config.primaryMonitor; sourceComponent: Tray {} }
}

Per-screen compositor data#

Each compositor module can map a ShellScreen to its own monitor object:

import Quickshell.Hyprland
readonly property HyprlandMonitor hyprMon: Hyprland.monitorFor(modelData)
// hyprMon.activeWorkspace, hyprMon.focused, hyprMon.scale …

import Quickshell.I3
readonly property I3Monitor swayMon: I3.monitorFor(modelData)

This is how each monitor's bar shows its own active workspace.

A single window on the focused monitor#

Launchers, OSDs and notifications usually appear only on the monitor you're using, not on all of them:

import Quickshell.Hyprland

PanelWindow {
    screen: Quickshell.screens.find(s => s.name === Hyprland.focusedMonitor?.name) ?? Quickshell.screens[0]
    // …
}

Or keep one window per screen and show only the focused one:

Variants {
    model: Quickshell.screens
    PanelWindow {
        required property ShellScreen modelData
        screen: modelData
        visible: GlobalStates.launcherOpen && Hyprland.focusedMonitor?.name === modelData.name
    }
}

The first approach uses one window (less memory). The second avoids recreating the surface when focus moves.

HiDPI notes#

  • Qt works in logical pixels: implicitHeight: 32 is 32 logical px, which is 48 physical px at 1.5× scale.
  • For crisp images, set sourceSize to the display size × screen.devicePixelRatio.
  • Fractional scales can blur 1 px lines; stick to whole logical pixels for borders.
Exercises
  1. Show each monitor's name and scale factor in its own bar.
  2. Make the bar on your laptop screen thinner than on external monitors.
  3. Make a centered "Hello" overlay that appears only on the focused monitor.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Popups, Anchors and Menus

Click the clock and a calendar drops down. Click a tray icon and a menu appears. Hover a module and a tooltip shows. These are popups: separate surfaces positioned relative to something in your bar. Quickshell provides PopupWindow, the PopupAnchor positioning system, and QsMenuAnchor / QsMenuOpener for menus.

Why not just a bigger rectangle?#

Your bar window is 36 px tall. Anything drawn below that is clipped, invisible. A popup needs its own window. That's what PopupWindow creates, positioned by the compositor relative to the parent window, even across screen edges.

PopupWindow basics#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    id: bar
    anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }
    implicitHeight: 36

    Text {
        id: clockText
        anchors.centerIn: parent
        text: "14:32"
        MouseArea { anchors.fill: parent; onClicked: cal.visible = !cal.visible }
    }

    PopupWindow {
        id: cal
        anchor.window: bar               // positioned relative to the bar window…
        anchor.item: clockText           // …and to this item inside it
        anchor.edges: Edges.Bottom       // attach to the item's bottom edge
        anchor.gravity: Edges.Bottom     // and grow downward from there
        anchor.margins.top: 8            // gap between bar and popup
        implicitWidth: 280
        implicitHeight: 300
        color: "transparent"
        visible: false
        grabFocus: true                  // close automatically when clicking outside

        Rectangle {
            anchors.fill: parent
            radius: 16
            color: "#1e1e2e"
            Text { anchors.centerIn: parent; color: "white"; text: Qt.formatDate(new Date(), "MMMM yyyy") }
        }
    }
}

PopupWindow members#

Member Meaning
anchor a PopupAnchor group describing where the popup attaches (below)
visible show or hide (defaults to false)
grabFocus if true, clicking outside dismisses the popup and sets visible to false
implicitWidth, implicitHeight, color, mask… inherited from QsWindow
screen read-only: where it ended up
grabFocus

grabFocus: true gives you "click outside to close" on any compositor that supports popup grabs, with no extra code. While open, the popup receives keyboard input too.

PopupAnchor: where the popup goes#

The anchor group positions the popup:

Property Meaning
window the parent window (required, unless item is set, in which case its window is used)
item an item to attach to; the anchor rectangle becomes that item's rectangle
rect.x, rect.y, rect.width, rect.height a manual anchor rectangle, relative to item or window
margins.left/right/top/bottom shrink or grow the anchor rectangle
edges which point of the anchor rectangle to attach to (Edges flags)
gravity which direction the popup extends from that point
adjustment what to do if it doesn't fit on screen (PopupAdjustment: Slide, Flip, Resize, All…)
updateAnchor() recompute when the anchor item moved but no property changed
anchoring() signal fires just before positioning, so you can tweak rect

edges + gravity, visually#

Common setups:

// dropdown centered under an item
anchor.item: btn; anchor.edges: Edges.Bottom; anchor.gravity: Edges.Bottom

// menu aligned to the item's left edge
anchor.edges: Edges.Bottom | Edges.Left; anchor.gravity: Edges.Bottom | Edges.Right

// for a bottom bar: open upward
anchor.edges: Edges.Top; anchor.gravity: Edges.Top

// for a left vertical bar: open to the right
anchor.edges: Edges.Right; anchor.gravity: Edges.Right

// manual position relative to the window
anchor.window: bar
anchor.rect.x: bar.width - width - 10
anchor.rect.y: bar.height + 6

Keeping popups on screen#

anchor.adjustment: PopupAdjustment.Slide | PopupAdjustment.Flip   // slide along the edge, flip if needed

Hover tooltips#

A tooltip is a PopupWindow shown while hovering, after a short delay:

widgets/Tooltip.qmlimport Quickshell
import QtQuick

PopupWindow {
    id: tip
    required property Item target
    property string text
    property bool show: false

    anchor.item: target
    anchor.edges: Edges.Bottom
    anchor.gravity: Edges.Bottom
    anchor.margins.top: 6
    implicitWidth: label.implicitWidth + 16
    implicitHeight: label.implicitHeight + 10
    color: "transparent"
    visible: show && text !== ""

    Rectangle { anchors.fill: parent; radius: 8; color: "#11111b"; border.color: "#313244" }
    Text { id: label; anchors.centerIn: parent; text: tip.text; color: "#cdd6f4"; font.pixelSize: 12 }
}
Rectangle {
    id: wifiIcon
    HoverHandler { id: hh }
    Timer { id: delay; interval: 500; running: hh.hovered }
    Tooltip { target: wifiIcon; text: "Connected to Home-5G"; show: hh.hovered && !delay.running }
}

Menus#

System tray menus: QsMenuAnchor#

Tray items expose a menu handle (SystemTrayItem.menu). QsMenuAnchor displays it as a native-looking menu at an anchor:

QsMenuAnchor {
    id: menuAnchor
    menu: trayItem.menu                   // a QsMenuHandle
    anchor.item: trayIcon
    anchor.edges: Edges.Bottom
    anchor.gravity: Edges.Bottom
}
// on right click: menuAnchor.open()

Members: anchor, menu, visible, open(), close(), signals opened(), closed().

Fully custom menus: QsMenuOpener#

To draw the menu in your own style, read its entries with QsMenuOpener and build the UI yourself in a PopupWindow:

QsMenuOpener {
    id: opener
    menu: trayItem.menu
}

ColumnLayout {
    Repeater {
        model: opener.children                  // ObjectModel of QsMenuEntry
        Rectangle {
            required property QsMenuEntry modelData
            Layout.fillWidth: true
            implicitHeight: modelData.isSeparator ? 1 : 30
            color: modelData.isSeparator ? "#45475a" : hov.hovered ? "#313244" : "transparent"
            HoverHandler { id: hov }
            Text {
                visible: !modelData.isSeparator
                anchors.verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter; x: 10
                text: modelData.text
                color: modelData.enabled ? "#cdd6f4" : "#6c7086"
            }
            TapHandler { enabled: modelData.enabled && !modelData.isSeparator; onTapped: modelData.triggered() }
        }
    }
}

QsMenuEntry gives you text, icon, enabled, isSeparator, buttonType (checkbox or radio), checkState, hasChildren (for submenus: open another QsMenuOpener with menu: entry), the triggered() signal to activate it, and display(window, x, y) for a native submenu. Project: System Tray with Custom Menus builds a complete custom tray menu, submenus included.

Popups from deep inside components#

A widget nested deep in a bar can find its window with the attached QsWindow.window:

PopupWindow {
    anchor.window: QsWindow.window      // whatever window contains this component
    anchor.item: myButton
}

Popups vs separate panels#

Use a PopupWindow when… Use a separate PanelWindow when…
it belongs to one bar element (calendar under clock) it's a big standalone panel (sidebar, launcher)
it should follow that element it has its own position (screen edge, center)
it's small and transient it needs exclusive keyboard focus or its own layer
Exercises
  1. Add a calendar popup under your clock with grabFocus: true.
  2. Build Tooltip.qml and add tooltips to three bar modules.
  3. Make the calendar open upward if the bar is at the bottom (bind edges/gravity to a property bool bottomBar).
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Singletons and Global State

Your bar shows the volume. So do the OSD, the control center and the lock screen. Your theme colors are used in every file. The question "is the launcher open?" matters to the bar button, the launcher window and a keybind. Passing all of that through properties would be a nightmare. Singletons solve it: one global object, accessible by name from any file.

What a singleton is#

You already use Quickshell's singletons: Quickshell, Hyprland, UPower, Pipewire, Mpris, SystemTray, DesktopEntries… There's exactly one of each, and you refer to them by type name without creating them.

You can write your own the same way.

Writing a singleton#

services/GlobalStates.qmlpragma Singleton                       // 1. this line makes the file a singleton

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Singleton {                            // 2. root type: Quickshell's Singleton
    id: root

    property bool launcherOpen: false
    property bool sidebarOpen: false
    property bool dnd: false

    function toggleLauncher(): void {
        launcherOpen = !launcherOpen
    }
}

Use it from any file that imports its folder:

modules/bar/LauncherButton.qmlimport QtQuick
import qs.services                      // the folder containing GlobalStates.qml

Text {
    text: GlobalStates.launcherOpen ? "close" : "apps"
    font.family: "Material Symbols Rounded"
    TapHandler { onTapped: GlobalStates.toggleLauncher() }
}
modules/launcher/Launcher.qmlimport Quickshell
import qs.services

PanelWindow {
    visible: GlobalStates.launcherOpen   // the same global state
    // …
}

Both files bind to the same property. Toggle it anywhere and both update.

Rules#

  1. pragma Singleton as the first non-comment line.
  2. The root object is Singleton (Quickshell's reload-aware singleton root).
  3. The file lives in a folder you import (import qs.services or import "services"). Quickshell detects the pragma automatically; you don't need a qmldir file.
  4. Refer to it by file name: services/Audio.qml becomes Audio.

Singletons are lazy#

A singleton is created the first time something uses it. If nothing references it, it never runs. That's usually great, but it matters for things that must start at login, like a notification server or a battery warning:

shell.qmlimport Quickshell
import qs.services

ShellRoot {
    // reference it once so it starts immediately
    Component.onCompleted: Notifs.init()
    // or simply bind something to it:  property var _keepAlive: [Notifs, BatteryWarning]
}

The service pattern#

The most important use of singletons in real shells is services: a singleton that wraps one area of the system and exposes clean properties and functions. UI files read services and never talk to the system directly.

services/Audio.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root

    readonly property PwNode sink: Pipewire.defaultAudioSink
    readonly property bool ready: sink?.ready ?? false
    readonly property real volume: sink?.audio?.volume ?? 0
    readonly property bool muted: sink?.audio?.muted ?? false
    readonly property string icon: muted ? "volume_off"
                                 : volume > 0.6 ? "volume_up"
                                 : volume > 0 ? "volume_down" : "volume_mute"

    function setVolume(v: real): void {
        if (ready) sink.audio.volume = Math.max(0, Math.min(1.5, v))
    }
    function toggleMute(): void {
        if (ready) sink.audio.muted = !sink.audio.muted
    }

    PwObjectTracker { objects: [root.sink] }     // required for PipeWire, see Chapter 41
}

Now every UI file just writes Audio.volume, Audio.icon, Audio.setVolume(…):

Benefits:

  • One place to fix bugs and change behavior.
  • Swap implementations without touching UI (e.g. switch Wi-Fi from nmcli to the Networking module).
  • Derived values (like icon) computed once and shared.
In the wild

end-4's services/ folder has Audio, Battery, Brightness, Network, Notifications, MprisController, HyprlandData, Ai and more, all singletons. Caelestia's services/ has the same idea. Read them after Part VII.

Singletons that use each other#

Singletons can reference other singletons:

services/Colors.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    readonly property color accent: Config.appearance.accent     // Config is another singleton
    readonly property color barBg: Qt.rgba(0.1, 0.1, 0.15, Config.appearance.transparency)
}

Avoid circular dependencies (A reads B while B reads A during creation), which can cause binding loops or undefined values.

What belongs in a singleton?#

Put in a singleton Keep local
System state (audio, battery, network, media) Hover and pressed state of a button
Panel open/closed states Animation progress
Theme colors, sizes, fonts Layout details of one component
User config Temporary text in a text field
Shared helper functions (formatting)

Alternatives#

  • Properties down, signals up for parent/child relationships (Components, Files and Imports).
  • PersistentProperties for state that must survive reloads.
  • FileView + JsonAdapter for state that must survive restarts, often inside a singleton (Files, Watching and JSON Config).
Exercises
  1. Create services/GlobalStates.qml with property bool calendarOpen, and toggle it from a bar button.
  2. Write services/Time.qml that owns one SystemClock and exposes property string time and property string date. Use it in two places.
  3. Write the Audio service above and show Audio.icon plus a percentage in your bar.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Lazy Loading and Memory

A full shell has a dozen panels: launcher, sidebar, overview, power menu, wallpaper picker, settings, cheatsheet. If all of them existed all the time, your shell would use hundreds of megabytes and start slowly. The fix: create panels only while they're open.

LazyLoader#

LazyLoader creates a component when needed and destroys it when not. Unlike Qt's Loader, it's designed for windows and non-visual objects (anything, not just Items), and it can pre-load in the background.

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

Scope {
    LazyLoader {
        id: loader
        active: GlobalStates.launcherOpen     // true → create now; false → destroy

        PanelWindow {                         // the component (implicit)
            implicitWidth: 600; implicitHeight: 400
            WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay
            WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive
            // …launcher UI…
        }
    }
}

LazyLoader members#

Member Meaning
active true: load fully now (synchronously, blocking) and keep it. false: destroy it.
activeAsync Like active, but loads asynchronously first (no stutter), then activates.
loading true: start loading in the background without showing it, so a later active: true is instant.
component The component to load (implicit when you write a child).
source Load from a file URL instead.
item The created object, or null.

Three strategies#

// 1. Create on open, destroy on close (lowest memory)
LazyLoader { active: GlobalStates.overviewOpen; Overview {} }

// 2. Pre-load in the background at startup, show instantly later
LazyLoader {
    loading: true                         // build in the background
    active: GlobalStates.launcherOpen     // flip to visible instantly when needed
    Launcher {}
}

// 3. Async activation (no frame drop for heavy panels)
LazyLoader { activeAsync: GlobalStates.settingsOpen; SettingsWindow {} }
Closing animations with LazyLoader

If active goes false the window is destroyed immediately, so there's no time for a closing animation. Keep it active during the animation: active: GlobalStates.sidebarOpen || closeAnim.running, or keep a separate property bool shown that turns false only after the animation finishes.

Loader (for items inside a window)#

For parts of a window (tab pages, heavy widgets), use Qt's Loader (Object Lifecycle and Dynamic Creation):

Loader {
    active: tabs.currentIndex === 2
    asynchronous: true
    sourceComponent: BigMediaDashboard {}
}

visible vs LazyLoader vs Loader#

Memory while hidden Opens instantly State kept when hidden Use for
visible: false full yes yes small or frequently toggled things
LazyLoader { active } none small delay no big windows opened sometimes
LazyLoader { loading: true; active } full after preload yes yes big windows opened often (launcher)
Loader { active } none small delay no heavy parts inside a window

Keeping state across loads#

Destroyed panels forget their state (scroll position, selected tab, typed text). Keep anything worth remembering in a singleton, so the new instance picks it up:

// in the panel:
TabBar { currentIndex: GlobalStates.sidebarTab; onCurrentIndexChanged: GlobalStates.sidebarTab = currentIndex }

Other memory tips#

  • Set sourceSize on every image (Rectangle, Text and Image).
  • Use ListView instead of Repeater for long lists: it only creates visible delegates.
  • Don't keep ScreencopyView.live: true for hidden previews.
  • Watch memory: ps -o rss,cmd -p $(pgrep -f "qs -c myshell") shows resident memory in KB.
In the wild

end-4 loads its sidebars, overview, session screen and cheatsheet lazily, controlled by GlobalStates. Caelestia keeps its drawers mostly loaded so they animate out of the bar instantly, a deliberate memory-for-smoothness trade.

Exercises
  1. Wrap a big test window in a LazyLoader toggled by a bar button. Add Component.onCompleted/onDestruction logs and watch them.
  2. Switch it to loading: true and notice that it opens instantly.
  3. Keep it alive during a 300 ms fade-out using active: open || fade.running.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Masks, Regions and Click-Through

A window catches every click inside its rectangle, even where it's transparent. That's a problem for screen-corner overlays, OSDs, floating widgets and Caelestia-style fullscreen shells. The mask property controls exactly which parts of a window accept input.

mask and Region#

Every QsWindow has a mask property that takes a Region. When it's set, only the region is clickable; everything else passes through to the windows underneath.

Fully click-through#

PanelWindow {
    anchors { top: true; bottom: true; left: true; right: true }
    exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
    color: "transparent"
    WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay
    mask: Region {}                 // empty region → no input anywhere
    // decorations, screen corners, visual effects…
}

Use it for anything purely visual on top of your desktop: screen corners, a desktop clock you don't interact with, OSDs.

Clickable only where an item is#

PanelWindow {
    anchors { top: true; bottom: true; left: true; right: true }
    exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
    color: "transparent"

    mask: Region { item: card }     // only the card catches clicks

    Rectangle {
        id: card
        x: 100; y: 100; width: 300; height: 200; radius: 16
        color: "#1e1e2e"
    }
}

The region follows the item's geometry automatically: move or resize card (even with an animation) and the clickable area moves with it.

Region properties#

Property Meaning
item Take geometry from this item (overrides x/y/width/height)
x, y, width, height Manual geometry (window coordinates)
shape RegionShape: RegionShape.Rect (default) or RegionShape.Ellipse
radius, topLeftRadius, topRightRadius, bottomLeftRadius, bottomRightRadius Rounded rectangle corners
intersection How it combines with its parent region (Intersection): Combine, Subtract, Intersect, Xor
regions Child regions (default property: write them inside)
changed() Emitted when geometry changes

Combining regions#

Nest regions to build complex shapes. Children combine with their parent according to intersection:

mask: Region {
    item: bar                                           // the bar is clickable…
    Region { item: drawer }                             // …plus the drawer (Combine is the default)
    Region { item: notifications }                      // …plus the notification stack
    Region { item: hole; intersection: Intersection.Subtract }   // minus this hole
}
Intersection Result
Combine union: parent OR child
Subtract parent minus child
Intersect only where both overlap
Xor where exactly one of them is

The fullscreen-shell architecture (Caelestia style)#

Instead of one window per bar, popup and drawer, some shells use one fullscreen transparent window per monitor that contains everything (bar, drawers, popups, notifications), with a mask covering only the visible parts:

Why do this?

  • Drawers can animate out of the bar seamlessly: same window, same coordinates, shared shapes.
  • Inverted corners and outlines connect bar and panels in one Shape.
  • Popups never need cross-window positioning.

What you must handle yourself:

  1. Space reservation: with ExclusionMode.Ignore the big window reserves nothing, so add a second, invisible PanelWindow per screen with an exclusiveZone equal to your bar size.
  2. Masking: keep the mask in sync with what's visible (bind each region's item to visible parts).
  3. Keyboard focus: switch WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus to OnDemand or Exclusive only while a panel that needs typing is open.
// the reservation window (one per screen)
PanelWindow {
    required property ShellScreen modelData
    screen: modelData
    anchors { left: true; top: true; bottom: true }
    implicitWidth: 1                     // tiny, invisible
    exclusiveZone: 44                    // = bar width
    color: "transparent"
    mask: Region {}
}

Project: Edge Drawers (Caelestia Style) builds this architecture in full.

HyprlandWindow.visibleMask#

On Hyprland, HyprlandWindow adds visibleMask: a hint about which regions are actually visible, so the compositor can skip rendering (and blurring) the transparent parts of a big window. That's a worthwhile optimization for fullscreen shells:

import Quickshell.Hyprland
PanelWindow {
    mask: Region { item: panel }
    HyprlandWindow.visibleMask: Region { item: panel }
}

Masks and blur#

With compositor blur (Hyprland layerrule = blur), blur applies to the whole layer surface, minus fully transparent pixels when ignorealpha is set. On fullscreen transparent windows, always use ignorealpha, otherwise the entire screen may get blurred.

Exercises
  1. Make a fullscreen overlay with a draggable card where only the card catches clicks (DragHandler + mask: Region { item: card }).
  2. Make the clickable region a circle with shape: RegionShape.Ellipse.
  3. Build a mask that's a bar region plus an animated drawer region, and confirm clicks pass through everywhere else.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

ObjectModel and ScriptModel

Quickshell gives you live lists: workspaces, windows, tray icons, media players, notifications, audio nodes, Bluetooth devices, apps. They come as ObjectModels. When you need to filter or sort them, ScriptModel keeps views fast and animated.

ObjectModel: live lists from services#

Many properties in the API reference have the type ObjectModel<…>:

Property Elements
Hyprland.workspaces HyprlandWorkspace
Hyprland.toplevels HyprlandToplevel
ToplevelManager.toplevels Toplevel
SystemTray.items SystemTrayItem
Mpris.players MprisPlayer
UPower.devices UPowerDevice
DesktopEntries.applications DesktopEntry
NotificationServer.trackedNotifications Notification
Pipewire.nodes PwNode
Bluetooth.devices BluetoothDevice

Use one directly as a model#

Repeater {
    model: Mpris.players
    Text { required property MprisPlayer modelData; text: modelData.identity }
}

When a player appears or disappears, the Repeater adds or removes exactly that delegate.

.values: as a JavaScript array#

objectModel.values is a normal list you can filter, find, map or sort, and bindings that use it update when the list changes:

readonly property MprisPlayer active: Mpris.players.values.find(p => p.isPlaying) ?? Mpris.players.values[0] ?? null
readonly property int windowCount: Hyprland.toplevels.values.length
readonly property list<HyprlandWorkspace> occupied: Hyprland.workspaces.values.filter(w => w.toplevels.values.length > 0)

ObjectModel signals and methods#

indexOf(object), and signals objectInsertedPre/Post(object, index) and objectRemovedPre/Post(object, index) if you need to react to individual changes:

Connections {
    target: Mpris.players
    function onObjectInsertedPost(player, index) { console.log("new player:", player.identity) }
}

The problem with filtered arrays#

Repeater {
    model: DesktopEntries.applications.values.filter(a => a.name.toLowerCase().includes(query))
    delegate: AppItem {}
}

This works, but every time query changes, the binding produces a brand-new array. The Repeater can't tell which items stayed the same, so it destroys all delegates and creates new ones. That means no add/remove animations, scroll and hover state lost, and more CPU.

ScriptModel: a diffing model#

ScriptModel takes a JS array in values, compares it with the previous one, and reports only the actual insertions and removals:

ListView {
    model: ScriptModel {
        values: DesktopEntries.applications.values
            .filter(a => a.name.toLowerCase().includes(search.text.toLowerCase()))
            .sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))
    }
    delegate: AppItem { required property DesktopEntry modelData }
    add:    Transition { NumberAnimation { property: "opacity"; from: 0; to: 1; duration: 150 } }
    remove: Transition { NumberAnimation { property: "opacity"; to: 0; duration: 150 } }
    displaced: Transition { NumberAnimation { property: "y"; duration: 150 } }
}

Now typing in the search box smoothly removes non-matching apps and keeps matching delegates alive.

ScriptModel members#

Member Meaning
values The array to reflect (usually a binding)
objectProp For plain JS objects: which key identifies "the same" item (e.g. "id")
comparisonMode ObjectComparison: Structure (default, compares contents) or Identity (faster, same object reference)
Unique values

ScriptModel expects each value in the list to be unique. Duplicates confuse the diff. For lists of plain objects (parsed JSON, nmcli results), set objectProp to a unique key like "ssid" or "id".

ListView {
    model: ScriptModel {
        values: Network.networks            // [{ ssid, signal, secure }, …], rebuilt on each scan
        objectProp: "ssid"                   // same ssid = same row, so it updates in place
    }
    delegate: NetworkRow { required property var modelData }
}

When to use which#

Situation Use
Show a service list as-is the ObjectModel directly
Read or compute from a list (count, find, any) .values in a binding
Filtered or sorted list shown in a view ScriptModel { values: … }
A list you edit by hand (todo, history) ListModel
A static list a JS array literal

Sorting workspaces and other gotchas#

  • Hyprland.workspaces is sorted by id. Named and special workspaces have negative ids and come first, so filter them out for a 1–10 indicator: .filter(w => w.id > 0).
  • Elements can be destroyed while you hold them (a player quits). Always use ?. on references you keep.
  • Don't mutate .values (push/splice); it's a read-only view.
Exercises
  1. Show the number of open windows (Hyprland.toplevels.values.length or ToplevelManager.toplevels.values.length).
  2. Build an app list filtered by a TextField with ScriptModel and add/remove transitions.
  3. Log every time a tray icon appears using Connections on SystemTray.items.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Running Commands with Process

Quickshell has native services for audio, battery, media and more, but there will always be something without one: CPU temperature, a weather API, brightnessctl, a script you wrote. Process runs any program asynchronously (your UI never freezes) and gives you its output.

Your first Process#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Scope {
    id: root
    property string kernel: "…"

    Process {
        command: ["uname", "-r"]               // program + arguments, as a LIST
        running: true                          // start immediately
        stdout: StdioCollector {
            onStreamFinished: root.kernel = this.text.trim()   // all output, once the program ends
        }
    }
}
  1. command is an argv list: the program name, then each argument as its own string. No quoting headaches.
  2. Setting running: true starts it. When the program exits, running becomes false on its own.
  3. stdout: StdioCollector { … } collects everything the program prints; onStreamFinished fires when it's done.
Always .trim()

Command output usually ends with a newline. "6.12.1\n" displays oddly and fails comparisons. Call .trim().

Shell features need a shell#

command runs a program directly, not through bash. Pipes (|), redirects (>), &&, globs (*) and $VARIABLES are terminal-shell features, so wrap them in sh -c:

Process {
    command: ["sh", "-c", "cat /sys/class/power_supply/BAT*/capacity | head -1"]
    running: true
    stdout: StdioCollector { onStreamFinished: console.log("battery:", text.trim()) }
}

When you need to insert a value into a shell command, pass it as an argument instead of pasting it into the string, which avoids quoting bugs and injection:

// ✗ breaks on names with spaces or quotes
command: ["sh", "-c", "notify-send '" + title + "'"]
// ✓ $1 is the next argument, passed safely
command: ["sh", "-c", 'notify-send "$1"', "sh", title]
// ✓✓ best: no shell needed at all
command: ["notify-send", title]

Re-running: polling#

A Process runs once each time running becomes true. To refresh periodically, pair it with a Timer:

Scope {
    id: root
    property int temp: 0

    Process {
        id: tempProc
        command: ["sh", "-c", "cat /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp"]
        stdout: StdioCollector { onStreamFinished: root.temp = Math.round(parseInt(text) / 1000) }
    }
    Timer {
        interval: 3000; running: true; repeat: true; triggeredOnStart: true
        onTriggered: tempProc.running = true
    }
}
Prefer FileView for files

Reading /sys or /proc files doesn't need a process at all. FileView reads the file directly, with no fork and exec (Files, Watching and JSON Config). Use Process for real programs.

Streaming output: SplitParser#

Some commands run forever and print events: nmcli monitor, pactl subscribe, niri msg -j event-stream, cava, inotifywait -m. Use SplitParser to get each line as it arrives:

Process {
    command: ["nmcli", "monitor"]
    running: true                              // keeps running
    stdout: SplitParser {
        splitMarker: "\n"                      // default; any string works
        onRead: line => {
            console.log("network event:", line)
            if (line.includes("connected")) refreshWifi()
        }
    }
}
Parser Gives you Use for
StdioCollector text (and data) when the stream ends; onStreamFinished one-shot commands
SplitParser onRead(chunk) per delimiter long-running event streams

StdioCollector.waitForEnd: false updates text continuously instead of only at the end.

Handling errors and exit codes#

Process {
    id: proc
    command: ["brightnessctl", "set", "50%"]
    stdout: StdioCollector { id: out }
    stderr: StdioCollector { id: err }
    onStarted: console.log("started, pid", processId)
    onExited: (exitCode, exitStatus) => {
        if (exitCode !== 0) console.warn("brightnessctl failed:", err.text)
    }
}

If a program doesn't exist, it fails to start and exited reports a non-zero code. Check which <program> in a terminal first.

Sending input: stdin#

Process {
    id: calc
    command: ["bc", "-l"]
    stdinEnabled: true
    running: true
    stdout: SplitParser { onRead: result => console.log("=", result) }
}
// later: calc.write("2^10\n")

Other Process members#

Member Meaning
command argv list
running start (true) / kill (false); turns false on exit
processId PID while running, else null
workingDirectory directory to run in
environment extra env vars: ({ LANG: "C", FOO: null }) (null removes a variable)
clearEnvironment start with an empty environment
stdout, stderr parsers
stdinEnabled, write(data) stdin
signal(sig) send a Unix signal (signal(15) = SIGTERM)
startDetached() launch a copy that outlives Quickshell
exec(command) stop the current run and start a new command in one call
onStarted, onExited(code, status) signals
Force English output

When parsing command output, set environment: ({ LANG: "C", LC_ALL: "C" }) so a German or Hindi locale doesn't change the text you're matching.

Fire and forget: Quickshell.execDetached#

To launch something without caring about its output (open an app, run a script, send a notification), use Quickshell.execDetached():

TapHandler { onTapped: Quickshell.execDetached(["kitty"]) }
TapHandler { onTapped: Quickshell.execDetached(["sh", "-c", "grim -g \"$(slurp)\" - | wl-copy"]) }

The process is detached, so it keeps running if Quickshell reloads or quits.

Launching apps properly#

Apps started from Quickshell become children of the Quickshell process. Many rices launch apps through the compositor or a launcher helper so they get their own scope and environment:

Hyprland.dispatch("exec kitty")                          // Hyprland
Quickshell.execDetached(["uwsm", "app", "--", "kitty"])  // UWSM-managed sessions
Quickshell.execDetached(["app2unit", "--", "kitty"])     // systemd scopes
entry.execute()                                          // DesktopEntry's own launcher

A complete example: CPU and RAM usage#

services/SystemUsage.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root
    property real cpu: 0          // 0..1
    property real ram: 0          // 0..1
    property var _last: null

    FileView { id: stat; path: "/proc/stat" }
    FileView { id: mem;  path: "/proc/meminfo" }

    Timer {
        interval: 2000; running: true; repeat: true; triggeredOnStart: true
        onTriggered: { stat.reload(); mem.reload(); root.update() }
    }

    function update(): void {
        // CPU: compare two samples of the first "cpu" line
        const p = (stat.text().split("\n")[0] || "").trim().split(/\s+/).slice(1).map(Number)
        if (p.length > 4) {
            const idle = p[3] + p[4], total = p.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0)
            if (_last) {
                const dt = total - _last.total
                cpu = dt > 0 ? 1 - (idle - _last.idle) / dt : 0
            }
            _last = { total, idle }
        }
        // RAM
        const t = mem.text()
        const total = parseInt((t.match(/MemTotal:\s+(\d+)/) || [])[1] || 0)
        const avail = parseInt((t.match(/MemAvailable:\s+(\d+)/) || [])[1] || 0)
        ram = total ? 1 - avail / total : 0
    }
}

(This uses FileView for the reading. Same idea, no processes needed.)

Exercises
  1. Show your kernel version and uptime (uptime -p) in the bar.
  2. Show the number of available package updates (checkupdates | wc -l), refreshed every 30 minutes.
  3. Run nmcli monitor with a SplitParser and log every line.
