Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Files, Watching and JSON Config

Your shell needs to read files (/sys brightness, generated colors), watch them for changes (a new wallpaper palette), and remember settings across restarts. FileView does all of this, and JsonAdapter turns a JSON file into live, two-way QML properties.

Reading a file#

import Quickshell.Io

FileView {
    id: hostname
    path: "/etc/hostname"
}

Text { text: hostname.text().trim() }

text() returns the content as a string. Although it's a function, bindings that call it update whenever the file is (re)loaded. data() returns the raw bytes.

Watching for changes#

FileView {
    id: colorsFile
    path: Quickshell.env("HOME") + "/.cache/myshell/colors.json"
    watchChanges: true                  // use inotify to detect changes on disk
    onFileChanged: reload()             // re-read when it changes
    onLoaded: console.log("colors loaded")
    onLoadFailed: error => console.warn("couldn't load colors:", FileViewError.toString(error))
}

This is the core of live theming: matugen writes colors.json and your shell instantly recolors (Colors and Wallpaper Theming).

/sys and /proc files

Many /sys files (like /proc/stat) don't send change notifications. For those, call reload() on a Timer instead of relying on watchChanges. Backlight brightness files usually do notify.

Paths#

Paths must be absolute. Build them with:

path: Quickshell.env("HOME") + "/.config/myshell/config.json"
path: Quickshell.shellPath("assets/data.json")      // inside your config folder
path: Quickshell.statePath("history.json")          // ~/.local/state/quickshell/by-shell/<id>/
path: Quickshell.cachePath("thumbs/index.json")     // ~/.cache/quickshell/by-shell/<id>/
path: Quickshell.dataPath("notes.txt")              // ~/.local/share/quickshell/by-shell/<id>/

Writing a file#

FileView {
    id: notes
    path: Quickshell.dataPath("notes.txt")
    onSaved: console.log("saved")
    onSaveFailed: err => console.warn("save failed", FileViewError.toString(err))
}
// notes.setText("remember to rice")

Writes are atomic by default (atomicWrites: true): the file is written to a temp file, then swapped in, so a crash never leaves it half-written.

Loading behavior#

Property Meaning
preload (default true) start loading as soon as path is set
blockLoading if the file isn't loaded yet when you call text(), wait for it. Use it for config that must be ready at startup, so nothing flashes with default values.
blockAllReads always block reads while a load is in progress
blockWrites make setText() block until written
printErrors (default true) log read and write errors
loaded read-only: is a file currently loaded

All members are on the FileView reference page.

JsonAdapter: settings as properties#

JsonAdapter maps a JSON file to properties. Declare properties with defaults and the adapter fills them from the file. Change a property in QML and (with one line) the file is rewritten.

services/Config.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root

    property alias bar: adapter.bar
    property alias appearance: adapter.appearance
    property alias terminal: adapter.terminal

    FileView {
        path: Quickshell.env("HOME") + "/.config/myshell/config.json"
        watchChanges: true
        onFileChanged: reload()                 // edited by hand → reload
        onAdapterUpdated: writeAdapter()        // changed from QML → save
        blockLoading: true                      // ready before the first frame
        onLoadFailed: error => {
            if (error === FileViewError.FileNotFound) writeAdapter()   // first run: create with defaults
        }

        JsonAdapter {
            id: adapter

            property JsonObject bar: JsonObject {
                property bool bottom: false
                property int height: 36
                property list<string> screens: []
                property bool showSeconds: false
            }
            property JsonObject appearance: JsonObject {
                property string font: "Inter"
                property real transparency: 0.85
                property int rounding: 14
            }
            property string terminal: "kitty"
        }
    }
}

The JSON file it reads and writes:

~/.config/myshell/config.json{
  "bar": { "bottom": false, "height": 36, "screens": [], "showSeconds": false },
  "appearance": { "font": "Inter", "transparency": 0.85, "rounding": 14 },
  "terminal": "kitty"
}

Use it anywhere:

import qs.services

PanelWindow {
    anchors.top: !Config.bar.bottom
    anchors.bottom: Config.bar.bottom
    implicitHeight: Config.bar.height
}

Switch {
    checked: Config.bar.showSeconds
    onToggled: Config.bar.showSeconds = checked    // → adapterUpdated → writeAdapter() → saved
}

How the pieces fit#

Piece Role
JsonAdapter { property … } each property is a top-level JSON key, with a default
property JsonObject x: JsonObject { … } a nested JSON object
onAdapterUpdated: writeAdapter() save on any change from QML
watchChanges + onFileChanged: reload() pick up manual edits
missing keys keep their defaults, so you can add options later safely
unknown keys in the file ignored

Supported property types: bool, int, real, string, color, list<…>, var (any JSON), and JsonObject for nesting.

In the wild

end-4's Config.qml is exactly this pattern with hundreds of options, and its settings app just binds controls to Config.options.*. Noctalia and DankMaterialShell do the same, which is why their settings GUIs and JSON files always agree.

Persisting state (not settings)#

For data that changes often (notification history, launcher frequency, last wallpaper), use a separate file in the state dir:

FileView {
    path: Quickshell.statePath("launcher.json")
    onAdapterUpdated: writeAdapter()
    JsonAdapter { id: launchCounts; property var counts: ({}) }   // { "firefox.desktop": 12, … }
}
// on launch:
// launchCounts.counts = Object.assign({}, launchCounts.counts, { [id]: (launchCounts.counts[id] ?? 0) + 1 })

Remember the var rule: assign a new object to trigger saving.

Reading other formats#

  • Plain text / key=value: text().split("\n") and parse.
  • JSON without an adapter: JSON.parse(text()).
  • INI/TOML: parse lines with regex, or convert with a CLI tool via Process.
Exercises
  1. Show your hostname from /etc/hostname.
  2. Write Config.qml with a bar.height option, delete the JSON file, and watch it get recreated with defaults.
  3. Edit config.json by hand while qs runs and watch the bar resize live.
  4. Add a Switch that toggles Config.bar.showSeconds and check that the file updates.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

IPC, Keybinds and Sockets

Press Super+Space and your launcher opens. Press Super+L and your lock screen appears. A script changes the wallpaper and your shell recolors. All of these need a way for the outside world to talk to your shell. Quickshell gives you three: IpcHandler (any compositor, any script), GlobalShortcut (Hyprland, lowest latency), and raw Sockets.

IpcHandler#

Declare functions on an IpcHandler with a target name, and they become callable from the terminal:

services/GlobalStates.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root
    property bool launcherOpen: false
    property bool locked: false

    IpcHandler {
        target: "shell"

        function toggleLauncher(): void { root.launcherOpen = !root.launcherOpen }
        function openLauncher(query: string): void { root.launcherOpen = true; root.launcherQuery = query }
        function lock(): void { root.locked = true }
        function isLocked(): bool { return root.locked }
        function setVolume(percent: int): void { Audio.setVolume(percent / 100) }
    }
    property string launcherQuery: ""
}

From any terminal, script or keybind:

qs ipc show                                   # list every target and function
qs ipc call shell toggleLauncher
qs ipc call shell openLauncher "fire"         # string argument
qs ipc call shell setVolume 40                # int argument
qs ipc call shell isLocked                    # prints: false
qs -c myshell ipc call shell lock             # pick the config if several run

The rules#

  • Every parameter and the return value must have a type annotation, or the function isn't exposed.
  • Allowed types: string, int, bool, real, color, and void for returns. At most 10 arguments.
  • target must be unique within your shell.
  • enabled: false temporarily disables a handler.

IPC signals and properties#

IpcHandler {
    target: "media"
    property string title: Media.active?.trackTitle ?? ""   // readable with: qs ipc prop get media title
    signal trackChanged(title: string)                      // observable with: qs ipc listen media trackChanged
}
qs ipc prop get media title
qs ipc listen media trackChanged      # prints each time the signal is emitted
qs ipc wait media trackChanged        # waits for one emission, then exits

These let external scripts react to your shell, e.g. a terminal widget that follows the current song.

Binding keys to IPC#

Hyprland#

hyprland.confbind = SUPER, Space, exec, qs -c myshell ipc call shell toggleLauncher
bind = SUPER, L,     exec, qs -c myshell ipc call shell lock

Sway / i3#

~/.config/sway/configbindsym $mod+space exec qs -c myshell ipc call shell toggleLauncher

niri#

~/.config/niri/config.kdlbinds {
    Mod+Space { spawn "qs" "-c" "myshell" "ipc" "call" "shell" "toggleLauncher"; }
}

hypridle / swayidle#

hypridle.confgeneral {
    lock_cmd = qs -c myshell ipc call shell lock
}

GlobalShortcut (Hyprland)#

On Hyprland, GlobalShortcut registers a shortcut through Hyprland's global-shortcuts protocol. Pressing the key notifies your shell directly, with no process spawned, so latency is lower. You also get press and release events, which is great for "hold to show" cheatsheets and overview-on-Super.

import Quickshell.Hyprland

GlobalShortcut {
    name: "launcher"                         // registers as quickshell:launcher
    description: "Toggle the app launcher"   // shown in `hyprctl globalshortcuts`
    onPressed: GlobalStates.launcherOpen = !GlobalStates.launcherOpen
}

GlobalShortcut {
    name: "cheatsheet"
    onPressed: GlobalStates.cheatsheetOpen = true     // show while held…
    onReleased: GlobalStates.cheatsheetOpen = false   // …hide on release
}
hyprland.confbind  = SUPER, Space,    global, quickshell:launcher
bind  = SUPER, slash,    global, quickshell:cheatsheet
bindr = SUPER, SUPER_L,  global, quickshell:overview      # fires on RELEASE of Super alone
Member Meaning
name shortcut name (can't change at runtime)
appid prefix, defaults to quickshell → quickshell:name
description human description
pressed (property) currently held?
onPressed, onReleased signals
Unique names

Two Quickshell instances (or XDPH) registering the same appid:name will collide, and the later one may crash. Use a custom appid if you run more than one shell config.

IpcHandler or GlobalShortcut?#

IpcHandler GlobalShortcut
Compositors all Hyprland only
Latency spawns qs (~tens of ms) direct, instant
Release events no yes
Callable from scripts yes no
Arguments and return values yes no

Many shells use both: GlobalShortcut for keys on Hyprland, IpcHandler for scripts and other compositors.

Sockets#

Socket connects to a Unix socket, and SocketServer creates one. You'll rarely need them because compositor modules handle their sockets for you, but they're useful for custom daemons:

// Talk to a daemon's socket
Socket {
    id: sock
    path: "/run/user/1000/mydaemon.sock"
    connected: true
    parser: SplitParser { onRead: line => console.log("daemon says", line) }
    onError: e => console.warn("socket error", e)
}
// sock.write("status\n"); sock.flush()

// Offer your own socket
SocketServer {
    active: true
    path: Quickshell.env("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR") + "/myshell.sock"
    handler: Socket {
        parser: SplitParser {
            onRead: cmd => { if (cmd === "toggle") GlobalStates.launcherOpen = !GlobalStates.launcherOpen }
        }
    }
}
echo toggle | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/myshell.sock

Talking the other way: shell → compositor#

To control the compositor from your shell:

Hyprland.dispatch("workspace 3")               // Hyprland dispatchers
I3.dispatch("workspace number 3")              // Sway/i3 commands
Niri.dispatch(["focus-workspace", "3"])        // niri (noctalia-qs fork module)
Quickshell.execDetached(["hyprctl", "keyword", "general:gaps_out", "20"])   // anything hyprctl can do
In the wild

Caelestia's caelestia CLI is a wrapper around qs ipc call: caelestia shell drawers toggle launcher and similar. JaKooLit-style setups bind keys to qs ipc call so Quickshell components coexist with Waybar and rofi.

Exercises
  1. Add an IpcHandler bar with toggle(): void that hides or shows your bar, bound to Super+B.
  2. Add setTheme(name: string): void and call it from the terminal.
  3. On Hyprland, make a GlobalShortcut that shows a cheatsheet only while the key is held.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

Talking to Your Compositor

Workspaces, the focused window's title, window lists for docks, live previews: all of these come from the compositor. Quickshell has dedicated modules for Hyprland and Sway/i3, the noctalia-qs fork adds niri and DWL, and there are generic Wayland types that work almost everywhere.

Compositor Module Singleton
Hyprland Quickshell.Hyprland Hyprland
Sway, i3 Quickshell.I3 I3
niri Quickshell.Niri (noctalia-qs fork) Niri
dwl Quickshell.DWL (noctalia-qs fork) DwlIpc
any with ext-workspace Quickshell.WindowManager WindowManager
any with foreign-toplevel Quickshell.Wayland ToplevelManager

Hyprland#

import Quickshell.Hyprland

Workspaces#

Row {
    spacing: 6
    Repeater {
        model: Hyprland.workspaces                    // ObjectModel<HyprlandWorkspace>, sorted by id
        Rectangle {
            required property HyprlandWorkspace modelData
            visible: modelData.id > 0                 // hide special/named workspaces (negative ids)
            width: modelData.focused ? 28 : 12; height: 12; radius: 6
            color: modelData.focused ? "#cba6f7"
                 : modelData.urgent ? "#f38ba8"
                 : modelData.toplevels.values.length ? "#6c7086" : "#313244"
            Behavior on width { NumberAnimation { duration: 200 } }
            TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.activate() }
        }
    }
}

HyprlandWorkspace: id, name, active (shown on its monitor), focused (active and its monitor is focused), urgent, hasFullscreen, monitor, toplevels, lastIpcObject, activate().

Show 1–10 even when empty

Hyprland.workspaces only contains workspaces that exist, and Hyprland destroys empty ones. For a fixed 1–10 indicator, use Repeater { model: 10 } and look each id up: Hyprland.workspaces.values.find(w => w.id === index + 1). Project: Workspace Indicators (All Compositors) does this.

Monitors, focus, active window#

Text { text: Hyprland.focusedWorkspace?.name ?? "" }
Text { text: Hyprland.activeToplevel?.title ?? "Desktop" }
// per bar: the monitor this bar is on
readonly property HyprlandMonitor mon: Hyprland.monitorFor(screen)
Text { text: "ws " + (mon?.activeWorkspace?.id ?? "?") }

Hyprland properties: focusedMonitor, focusedWorkspace, activeToplevel, monitors, workspaces, toplevels, usingLua, requestSocketPath, eventSocketPath. HyprlandMonitor: id, name, description, x, y, width, height, scale, focused, activeWorkspace, lastIpcObject.

Windows (toplevels)#

HyprlandToplevel: address, title, activated, urgent, workspace, monitor, wayland (the generic Toplevel, for previews and activation), lastIpcObject (full hyprctl clients -j data: class, position, size, floating…).

Dispatching#

Hyprland.dispatch("workspace 3")
Hyprland.dispatch("movetoworkspace 5")
Hyprland.dispatch("togglefloating")
Hyprland.dispatch(`focuswindow address:0x${toplevel.address}`)
Hyprland.dispatch("exec kitty")
Hyprland Lua configs

Newer Hyprland versions can use a Lua config. In Lua mode the dispatcher syntax changes (for example hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = "3" }) instead of workspace 3). Hyprland.usingLua tells you which mode is active. Prefer helper methods like HyprlandWorkspace.activate(), which pick the right syntax for you.

lastIpcObject and refreshing#

Much data (window position and size, workspace window count) only comes from Hyprland's JSON. It's in lastIpcObject, but it isn't refreshed automatically for every change. Call Hyprland.refreshToplevels(), refreshWorkspaces() or refreshMonitors() when you need fresh data (e.g. when the overview opens).

Raw events#

Connections {
    target: Hyprland
    function onRawEvent(event) {            // HyprlandEvent: name, data, parse(n)
        switch (event.name) {
        case "activelayout": root.layout = event.parse(2)[1]; break      // keyboard layout name
        case "submap":       root.submap = event.data; break
        case "openwindow":
        case "closewindow":  Hyprland.refreshToplevels(); break
        }
    }
}

See the Hyprland wiki's IPC page for all event names.

Other Hyprland types#

  • GlobalShortcut: keybinds into your shell (IPC, Keybinds and Sockets).
  • HyprlandFocusGrab: detect clicks outside your windows. windows: [popup, bar], active: true, onCleared: close().
  • HyprlandWindow (attached): HyprlandWindow.opacity and HyprlandWindow.visibleMask on your windows.

Sway and i3#

import Quickshell.I3

Row {
    Repeater {
        model: I3.workspaces
        Text {
            required property I3Workspace modelData
            text: modelData.name
            color: modelData.focused ? "#cba6f7" : modelData.urgent ? "#f38ba8" : "#6c7086"
            TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.activate() }
        }
    }
}
Text { text: I3.focusedWorkspace?.name ?? "" }

I3: workspaces, monitors, focusedWorkspace, focusedMonitor, socketPath, dispatch(cmd), monitorFor(screen), findWorkspaceByName(), findMonitorByName(), refreshWorkspaces(), refreshMonitors(), signals rawEvent(event) and connected(). I3Workspace: id, name, number, focused, active, urgent, monitor, lastIpcObject, activate(). I3IpcListener subscribes to arbitrary i3/Sway events (e.g. ["window", "mode"]).

niri (noctalia-qs fork)#

import Quickshell.Niri

Row {
    Repeater {
        model: Niri.workspaces                 // sorted by output, then index
        Rectangle {
            required property NiriWorkspace modelData
            width: modelData.focused ? 24 : 10; height: 10; radius: 5
            color: modelData.focused ? "#cba6f7" : modelData.occupied ? "#6c7086" : "#313244"
            TapHandler { onTapped: Niri.dispatch(["focus-workspace", String(modelData.idx)]) }
        }
    }
}
Text { text: Niri.focusedWindow?.title ?? "" }
Text { text: Niri.currentKeyboardLayoutName }

Niri also exposes windows, outputs, overviewActive, keyboard layouts, refresh functions and signals (rawEvent, workspacesUpdated, windowsUpdated…).

niri on upstream Quickshell#

Without the fork, read niri's event stream yourself:

Process {
    command: ["niri", "msg", "--json", "event-stream"]
    running: true
    stdout: SplitParser {
        onRead: line => {
            const ev = JSON.parse(line)
            if (ev.WorkspacesChanged) root.workspaces = ev.WorkspacesChanged.workspaces
            else if (ev.WorkspaceActivated) root.focusedId = ev.WorkspaceActivated.id
            else if (ev.WindowFocusChanged) root.focusedWindowId = ev.WindowFocusChanged.id
        }
    }
}

dwl (noctalia-qs fork)#

DwlIpc exposes tagCount, layouts and outputs (DwlIpcOutput with tags, title, appId, layoutSymbol, setTags(), setLayout()…). Each DwlTag has active, urgent, clientCount.

Compositor-independent: ToplevelManager#

The foreign-toplevel protocol is supported by Hyprland, Sway, niri, river, labwc, Wayfire and others. ToplevelManager lists every window:

import Quickshell.Wayland

Repeater {
    model: ToplevelManager.toplevels
    Text {
        required property Toplevel modelData
        text: (modelData.activated ? "▶ " : "  ") + modelData.appId + " — " + modelData.title
        TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.activate() }
        TapHandler { acceptedButtons: Qt.MiddleButton; onTapped: modelData.close() }
    }
}

Toplevel: appId, title, activated, maximized, minimized, fullscreen (settable as requests), parent, screens, activate(), close(), fullscreenOn(screen), setRectangle(window, rect) (tells the compositor where the dock icon is, for minimize animations). ToplevelManager.activeToplevel is the focused window. This is enough for taskbars and docks on any compositor.

Compositor-independent workspaces: WindowManager#

WindowManager (module Quickshell.WindowManager) implements the ext-workspace-v1 protocol, a standard workspace API that compositors are adopting. It exposes Windowsets (workspaces or tags) with name, active, urgent, activate(), grouped into projections (screens). It's newer and depends on compositor support; check yours.

Live previews: ScreencopyView#

ScreencopyView shows a live (or still) image of a window or screen:

ScreencopyView {
    captureSource: hyprToplevel.wayland      // a Toplevel, or a ShellScreen for a whole monitor
    live: true                               // continuous video; false = one frame (captureFrame())
    constraintSize: Qt.size(320, 200)        // fit inside this size, keeping aspect ratio
    paintCursor: false
}

Members: captureSource, live, paintCursor, constraintSize, hasContent, sourceSize, captureFrame(), stopped(). Used for overviews and alt-tab switchers. Keep live on only while visible.

Writing compositor-portable code#

Wrap compositor differences in one service so the UI doesn't care:

services/Workspaces.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Hyprland
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    readonly property bool isHyprland: Quickshell.env("HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE") !== null
    readonly property int focusedId: isHyprland ? (Hyprland.focusedWorkspace?.id ?? 1) : 1
    function focus(id: int): void { if (isHyprland) Hyprland.dispatch("workspace " + id) }
}
Importing compositor modules elsewhere

Importing Quickshell.Hyprland on Sway is harmless (the singleton just isn't connected), but referencing data from a compositor that isn't running gives null values. Guard with ?. and environment checks.

Exercises
  1. Show the focused window's title, elided to 300 px.
  2. Show the keyboard layout from Hyprland's activelayout event (or niri's currentKeyboardLayoutName).
  3. Build a taskbar with ToplevelManager that shows app icons and activates windows on click.
Part IV · Quickshell Concepts

A Tour of the System Services

This chapter walks through every system service module with a short working example for each. Each section links to the full API reference, where every property, function and signal is documented with a complete example.

Module Singleton(s) Replaces
Quickshell.Services.Pipewire Pipewire wpctl/pactl polling
Quickshell.Services.Mpris Mpris playerctl
Quickshell.Services.UPower UPower, PowerProfiles acpi, powerprofilesctl
Quickshell.Services.SystemTray SystemTray Waybar tray, snixembed
Quickshell.Services.Notifications (you create NotificationServer) dunst, mako, swaync
Quickshell.Bluetooth Bluetooth bluetoothctl
Quickshell.Networking Networking nmcli
Quickshell.Services.Pam (you create PamContext) swaylock/hyprlock auth
Quickshell.Services.Polkit (you create PolkitAgent) polkit-gnome, hyprpolkitagent
Quickshell.Services.Greetd Greetd tuigreet, regreet
Quickshell DesktopEntries rofi's app list

Audio: Pipewire#

import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire

Item {
    readonly property PwNode sink: Pipewire.defaultAudioSink        // speakers / headphones
    readonly property PwNode source: Pipewire.defaultAudioSource    // microphone

    // REQUIRED: bind the nodes, or their audio properties stay invalid
    PwObjectTracker { objects: [sink, source] }

    Text {
        text: sink?.audio ? Math.round(sink.audio.volume * 100) + "%" + (sink.audio.muted ? " (muted)" : "") : "…"
        WheelHandler { onWheel: e => sink.audio.volume = Math.max(0, Math.min(1.5, sink.audio.volume + (e.angleDelta.y > 0 ? 0.05 : -0.05))) }
        TapHandler { onTapped: sink.audio.muted = !sink.audio.muted }
    }
}

Key facts:

  • PwNode is any node: devices (isStream: false) or app streams (isStream: true); isSink tells direction. description and nickname are human names.
  • PwNodeAudio (node.audio): volume (0–1, can exceed 1), muted, volumes (per channel), channels.
  • PwObjectTracker is mandatory for any node whose audio you read or write.
  • Switch the output device: Pipewire.preferredDefaultAudioSink = node.
  • Per-app mixer: Pipewire.nodes.values.filter(n => n.isStream && n.audio).
  • Live level meters: PwNodePeakMonitor gives peak/peaks (0–1) for a node.
  • Pipewire.ready becomes true after the initial sync.

Media: Mpris#

import Quickshell.Services.Mpris

Item {
    readonly property MprisPlayer player: Mpris.players.values.find(p => p.isPlaying) ?? Mpris.players.values[0] ?? null

    Column {
        visible: player !== null
        Text { text: player?.trackTitle || "Unknown title" }
        Text { text: player?.trackArtist || "Unknown artist" }
        Row {
            Text { text: "⏮"; TapHandler { onTapped: player.previous() } }
            Text { text: player?.isPlaying ? "⏸" : "▶"; TapHandler { onTapped: player.togglePlaying() } }
            Text { text: "⏭"; TapHandler { onTapped: player.next() } }
        }
    }
    // position doesn't update on its own; poke it while playing
    Timer { running: player?.isPlaying ?? false; interval: 1000; repeat: true; onTriggered: player.positionChanged() }
}

MprisPlayer has trackTitle, trackArtist, trackAlbum, trackArtUrl, length, position (settable to seek), isPlaying, playbackState, loopState, shuffle, volume, rate, the can* capability flags, and play(), pause(), togglePlaying(), next(), previous(), seek(offset), raise(), quit().

Battery and power: UPower and PowerProfiles#

import Quickshell.Services.UPower

Text {
    readonly property UPowerDevice bat: UPower.displayDevice
    visible: bat.isLaptopBattery
    text: Math.round(bat.percentage * 100) + "% " + UPowerDeviceState.toString(bat.state)
}
Text { text: "Profile: " + PowerProfile.toString(PowerProfiles.profile)
       TapHandler { onTapped: PowerProfiles.profile = PowerProfile.PowerSaver } }
  • UPowerDevice: percentage (0–1), state, timeToEmpty/timeToFull (seconds), energy, energyCapacity, changeRate, healthPercentage (0–100), isLaptopBattery, iconName, type, model.
  • UPower: displayDevice, devices (mice, headsets…), onBattery.
  • PowerProfiles: profile (settable), hasPerformanceProfile, degradationReason, holds.

System tray: SystemTray#

import Quickshell.Services.SystemTray
import Quickshell.Widgets

Row {
    Repeater {
        model: SystemTray.items
        IconImage {
            id: icon
            required property SystemTrayItem modelData
            implicitSize: 18
            source: modelData.icon
            TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.onlyMenu ? menu.open() : modelData.activate() }
            TapHandler { acceptedButtons: Qt.RightButton; onTapped: menu.open() }
            TapHandler { acceptedButtons: Qt.MiddleButton; onTapped: modelData.secondaryActivate() }
            QsMenuAnchor { id: menu; menu: icon.modelData.menu; anchor.item: icon; anchor.edges: Edges.Bottom; anchor.gravity: Edges.Bottom }
        }
    }
}

SystemTrayItem has id, title, icon, tooltipTitle, tooltipDescription, status, category, hasMenu, onlyMenu, menu, activate(), secondaryActivate(), scroll(delta, horizontal) and display(window, x, y). A custom-styled tray menu is built in Project: System Tray with Custom Menus.

Notifications: NotificationServer#

You become the notification daemon (stop dunst/mako first):

import Quickshell.Services.Notifications

NotificationServer {
    id: server
    actionsSupported: true
    imageSupported: true
    bodyMarkupSupported: true
    keepOnReload: true
    onNotification: n => {
        n.tracked = true                    // REQUIRED, or it's discarded immediately
        console.log(n.appName, ":", n.summary, "-", n.body)
    }
}
// all current notifications: server.trackedNotifications (ObjectModel<Notification>)

Notification has summary, body, appName, appIcon, image, urgency, actions (each with text, identifier, invoke()), expireTimeout (seconds), resident, transient, hints, hasInlineReply, dismiss(), expire(), sendInlineReply(text) and the closed(reason) signal. By default the server advertises few capabilities: turn on what your UI supports. The full popup UI is Project: Notification Daemon.

Bluetooth#

import Quickshell.Bluetooth

Column {
    readonly property BluetoothAdapter adapter: Bluetooth.defaultAdapter
    Switch { checked: adapter?.enabled ?? false; onToggled: adapter.enabled = checked }
    Repeater {
        model: adapter?.devices ?? []
        Text {
            required property BluetoothDevice modelData
            text: modelData.name + (modelData.connected ? " ✓" : "")
                  + (modelData.batteryAvailable ? `  ${Math.round(modelData.battery * 100)}%` : "")
            TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.connected ? modelData.disconnect() : modelData.connect() }
        }
    }
}

BluetoothAdapter: enabled, discovering (set true to scan), discoverable, pairable, devices, state. BluetoothDevice: name, address, icon, connected, paired, trusted, blocked, battery (0–1), connect(), disconnect(), pair(), cancelPair(), forget().

Network: Networking#

import Quickshell.Networking

Column {
    readonly property WifiDevice wifi: Networking.devices.values.find(d => d.type === DeviceType.Wifi) ?? null
    Switch { checked: Networking.wifiEnabled; onToggled: Networking.wifiEnabled = checked }
    Repeater {
        model: wifi?.networks ?? []
        Text {
            required property WifiNetwork modelData
            text: (modelData.connected ? "● " : "  ") + modelData.name + "  " + Math.round(modelData.signalStrength * 100) + "%"
            TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.known ? modelData.connect() : passwordDialog.ask(modelData) }
        }
    }
    Component.onCompleted: if (wifi) wifi.scannerEnabled = true     // scan for networks
}
  • Networking: devices, wifiEnabled, wifiHardwareEnabled, connectivity, checkConnectivity(), backend.
  • NetworkDevice / WifiDevice / WiredDevice: type, name, connected, state, networks, scannerEnabled (Wi-Fi), hasLink and linkSpeed (wired).
  • Network / WifiNetwork: name, connected, known, state, signalStrength (0–1), security, connect(), connectWithPsk(password), disconnect(), forget(), connectionFailed(reason).

Requires NetworkManager. On setups without it, use nmcli/iwctl through Process.

Authentication: PamContext#

import Quickshell.Services.Pam

PamContext {
    id: pam
    config: "login"                         // /etc/pam.d/login
    onPamMessage: if (responseRequired) respond(passwordField.text)
    onCompleted: result => {
        if (result === PamResult.Success) unlock()
        else showError()
    }
}
// start: pam.start()

PamContext: config, configDirectory, user, active, message, messageIsError, responseRequired, responseVisible, start(), abort(), respond(text), signals pamMessage, completed(result), error(err). Used for lock screens (Project: Lock Screen).

Polkit agent: PolkitAgent#

When an app asks "authenticate to continue", a polkit agent shows the dialog. Quickshell can be that agent:

import Quickshell.Services.Polkit

PolkitAgent {
    id: agent
    onAuthenticationRequestStarted: console.log("auth needed:", flow.message)
}
// agent.flow: AuthFlow (message, iconName, inputPrompt, isResponseRequired, submit(pw), cancelAuthenticationRequest() …)

Full dialog: Project: Polkit Authentication Agent.

Login greeter: Greetd#

Greetd lets a Quickshell config run as a graphical login screen under greetd: createSession(user), respond(password), launch(command), signals authMessage, authFailure, readyToLaunch. See Project: Login Greeter.

Applications: DesktopEntries#

ListView {
    model: DesktopEntries.applications          // every visible installed app
    delegate: Text {
        required property DesktopEntry modelData
        text: modelData.name
        TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.execute() }
    }
}

DesktopEntry: id, name, genericName, comment, icon, categories, keywords, command, execString, runInTerminal, noDisplay, startupClass, actions, execute(). DesktopEntries: applications, byId(id), heuristicLookup(name) (match a window's app id to its entry).

Things without a module#

Need Approach
Brightness FileView on /sys/class/backlight/*/brightness + brightnessctl to set
CPU, RAM, temperature FileView on /proc and /sys
Disk usage Process running df
Weather Process running curl against an API, JSON.parse
Clipboard history cliphist via Process
Keyboard layout compositor events
Night light hyprsunset / wlsunset via Process
Screenshots grim + slurp via execDetached
Idle and lock timing IdleMonitor, IdleInhibitor
Clipboard text Quickshell.clipboardText (needs a focused Quickshell window on Wayland)
Exercises
  1. Show the volume and a mute icon, scrollable, using the Audio service from Singletons and Global State.
  2. Show the current song title and a play/pause button.
  3. Show battery percentage and charging state, hidden on desktops.
  4. Count connected Bluetooth devices.
Part V · Design and Architecture

Project Layout of a Real Shell

You know the building blocks. Now let's organize them the way end-4, Caelestia, Noctalia and DankMaterialShell do, so your config can grow to dozens of components without becoming spaghetti. Every project in Part VI drops into this structure.

The layout#

~/.config/quickshell/myshell/
├── shell.qml                  ← entry point: lists modules, starts services
├── .qmlls.ini                 ← empty; editor support (git-ignore it)
│
├── services/                  ← SINGLETONS that wrap the system (no UI!)
│   ├── GlobalStates.qml       ← which panels are open
│   ├── Config.qml             ← user options (FileView + JsonAdapter)
│   ├── Colors.qml             ← color palette (from matugen JSON)
│   ├── Appearance.qml         ← sizes, rounding, fonts, animation tokens
│   ├── Audio.qml   Media.qml   Battery.qml   Brightness.qml
│   ├── Network.qml Bluetooth.qml Notifs.qml  Time.qml
│   └── Workspaces.qml         ← compositor abstraction
│
├── widgets/                   ← REUSABLE STYLED PRIMITIVES
│   ├── StyledText.qml   MaterialIcon.qml   StyledRect.qml
│   ├── IconButton.qml   StyledSlider.qml   StyledSwitch.qml
│   ├── Tooltip.qml      Anim.qml           ColorAnim.qml
│
├── modules/                   ← FEATURES: one folder each
│   ├── bar/            Bar.qml  Workspaces.qml  Clock.qml  Tray.qml  StatusIcons.qml
│   ├── notifications/  NotificationPopups.qml  NotificationCard.qml
│   ├── launcher/       Launcher.qml  AppItem.qml
│   ├── osd/            Osd.qml
│   ├── controlcenter/  ControlCenter.qml  QuickToggle.qml  SliderRow.qml
│   ├── session/        Session.qml
│   ├── lock/           Lock.qml  LockSurface.qml
│   ├── overview/       Overview.qml
│   ├── dock/           Dock.qml
│   ├── wallpaper/      Wallpaper.qml  WallpaperPicker.qml
│   └── decorations/    ScreenCorners.qml  DesktopClock.qml
│
├── assets/                    ← images, bundled fonts, icons
└── scripts/                   ← shell helpers (wallpaper.sh …)

The three layers#

The golden rules:

  1. Services know nothing about UI. No colors, no Items: properties and functions only.
  2. Widgets know nothing about the system. A StyledSlider doesn't know it's controlling volume.
  3. Modules glue them together: StyledSlider { value: Audio.volume; onMoved: Audio.setVolume(value) }.
  4. Only services import Quickshell.Services.*, Quickshell.Io (mostly) and compositor modules.

That gives you:

  • Reuse: the bar, OSD and control center all use Audio.
  • Swappability: move from nmcli to Quickshell.Networking by editing one file.
  • Consistency: change Appearance.rounding.normal and every widget follows.
  • Testability: you can fake a service's values to test UI.

shell.qml: the table of contents#

shell.qml//@ pragma UseQApplication
//@ pragma IconTheme Papirus-Dark
//@ pragma Env QS_NO_RELOAD_POPUP=1
//@ pragma Env QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE=Basic

import Quickshell
import QtQuick
import qs.services
import qs.modules.bar
import qs.modules.notifications
import qs.modules.launcher
import qs.modules.osd
import qs.modules.controlcenter
import qs.modules.session
import qs.modules.lock
import qs.modules.overview
import qs.modules.dock
import qs.modules.wallpaper
import qs.modules.decorations

ShellRoot {
    Wallpaper {}
    ScreenCorners {}
    Bar {}
    Dock {}
    NotificationPopups {}
    Launcher {}
    Osd {}
    ControlCenter {}
    Session {}
    Lock {}
    Overview {}

    // singletons are lazy; start the ones that must run from login
    Component.onCompleted: {
        Notifs.init()
        BatteryWarning.init()
    }
}

To disable a feature, comment out one line. To make features optional per user, wrap them: LazyLoader { active: Config.modules.dock; Dock {} }.

Naming conventions#

Thing Convention Example
Component files PascalCase NotificationCard.qml
Folders imported with qs. lowercase, no dashes controlcenter
ids camelCase, root is root id: clockText
Properties camelCase, booleans read like questions isOpen, hasBattery, showSeconds
Signals past tense or event names clicked, dismissed, requestClose
Layer namespaces <shell>:<module> myshell:bar
IPC targets short nouns launcher, session, wallpaper

Module folder structure#

Each module folder has:

  • one entry component with the folder's name (Bar.qml, Launcher.qml). It's usually a Scope containing the window(s), often inside Variants or LazyLoader.
  • subcomponents used only by that module (Workspaces.qml, AppItem.qml).
  • optionally its own IpcHandler and GlobalShortcuts, so the module is self-contained.
modules/launcher/Launcher.qmlimport Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import qs.services

Scope {
    IpcHandler { target: "launcher"; function toggle(): void { GlobalStates.toggle("launcher") } }
    LazyLoader { active: GlobalStates.launcherOpen; LauncherWindow {} }
}

Version control and sharing#

cd ~/.config/quickshell/myshell
git init
printf '.qmlls.ini\n' > .gitignore
git add -A && git commit -m "initial shell"

Keep your shell in a dotfiles repo and symlink it into place:

ln -s ~/dotfiles/quickshell/myshell ~/.config/quickshell/myshell

Growing pains to avoid#

Smell Fix
A 600-line Bar.qml split into subcomponents in modules/bar/
Colors hard-coded everywhere Colors singleton (Colors and Wallpaper Theming)
Process calls scattered in UI files move them into services
../../../widgets imports import qs.widgets
Copy-pasted button code widgets/IconButton.qml
Panels fighting over the screen central GlobalStates.toggle() (Orchestrating Panels and State)
Exercise

Create this folder structure, move your existing bar into modules/bar/Bar.qml, write services/GlobalStates.qml, and make shell.qml a short ShellRoot listing modules. Confirm everything still works.

Part V · Design and Architecture

Building a Design System

A design system is a small set of shared tokens (colors, sizes, fonts, motion) plus primitive components built from them. Every rice that looks cohesive has one. In this chapter you'll build Appearance.qml and a library of styled widgets that the projects in Part VI use.

Tokens: Appearance.qml#

services/Appearance.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root

    readonly property QtObject rounding: QtObject {
        readonly property int small: 8
        readonly property int normal: 14
        readonly property int large: 22
        readonly property int full: 9999          // pill
    }
    readonly property QtObject spacing: QtObject {
        readonly property int tiny: 2
        readonly property int small: 4
        readonly property int normal: 8
        readonly property int large: 14
        readonly property int huge: 24
    }
    readonly property QtObject padding: QtObject {
        readonly property int small: 6
        readonly property int normal: 10
        readonly property int large: 16
    }
    readonly property QtObject font: QtObject {
        readonly property string family: Config.appearance.font ?? "Inter"
        readonly property string mono: "JetBrainsMono Nerd Font"
        readonly property string icons: "Material Symbols Rounded"
        readonly property QtObject size: QtObject {
            readonly property int tiny: 10
            readonly property int small: 12
            readonly property int normal: 13
            readonly property int large: 16
            readonly property int title: 20
            readonly property int huge: 32
            readonly property int display: 72
        }
    }
    readonly property QtObject anim: QtObject {
        readonly property int fast: 150
        readonly property int normal: 250
        readonly property int slow: 400
        readonly property int verySlow: 600
        readonly property var standard:   [0.2, 0, 0, 1, 1, 1]
        readonly property var emphasized: [0.05, 0.7, 0.1, 1, 1, 1]
        readonly property var emphasizedAccel: [0.3, 0, 0.8, 0.15, 1, 1]
        readonly property var expressive: [0.38, 1.21, 0.22, 1, 1, 1]   // slight overshoot
    }
    readonly property QtObject sizes: QtObject {
        readonly property int barHeight: Config.bar.height ?? 36
        readonly property int iconButton: 32
        readonly property int notificationWidth: 380
    }
}

QtObject groups related values so you can write Appearance.rounding.normal and Appearance.font.size.large. All readonly, because tokens are set here and only here.

Primitive widgets#

StyledText#

widgets/StyledText.qmlimport QtQuick
import qs.services

Text {
    color: Colors.onSurface
    font.family: Appearance.font.family
    font.pixelSize: Appearance.font.size.normal
    verticalAlignment: Text.AlignVCenter
    elide: Text.ElideRight
    Behavior on color { ColorAnimation { duration: Appearance.anim.normal } }
}

MaterialIcon#

widgets/MaterialIcon.qmlimport QtQuick
import qs.services

StyledText {
    property string icon
    property real fill: 0
    property int size: 20
    text: icon
    font.family: Appearance.font.icons
    font.pixelSize: size
    font.variableAxes: ({ "FILL": fill, "opsz": Math.max(20, Math.min(48, size)) })
    horizontalAlignment: Text.AlignHCenter
    elide: Text.ElideNone
    Behavior on fill { NumberAnimation { duration: Appearance.anim.fast } }
}

Anim: one animation, house style#

widgets/Anim.qmlimport QtQuick
import qs.services

NumberAnimation {
    duration: Appearance.anim.normal
    easing.type: Easing.BezierSpline
    easing.bezierCurve: Appearance.anim.emphasized
}
widgets/CAnim.qmlimport QtQuick
import qs.services

ColorAnimation { duration: Appearance.anim.normal }

Now every component writes Behavior on x { Anim {} } and gets identical motion.

StateLayer: hover and press feedback#

Material Design shows a translucent overlay on hover and press. Make it reusable:

widgets/StateLayer.qmlimport QtQuick
import qs.services

MouseArea {
    id: root
    property color tint: Colors.onSurface
    property real radius: parent.radius ?? 0
    anchors.fill: parent
    hoverEnabled: true
    cursorShape: Qt.PointingHandCursor

    Rectangle {
        anchors.fill: parent
        radius: root.radius
        color: root.tint
        opacity: root.pressed ? 0.16 : root.containsMouse ? 0.08 : 0
        Behavior on opacity { NumberAnimation { duration: Appearance.anim.fast } }
    }
}

IconButton#

widgets/IconButton.qmlimport QtQuick
import qs.services

Rectangle {
    id: root
    property alias icon: ic.icon
    property bool toggled: false
    property int size: Appearance.sizes.iconButton
    signal clicked()
    signal rightClicked()

    implicitWidth: size; implicitHeight: size
    radius: toggled ? Appearance.rounding.normal : size / 2        // shape morphs when toggled
    color: toggled ? Colors.primary : "transparent"
    Behavior on radius { Anim {} }
    Behavior on color { CAnim {} }

    MaterialIcon {
        id: ic
        anchors.centerIn: parent
        size: root.size * 0.6
        fill: root.toggled ? 1 : 0
        color: root.toggled ? Colors.onPrimary : Colors.onSurface
    }
    StateLayer {
        tint: root.toggled ? Colors.onPrimary : Colors.onSurface
        acceptedButtons: Qt.LeftButton | Qt.RightButton
        onClicked: m => m.button === Qt.RightButton ? root.rightClicked() : root.clicked()
    }
}

StyledSlider#

widgets/StyledSlider.qmlimport QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls
import qs.services

Slider {
    id: s
    from: 0; to: 1
    implicitHeight: 28
    background: Rectangle {
        x: s.leftPadding; y: s.topPadding + s.availableHeight / 2 - height / 2
        width: s.availableWidth; height: 8; radius: 4
        color: Colors.surfaceContainerHighest
        Rectangle {
            width: s.visualPosition * parent.width; height: parent.height; radius: 4
            color: Colors.primary
            Behavior on width { enabled: !s.pressed; Anim { duration: Appearance.anim.fast } }
        }
    }
    handle: Rectangle {
        x: s.leftPadding + s.visualPosition * (s.availableWidth - width)
        y: s.topPadding + s.availableHeight / 2 - height / 2
        width: 6; height: 22; radius: 3
        color: Colors.primary
        scale: s.pressed ? 1.15 : 1
        Behavior on scale { Anim { duration: Appearance.anim.fast } }
    }
}

StyledSwitch#

widgets/StyledSwitch.qmlimport QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls
import qs.services

Switch {
    id: sw
    implicitWidth: 52; implicitHeight: 30
    indicator: Rectangle {
        anchors.fill: parent; radius: height / 2
        color: sw.checked ? Colors.primary : Colors.surfaceContainerHighest
        border.width: sw.checked ? 0 : 2; border.color: Colors.outline
        Behavior on color { CAnim {} }
        Rectangle {
            readonly property int d: sw.checked ? 22 : 16
            width: d; height: d; radius: d / 2
            anchors.verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter
            x: sw.checked ? parent.width - width - 4 : 7
            color: sw.checked ? Colors.onPrimary : Colors.outline
            Behavior on x { Anim {} }
            Behavior on width { Anim {} }
        }
    }
    contentItem: Item {}
}

StyledRect (surface with elevation)#

widgets/StyledRect.qmlimport QtQuick
import QtQuick.Effects
import qs.services

Rectangle {
    property int level: 1                 // 0 flat … 3 high
    radius: Appearance.rounding.large
    color: level >= 2 ? Colors.surfaceContainerHigh : Colors.surfaceContainer
    layer.enabled: level > 0
    layer.effect: MultiEffect {
        shadowEnabled: true
        shadowColor: Colors.shadow
        shadowOpacity: 0.25 + 0.1 * level
        shadowBlur: 0.4 + 0.2 * level
        shadowVerticalOffset: level * 2
    }
    Behavior on color { CAnim {} }
}

Using the system#

import qs.widgets
import qs.services

Row {
    spacing: Appearance.spacing.small
    IconButton { icon: "wifi"; toggled: Network.connected; onClicked: Network.toggle() }
    IconButton { icon: Audio.icon; onClicked: Audio.toggleMute() }
    StyledText { text: Math.round(Audio.volume * 100) + "%" }
}

No colors, no sizes, no easing curves in feature code: it's all tokens.

Design tips for beginners#

  1. Pick one radius scale and stick to it. Inner radius = outer radius − padding looks right for nested rounded rectangles.
  2. Use a spacing scale (4, 8, 14, 24). Random paddings make things look off.
  3. Limit font sizes to 4–5 values.
  4. Contrast: text on surface should have strong contrast. M3's on* colors are designed for this.
  5. One accent. Use primary for "active/selected", and keep everything else neutral.
  6. Consistent motion. Same durations and curves everywhere, via Anim.
  7. Steal from the greats: study end-4's modules/common/widgets/ and Caelestia's components/ for ideas, then re-implement them in your own tokens.
Exercises
  1. Create Appearance.qml and the widgets above. Replace hard-coded values in your bar with tokens.
  2. Change rounding.normal from 14 to 4 and watch the whole shell go sharp.
  3. Add widgets/Chip.qml (icon + text pill) using only tokens.
Part V · Design and Architecture

Colors and Wallpaper Theming

The signature of modern rices: change the wallpaper and everything recolors to match (bar, popups, terminal, GTK apps). This is Material You-style dynamic color. You'll build the pipeline end to end, then add static themes like Catppuccin as an alternative.

The pipeline#

  1. A generator (matugen) extracts a Material 3 palette from the wallpaper.
  2. It renders templates into config files: one JSON file for your shell, plus files for kitty, Hyprland, GTK…
  3. Your Colors singleton reads the JSON with a watching FileView.
  4. Every widget binds to Colors.*, so they all update instantly. Add Behavior on color and they crossfade.

Material 3 color roles (quick primer)#

M3 generates roles, not just "a few colors". The ones you'll use:

Role Use
primary / onPrimary main accent (active toggle, selected workspace) / text on it
primaryContainer / onPrimaryContainer softer accent backgrounds
secondary, secondaryContainer, onSecondaryContainer secondary accents (chips, media)
tertiary, tertiaryContainer a contrasting third accent
surface / onSurface main background / main text
surfaceContainerLowest … surfaceContainerHighest layered backgrounds (cards on panels on bar)
onSurfaceVariant secondary text
outline, outlineVariant borders, dividers
error / onError warnings (low battery)
shadow, scrim shadows, dimming overlays

Rule: put onX text on an X background, and contrast is guaranteed.

Step 1: matugen#

paru -S matugen-bin       # or: cargo install matugen
matugen image ~/Pictures/Wallpapers/forest.jpg --dry-run --show-colors   # preview the palette

Matugen reads ~/.config/matugen/config.toml, which lists templates to render:

~/.config/matugen/config.toml[config]

[templates.quickshell]
input_path  = "~/.config/matugen/templates/quickshell.json"
output_path = "~/.cache/myshell/colors.json"

[templates.kitty]
input_path  = "~/.config/matugen/templates/kitty.conf"
output_path = "~/.config/kitty/colors.conf"
post_hook   = "pkill -USR1 kitty"

[templates.hyprland]
input_path  = "~/.config/matugen/templates/hyprland.conf"
output_path = "~/.config/hypr/colors.conf"

Templates use {{colors.<role>.<scheme>.hex}} placeholders (default follows the chosen mode; also light and dark):

~/.config/matugen/templates/quickshell.json{
  "primary": "{{colors.primary.default.hex}}",
  "onPrimary": "{{colors.on_primary.default.hex}}",
  "primaryContainer": "{{colors.primary_container.default.hex}}",
  "onPrimaryContainer": "{{colors.on_primary_container.default.hex}}",
  "secondary": "{{colors.secondary.default.hex}}",
  "secondaryContainer": "{{colors.secondary_container.default.hex}}",
  "onSecondaryContainer": "{{colors.on_secondary_container.default.hex}}",
  "tertiary": "{{colors.tertiary.default.hex}}",
  "error": "{{colors.error.default.hex}}",
  "onError": "{{colors.on_error.default.hex}}",
  "surface": "{{colors.surface.default.hex}}",
  "surfaceContainerLow": "{{colors.surface_container_low.default.hex}}",
  "surfaceContainer": "{{colors.surface_container.default.hex}}",
  "surfaceContainerHigh": "{{colors.surface_container_high.default.hex}}",
  "surfaceContainerHighest": "{{colors.surface_container_highest.default.hex}}",
  "onSurface": "{{colors.on_surface.default.hex}}",
  "onSurfaceVariant": "{{colors.on_surface_variant.default.hex}}",
  "outline": "{{colors.outline.default.hex}}",
  "outlineVariant": "{{colors.outline_variant.default.hex}}",
  "shadow": "{{colors.shadow.default.hex}}"
}
~/.config/matugen/templates/hyprland.conf$primary = rgb({{colors.primary.default.hex_stripped}})
$surface = rgb({{colors.surface.default.hex_stripped}})
general {
    col.active_border = $primary
    col.inactive_border = $surface
}

(Then source = ~/.config/hypr/colors.conf in hyprland.conf.)

Step 2: the wallpaper script#

scripts/wallpaper.sh#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: wallpaper.sh /path/to/image [dark|light]
set -euo pipefail
img="$(realpath "$1")"
mode="${2:-dark}"
mkdir -p ~/.cache/myshell
ln -sf "$img" ~/.cache/myshell/wallpaper        # the shell's Wallpaper module shows this
matugen image "$img" --mode "$mode"             # renders all templates → colors.json changes
chmod +x ~/.config/quickshell/myshell/scripts/wallpaper.sh
~/.config/quickshell/myshell/scripts/wallpaper.sh ~/Pictures/Wallpapers/forest.jpg

Step 3: the Colors singleton#

services/Colors.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root

    // public roles: bound to the JSON, with smooth transitions
    property color primary: c.primary
    property color onPrimary: c.onPrimary
    property color primaryContainer: c.primaryContainer
    property color onPrimaryContainer: c.onPrimaryContainer
    property color secondary: c.secondary
    property color secondaryContainer: c.secondaryContainer
    property color onSecondaryContainer: c.onSecondaryContainer
    property color tertiary: c.tertiary
    property color error: c.error
    property color onError: c.onError
    property color surface: c.surface
    property color surfaceContainerLow: c.surfaceContainerLow
    property color surfaceContainer: c.surfaceContainer
    property color surfaceContainerHigh: c.surfaceContainerHigh
    property color surfaceContainerHighest: c.surfaceContainerHighest
    property color onSurface: c.onSurface
    property color onSurfaceVariant: c.onSurfaceVariant
    property color outline: c.outline
    property color outlineVariant: c.outlineVariant
    property color shadow: c.shadow

    // derived colors
    readonly property color barBackground: Qt.rgba(surface.r, surface.g, surface.b, Config.appearance.transparency ?? 0.85)
    function alpha(col: color, a: real): color { return Qt.rgba(col.r, col.g, col.b, a) }

    // crossfade when the palette changes
    Behavior on primary { ColorAnimation { duration: 600 } }
    Behavior on surface { ColorAnimation { duration: 600 } }
    Behavior on onSurface { ColorAnimation { duration: 600 } }
    Behavior on surfaceContainer { ColorAnimation { duration: 600 } }
    Behavior on secondaryContainer { ColorAnimation { duration: 600 } }

    FileView {
        path: Quickshell.env("HOME") + "/.cache/myshell/colors.json"
        watchChanges: true
        onFileChanged: reload()
        blockLoading: true
        printErrors: false            // first run: file may not exist yet, defaults are used

        JsonAdapter {
            id: c
            // defaults (Catppuccin Mocha-ish) used until matugen has run
            property string primary: "#cba6f7"
            property string onPrimary: "#1e1e2e"
            property string primaryContainer: "#45475a"
            property string onPrimaryContainer: "#f5e0dc"
            property string secondary: "#89b4fa"
            property string secondaryContainer: "#313244"
            property string onSecondaryContainer: "#cdd6f4"
            property string tertiary: "#f5c2e7"
            property string error: "#f38ba8"
            property string onError: "#1e1e2e"
            property string surface: "#1e1e2e"
            property string surfaceContainerLow: "#181825"
            property string surfaceContainer: "#24243a"
            property string surfaceContainerHigh: "#2a2a40"
            property string surfaceContainerHighest: "#313244"
            property string onSurface: "#cdd6f4"
            property string onSurfaceVariant: "#a6adc8"
            property string outline: "#6c7086"
            property string outlineVariant: "#45475a"
            property string shadow: "#000000"
        }
    }
}

Change the wallpaper with the script: the JSON is rewritten, fileChanged fires, the adapter reloads, every Colors.* binding updates, and the Behaviors animate the change.

Static themes as an alternative#

Ship theme files with the same keys and switch the path:

assets/themes/catppuccin-mocha.json
assets/themes/gruvbox-dark.json
assets/themes/rose-pine.json
FileView {
    path: Config.appearance.theme === "dynamic"
        ? Quickshell.env("HOME") + "/.cache/myshell/colors.json"
        : Quickshell.shellPath("assets/themes/" + Config.appearance.theme + ".json")
    // …same adapter…
}

Now theme switching is one config value, and it even animates.

Light and dark mode#

Run matugen with --mode light or --mode dark. Store the mode in Config, and expose an IPC function that re-runs the script with the current wallpaper and the new mode:

IpcHandler {
    target: "theme"
    function setMode(mode: string): void {
        Config.appearance.mode = mode
        Quickshell.execDetached([Quickshell.shellPath("scripts/wallpaper.sh"),
                                 Quickshell.env("HOME") + "/.cache/myshell/wallpaper", mode])
    }
}

Quick colors without matugen: ColorQuantizer#

For per-widget colors (a media card tinted by its album art), Quickshell's ColorQuantizer extracts dominant colors from any image in-process:

ColorQuantizer {
    id: q
    source: Media.active?.trackArtUrl ?? ""
    depth: 3                 // 2^3 = 8 colors
    rescaleSize: 64          // downscale first (fast)
}
Rectangle { color: q.colors.length ? q.colors[0] : Colors.secondaryContainer }

Theming everything else#

App How
kitty, foot, alacritty matugen template + reload signal
Hyprland borders template sourced into hyprland.conf
GTK 3/4 matugen template to ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css (@define-color accent_color …)
Qt apps qt6ct color scheme template
Firefox pywalfox-style extensions or userChrome.css
VS Code / Neovim theme extensions reading generated files
In the wild

end-4 runs matugen plus its own Python scripts (switchwall.sh) to produce Material colors, and its Appearance.qml reads the result. Caelestia's caelestia scheme command writes a scheme file that its Colours service loads, supporting both dynamic and static schemes. Same pipeline, different tools.

Exercises
  1. Set up matugen, the template and Colors.qml, and run the script on two different wallpapers.
  2. Replace every hard-coded color in your bar with Colors.*.
  3. Add a Catppuccin static theme and a Config option to switch between dynamic and static.
Part V · Design and Architecture

Motion Design

Part III taught the mechanics of animation. This chapter covers the craft: how to make motion feel intentional and premium, the way the motion-heavy rices (Caelestia, end-4) do.

Principles#

  1. Motion explains change. A panel slides from the button that opened it; a notification enters from the edge it lives on. Motion shows where things come from and go to.
  2. Fast in, slow settle. Use decelerating curves (OutCubic, M3 emphasized) for things entering, accelerating curves (InCubic) for things leaving.
  3. Leaving is faster than entering. Open in 350 ms, close in 200 ms. People wait for things to appear but not for them to disappear.
  4. Small things move fast, big things move slower. 150 ms for a hover, 250 ms for a chip resizing, 400 ms+ for a full panel.
  5. Consistency beats cleverness. The same few durations and curves everywhere (Building a Design System).
  6. Don't animate what the user is directly dragging. Disable Behaviors while a slider is pressed so the fill sticks to the finger.

Duration and curve table#

Interaction Duration Curve
Hover color, opacity 120–150 ms linear or standard
Press scale 100 ms standard
Toggle / switch knob 200 ms emphasized
Chip expand, workspace pill 250–300 ms emphasized or OutBack (playful)
Popup open 250–300 ms emphasized decelerate
Popup close 150–200 ms emphasized accelerate
Side panel slide in 350–450 ms emphasized decelerate
Fullscreen overlay fade 200–250 ms standard
Theme crossfade 500–700 ms standard

Techniques#

1. Sliding indicator (workspaces, tabs)#

One indicator that moves between items is far smoother than recoloring each item:

Item {
    id: tabs
    property int current: 0
    Row { id: row; spacing: 8
        Repeater { model: 5; Rectangle { required property int index; width: 40; height: 28; color: "transparent"
            TapHandler { onTapped: tabs.current = parent.index } } } }
    Rectangle {
        readonly property Item target: row.children[tabs.current] ?? null
        x: target?.x ?? 0
        width: target?.width ?? 0
        height: 28; radius: 14; color: Colors.primary; z: -1
        Behavior on x { Anim {} }
        Behavior on width { Anim {} }
    }
}

Stretchy indicator (end-4 style): animate the left and right edges separately, with the leading edge fast and the trailing edge slower, so the pill stretches while moving:

Rectangle {
    property real targetLeft: target.x
    property real targetRight: target.x + target.width
    property real left: targetLeft
    property real right: targetRight
    Behavior on left  { NumberAnimation { duration: movingRight ? 400 : 200; easing.type: Easing.OutCubic } }
    Behavior on right { NumberAnimation { duration: movingRight ? 200 : 400; easing.type: Easing.OutCubic } }
    property bool movingRight: false
    onTargetLeftChanged: movingRight = targetLeft > left
    x: left; width: right - left
}

2. Shape morphing#

Animating radius changes the shape: circle to rounded square when toggled. M3 calls this expressive shape:

radius: toggled ? Appearance.rounding.normal : height / 2
Behavior on radius { Anim {} }

3. Grow from the source#

Scale a popup up from where it was triggered by setting transformOrigin toward the trigger:

Rectangle {
    transformOrigin: Item.Top
    scale: open ? 1 : 0.9
    opacity: open ? 1 : 0
    Behavior on scale { Anim {} }
    Behavior on opacity { Anim { duration: Appearance.anim.fast } }
}

4. Staggered entrances#

Delay each item slightly by its index for a cascading reveal:

Repeater {
    model: toggles
    QuickToggle {
        required property int index
        opacity: 0; y: 10
        Component.onCompleted: appear.start()
        SequentialAnimation {
            id: appear
            PauseAnimation { duration: index * 30 }
            ParallelAnimation {
                NumberAnimation { target: parent; property: "opacity"; to: 1; duration: 200 }
                NumberAnimation { target: parent; property: "y"; to: 0; duration: 300; easing.type: Easing.OutCubic }
            }
        }
    }
}

5. Content fades after the container grows#

When a card expands, fade its new content in after most of the size change, and fade it out first when collapsing (see Animation II: States, Transitions, Sequences).

6. Number tickers#

Animate numbers (volume %, battery %) instead of jumping:

property real shownVolume: Audio.volume
Behavior on shownVolume { NumberAnimation { duration: 200 } }
Text { text: Math.round(shownVolume * 100) + "%" }

7. Elastic edges and overshoot#

Easing.OutBack with a small overshoot (1.2–1.5) gives pills and buttons a lively "land". Use it on small elements only.

8. Window open/close with layer shell#

The compositor can animate layer surfaces (Hyprland's layerrule = animation slide top, …). It's often better to animate in QML yourself for full control, and disable the compositor's animation with layerrule = noanim, quickshell:osd.

Respecting performance#

  • Prefer x, y, scale, opacity over width/height for big items.
  • Stop infinite animations when hidden.
  • Avoid animating MultiEffect blur radius on large areas every frame.

Respecting users#

Offer a "reduce motion" option:

// Appearance.qml
readonly property real motionScale: Config.appearance.reduceMotion ? 0 : 1
readonly property QtObject anim: QtObject {
    readonly property int normal: 250 * root.motionScale
}

Durations of 0 make every Behavior instant.

Exercises
  1. Build a 5-tab bar with a stretchy sliding indicator.
  2. Make an IconButton whose shape morphs when toggled.
  3. Make a popup that scales from 0.9 to 1 from the top, opening in 300 ms and closing in 180 ms.
Part V · Design and Architecture

Orchestrating Panels and State

With a launcher, control center, overview, power menu and wallpaper picker, you need rules: should two panels be open at once? What happens on Esc? Which monitor? What closes when the screen locks? A central GlobalStates singleton answers all of these in one place.

The GlobalStates singleton#

services/GlobalStates.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import Quickshell.Hyprland
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root

    // ---- panels ----
    property bool launcherOpen: false
    property bool controlCenterOpen: false
    property bool overviewOpen: false
    property bool sessionOpen: false
    property bool wallpaperPickerOpen: false
    property bool clipboardOpen: false

    // ---- modes ----
    property bool locked: false
    property bool dnd: false
    property bool caffeine: false
    property bool barHidden: false

    // ---- extra context ----
    property string launcherQuery: ""
    property string activeScreen: Hyprland.focusedMonitor?.name ?? (Quickshell.screens[0]?.name ?? "")

    readonly property bool anyPanelOpen: launcherOpen || controlCenterOpen || overviewOpen
                                      || sessionOpen || wallpaperPickerOpen || clipboardOpen

    // ---- the rules ----
    readonly property var panels: ["launcher", "controlCenter", "overview", "session", "wallpaperPicker", "clipboard"]

    function closeAll(): void {
        for (const p of panels) root[p + "Open"] = false
    }
    function open(name: string): void {           // exclusive: opening one closes the others
        closeAll()
        root[name + "Open"] = true
    }
    function toggle(name: string): void {
        const was = root[name + "Open"]
        closeAll()
        root[name + "Open"] = !was
    }

    // locking closes everything
    onLockedChanged: if (locked) closeAll()

    // ---- external control ----
    IpcHandler {
        target: "shell"
        function toggle(panel: string): void { root.toggle(panel) }
        function open(panel: string): void { root.open(panel) }
        function close(): void { root.closeAll() }
        function lock(): void { root.locked = true }
        function dnd(on: bool): void { root.dnd = on }
    }

    GlobalShortcut { name: "launcher";      onPressed: root.toggle("launcher") }
    GlobalShortcut { name: "controlCenter"; onPressed: root.toggle("controlCenter") }
    GlobalShortcut { name: "overview";      onPressed: root.toggle("overview") }
    GlobalShortcut { name: "session";       onPressed: root.toggle("session") }
    GlobalShortcut { name: "wallpaper";     onPressed: root.toggle("wallpaperPicker") }
    GlobalShortcut { name: "clipboard";     onPressed: root.toggle("clipboard") }
    GlobalShortcut { name: "lock";          onPressed: root.locked = true }
}
hyprland.confbind = SUPER, Space,  global, quickshell:launcher
bind = SUPER, N,      global, quickshell:controlCenter
bind = SUPER, Tab,    global, quickshell:overview
bind = SUPER, Escape, global, quickshell:session
bind = SUPER, W,      global, quickshell:wallpaper
bind = SUPER, V,      global, quickshell:clipboard
bind = SUPER, L,      global, quickshell:lock
# other compositors:  qs -c myshell ipc call shell toggle launcher

Each panel follows the same pattern#

modules/launcher/Launcher.qmlimport Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import Quickshell.Hyprland
import QtQuick
import qs.services

Scope {
    LazyLoader {
        active: GlobalStates.launcherOpen
        PanelWindow {
            id: win
            screen: Quickshell.screens.find(s => s.name === GlobalStates.activeScreen) ?? null
            WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay
            WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive
            exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
            color: "transparent"
            implicitWidth: 600; implicitHeight: 440

            // close on click outside (Hyprland); grabFocus on PopupWindow does this for popups
            HyprlandFocusGrab { windows: [win]; active: true; onCleared: GlobalStates.launcherOpen = false }

            Item {
                anchors.fill: parent
                focus: true
                Keys.onEscapePressed: GlobalStates.launcherOpen = false
                // …content…
            }
        }
    }
}

The checklist for every panel:

  1. active/visible bound to its GlobalStates flag.
  2. screen = the active screen.
  3. Overlay layer; keyboard focus only if it needs typing.
  4. Close on Esc, on click outside, and after its action completes (launching an app closes the launcher).
  5. Never set another panel's flag directly; call GlobalStates.open/toggle/closeAll.

The bar reflects state too#

IconButton { icon: "apps"; toggled: GlobalStates.launcherOpen; onClicked: GlobalStates.toggle("launcher") }
IconButton { icon: "tune"; toggled: GlobalStates.controlCenterOpen; onClicked: GlobalStates.toggle("controlCenter") }

Dimming the background when a panel is open#

One fullscreen scrim window per screen, visible whenever any modal panel is open:

modules/decorations/Scrim.qmlimport Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick
import qs.services

Variants {
    model: Quickshell.screens
    PanelWindow {
        required property ShellScreen modelData
        screen: modelData
        anchors { top: true; bottom: true; left: true; right: true }
        exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
        WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Top
        WlrLayershell.namespace: "quickshell:scrim"
        visible: GlobalStates.sessionOpen || fade.running
        color: Qt.rgba(0, 0, 0, GlobalStates.sessionOpen ? 0.45 : 0)
        Behavior on color { ColorAnimation { id: fade; duration: 250 } }
        MouseArea { anchors.fill: parent; onClicked: GlobalStates.closeAll() }
    }
}

Remembering state across reloads and restarts#

Should survive… Use
nothing (panels start closed) plain properties
hot reload only PersistentProperties
restarts Config / state file with JsonAdapter

DND and caffeine are good candidates to persist across restarts: move them into a state JSON file.

Idle, lock and caffeine together#

services/Idle.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    IdleMonitor {
        timeout: 300                          // 5 minutes
        respectInhibitors: true               // videos and caffeine keep the screen awake
        enabled: !GlobalStates.caffeine
        onIsIdleChanged: if (isIdle) GlobalStates.locked = true
    }
    IdleMonitor {
        timeout: 600
        enabled: !GlobalStates.caffeine
        onIsIdleChanged: Quickshell.execDetached(["hyprctl", "dispatch", "dpms", isIdle ? "off" : "on"])
    }
}

IdleMonitor reports idleness after timeout seconds. An IdleInhibitor attached to a visible window (with enabled: GlobalStates.caffeine) prevents idling system-wide while enabled.

Exercises
  1. Implement GlobalStates with open/toggle/closeAll, and wire two panels so opening one closes the other.
  2. Add IPC and keybinds for both panels.
  3. Add a caffeine toggle in the bar that controls an IdleInhibitor and an IdleMonitor.
Part VI · Build-Along Projects

Project: The Bar

Time to build a complete, daily-driver bar on top of the design system from Part V. It's floating and rounded, appears on every monitor, and contains:

  • left: launcher button, workspaces, active window title
  • center: clock (truly centered) with a calendar popup
  • right: media chip, system tray, status icons (network, bluetooth, volume, battery), control-center button

Prerequisites: services/{Colors,Appearance,Config,GlobalStates,Audio}.qml and widgets/* from Project Layout of a Real Shell to Orchestrating Panels and State.

Services this bar needs#

Battery#

services/Battery.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.UPower
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root
    readonly property UPowerDevice dev: UPower.displayDevice
    readonly property bool available: dev?.isLaptopBattery ?? false
    readonly property real percent: dev?.percentage ?? 0                 // 0..1
    readonly property bool charging: dev?.state === UPowerDeviceState.Charging
                                  || dev?.state === UPowerDeviceState.PendingCharge
    readonly property bool full: dev?.state === UPowerDeviceState.FullyCharged
    readonly property bool low: available && !charging && percent <= 0.15
    readonly property int secondsLeft: charging ? (dev?.timeToFull ?? 0) : (dev?.timeToEmpty ?? 0)
    readonly property string icon: charging ? "battery_charging_full"
                                 : full ? "battery_full"
                                 : "battery_" + Math.min(6, Math.floor(percent * 7)) + "_bar"
}

Media#

services/Media.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Mpris
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root
    readonly property list<MprisPlayer> players: Mpris.players.values
    property MprisPlayer manualPlayer: null                      // user-picked player, if any
    readonly property MprisPlayer active: (manualPlayer && players.includes(manualPlayer)) ? manualPlayer
                                        : players.find(p => p.isPlaying) ?? players[0] ?? null

    // MPRIS position is not pushed continuously: refresh it while playing
    Timer {
        running: root.active?.isPlaying ?? false
        interval: 1000; repeat: true
        onTriggered: root.active.positionChanged()
    }
}

Network (using the Networking module)#

services/Network.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Networking
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root
    readonly property NetworkDevice wifiDevice: Networking.devices.values.find(d => d.type === DeviceType.Wifi) ?? null
    readonly property NetworkDevice wiredDevice: Networking.devices.values.find(d => d.type === DeviceType.Wired) ?? null
    readonly property Network activeWifi: wifiDevice?.networks.values.find(n => n.connected) ?? null
    readonly property bool wired: wiredDevice?.connected ?? false
    readonly property bool wifiEnabled: Networking.wifiEnabled
    readonly property string ssid: activeWifi?.name ?? ""
    readonly property real strength: activeWifi?.signalStrength ?? 0      // 0..1
    readonly property bool online: wired || activeWifi !== null
    readonly property string icon: wired ? "lan"
                                 : !wifiEnabled ? "wifi_off"
                                 : !activeWifi ? "signal_wifi_0_bar"
                                 : strength > 0.66 ? "wifi" : strength > 0.33 ? "wifi_2_bar" : "wifi_1_bar"
    function toggleWifi(): void { Networking.wifiEnabled = !Networking.wifiEnabled }
}
No NetworkManager?

If Networking.backend is NetworkBackendType.None, use the nmcli or iwctl approach with Process from Running Commands with Process, keeping the same public properties so the bar doesn't change.

The bar entry point#

modules/bar/Bar.qmlimport Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Layouts
import qs.services
import qs.widgets

Scope {
    Variants {
        model: Config.bar.screens.length
               ? Quickshell.screens.filter(s => Config.bar.screens.includes(s.name))
               : Quickshell.screens

        PanelWindow {
            id: bar
            required property ShellScreen modelData
            screen: modelData
            visible: !GlobalStates.barHidden

            anchors {
                top: !Config.bar.bottom
                bottom: Config.bar.bottom
                left: true
                right: true
            }
            margins { top: 6; bottom: 6; left: 8; right: 8 }
            implicitHeight: Appearance.sizes.barHeight
            color: "transparent"
            WlrLayershell.namespace: "quickshell:bar"

            StyledRect {
                id: bg
                anchors.fill: parent
                level: 1
                radius: Appearance.rounding.large
                color: Colors.barBackground
                border.width: 1
                border.color: Colors.alpha(Colors.outlineVariant, 0.5)

                // ---------------- LEFT ----------------
                RowLayout {
                    anchors { left: parent.left; leftMargin: 6; verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter }
                    spacing: Appearance.spacing.normal

                    IconButton {
                        icon: "apps"
                        toggled: GlobalStates.launcherOpen
                        onClicked: GlobalStates.toggle("launcher")
                    }
                    Workspaces { screen: bar.modelData }
                    ActiveWindow { Layout.maximumWidth: 260 }
                }

                // ---------------- CENTER ----------------
                Clock {
                    anchors.centerIn: parent
                    bar: bar
                }

                // ---------------- RIGHT ----------------
                RowLayout {
                    anchors { right: parent.right; rightMargin: 6; verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter }
                    spacing: Appearance.spacing.small

                    MediaChip { bar: bar }
                    Tray { bar: bar }
                    StatusIcons {}
                    IconButton {
                        icon: GlobalStates.dnd ? "notifications_off"
                            : Notifs.count > 0 ? "notifications_unread" : "notifications"
                        toggled: GlobalStates.controlCenterOpen
                        onClicked: GlobalStates.toggle("controlCenter")
                        onRightClicked: GlobalStates.dnd = !GlobalStates.dnd
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Notifs.count comes from the notification service in Project: Notification Daemon. Until then, replace it with 0.

Status icons#

The remaining pieces#

Workspaces.qml, Clock.qml and Tray.qml each get their own chapter next:

  • Project: Workspace Indicators (All Compositors): workspaces for Hyprland, Sway, niri and generic compositors
  • Project: Clock and Calendar Popup: clock plus calendar popup
  • Project: System Tray with Custom Menus: tray plus custom menus

Add Bar {} to shell.qml and you have a complete bar.

Making it yours#

  • Vertical bar: anchor left, top, bottom; swap RowLayout for ColumnLayout; rotate or stack text.
  • Hide on fullscreen: visible: !(Hyprland.monitorFor(modelData)?.activeWorkspace?.hasFullscreen ?? false).
  • Per-monitor modules: Tray { visible: bar.modelData.name === Config.bar.trayScreen }.
  • Island bar: three separate StyledRects (left, center, right) instead of one background.
  • Auto-hide: a 2 px trigger strip plus exclusiveZone animation, as the dock does in Project: Dock.

  1. Add a CPU/RAM chip using the SystemUsage service from Running Commands with Process.
