Weather card#

services/Weather.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    id: root
    property string location: Config.weather?.location ?? ""        // "" = auto by IP
    property real tempC: NaN
    property string condition: ""
    property string icon: "cloud"

    function iconFor(code: int): string {                             // wttr.in weatherCode → Material Symbol
        if (code === 113) return "sunny"
        if ([116, 119].includes(code)) return "partly_cloudy_day"
        if (code === 122) return "cloud"
        if ([143, 248, 260].includes(code)) return "foggy"
        if (code >= 386) return "thunderstorm"
        if ([179, 227, 230].includes(code) || (code >= 323 && code <= 377)) return "weather_snowy"
        return "rainy"
    }

    Process {
        id: fetch
        command: ["curl", "-sf", "--max-time", "10", "https://wttr.in/" + encodeURIComponent(root.location) + "?format=j1"]
        stdout: StdioCollector {
            onStreamFinished: {
                try {
                    const cur = JSON.parse(text).current_condition[0]
                    root.tempC = parseFloat(cur.temp_C)
                    root.condition = cur.weatherDesc[0].value
                    root.icon = root.iconFor(parseInt(cur.weatherCode))
                } catch (e) { console.warn("weather parse failed", e) }
            }
        }
    }
    Timer { interval: 15 * 60 * 1000; running: true; repeat: true; triggeredOnStart: true; onTriggered: fetch.running = true }
}
StyledRect {
    width: 220; height: 90
    RowLayout {
        anchors.centerIn: parent
        spacing: 12
        MaterialIcon { icon: Weather.icon; size: 44; fill: 1; color: Colors.primary }
        Column {
            StyledText { text: isNaN(Weather.tempC) ? "—" : Math.round(Weather.tempC) + "°C"; font.pixelSize: 28; font.bold: true }
            StyledText { text: Weather.condition; color: Colors.onSurfaceVariant }
        }
    }
}
Exercises
  1. Add a CPU history graph (Canvas) to the system monitor.
  2. Add a "now playing" desktop widget that only shows while music plays.
  3. Add a Config toggle for each widget.
Part VI · Build-Along Projects

Project: Polkit Authentication Agent

When you run pkexec, mount a drive, or change a system setting in an app, polkit asks an authentication agent to show a password dialog. Instead of polkit-gnome or hyprpolkitagent, Quickshell's PolkitAgent lets you draw that dialog in your own style.

How a polkit request flows#

  1. An app asks polkit to authorize an action (e.g. org.freedesktop.udisks2.filesystem-mount).
  2. polkit calls your agent. PolkitAgent emits authenticationRequestStarted and exposes the request as flow (AuthFlow).
  3. flow.message describes the action; flow.inputPrompt / isResponseRequired ask for input.
  4. You call flow.submit(password). On failure, authenticationFailed fires and a new attempt starts automatically; on success, authenticationSucceeded.
  5. flow.cancelAuthenticationRequest() cancels from your side; authenticationRequestCancelled means polkit cancelled.
One agent at a time

Stop other agents first (pkill -f polkit-gnome; pkill hyprpolkitagent) and remove them from autostart. agent.isRegistered tells you if registration succeeded.

The agent and dialog#

modules/polkit/Polkit.qmlimport Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import Quickshell.Widgets
import Quickshell.Services.Polkit
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Layouts
import QtQuick.Controls
import qs.services
import qs.widgets

Scope {
    id: root

    PolkitAgent {
        id: agent
        onIsRegisteredChanged: console.info("polkit agent registered:", isRegistered)
    }

    LazyLoader {
        active: agent.isActive && agent.flow !== null

        PanelWindow {
            id: win
            readonly property AuthFlow flow: agent.flow
            screen: Quickshell.screens.find(s => s.name === GlobalStates.activeScreen) ?? null
            anchors { top: true; bottom: true; left: true; right: true }
            exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
            color: Colors.alpha("#000000", 0.5)
            WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay
            WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive
            WlrLayershell.namespace: "quickshell:polkit"

            Connections {
                target: win.flow
                function onAuthenticationFailed() { pw.text = ""; shake.restart() }
            }

            StyledRect {
                anchors.centerIn: parent
                width: 420
                height: col.implicitHeight + 40
                level: 3
                color: Colors.surface

                transform: Translate { id: tr }
                SequentialAnimation {
                    id: shake
                    NumberAnimation { target: tr; property: "x"; to: -12; duration: 50 }
                    NumberAnimation { target: tr; property: "x"; to: 12; duration: 100 }
                    NumberAnimation { target: tr; property: "x"; to: 0; duration: 50 }
                }

                ColumnLayout {
                    id: col
                    anchors { left: parent.left; right: parent.right; top: parent.top; margins: 20 }
                    spacing: 14

                    RowLayout {
                        spacing: 12
                        IconImage {
                            implicitSize: 40
                            source: Quickshell.iconPath(win.flow?.iconName || "dialog-password", "dialog-password")
                        }
                        ColumnLayout {
                            Layout.fillWidth: true
                            spacing: 2
                            StyledText { text: "Authentication required"; font.bold: true; font.pixelSize: Appearance.font.size.large }
                            StyledText { text: win.flow?.actionId ?? ""; color: Colors.outline; font.pixelSize: Appearance.font.size.tiny; Layout.fillWidth: true }
                        }
                    }

                    StyledText {
                        Layout.fillWidth: true
                        text: win.flow?.message ?? ""
                        wrapMode: Text.Wrap
                        elide: Text.ElideNone
                    }

                    // choose which identity (user/admin) to authenticate as
                    ComboBox {
                        Layout.fillWidth: true
                        visible: (win.flow?.identities.length ?? 0) > 1
                        model: (win.flow?.identities ?? []).map(i => String(i))
                        onActivated: idx => win.flow.selectedIdentity = win.flow.identities[idx]
                    }

                    TextField {
                        id: pw
                        Layout.fillWidth: true
                        placeholderText: win.flow?.inputPrompt || "Password"
                        echoMode: win.flow?.responseVisible ? TextInput.Normal : TextInput.Password
                        enabled: win.flow?.isResponseRequired ?? false
                        focus: true
                        onAccepted: if (text) win.flow.submit(text)
                        Keys.onEscapePressed: win.flow.cancelAuthenticationRequest()
                    }

                    StyledText {
                        Layout.fillWidth: true
                        visible: text !== ""
                        text: win.flow?.failed && !win.flow?.supplementaryMessage ? "Authentication failed, try again"
                                                                                  : (win.flow?.supplementaryMessage ?? "")
                        color: win.flow?.supplementaryIsError || win.flow?.failed ? Colors.error : Colors.onSurfaceVariant
                        wrapMode: Text.Wrap
                    }

                    RowLayout {
                        Layout.alignment: Qt.AlignRight
                        spacing: 8
                        Button { text: "Cancel"; onClicked: win.flow.cancelAuthenticationRequest() }
                        Button { text: "Authenticate"; highlighted: true; enabled: pw.text !== ""; onClicked: win.flow.submit(pw.text) }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Add Polkit {} to shell.qml (it must be created at startup to register).

Test it#

pkexec echo "it works"          # should show your dialog
Fingerprint

polkit uses the PAM stack in /etc/pam.d/polkit-1. If that includes pam_fprintd.so, supplementaryMessage will say something like "Swipe your finger" and you may not need to type anything.

Exercises
  1. Show the requesting program's details (inspect flow properties in the reference).
  2. Blur the background with a layerrule.
  3. Add a short success animation before the window closes.
Part VI · Build-Along Projects

Project: Login Greeter

Your rice can start at the login screen. With greetd (a minimal login daemon) and Quickshell's Greetd service, a Quickshell config becomes your graphical greeter: user picker, password field, session chooser, clock and wallpaper.

Test in a VM or keep a fallback

A broken greeter means you can't log in graphically. Keep a TTY login available (Ctrl+Alt+F2) and know how to switch greetd back to tuigreet in /etc/greetd/config.toml.

How greetd works#

  1. greetd runs a greeter program as the greeter user, inside a minimal compositor (e.g. cage, or Hyprland with a tiny config).
  2. The greeter talks to greetd over a socket: "create session for user X" → greetd asks auth questions (password, OTP) → the greeter answers.
  3. When authenticated, the greeter tells greetd which command to run (e.g. Hyprland), then exits.

Quickshell's Greetd singleton wraps this protocol: createSession(user), the authMessage(message, error, responseRequired, echoResponse) signal, respond(text), readyToLaunch, launch(command), authFailure, state.

Install#

sudo pacman -S greetd cage
sudo mkdir -p /etc/greetd/quickshell
sudo cp -r ~/.config/quickshell/greeter/* /etc/greetd/quickshell/    # the config below
/etc/greetd/config.toml[terminal]
vt = 1

[default_session]
command = "cage -s -- qs -p /etc/greetd/quickshell"
user = "greeter"
sudo systemctl disable --now sddm gdm lightdm 2>/dev/null
sudo systemctl enable greetd

The greeter config#

/etc/greetd/quickshell/shell.qml//@ pragma Env QT_QUICK_CONTROLS_STYLE=Basic
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import Quickshell.Services.Greetd
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Layouts
import QtQuick.Controls

ShellRoot {
    id: root
    property string user: users.length ? users[0] : ""
    property var users: []
    property var sessions: [{ name: "Hyprland", exec: ["Hyprland"] }, { name: "niri", exec: ["niri-session"] },
                            { name: "Sway", exec: ["sway"] }]
    property int sessionIndex: 0
    property string error: ""
    property bool busy: false

    // list normal users (uid >= 1000) from /etc/passwd
    FileView {
        path: "/etc/passwd"
        onLoaded: root.users = text().split("\n").map(l => l.split(":"))
                    .filter(p => parseInt(p[2]) >= 1000 && parseInt(p[2]) < 60000 && !p[6]?.endsWith("nologin"))
                    .map(p => p[0])
    }

    function login(): void {
        error = ""
        busy = true
        Greetd.createSession(user)
    }

    Connections {
        target: Greetd
        function onAuthMessage(message, isError, responseRequired, echoResponse) {
            if (isError) root.error = message            // recoverable, e.g. fingerprint misread
            else if (!responseRequired) root.error = ""
            if (responseRequired) Greetd.respond(pw.text) // only respond when asked
        }
        function onAuthFailure(message) {
            root.busy = false
            root.error = message || "Login failed"
            pw.text = ""
        }
        function onReadyToLaunch() {
            Greetd.launch(root.sessions[root.sessionIndex].exec)
        }
        function onError(err) { root.busy = false; root.error = err }
    }

    FloatingWindow {                                    // cage shows it fullscreen
        color: "#11111b"
        visible: true

        Image {
            anchors.fill: parent
            source: "file:///etc/greetd/quickshell/wallpaper.jpg"
            fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectCrop
            opacity: 0.5
        }

        SystemClock { id: clock; precision: SystemClock.Minutes }

        ColumnLayout {
            anchors.centerIn: parent
            spacing: 14
            width: 340

            Text { Layout.alignment: Qt.AlignHCenter; text: Qt.formatTime(clock.date, "hh:mm"); color: "white"; font.pixelSize: 96; font.bold: true }
            Text { Layout.alignment: Qt.AlignHCenter; text: Qt.formatDate(clock.date, "dddd, d MMMM"); color: "#ccffffff"; font.pixelSize: 18 }

            ComboBox {
                Layout.fillWidth: true
                model: root.users
                onActivated: i => root.user = root.users[i]
            }
            TextField {
                id: pw
                Layout.fillWidth: true
                placeholderText: "Password"
                echoMode: TextInput.Password
                focus: true
                enabled: !root.busy
                onAccepted: root.login()
            }
            ComboBox {
                Layout.fillWidth: true
                model: root.sessions.map(s => s.name)
                onActivated: i => root.sessionIndex = i
            }
            Button { Layout.fillWidth: true; text: root.busy ? "Logging in…" : "Log in"; enabled: !root.busy; onClicked: root.login() }
            Text { Layout.alignment: Qt.AlignHCenter; visible: root.error !== ""; text: root.error; color: "#f38ba8" }

            RowLayout {
                Layout.alignment: Qt.AlignHCenter
                Button { text: "Reboot"; onClicked: Quickshell.execDetached(["systemctl", "reboot"]) }
                Button { text: "Shut down"; onClicked: Quickshell.execDetached(["systemctl", "poweroff"]) }
            }
        }
    }
}

Notes#

  • The greeter runs as the greeter user: it can't read your home folder. Put assets in /etc/greetd/quickshell/.
  • Remember the last user/session by writing a file the greeter can access (e.g. /var/cache/greetd/, owned by greeter).
  • Greetd.available is false when not started by greetd, useful for testing the UI as a normal user (qs -p /etc/greetd/quickshell) without logging in for real.
  • launch(command, environment, quit) lets you pass extra environment variables such as XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland.
Exercises
  1. Read available sessions from /usr/share/wayland-sessions/*.desktop instead of hard-coding them.
  2. Show user avatars from /var/lib/AccountsService/icons/<user>.
  3. Theme the greeter with the same colors.json as your shell (copy it at wallpaper change).
Part VI · Build-Along Projects

Project: Edge Drawers (Caelestia Style)

The capstone. Instead of separate windows for the bar and every panel, build one fullscreen, transparent window per monitor holding a vertical bar on the left edge and "drawers" that grow out of the screen edges, connected to the bar by smooth concave curves, as if the whole UI were one continuous liquid shape. This is the architecture behind Caelestia.

Everything here uses techniques you already know: masks (Masks, Regions and Click-Through), shapes (Shapes and Canvas), motion (Motion Design) and state (Orchestrating Panels and State).

Architecture#

Per screen:

  1. Exclusion window: an invisible PanelWindow that reserves the bar's width (exclusiveZone).
  2. Drawers window: fullscreen, transparent, ExclusionMode.Ignore, Top layer. Contains: - a background Shape that draws bar + all open drawers as one filled path with concave joints, - the content of the bar and each drawer on top of it, - a mask that covers only the bar and open drawers.
  3. State: GlobalStates flags plus "hover to peek" logic.

The exclusion window#

modules/drawers/Exclusion.qmlimport Quickshell
import QtQuick
import qs.services

PanelWindow {
    required property ShellScreen screenRef
    screen: screenRef
    anchors { left: true; top: true; bottom: true }
    implicitWidth: 1
    exclusiveZone: Appearance.sizes.barHeight          // reserve the bar's width
    color: "transparent"
    mask: Region {}
}

A drawer = a size that animates#

Each drawer is just an Item whose width/height animate between 0 and its content size. The content is clipped, so it appears to grow out of the edge.

modules/drawers/Drawer.qmlimport QtQuick
import qs.services
import qs.widgets

Item {
    id: root
    property bool open: false
    property int edge: Qt.LeftEdge          // which screen edge it grows from
    default property alias content: inner.data
    readonly property real contentW: inner.childrenRect.width
    readonly property real contentH: inner.childrenRect.height

    // horizontal drawers animate width, vertical ones animate height
    readonly property bool horizontal: edge === Qt.LeftEdge || edge === Qt.RightEdge
    width: horizontal ? (open ? contentW : 0) : contentW
    height: horizontal ? contentH : (open ? contentH : 0)
    clip: true
    visible: width > 0 && height > 0

    Behavior on width { enabled: root.horizontal; Anim { duration: Appearance.anim.slow } }
    Behavior on height { enabled: !root.horizontal; Anim { duration: Appearance.anim.slow } }

    Item {
        id: inner
        // keep content pinned to the edge it grows from
        x: root.edge === Qt.RightEdge ? root.width - root.contentW : (root.edge === Qt.LeftEdge ? root.width - root.contentW : 0)
        y: root.edge === Qt.BottomEdge ? root.height - root.contentH : (root.edge === Qt.TopEdge ? root.height - root.contentH : 0)
        width: root.contentW; height: root.contentH
        opacity: root.open ? 1 : 0
        Behavior on opacity { Anim { duration: root.open ? Appearance.anim.slow : Appearance.anim.fast } }
    }
}

The content slides in from the edge because it's positioned relative to the growing side.

The connecting background shape#

The trick that makes it look liquid: the background is drawn separately from the content, as one Shape per drawer. Each shape is a rounded rectangle attached to an edge, with concave flares where it meets the bar or screen edge.

modules/drawers/DrawerBackground.qmlimport QtQuick
import QtQuick.Shapes
import qs.services

// background for a drawer attached to the LEFT (bar) side.
Shape {
    id: bg
    required property Item drawer            // the Drawer it decorates
    property real r: Appearance.rounding.large
    readonly property real w: drawer.width
    readonly property real h: drawer.height

    x: drawer.x
    y: drawer.y - r                          // flares extend above and below
    width: w + r
    height: h + 2 * r
    visible: w > 1 && h > 1
    preferredRendererType: Shape.CurveRenderer

    ShapePath {
        fillColor: Colors.surface
        strokeWidth: -1
        startX: 0; startY: 0
        // concave flare at the top, curving from the bar into the drawer
        PathArc { x: Math.min(bg.r, bg.w); y: bg.r; radiusX: Math.min(bg.r, bg.w); radiusY: bg.r }
        PathLine { x: bg.w - bg.r; y: bg.r }
        // convex top-right corner
        PathArc { x: bg.w; y: bg.r * 2; radiusX: bg.r; radiusY: bg.r }
        PathLine { x: bg.w; y: bg.h }
        // convex bottom-right corner
        PathArc { x: bg.w - bg.r; y: bg.h + bg.r; radiusX: bg.r; radiusY: bg.r }
        PathLine { x: Math.min(bg.r, bg.w); y: bg.h + bg.r }
        // concave flare at the bottom
        PathArc { x: 0; y: bg.h + 2 * bg.r; radiusX: Math.min(bg.r, bg.w); radiusY: bg.r }
        PathLine { x: 0; y: 0 }
    }
}

Because w and h follow the drawer's animated size, the background reshapes every frame of the animation.

The drawers window#

modules/drawers/Drawers.qmlimport Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import Quickshell.Hyprland
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Layouts
import qs.services
import qs.widgets
import qs.modules.bar

Scope {
    Variants {
        model: Quickshell.screens

        Scope {
            id: perScreen
            required property ShellScreen modelData
            readonly property bool focusedScreen: GlobalStates.activeScreen === modelData.name

            Exclusion { screenRef: perScreen.modelData }

            PanelWindow {
                id: win
                screen: perScreen.modelData
                anchors { top: true; bottom: true; left: true; right: true }
                exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
                color: "transparent"
                WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Top
                WlrLayershell.namespace: "quickshell:drawers"
                WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: launcher.open ? WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive : WlrKeyboardFocus.None

                // input only where something is visible
                mask: Region {
                    item: bar
                    Region { item: launcher }
                    Region { item: dashboard }
                    Region { item: osd }
                    Region { item: launcherHot }
                }
                // hint Hyprland to skip transparent areas
                HyprlandWindow.visibleMask: Region {
                    item: bar
                    Region { item: launcher }
                    Region { item: dashboard }
                    Region { item: osd }
                }

                // ---------------- the bar ----------------
                Rectangle {
                    id: bar
                    anchors { left: parent.left; top: parent.top; bottom: parent.bottom }
                    width: Appearance.sizes.barHeight
                    color: Colors.surface

                    ColumnLayout {
                        anchors { fill: parent; topMargin: 10; bottomMargin: 10 }
                        spacing: 10
                        IconButton {
                            Layout.alignment: Qt.AlignHCenter
                            icon: "apps"
                            toggled: GlobalStates.launcherOpen
                            onClicked: GlobalStates.toggle("launcher")
                        }
                        Item { Layout.fillHeight: true }
                        StyledText {                                   // vertical clock
                            Layout.alignment: Qt.AlignHCenter
                            horizontalAlignment: Text.AlignHCenter
                            text: Qt.formatDateTime(Time.now, "hh\nmm")
                            font.bold: true
                            lineHeight: 0.9
                        }
                        Item { Layout.fillHeight: true }
                        IconButton {
                            Layout.alignment: Qt.AlignHCenter
                            icon: "power_settings_new"
                            onClicked: GlobalStates.toggle("session")
                        }
                    }
                }

                // ---------------- drawers (content) ----------------
                Drawer {
                    id: launcher
                    edge: Qt.LeftEdge
                    open: GlobalStates.launcherOpen && perScreen.focusedScreen
                    anchors.left: bar.right
                    anchors.verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter
                    LauncherContent { width: 460; height: 520 }      // your launcher UI from Chapter 52, as an Item
                }

                Drawer {
                    id: dashboard
                    edge: Qt.TopEdge
                    open: (GlobalStates.controlCenterOpen || dashHover.hovered) && perScreen.focusedScreen
                    anchors.top: parent.top
                    anchors.horizontalCenter: parent.horizontalCenter
                    DashboardContent { width: 640; height: 260 }
                    HoverHandler { id: dashHover }
                }

                Drawer {
                    id: osd
                    edge: Qt.RightEdge
                    open: OsdState.shown && perScreen.focusedScreen
                    anchors.right: parent.right
                    anchors.verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter
                    OsdContent { width: 64; height: 240 }
                }

                // hot zone: hovering the top edge peeks the dashboard
                Item {
                    id: launcherHot
                    anchors { top: parent.top; horizontalCenter: parent.horizontalCenter }
                    width: 300; height: 2
                    HoverHandler { onHoveredChanged: if (hovered) GlobalStates.open("controlCenter") }
                }

                // ---------------- backgrounds (behind content) ----------------
                DrawerBackground { drawer: launcher; z: -1 }
                TopDrawerBackground { drawer: dashboard; z: -1 }
                RightDrawerBackground { drawer: osd; z: -1 }

                Keys.onEscapePressed: GlobalStates.closeAll()
            }
        }
    }
}

TopDrawerBackground and RightDrawerBackground are the same shape as DrawerBackground, rotated: write the path for the top edge (flares on the left and right of the drawer, convex corners at the bottom), or wrap one shape in an Item with rotation: 90/-90 and swap width/height.

Making content components#

Turn each module's UI into a plain Item (no window) so it can live inside a drawer: LauncherContent.qml, DashboardContent.qml, OsdContent.qml. The logic is identical to Part VI; only the outer PanelWindow goes away. Keyboard focus is handled by the drawers window (WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive while the launcher drawer is open).

Why this architecture is powerful#

  • Seamless shapes: bar and drawers share one coordinate space, so their outlines join perfectly.
  • No popup positioning: every drawer is just an Item anchored in the same window.
  • Peek interactions: hovering an edge can open a drawer without any extra window.
  • One mask controls all input.

Costs: a fullscreen surface per monitor (keep it transparent and use HyprlandWindow.visibleMask so the compositor skips empty areas), and you manage keyboard focus yourself.

In the wild

Caelestia's modules/drawers/ implements exactly this: Drawers.qml (the window, mask and exclusion), Backgrounds.qml (the shape paths), Interactions.qml (hover/peek logic) and Panels.qml (content). Read it now: you'll recognize every piece.

Exercises
  1. Get the launcher drawer working with the background shape.
  2. Add the top dashboard drawer with hover-to-peek and a 300 ms close delay when the mouse leaves.
  3. Add a 1 px outline to the combined shape (strokeColor) for a crisp edge.
Part VII · Mastery

Debugging

Every shell breaks sometimes. This chapter is your toolbox: reading errors, logging, inspecting state, and a big table of symptoms and fixes.

Read the error properly#

WARN qml: file:///home/you/.config/quickshell/myshell/modules/bar/Clock.qml:42:9: TypeError: Cannot read property 'title' of null
Part Meaning
WARN / ERROR severity
file:///…/Clock.qml which file
42:9 line 42, column 9
TypeError: Cannot read property 'title' of null the actual problem: something before .title was null

Fix: foo?.title ?? "".

Logging#

console.log("volume:", Audio.volume)                         // INFO
console.warn("weird state", JSON.stringify(obj))             // WARN
console.error("failed")                                      // ERROR
console.log(JSON.stringify(Hyprland.focusedMonitor?.lastIpcObject, null, 2))
console.trace()                                              // call stack
console.time("search"); /* … */ console.timeEnd("search")   // timing
qs -c myshell                    # logs in the terminal
qs -c myshell -v                 # + Quickshell INFO internals
qs -c myshell -vv                # + DEBUG internals
qs -c myshell --log-times        # timestamps
qs log -c myshell -f             # follow the log of a daemonized instance
qs log -c myshell -t 100         # last 100 lines
qs -c myshell --log-rules "quickshell.service.pipewire*=true"   # enable one category

Inspecting live state from outside#

Add a debug IPC target:

IpcHandler {
    target: "debug"
    function eval(expr: string): string {
        try { return String(eval(expr)) } catch (e) { return "error: " + e }
    }
    function dump(): string { return JSON.stringify({ launcher: GlobalStates.launcherOpen, vol: Audio.volume }) }
}
qs ipc call debug dump
qs ipc call debug eval "Mpris.players.values.map(p => p.identity).join(', ')"
Remove eval before sharing

An eval IPC function lets anything running as your user execute code in your shell. Keep it for local debugging only.

Visual debugging#

// outline any item
Rectangle { anchors.fill: parent; color: "transparent"; border.color: "red"; border.width: 1; z: 999 }

// show an item's size
Text { text: parent.width.toFixed(0) + "×" + parent.height.toFixed(0); color: "red"; z: 999 }

Environment variables for Qt Quick:

QSG_VISUALIZE=overdraw qs -c myshell     # see overdraw
QSG_VISUALIZE=batches qs -c myshell      # see draw batches
QSG_RENDER_TIMING=1 qs -c myshell        # print frame render times
QT_QUICK_BACKEND=software qs -c myshell  # rule out GPU driver issues

Symptom → fix table#

Symptom Cause Fix
X is not a type missing import, wrong file name case, typo add the import; files must be Capitalized.qml
Cannot assign to non-existent property wrong property name or type check the reference page
ReferenceError: foo is not defined id from another file, or singleton not imported pass as property; import qs.services
TypeError: … of null/undefined object not ready, or nothing playing/connected ?. and ??
Binding loop detected size depends on itself implicit sizes up, actual sizes down (Sizing and Implicit Size)
Value stops updating assignment destroyed a binding; or var mutated in place bind to state; reassign arrays/objects
Window doesn't appear zero size, visible: false, null screen set implicitWidth/Height ≥ 1
Window is white color defaults to white color: "transparent"
Typing doesn't reach my TextInput layer window has no keyboard focus WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus + focus: true
Can't click apps behind my overlay window catches clicks mask: Region {} or a precise mask
Volume always 0 / can't set it node not bound PwObjectTracker { objects: [...] }
Notifications vanish not tracked n.tracked = true in onNotification
Notification server doesn't start another daemon owns the name stop dunst/mako/swaync
Singleton logic never runs singletons are lazy reference it from shell.qml
qs -c name says no config a default ~/.config/quickshell/shell.qml exists use only named configs
GlobalShortcut does nothing missing Hyprland bind / name mismatch bind = …, global, quickshell:<name>
IPC function missing in qs ipc show untyped parameters or return add types to every param and the return
Popup cut off drawn inside the bar window use PopupWindow
Icon missing name not in theme / wrong theme //@ pragma IconTheme …, fallback in iconPath
Text blurry fractional scaling, default rendering renderType: Text.NativeRendering
Image looks pixelated sourceSize too small for HiDPI multiply by devicePixelRatio
Hot reload changed nothing error in file (check terminal), or watchFiles: false read the log
Old notification popups after reload re-emitted with keepOnReload skip n.lastGeneration
Process output empty pipes without sh -c; program not on PATH wrap in sh -c; check which
Process output parsed wrongly localized output environment: ({ LC_ALL: "C" })
Lock screen shows solid color after crash shell died while locked (by design) restart your shell / see Project: Lock Screen

Bisecting a broken config#

  1. Comment out half of the modules in shell.qml. Still broken? The bug is in the remaining half.
  2. Repeat until one module is left.
  3. In that module, comment out children or bindings the same way.

With git: git stash to confirm the last commit works, git diff to see what changed, git bisect for older regressions.

Crash reports#

If Quickshell itself crashes, it writes a crash report and prints its location in the log. When reporting a bug upstream, include:

  • qs --version, your distro, compositor version, and Qt version (qtpaths6 --qt-version)
  • the crash report or log
  • a minimal shell.qml that reproduces it
Exercises
  1. Add a debug IPC target with a dump() function for your shell's main states.
  2. Run with QSG_VISUALIZE=overdraw and find your most overdrawn widget.
  3. Break a binding on purpose and find it using only logs.
Part VII · Mastery

Performance

A well-built Quickshell shell idles near 0% CPU and a modest amount of RAM. A badly built one can keep a CPU core busy and drain your battery. This chapter shows how to measure and what to fix.

Measure first#

pid=$(pgrep -f "qs -c myshell" | head -1)
top -p $pid                                   # CPU% and RES (memory)
ps -o rss=,etime= -p $pid                     # resident memory in KB, uptime
pidstat -p $pid 1                             # CPU per second (sysstat)
QSG_RENDER_TIMING=1 qs -c myshell             # per-frame render times

Watch idle CPU with no interaction for a minute. Anything consistently above ~1% means something is waking up too often.

The big wins#

1. Don't render when nothing changes#

Qt only redraws when something changes. Things that change every frame:

  • infinite animations (spinners, pulsing dots, visualizers),
  • ScreencopyView { live: true },
  • AnimatedImage, Video,
  • Timers with short intervals that change visible properties.

Bind them to visibility:

RotationAnimation on rotation { running: busy && root.visible; loops: Animation.Infinite; from: 0; to: 360; duration: 1000 }
ScreencopyView { live: GlobalStates.overviewOpen }
AnimatedImage { playing: visible }

2. Prefer events to polling#

Instead of polling… Use
wpctl get-volume every second Pipewire
playerctl Mpris
cat /sys/…/capacity UPower
hyprctl activeworkspace Hyprland
nmcli every 5 s Networking or nmcli monitor + SplitParser
date SystemClock with the lowest precision you need

3. Poll slowly, and only when visible#

Timer { interval: 2000; repeat: true; running: dashboard.visible; onTriggered: refresh() }

4. FileView over Process#

Reading /proc/stat with FileView is a file read. Running sh -c "head -1 /proc/stat" forks and execs two processes each time.

5. Lazy-load windows and heavy items#

LazyLoader for panels, Loader { active: … } for heavy parts (Lazy Loading and Memory).

6. Decode images at display size#

Always sourceSize. A wallpaper picker with 100 thumbnails at full 4K resolution can use several gigabytes; with sourceSize: Qt.size(560, 360) it uses ~80 MB.

7. Views, not Repeaters, for long lists#

ListView creates only visible delegates. Repeater over 500 apps creates 500 delegates.

8. ScriptModel for filtered lists#

Avoids destroying and recreating every delegate on each keystroke (ObjectModel and ScriptModel).

9. Keep bindings cheap#

A binding that sorts 500 entries re-runs whenever any dependency changes. Compute heavy things once in a readonly property and reuse it, or debounce with a Timer.

10. Effects and layers cost GPU#

  • layer.enabled and MultiEffect allocate offscreen textures. Disable them while hidden (layer.enabled: visible).
  • Large blurs (blurMax: 64 over a fullscreen image) are expensive; blur a downscaled image instead (decode the wallpaper at half size for the lock screen).
  • Prefer compositor blur (layer rules) for backgrounds.

11. Fullscreen transparent windows#

For Caelestia-style shells, set HyprlandWindow.visibleMask so the compositor doesn't composite (or blur) the empty areas.

12. Opaque surfaces where possible#

If a window is fully opaque, surfaceFormat.opaque: true lets the compositor skip blending.

Memory checklist#

Check Typical fix
Many hidden windows LazyLoader
Big images sourceSize, cache: false for one-off images
Notification history growing forever cap it: dismiss the oldest beyond 100
Clipboard image previews delete temp files, cap the list
Leaking objects created with createObject destroy() them, or use Loader/Repeater instead

Startup time#

  • //@ pragma DropExpensiveFonts can save memory and startup time.
  • Avoid blockLoading on files that aren't needed for the first frame.
  • LazyLoader { loading: true } builds panels in the background after startup instead of during it.
  • Run fewer Processes at startup; stagger polling timers.

A performance budget#

State Target
Idle, nothing animating < 0.5% CPU
Music playing with progress bar < 2% CPU
Overview open with live previews GPU-bound, but no stutter
RAM, full shell 150–350 MB is typical for Qt Quick shells
Exercises
  1. Measure your shell's idle CPU for a minute; find and fix the top offender.
  2. Make every infinite animation in your shell stop when invisible.
  3. Compare memory of your wallpaper picker with and without sourceSize.
Part VII · Mastery

Reading Other People's Rices

The fastest way to grow after this book is to read real shells. This chapter is a field guide: how to approach a large config, where things usually live, and what to look for in the popular ones.

How to read a big config#

  1. Run it in isolation. Clone into ~/.config/quickshell/<name> and run qs -c <name>. Many shells have dependencies (fonts, CLI tools, a C++ plugin); check their README.
  2. Start at shell.qml. It lists the top-level modules, the table of contents.
  3. Find the services folder. Singletons there show how they talk to the system.
  4. Find the design tokens. Appearance.qml, Config.qml, Colours.qml, Theme.qml.
  5. Pick one feature you like (a workspace indicator, a notification animation) and trace it: find the file (grep -rn "Workspaces" .), read its imports, follow the services it uses.
  6. Re-implement it in your own structure, using your own tokens. Don't paste whole files; you'll understand nothing and inherit their dependencies.
grep -rn "PanelWindow" --include=*.qml . | head          # where are the windows?
grep -rln "pragma Singleton" --include=*.qml .            # list all singletons
grep -rn "IpcHandler" -A2 --include=*.qml .               # which IPC targets exist?
grep -rn "GlobalShortcut" -A2 --include=*.qml .           # which keybinds?

end-4 / dots-hyprland (illogical-impulse)#

You want Look for
Entry and panel wiring shell.qml, GlobalStates.qml
Config system (hundreds of options) modules/common/Config.qml (FileView + JsonAdapter)
Colors and sizes modules/common/Appearance.qml
Styled widget library modules/common/widgets/
System services services/ (audio, battery, network, brightness, notifications, AI, booru, Hyprland data…)
Bar modules/bar/
Overview with live previews modules/overview/
Sidebars modules/sidebarLeft/, modules/sidebarRight/
Wallpaper → colors scripts/colors/ (matugen + Python)

Techniques worth studying: centralized Config, the sliding/stretching workspace indicator, the overview's window positioning math, search with fuzzysort, Material 3 shape morphing.

Caelestia shell#

You want Look for
Drawer architecture modules/drawers/ (window, backgrounds, interactions, panels)
Config config/ (one file per area)
Colors services/Colours.qml + the caelestia CLI's scheme files
Components components/ (styled primitives, animations)
Services services/
Native helpers plugin/ (C++ QML plugin: audio visualizer, beat detection, image tools)

Techniques: the one-window-per-screen drawer layout with masks, shape backgrounds with concave joints, expressive motion tokens, and a CLI that drives the shell over IPC.

Noctalia and DankMaterialShell#

Both are designed to be installed by other people, so they show:

  • settings GUIs bound to JSON config (FileView + JsonAdapter),
  • feature toggles and per-monitor settings,
  • compositor abstraction layers (Hyprland, niri, Sway),
  • plugin and widget systems.

Noctalia ships its own Quickshell fork (noctalia-qs) with extra modules like Quickshell.Niri and Quickshell.DWL; if you build on those modules, your shell requires that fork.

JaKooLit Hyprland-Dots#

A large classic setup (Waybar, rofi, swaync, many scripts) that adopted Quickshell for selected components. It's useful to see how Quickshell coexists with other tools: separate small configs started with qs -c …, toggled by keybinds calling qs ipc call.

Upstream examples and docs#

  • The Quickshell repository and the official docs at quickshell.org (type reference and guides; this book's API reference is generated from the same source comments).
  • The examples in the docs: small focused configs for one feature each.

Etiquette#

  • Respect licenses. Most rices are GPL or MIT; keep notices if you copy code.
  • Credit ideas you borrow in your README.
  • Report bugs upstream with minimal reproductions; don't open issues for your own modifications.
Exercises
  1. Clone one of the shells above, run it as a named config, and list all its IPC targets with qs ipc show.
  2. Pick one widget from it and rebuild it from scratch in your shell using your own design tokens.
Part VII · Mastery

Cookbook: 60 Small Recipes

Short, copy-ready answers to "how do I…?". Each assumes the design-system widgets and services from Part V where relevant.

Windows and layout#

1. Bar on the bottom#

anchors { bottom: true; left: true; right: true }

2. Vertical bar on the right#

anchors { right: true; top: true; bottom: true }
implicitWidth: 44

3. Hide the bar when a window is fullscreen (Hyprland)#

visible: !(Hyprland.monitorFor(screen)?.activeWorkspace?.hasFullscreen ?? false)

4. Toggle the bar with a key#

IpcHandler { target: "bar"; function toggle(): void { GlobalStates.barHidden = !GlobalStates.barHidden } }
bind = SUPER, B, exec, qs -c myshell ipc call bar toggle

5. Window only on the primary monitor#

screen: Quickshell.screens.find(s => s.name === "DP-1") ?? Quickshell.screens[0]

6. Click-through overlay#

mask: Region {}

7. Center a window on screen#

Leave all anchors false and set both implicit sizes.

8. Floating bar with gaps that match Hyprland's#

margins { top: 10; left: 10; right: 10 }      // = general:gaps_out

9. Make a window appear above fullscreen apps#

WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay

10. Reserve space without drawing anything#

PanelWindow { anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true } implicitHeight: 1; exclusiveZone: 40; color: "transparent"; mask: Region {} }

Text and icons#

11. Truncate long text with "…"#

Text { width: 200; elide: Text.ElideRight }

12. Digits that don't jiggle#

font.features: ({ "tnum": 1 })

13. Filled Material icon on hover#

font.variableAxes: ({ "FILL": hover.hovered ? 1 : 0 })

14. App icon for a window#

IconImage { source: Quickshell.iconPath(DesktopEntries.heuristicLookup(toplevel.appId)?.icon ?? "", "application-x-executable") }

15. Marquee (scrolling) text for long titles#

Item {
    width: 180; height: t.height; clip: true
    Text {
        id: t; text: Media.active?.trackTitle ?? ""
        NumberAnimation on x {
            running: t.width > 180; loops: Animation.Infinite
            from: 180; to: -t.width; duration: (t.width + 180) * 25
        }
    }
}

16. Rich text notification body safely#

textFormat: Text.StyledText          // never Text.RichText for untrusted input

Interaction#

17. Right-click menu on any item#

TapHandler { acceptedButtons: Qt.RightButton; onTapped: menuPopup.visible = true }

18. Scroll to change volume (touchpad-safe)#

WheelHandler { onWheel: e => Audio.setVolume(Audio.volume + e.angleDelta.y / 120 * 0.05) }

19. Long-press action#

TapHandler { onLongPressed: doSomething() }

20. Double-click action#

TapHandler { onDoubleTapped: doSomething() }

21. Close a popup when clicking outside#

PopupWindow { grabFocus: true }
// panels on Hyprland: HyprlandFocusGrab { windows: [win]; active: true; onCleared: close() }

22. Hover delay before showing a tooltip#

HoverHandler { id: hh }
Timer { id: d; interval: 500; running: hh.hovered }
Tooltip { show: hh.hovered && !d.running }

23. Keyboard shortcut inside a panel#

Keys.onPressed: e => { if (e.key === Qt.Key_F && e.modifiers & Qt.ControlModifier) search.forceActiveFocus() }

System#

24. Volume percentage#

Text { text: Math.round((Pipewire.defaultAudioSink?.audio?.volume ?? 0) * 100) + "%" }
PwObjectTracker { objects: [Pipewire.defaultAudioSink] }

25. Microphone mute toggle#

PwObjectTracker { objects: [Pipewire.defaultAudioSource] }
TapHandler { onTapped: Pipewire.defaultAudioSource.audio.muted = !Pipewire.defaultAudioSource.audio.muted }

26. Is the mic in use (privacy indicator)?#

readonly property bool micInUse: Pipewire.linkGroups.values.some(g => g.source?.type === PwNodeType.AudioSource && g.target?.isStream)

27. Switch audio output to headphones#

Pipewire.preferredDefaultAudioSink = Pipewire.nodes.values.find(n => n.isSink && !n.isStream && n.description.includes("Headphones"))

28. Battery time remaining#

text: { const s = UPower.displayDevice.timeToEmpty; return s > 0 ? Math.floor(s / 3600) + "h " + Math.round(s % 3600 / 60) + "m" : "" }

29. Plugged in?#

visible: !UPower.onBattery

30. Power profile cycle button#

TapHandler { onTapped: PowerProfiles.profile = (PowerProfiles.profile + 1) % (PowerProfiles.hasPerformanceProfile ? 3 : 2) }

31. Current song as "Artist — Title"#

text: Media.active ? `${Media.active.trackArtist} — ${Media.active.trackTitle}` : ""

32. Bluetooth headset battery#

text: Bluetooth.devices.values.filter(d => d.connected && d.batteryAvailable).map(d => `${d.name} ${Math.round(d.battery * 100)}%`).join("  ")

33. Wi-Fi name#

text: Networking.devices.values.find(d => d.type === DeviceType.Wifi)?.networks.values.find(n => n.connected)?.name ?? "offline"

34. Internet connectivity state#

text: NetworkConnectivity.toString(Networking.connectivity)       // None / Portal / Limited / Full

35. CPU temperature#

FileView { id: temp; path: "/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp" }
Timer { interval: 3000; running: true; repeat: true; onTriggered: temp.reload() }
Text { text: Math.round(parseInt(temp.text()) / 1000) + "°C" }

36. Disk usage of /#

Process { id: df; command: ["sh", "-c", "df -h / | awk 'NR==2{print $5}'"]; running: true
          stdout: StdioCollector { onStreamFinished: disk.text = text.trim() } }

37. Pending updates (Arch)#

Process { command: ["sh", "-c", "checkupdates 2>/dev/null | wc -l"]; running: true
          stdout: StdioCollector { onStreamFinished: updates.text = text.trim() } }

38. Keyboard layout (Hyprland)#

Connections { target: Hyprland; function onRawEvent(e) { if (e.name === "activelayout") layout.text = e.parse(2)[1] } }

39. Caps Lock indicator#

FileView { id: caps; path: "/sys/class/leds/input0::capslock/brightness"; watchChanges: true; onFileChanged: reload() }
visible: caps.text().trim() === "1"

(The LED name varies; ls /sys/class/leds.)

40. Screen recording indicator#

Process { id: rec; command: ["pgrep", "-x", "wf-recorder"]; onExited: code => recording = code === 0 }
Timer { interval: 2000; running: true; repeat: true; onTriggered: rec.running = true }

41. Take a region screenshot#

Quickshell.execDetached(["sh", "-c", 'grim -g "$(slurp)" - | wl-copy && notify-send "Screenshot copied"'])

42. Copy text to the clipboard#

Quickshell.execDetached(["wl-copy", text])
// or, while a Quickshell window is focused: Quickshell.clipboardText = text

43. Open a URL or file#

Qt.openUrlExternally("https://quickshell.org")

44. Launch the terminal in a folder#

Quickshell.execDetached(["kitty", "--directory", Quickshell.env("HOME") + "/projects"])

45. Run a command as root (with your polkit agent)#

Quickshell.execDetached(["pkexec", "systemctl", "restart", "NetworkManager"])

Data and state#

46. Remember a value across restarts#

FileView { path: Quickshell.statePath("x.json"); onAdapterUpdated: writeAdapter(); JsonAdapter { id: st; property int count: 0 } }

47. Keep a value across hot reloads#

PersistentProperties { reloadableId: "ui"; property bool sidebarOpen: false }

48. Add to an array so bindings update#

list = [...list, item]

49. Debounce an expensive search#

onTextChanged: deb.restart()
Timer { id: deb; interval: 150; onTriggered: results = search(text) }

50. Run something once after startup#

Timer { interval: 3000; running: true; onTriggered: init() }

51. Detect hot reload#

Connections { target: Quickshell; function onReloadCompleted() { console.log("reloaded") } }

52. Version-gate a feature#

visible: Quickshell.hasVersion(0, 3)

Visual polish#

53. Pill that grows to fit its text#

Rectangle { implicitWidth: t.implicitWidth + 20; implicitHeight: 28; radius: 14; Behavior on implicitWidth { Anim {} }
            Text { id: t; anchors.centerIn: parent } }

54. Soft shadow#

layer.enabled: true
layer.effect: MultiEffect { shadowEnabled: true; shadowBlur: 0.8; shadowOpacity: 0.4; shadowVerticalOffset: 4 }

55. Rounded image#

ClippingRectangle { radius: 16; Image { anchors.fill: parent; fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectCrop } }

56. Gradient border#

Rectangle {
    radius: 16; gradient: Gradient { orientation: Gradient.Horizontal
        GradientStop { position: 0; color: Colors.primary } GradientStop { position: 1; color: Colors.tertiary } }
    Rectangle { anchors.fill: parent; anchors.margins: 2; radius: 14; color: Colors.surface }
}

57. Animated gradient#

GradientStop { position: 0; color: Qt.hsla(hue, 0.6, 0.6, 1) }
property real hue: 0
NumberAnimation on hue { from: 0; to: 1; duration: 10000; loops: Animation.Infinite; running: visible }

58. Glass panel (Hyprland blur)#

color: Qt.rgba(Colors.surface.r, Colors.surface.g, Colors.surface.b, 0.6)
WlrLayershell.namespace: "quickshell:glass"     // + layerrule = blur, quickshell:glass

59. Ripple on click#

Rectangle {
    id: ripple; width: 0; height: width; radius: width / 2; color: Colors.alpha(Colors.onSurface, 0.15); opacity: 0
    ParallelAnimation { id: rip
        NumberAnimation { target: ripple; property: "width"; from: 0; to: 200; duration: 400 }
        NumberAnimation { target: ripple; property: "opacity"; from: 1; to: 0; duration: 400 } }
}
TapHandler { onTapped: p => { ripple.x = p.position.x - 100; ripple.y = p.position.y - 100; rip.restart() } }

(Set clip: true on the parent.)

60. Reduce motion globally#

// Appearance.qml
readonly property real motion: Config.appearance.reduceMotion ? 0 : 1
readonly property int animNormal: 250 * motion
Part VII · Mastery

Beyond QML: Plugins and Helpers

QML and JavaScript cover almost everything. When they don't (heavy number crunching, a library only available in C++ or Python, a protocol Quickshell doesn't speak), you have three escape hatches, from easiest to most powerful.

1. Helper programs over stdout (easiest)#

Write a small program in any language that prints one JSON object per line. Run it with Process + SplitParser.

scripts/sysinfo.py#!/usr/bin/env python3
import json, time, psutil

while True:
    print(json.dumps({
        "cpu": psutil.cpu_percent() / 100,
        "ram": psutil.virtual_memory().percent / 100,
        "net_rx": psutil.net_io_counters().bytes_recv,
    }), flush=True)                     # flush! otherwise output is buffered
    time.sleep(2)
Process {
    command: ["python3", Quickshell.shellPath("scripts/sysinfo.py")]
    running: true
    stdout: SplitParser {
        onRead: line => {
            try { const d = JSON.parse(line); root.cpu = d.cpu; root.ram = d.ram } catch (e) {}
        }
    }
}

Pros: any language, crash-isolated, easy to test in a terminal. Cons: an extra process; data only flows one way unless you use stdin (stdinEnabled + write()).

Always flush

Most languages buffer stdout when it isn't a terminal. Use flush=True (Python), fflush(stdout) (C), std::io::stdout().flush() (Rust), or stdbuf -oL in front of the command.

2. Sockets and D-Bus#

  • A long-running helper can expose a Unix socket; connect with Socket for two-way communication.
  • Many services already speak D-Bus. Without a Quickshell module, use busctl/gdbus through Process:
gdbus monitor --system --dest org.freedesktop.login1        # watch logind events (lid, sleep)
busctl --user call org.freedesktop.Notifications /org/freedesktop/Notifications org.freedesktop.Notifications GetServerInformation
Process {
    command: ["gdbus", "monitor", "--system", "--dest", "org.freedesktop.login1"]
    running: true
    stdout: SplitParser { onRead: l => { if (l.includes("PrepareForSleep") && l.includes("true")) GlobalStates.locked = true } }
}

That snippet locks your screen right before suspend, without hypridle.

3. C++ QML plugins (most powerful)#

A QML module written in C++ can expose new types with the same performance as Quickshell's own. Caelestia uses one for its audio visualizer and beat detection.

Minimal plugin#

myplugin/
├── CMakeLists.txt
├── counter.hpp
└── counter.cpp
myplugin/CMakeLists.txtcmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(myplugin LANGUAGES CXX)
find_package(Qt6 REQUIRED COMPONENTS Quick)
qt_standard_project_setup(REQUIRES 6.6)

qt_add_qml_module(myplugin
    URI MyPlugin
    VERSION 1.0
    SHARED
    SOURCES counter.hpp counter.cpp
)
target_link_libraries(myplugin PRIVATE Qt6::Quick)
myplugin/counter.hpp#pragma once
#include <QObject>
#include <QTimer>
#include <qqmlintegration.h>

class Counter : public QObject {
    Q_OBJECT
    QML_ELEMENT                                       // usable as `Counter {}` in QML
    Q_PROPERTY(int value READ value NOTIFY valueChanged)
public:
    explicit Counter(QObject* parent = nullptr);
    int value() const { return m_value; }
    Q_INVOKABLE void reset();
signals:
    void valueChanged();
private:
    int m_value = 0;
    QTimer m_timer;
};
myplugin/counter.cpp#include "counter.hpp"

Counter::Counter(QObject* parent) : QObject(parent) {
    connect(&m_timer, &QTimer::timeout, this, [this] { m_value++; emit valueChanged(); });
    m_timer.start(1000);
}
void Counter::reset() { m_value = 0; emit valueChanged(); }
cmake -B build -G Ninja && cmake --build build
# install to a QML import path, e.g. user-local:
mkdir -p ~/.local/lib/qt6/qml && cp -r build/MyPlugin ~/.local/lib/qt6/qml/

Make Quickshell find it:

shell.qml//@ pragma Env QML_IMPORT_PATH=/home/you/.local/lib/qt6/qml
import MyPlugin

ShellRoot { Counter { onValueChanged: console.log(value) } }
Qt version must match

A C++ plugin must be compiled against the same Qt version Quickshell uses. After a Qt update you must rebuild it, or Quickshell fails to load the module.

4. Contributing to Quickshell#

If what you built is generally useful (a protocol, a service), consider contributing upstream. The source uses the same Q_PROPERTY + doc-comment style shown above; the API reference in this book is generated from those comments.

Exercises
  1. Write a helper in any language that prints the number of unread emails as JSON lines, and show it in your bar.
  2. Lock the screen before suspend using the gdbus monitor snippet.
  3. Build the minimal C++ plugin and use Counter in a test config.
Part VII · Mastery

Sharing and Maintaining Your Rice

Your shell works. Now make it easy to keep running, to restore on a new machine, and to share with others.

Run it reliably#

From the compositor (simplest)#

hyprland.confexec-once = qs -c myshell

As a systemd user service (auto-restart on crash)#

~/.config/systemd/user/myshell.service[Unit]
Description=My Quickshell shell
PartOf=graphical-session.target
After=graphical-session.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/qs -c myshell
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=1

[Install]
WantedBy=graphical-session.target
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now myshell.service
journalctl --user -u myshell -f          # logs

This requires your compositor to start graphical-session.target (UWSM does; with plain Hyprland add exec-once = systemctl --user start graphical-session.target or use uwsm).

Version control#

cd ~/.config/quickshell/myshell
git init
cat > .gitignore <<'EOF'
.qmlls.ini
*.qsb
EOF
git add -A && git commit -m "my shell"

Commit small, working steps. When something breaks, git diff shows what changed and git stash gets you back to a working state instantly.

Dotfiles layout#

~/dotfiles/
├── quickshell/myshell/      → ~/.config/quickshell/myshell
├── hypr/                    → ~/.config/hypr
├── matugen/                 → ~/.config/matugen
├── kitty/                   → ~/.config/kitty
└── install.sh

Use symlinks (ln -s) or GNU Stow (stow -t ~ quickshell) to put them in place.

Make it work on other machines#

  • No hard-coded paths or names. Use Quickshell.env("HOME"), Quickshell.shellPath(), Quickshell.statePath(), and read monitor names, wallpaper folders and the terminal from Config.
  • Defaults for everything in JsonAdapter, so a fresh install runs without a config file.
  • Graceful degradation: hide modules whose service isn't available (Battery.available, Networking.backend, Bluetooth.defaultAdapter !== null, Brightness.available).
  • Check for helper programs before showing features that need them:
Process {
    command: ["sh", "-c", "command -v cliphist"]
    running: true
    onExited: code => GlobalStates.hasCliphist = code === 0
}
  • Compositor abstraction (services/Workspaces.qml) if you want to support more than one compositor.

A good README#

  1. Screenshot or short video first.
  2. Features list.
  3. Dependencies: Quickshell version (or fork), Qt modules, fonts, CLI tools, with install commands per distro.
  4. Install steps (clone, symlink, autostart line, keybinds).
  5. Configuration: where the JSON lives and its options.
  6. IPC targets and keybinds table (qs ipc show output).
  7. Credits and license.

Licensing#

Pick a license (MIT, GPL-3.0…) and add a LICENSE file. If you borrowed code from another rice, keep its license notice and credit it.

Keeping up with Quickshell#

  • Read release notes before updating: occasionally properties are renamed or deprecated (the reference marks deprecated members, e.g. PopupWindow.parentWindow → anchor.window).
  • Use Quickshell.hasVersion() to support old and new versions during transitions.
  • After a Qt update, rebuild any C++ plugins.
  • Test new versions in a separate config (qs -c myshell-next) before switching.

Final words#

You've gone from "what is a property?" to building every major component of a desktop shell. The rest is imagination:

  • Sketch the desktop you want on paper.
  • Break it into windows (which layer, which edges, which screens), services (what data) and widgets (what shapes and motion).
  • Build one piece at a time, using the API reference as your dictionary.

There's no layout Quickshell can't draw. Go rice something nobody has seen before.

Qt Reference: Visual Types

Import: import QtQuick

XMLHttpRequest example#

function fetchJson(url, cb) {
    const xhr = new XMLHttpRequest()
    xhr.onreadystatechange = () => {
        if (xhr.readyState === XMLHttpRequest.DONE)
            cb(xhr.status === 200 ? JSON.parse(xhr.responseText) : null)
    }
    xhr.open("GET", url)
    xhr.send()
}
Component.onCompleted: fetchJson("https://wttr.in/?format=j1", d => console.log(d?.current_condition[0].temp_C))

QuickshellSettings

provided by Quickshell

Accessor for some options under the Quickshell type.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
QuickshellSettings → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (singleton). Quickshell gives you instances through: ShellRoot.settings.

Overview#

Settings accessible as settings on a ShellRoot. The same values are also available directly on the Quickshell singleton (Quickshell.watchFiles, Quickshell.workingDirectory), which is usually simpler.

Example#

ShellRoot {
    settings.watchFiles: true                         // reload on save (default)
    settings.workingDirectory: Quickshell.env("HOME") // where relative paths in processes start
    settings.onLastWindowClosed: console.log("no windows left")
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onWorkingDirectoryChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
workingDirectorystringread / write

Quickshell's working directory. Defaults to whereever quickshell was launched from.

watchFilesboolread / write

If true then the configuration will be reloaded whenever any files change. Defaults to true.

Signals#

lastWindowClosed()handler: onLastWindowClosed

Sent when the last window is closed.

To make the application exit when the last window is closed run Qt.quit().

Where this type appears#

  • ShellRoot.settings (property)
Quickshell

Quickshell

singleton
Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
Quickshell → QtObject
How to get one
This is a singleton: exactly one exists, created by Quickshell. Use it from anywhere by its name, e.g. Quickshell.processId. Never write Quickshell { }.

Overview#

The Quickshell singleton is your handle on Quickshell itself: the list of screens, your config folder and per-shell data directories, environment variables, launching detached processes, icon lookup, reload control and version checks. You use it in almost every config.

Use it from any file: Quickshell.screens, Quickshell.env("HOME"), Quickshell.execDetached([...]).

Example: using every property and function#

~/.config/quickshell/qs-test/shell.qmlimport Quickshell
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Layouts

FloatingWindow {
    implicitWidth: 640; implicitHeight: 720
    color: "#1e1e2e"

    component Row2: RowLayout {
        property string k; property string v
        Text { text: parent.k; color: "#a6adc8"; Layout.preferredWidth: 200 }
        Text { text: parent.v; color: "#cdd6f4"; Layout.fillWidth: true; elide: Text.ElideMiddle }
    }

    ColumnLayout {
        anchors { fill: parent; margins: 16 }
        spacing: 4
        // ---- identity ----
        Row2 { k: "processId";  v: Quickshell.processId }
        Row2 { k: "instanceId"; v: Quickshell.instanceId }
        Row2 { k: "shellId";    v: Quickshell.shellId }
        Row2 { k: "appId";      v: Quickshell.appId }
        Row2 { k: "launchTime"; v: Qt.formatDateTime(Quickshell.launchTime, "hh:mm:ss") }
        // ---- folders ----
        Row2 { k: "shellDir";  v: Quickshell.shellDir }
        Row2 { k: "dataDir";   v: Quickshell.dataDir }
        Row2 { k: "stateDir";  v: Quickshell.stateDir }
        Row2 { k: "cacheDir";  v: Quickshell.cacheDir }
        Row2 { k: "shellPath('a.png')"; v: Quickshell.shellPath("assets/a.png") }
        Row2 { k: "statePath('x.json')"; v: Quickshell.statePath("x.json") }
        Row2 { k: "workingDirectory"; v: Quickshell.workingDirectory }
        // ---- environment ----
        Row2 { k: "env('HOME')"; v: Quickshell.env("HOME") }
        Row2 { k: "env('NOPE')"; v: String(Quickshell.env("NOPE")) }      // null if unset
        // ---- screens ----
        Row2 { k: "screens"; v: Quickshell.screens.map(s => s.name).join(", ") }
        // ---- icons ----
        Row2 { k: "hasThemeIcon('firefox')"; v: Quickshell.hasThemeIcon("firefox") }
        Image { source: Quickshell.iconPath("firefox", "application-x-executable"); sourceSize: Qt.size(32, 32) }
        // ---- versions ----
        Row2 { k: "hasVersion(0, 2)"; v: Quickshell.hasVersion(0, 2) }
        Row2 { k: "hasQtVersion(6, 8)"; v: Quickshell.hasQtVersion(6, 8) }
        Row2 { k: "watchFiles"; v: Quickshell.watchFiles }

        RowLayout {
            Text { text: "[launch kitty]"; color: "#89b4fa"
                   TapHandler { onTapped: Quickshell.execDetached(["kitty"]) } }
            Text { text: "[soft reload]"; color: "#89b4fa"
                   TapHandler { onTapped: Quickshell.reload(false) } }
            Text { text: "[copy hello]"; color: "#89b4fa"
                   TapHandler { onTapped: Quickshell.clipboardText = "hello" } }
        }
    }

    Connections {
        target: Quickshell
        function onReloadCompleted() { Quickshell.inhibitReloadPopup(); console.log("reloaded") }
        function onReloadFailed(err) { console.warn("reload failed:", err) }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onProcessIdChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
processIdintconstant

Quickshell's process id.

instanceIdstringconstant

A unique identifier for this Quickshell instance

shellIdstringconstant

The shell ID, used to differentiate between different shell configurations.

Defaults to a stable value derived from the config path. Can be overridden with //@ pragma ShellId <id> in the root qml file.

appIdstringconstant

The desktop application ID.

Defaults to org.quickshell. Can be overridden with //@ pragma AppId <id> in the root qml file or the QS_APP_ID environment variable.

launchTimedateconstant

The time at which this Quickshell instance was launched.

screenslist<ShellScreen>read-only

All currently connected screens.

This property updates as connected screens change.

Reusing a window on every screen

ShellRoot {
  Variants {
    // see Variants for details
    variants: Quickshell.screens
    PanelWindow {
      property var modelData
      screen: modelData
    }
  }
}

This creates an instance of your window once on every screen. As screens are added or removed your window will be created or destroyed on those screens.

A list of ShellScreen. It updates when monitors are plugged or unplugged, so Variants { model: Quickshell.screens } creates one window per monitor automatically.

shellDirstringconstant

The full path to the root directory of your shell.

The root directory is the folder containing the entrypoint to your shell, often referred to as shell.qml.

configDirstringconstant
Deprecated: Renamed to shellDir for clarity.
shellRootstringconstant
Deprecated: Renamed to shellDir for consistency.
workingDirectorystringread / write

Quickshell's working directory. Defaults to whereever quickshell was launched from.

watchFilesboolread / write

If true then the configuration will be reloaded whenever any files change. Defaults to true.

clipboardTextstringread / write

The system clipboard.

Watch out

Under wayland the clipboard will be empty unless a quickshell window is focused.

On Wayland, reading or writing the clipboard only works while a Quickshell window has keyboard focus. For background use, run wl-copy/wl-paste with Process.

dataDirstringconstant

The per-shell data directory.

Usually ~/.local/share/quickshell/by-shell/<shell-id>

Can be overridden using //@ pragma DataDir $BASE/path in the root qml file, where $BASE corresponds to $XDG_DATA_HOME (usually ~/.local/share).

stateDirstringconstant

The per-shell state directory.

Usually ~/.local/state/quickshell/by-shell/<shell-id>

Can be overridden using //@ pragma StateDir $BASE/path in the root qml file, where $BASE corresponds to $XDG_STATE_HOME (usually ~/.local/state).

cacheDirstringconstant

The per-shell cache directory.

Usually ~/.cache/quickshell/by-shell/<shell-id>

Can be overridden using //@ pragma CacheDir $BASE/path in the root qml file, where $BASE corresponds to $XDG_CACHE_HOME (usually ~/.cache).

Functions#

reload(hard: bool): void

Reload the shell.

hard - perform a hard reload. If this is false, Quickshell will attempt to reuse windows that already exist. If true windows will be recreated.

See Reloadable for more information on what can be reloaded and how.

env(variable: string): var

Returns the string value of an environment variable or null if it is not set.

Returns null if the variable isn't set, so Quickshell.env("SWAYSOCK") !== null tests for Sway.

execDetached(context: ProcessContext): void

Launch a process detached from Quickshell.

The context parameter can either be a list of command arguments or a JS object with the following fields: - command: A list containing the command and all its arguments. See Process.command. - environment: Changes to make to the process environment. See Process.environment. - clearEnvironment: Removes all variables from the environment if true. - workingDirectory: The working directory the command should run in.

This does not run command in a shell. All arguments to the command

must be in separate values in the list, e.g. ["echo", "hello"] and not ["echo hello"].

Additionally, shell scripts must be run by your shell, e.g. ["sh", "script.sh"] instead of ["script.sh"] unless the script has a shebang.

You can use ["sh", "-c", <your command>] to execute your command with

the system shell.

This function is equivalent to Process.startDetached().

Pass a list (["notify-send", "hi"]). The process isn't a child of Quickshell, so it keeps running if your shell reloads or exits. You can't read its output; use Process for that.

iconPath(icon: string): string

Returns a string usable for a Image.source for a given system icon.

Note

By default, icons are loaded from the theme selected by the qt platform theme, which means they should match with all other qt applications on your system.

If you want to use a different icon theme, you can put //@ pragma IconTheme <name> at the top of your root config file or set the QS_ICON_THEME variable to the name of your icon theme.

Three forms: iconPath(name), iconPath(name, true) (returns "" if the icon doesn't exist), iconPath(name, "fallback-name"). The theme comes from //@ pragma IconTheme.

iconPath(icon: string, check: bool): string

Setting the check parameter of iconPath to true will return an empty string if the icon does not exist, instead of an image showing a missing texture.

Three forms: iconPath(name), iconPath(name, true) (returns "" if the icon doesn't exist), iconPath(name, "fallback-name"). The theme comes from //@ pragma IconTheme.

iconPath(icon: string, fallback: string): string

Setting the fallback parameter of iconPath will attempt to load the fallback icon if the requested one could not be loaded.

Three forms: iconPath(name), iconPath(name, true) (returns "" if the icon doesn't exist), iconPath(name, "fallback-name"). The theme comes from //@ pragma IconTheme.

hasThemeIcon(icon: string): bool

Check if specified icon has an available icon in your icon theme

shellPath(path: string): string

Equivalent to ${Quickshell.configDir}/${path}

configPath(path: string): string
Deprecated: Renamed to shellPath() for clarity.
dataPath(path: string): string

Equivalent to ${Quickshell.dataDir}/${path}

statePath(path: string): string

Equivalent to ${Quickshell.stateDir}/${path}

cachePath(path: string): string

Equivalent to ${Quickshell.cacheDir}/${path}

inhibitReloadPopup(): void

When called from reloadCompleted() or reloadFailed(), prevents the default reload popup from displaying.

The popup can also be blocked by setting QS_NO_RELOAD_POPUP=1.

hasVersion(major: int, minor: int, features: list<string>): bool

Check if Quickshell's version is at least major.minor and the listed unreleased features are available. If Quickshell is newer than the given version it is assumed that all unreleased features are present. The unreleased feature list may be omitted.

You can version gate code blocks using Quickshell's preprocessor which

has the same function available.

//@ if hasVersion(0, 3, ["feature"])
...
//@ endif
hasVersion(major: int, minor: int): bool
No upstream description.
hasQtVersion(major: int, minor: int): bool

Check if Qt's version is at least major.minor.

You can version gate code blocks using Quickshell's preprocessor which

has the same function available.

//@ if hasVersion(6, 10)
...
//@ endif

Signals#

lastWindowClosed()handler: onLastWindowClosed

Sent when the last window is closed.

To make the application exit when the last window is closed run Qt.quit().

reloadCompleted()handler: onReloadCompleted

The reload sequence has completed successfully.

reloadFailed(errorString: string)handler: onReloadFailed

The reload sequence has failed.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

  • Prefer shellPath() over hard-coded paths so your config works wherever it's installed.
  • The data/state/cache dirs are per shell id (//@ pragma ShellId), so two different shells never overwrite each other's files.
  • configDir, shellRoot and configPath() are deprecated names for shellDir and shellPath().

See also#

Shell Structure, Pragmas and Reloading · QuickshellSettings · ShellScreen

ShellScreen

provided by Quickshell

Monitor object useful for setting the monitor for a QsWindow

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
ShellScreen → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (ShellScreen can only be obtained via Quickshell.screens). Quickshell gives you instances through: Hyprland.monitorFor, I3.monitorFor, PopupWindow.screen, QsWindow.screen, Quickshell.screens, Toplevel.fullscreenOn, Toplevel.screens, WindowManager.screenProjection, WindowsetProjection.screens, WlSessionLockSurface.screen.

Overview#

A ShellScreen is one connected monitor. You get them from Quickshell.screens and assign them to a window's screen property. All properties are read-only.

From the upstream documentation#

or querying information about the monitor.

If the monitor is disconnected, then any stored copies of its ShellMonitor will

be marked as dangling and all properties will return default values. Reconnecting the monitor will not reconnect it to the ShellMonitor object.

Due to some technical limitations, it was not possible to reuse the native qml Screen type.

Example: using every property#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Scope {
    Variants {
        model: Quickshell.screens
        PanelWindow {
            required property ShellScreen modelData
            screen: modelData
            anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }
            implicitHeight: 30
            color: "#11111b"
            Text {
                anchors.centerIn: parent
                color: "white"
                text: `${modelData.name} · ${modelData.model} · ${modelData.serialNumber}`
                    + ` · ${modelData.width}×${modelData.height} at (${modelData.x},${modelData.y})`
                    + ` · scale ${modelData.devicePixelRatio}`
                    + ` · ${modelData.physicalPixelDensity.toFixed(2)} px/mm physical`
                    + ` · ${modelData.logicalPixelDensity.toFixed(2)} px/mm logical`
                    + ` · orientation ${modelData.orientation} (primary ${modelData.primaryOrientation})`
            }
        }
    }
}

Quickshell

Reloadable

provided by Quickshell

The base class of all types that can be reloaded.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
Reloadable
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (Reloadable is the base class of reloadable types and cannot be created on its own.). Quickshell gives you instances.

Overview#

The base type of objects that take part in hot reloading (Scope, Variants, LazyLoader, windows, PersistentProperties…). You never create it directly; you use its one property on those types.

From the upstream documentation#

Reloadables will attempt to take specific state from previous config revisions if possible. Some examples are ProxyWindowBase and PersistentProperties

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onReloadableIdChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
reloadableIdstringread / write

An additional identifier that can be used to try to match a reloadable object to its previous state.

Simply keeping a stable identifier across config versions (saves) is enough to help the reloader figure out which object in the old revision corresponds to this object in the current revision, and facilitate smoother reloading.

Note that identifiers are scoped, and will try to do the right thing in context. For example if you have a Variants wrapping an object with an identified element inside, a scope is created at the variant level.

Variants {
  // multiple variants of the same object tree
  variants: [ { foo: 1 }, { foo: 2 } ]

  // any non `Reloadable` object
  QtObject {
    FloatingWindow {
      // this FloatingWindow will now be matched to the same one in the previous
      // widget tree for its variant. "myFloatingWindow" refers to both the variant in
      // `foo: 1` and `foo: 2` for each tree.
      reloadableId: "myFloatingWindow"

      // ...
    }
  }
}

Quickshell matches old and new objects across a reload by their position in the tree. If you reorder your config, matching can fail and state is lost. A stable reloadableId makes matching explicit:

PersistentProperties { reloadableId: "sidebar"; property bool open }

Scope

creatable

Scope that propagates reloads to child items in order.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
Scope → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: Scope { … }.
Default property
children — children you write inside Scope { } go here

Overview#

A non-visual container. Windows aren't Items, so they can't be children of a Rectangle; you group them (plus timers, processes, IPC handlers) inside a Scope. Most module files (Bar.qml, Launcher.qml) have a Scope as their root.

From the upstream documentation#

Convenience type equivalent to setting Reloadable.reloadableId for all children.

Note that this does not work for visible Item (all widgets).

`qml ShellRoot { Variants { variants: ...

Scope {
  // everything in here behaves the same as if it was defined
  // directly in Variants reload-wise.
}

} }

Example#

modules/bar/Bar.qmlimport Quickshell
import QtQuick

Scope {
    id: root
    property bool hidden: false          // Scopes can have their own state

    Variants {
        model: Quickshell.screens
        PanelWindow {
            required property ShellScreen modelData
            screen: modelData
            visible: !root.hidden
            anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }
            implicitHeight: 32
        }
    }
    Timer { interval: 5000; running: true; onTriggered: console.log("children:", root.children.length) }
}
