Variants

creatable

Creates instances of a component based on a given model.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
Variants → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: Variants { … }.
Default property
delegate — children you write inside Variants { } go here

Overview#

Variants creates one instance of its delegate per entry in model, and creates or destroys instances as the model changes. It's the standard way to get one bar per monitor. Unlike Repeater, it can create windows and other non-Item objects.

From the upstream documentation#

Creates and destroys instances of the given component when the given property changes.

Variants is similar to Repeater except it is for non Item objects, and acts as a reload scope.

Each non duplicate value passed to model will create a new instance of delegate with a modelData property set to that value.

See Quickshell.screens for an example of using Variants to create copies of a window per screen.

BUG: Variants currently fails to reload children if the variant set is changed as

it is instantiated. (usually due to a mutation during variant creation)

Example: one window per screen, using every property#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Scope {
    Variants {
        id: bars
        model: Quickshell.screens                       // list<var>; each entry becomes modelData
        delegate: PanelWindow {                         // `delegate:` can be omitted (default property)
            required property ShellScreen modelData
            screen: modelData
            anchors { bottom: true; left: true; right: true }
            implicitHeight: 28
            Text { anchors.centerIn: parent; text: modelData.name }
        }
    }
    // instances: the created objects
    Timer { interval: 2000; running: true; onTriggered: console.log("bars:", bars.instances.length) }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onDelegateChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
delegateComponentread / write

The component to create instances of.

The delegate should define a modelData property that will be populated with a value from the model.

modellist<var>read / write

The list of sets of properties to create instances with. Each set creates an instance of the component, which are updated when the input sets update.

Any list. With objects (screens), each instance gets modelData set to the element. With plain JS objects, each key becomes a property of the instance if it exists.

instanceslist<QtObject>read-only

Current instances of the delegate.

Inherited from Reloadable (1 properties)
reloadableIdstringread / write

An additional identifier that can be used to try to match a reloadable object to its previous state.

Simply keeping a stable identifier across config versions (saves) is enough to help the reloader figure out which object in the old revision corresponds to this object in the current revision, and facilitate smoother reloading.

Note that identifiers are scoped, and will try to do the right thing in context. For example if you have a Variants wrapping an object with an identified element inside, a scope is created at the variant level.

Variants {
  // multiple variants of the same object tree
  variants: [ { foo: 1 }, { foo: 2 } ]

  // any non `Reloadable` object
  QtObject {
    FloatingWindow {
      // this FloatingWindow will now be matched to the same one in the previous
      // widget tree for its variant. "myFloatingWindow" refers to both the variant in
      // `foo: 1` and `foo: 2` for each tree.
      reloadableId: "myFloatingWindow"

      // ...
    }
  }
}

Notes, tips and gotchas#

  • Declare required property … modelData in the delegate.
  • Filter screens with a JS expression: model: Quickshell.screens.filter(s => s.name !== "HDMI-A-1").

See also#

Multiple Monitors with Variants

Intersection

enum

Intersection strategy for Regions.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
Intersection
How to get one
This is an enum (a fixed list of named values). You never create it; you compare against or assign its values, e.g. Intersection.Combine.

Overview#

See Region.intersection.

Enum values#

ValueNumberMeaning
Intersection.Combine0

Combine this region, leaving a union of this and the other region. (opposite of Subtract)

Intersection.Subtract1

Subtract this region, cutting this region out of the other. (opposite of Combine)

Intersection.Intersect2

Create an intersection of this region and the other, leaving only the area covered by both. (opposite of Xor)

Intersection.Xor3

Create an intersection of this region and the other, leaving only the area not covered by both. (opposite of Intersect)

Example#

import Quickshell

// compare a value
if (Region.intersection === Intersection.Subtract) console.log("it is Subtract")

// used by: Region.intersection

Region

creatable

A composable region used as a mask.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
Region → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: Region { … }.
Default property
regions — children you write inside Region { } go here

Overview#

A Region describes an area of a window, used for QsWindow.mask (where clicks are accepted), HyprlandWindow.visibleMask and BackgroundEffect.blurRegion. Regions can follow an item's geometry automatically and can be nested and combined.

From the upstream documentation#

See QsWindow.mask.

Example: using every property#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    anchors { top: true; bottom: true; left: true; right: true }
    exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore
    color: "transparent"

    mask: Region {
        item: card                                 // follow this item (overrides x/y/width/height)
        shape: RegionShape.Rect                    // Rect (default) or Ellipse
        radius: 20                                 // rounded corners for Rect
        // per-corner overrides:
        topLeftRadius: 20; topRightRadius: 20; bottomLeftRadius: 4; bottomRightRadius: 4

        Region {                                   // child: add a circle button area
            x: 40; y: 40; width: 60; height: 60    // manual geometry
            shape: RegionShape.Ellipse
            intersection: Intersection.Combine     // Combine | Subtract | Intersect | Xor
        }
        Region {                                   // child: cut a hole out of the card
            item: hole
            intersection: Intersection.Subtract
        }
    }

    Rectangle { id: card; x: 200; y: 200; width: 400; height: 250; radius: 20; color: "#1e1e2e"
        Rectangle { id: hole; x: 150; y: 80; width: 100; height: 80; color: "transparent"; border.color: "red" } }
    Rectangle { x: 40; y: 40; width: 60; height: 60; radius: 30; color: "#cba6f7" }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onShapeChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
shapeRegionShaperead / write

Defaults to Rect.

intersectionIntersectionread / write

The way this region interacts with its parent region. Defaults to Combine.

itemItemread / write

The item that determines the geometry of the region. item overrides x, y, width and height.

xintread / write

Defaults to 0. Does nothing if item is set.

yintread / write

Defaults to 0. Does nothing if item is set.

widthintread / write

Defaults to 0. Does nothing if item is set.

heightintread / write

Defaults to 0. Does nothing if item is set.

radiusintread / write

Corner radius for rounded rectangles. Only applies when shape is Rect. Defaults to 0.

Acts as the default for topLeftRadius, topRightRadius, bottomLeftRadius, and bottomRightRadius.

topLeftRadiusintread / write

Top-left corner radius. Only applies when shape is Rect.

Defaults to radius, and may be reset by assigning undefined.

topRightRadiusintread / write

Top-right corner radius. Only applies when shape is Rect.

Defaults to radius, and may be reset by assigning undefined.

bottomLeftRadiusintread / write

Bottom-left corner radius. Only applies when shape is Rect.

Defaults to radius, and may be reset by assigning undefined.

bottomRightRadiusintread / write

Bottom-right corner radius. Only applies when shape is Rect.

Defaults to radius, and may be reset by assigning undefined.

regionslist<Region>read-only

Regions to apply on top of this region.

Regions can be nested to create a more complex region. For example this will create a square region with a cutout in the middle.

Region {
  width: 100; height: 100;

  Region {
    x: 50; y: 50;
    width: 50; height: 50;
    intersection: Intersection.Subtract
  }
}

Signals#

changed()handler: onChanged

Triggered when the region's geometry changes.

In some cases the region does not update automatically. In those cases you can emit this signal manually.

Enum values#

Enum CornerOverride — values are written Region.Value.

ValueNumberMeaning
Region.TopLeft0b1
Region.TopRight0b10
Region.BottomLeft0b100
Region.BottomRight0b1000

Notes, tips and gotchas#

  • mask: Region {} (empty) makes a window fully click-through.
  • Regions bound to items update when the item moves or resizes, including during animations.

Where this type appears#

  • BackgroundEffect.blurRegion (property)
  • HyprlandWindow.visibleMask (property)
  • QsWindow.mask (property)

Masks, Regions and Click-Through · RegionShape · Intersection

PersistentProperties

creatable

Object that holds properties that can persist across a config reload.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
PersistentProperties → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: PersistentProperties { … }.

Overview#

Holds properties that survive hot reloads. Declare your own properties inside it. Values reset only when Quickshell restarts (for restarts, save to a file with FileView + JsonAdapter).

From the upstream documentation#

PersistentProperties holds properties declated in it across a reload, which is often useful for things like keeping expandable popups open and styling them.

Below is an example of using PersistentProperties to keep track of the state of an expandable panel. When the configuration is reloaded, the expanderOpen property will be saved and the expandable panel will stay in the open/closed state.

PersistentProperties {
  id: persist
  reloadableId: "persistedStates"

  property bool expanderOpen: false
}

Button {
  id: expanderButton
  anchors.centerIn: parent
  text: "toggle expander"
  onClicked: persist.expanderOpen = !persist.expanderOpen
}

Rectangle {
  anchors.top: expanderButton.bottom
  anchors.left: expanderButton.left
  anchors.right: expanderButton.right
  height: 100

  color: "lightblue"
  visible: persist.expanderOpen
}

Example#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Scope {
    PersistentProperties {
        id: persist
        reloadableId: "ui-state"                   // stable id across edits
        property bool sidebarOpen: false
        property int selectedTab: 0
        property string lastQuery: ""

        onLoaded: console.log("ready (every reload)")
        onReloaded: console.log("restored values from the previous config")
    }
    // use: persist.sidebarOpen = true; save a file → value is still true
}

Properties#

Inherited from Reloadable (1 properties)
reloadableIdstringread / write

An additional identifier that can be used to try to match a reloadable object to its previous state.

Simply keeping a stable identifier across config versions (saves) is enough to help the reloader figure out which object in the old revision corresponds to this object in the current revision, and facilitate smoother reloading.

Note that identifiers are scoped, and will try to do the right thing in context. For example if you have a Variants wrapping an object with an identified element inside, a scope is created at the variant level.

Variants {
  // multiple variants of the same object tree
  variants: [ { foo: 1 }, { foo: 2 } ]

  // any non `Reloadable` object
  QtObject {
    FloatingWindow {
      // this FloatingWindow will now be matched to the same one in the previous
      // widget tree for its variant. "myFloatingWindow" refers to both the variant in
      // `foo: 1` and `foo: 2` for each tree.
      reloadableId: "myFloatingWindow"

      // ...
    }
  }
}

Signals#

loaded()handler: onLoaded

Called every time the reload stage completes. Will be called every time, including when nothing was loaded from an old instance.

reloaded()handler: onReloaded

Called every time the properties are reloaded. Will not be called if no old instance was loaded.

QsWindow

provided by Quickshellhas attached properties

Base class of Quickshell windows

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
QsWindow → Reloadable
How to get one
This is an attached type: you use it as QsWindow.property on another object.
Default property
data — children you write inside QsWindow { } go here

Overview#

The common base of PanelWindow, FloatingWindow and PopupWindow. You never create a QsWindow directly, but every window has these properties. From any Item inside a window, the attached property QsWindow.window returns that window.

From the upstream documentation#

Attached properties#

QSWindow can be used as an attached object of anything that subclasses Item. It provides the following properties - window - the QSWindow object. - contentItem - the contentItem property of the window.

itemPosition(), itemRect(), and mapFromItem() can also be called directly on the attached object.

Example: using the shared window properties#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    id: win
    anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }

    // ---- size & visibility ----
    implicitHeight: 40                     // desired size (preferred over width/height)
    visible: true                          // mapped or not
    color: "transparent"                   // background; default WHITE

    // ---- screen ----
    screen: Quickshell.screens[0]

    // ---- input ----
    mask: Region { item: pill }            // only the pill is clickable

    // ---- rendering ----
    surfaceFormat.opaque: false            // request an alpha surface
    updatesEnabled: true                   // false pauses rendering

    Rectangle {
        id: pill
        anchors.centerIn: parent
        width: 200; height: 30; radius: 15; color: "#313244"
        TapHandler {
            onTapped: {
                // read-only info + helpers
                console.log("dpr", win.devicePixelRatio, "backing visible", win.backingWindowVisible)
                console.log("pill rect in window:", win.itemRect(pill), "pos:", win.itemPosition(pill))
                console.log("attached:", pill.QsWindow.window === win)
            }
        }
    }

    onClosed: console.log("compositor closed the window")
    onResourcesLost: console.warn("GPU resources lost")
    onWindowConnected: console.log("surface created")
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onContentItemChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
contentItemItemconstantNo upstream description.
visibleboolread / write

If the window should be shown or hidden. Defaults to true.

backingWindowVisibleboolread-only

If the window is currently shown. You should generally prefer visible.

This property is useful for ensuring windows spawn in a specific order, and you should not use it in place of visible.

implicitWidthintread / write

The window's desired width.

implicitHeightintread / write

The window's desired height.

widthintread / write

The window's actual width.

Setting this property is deprecated. Set implicitWidth instead.

Deprecated for setting: use implicitWidth. Reading it gives the real width.

heightintread / write

The window's actual height.

Setting this property is deprecated. Set implicitHeight instead.

devicePixelRatiorealread-only

The ratio between logical pixels and monitor pixels.

Qt's coordinate system works in logical pixels, which equal N monitor pixels depending on scale factor. This property returns the amount of monitor pixels in a logical pixel for the current window.

screenShellScreenread / write

The screen that the window currently occupies.

This may be modified to move the window to the given screen.

windowTransformQtObjectread-only

Opaque property that will receive an update when factors that affect the window's position and transform changed.

This property is intended to be used to force a binding update, along with map[To|From]Item (which is not reactive).

colorcolorread / write

The background color of the window. Defaults to white.

Watch out

If the window color is opaque before it is made visible, it will not be able to become transparent later unless surfaceFormat is false.

Defaults to white. For rounded or floating designs, set "transparent" and draw a Rectangle inside.

maskRegionread / write

The clickthrough mask. Defaults to null.

If non null then the clickable areas of the window will be determined by the provided region.

ShellWindow {
  // The mask region is set to `rect`, meaning only `rect` is clickable.
  // All other clicks pass through the window to ones behind it.
  mask: Region { item: rect }

  Rectangle {
    id: rect

    anchors.centerIn: parent
    width: 100
    height: 100
  }
}

If the provided region's intersection mode is Combine (the default), then the region will be used as is. Otherwise it will be applied on top of the window region.

For example, setting the intersection mode to Xor will invert the mask and make everything in the mask region not clickable and pass through clicks inside it through the window.

ShellWindow {
  // The mask region is set to `rect`, but the intersection mode is set to `Xor`.
  // This inverts the mask causing all clicks inside `rect` to be passed to the window
  // behind this one.
  mask: Region { item: rect; intersection: Intersection.Xor }

  Rectangle {
    id: rect

    anchors.centerIn: parent
    width: 100
    height: 100
  }
}
surfaceFormatQsSurfaceFormatread / write

Set the surface format to request from the system.

  • opaque - If the requested surface should be opaque. Opaque windows allow the operating system to avoid drawing things behind them, or blending the window with those behind it, saving power and GPU load. If unset, this property defaults to true if color is opaque, or false if not. You should not need to modify this property unless you create a surface that starts opaque and later becomes transparent.
Note

The surface format cannot be changed after the window is created.

updatesEnabledboolread / write

If the window should receive render updates. Defaults to true.

When set to false, the window will not re-render in response to animations or other visual updates from other windows. This is useful for static windows such as wallpapers that do not need to update frequently, saving GPU cycles.

When set back to true, a new frame is rendered, including any changes made while updates were disabled.

datalist<QtObject>read-onlyNo upstream description.
Inherited from Reloadable (1 properties)

An additional identifier that can be used to try to match a reloadable object to its previous state.

Simply keeping a stable identifier across config versions (saves) is enough to help the reloader figure out which object in the old revision corresponds to this object in the current revision, and facilitate smoother reloading.

Note that identifiers are scoped, and will try to do the right thing in context. For example if you have a Variants wrapping an object with an identified element inside, a scope is created at the variant level.

Variants {
  // multiple variants of the same object tree
  variants: [ { foo: 1 }, { foo: 2 } ]

  // any non `Reloadable` object
  QtObject {
    FloatingWindow {
      // this FloatingWindow will now be matched to the same one in the previous
      // widget tree for its variant. "myFloatingWindow" refers to both the variant in
      // `foo: 1` and `foo: 2` for each tree.
      reloadableId: "myFloatingWindow"

      // ...

Functions#

itemPosition(item: Item): point

Returns the given Item's position relative to the window. Does not update reactively.

Equivalent to calling window.contentItem.mapFromItem(item, 0, 0)

See also: Item.mapFromItem()

itemRect(item: Item): rect

Returns the given Item's geometry relative to the window. Does not update reactively.

Equivalent to calling window.contentItem.mapFromItem(item, 0, 0, 0, 0)

See also: Item.mapFromItem()

mapFromItem(item: Item, point: point): point

Maps the given point in the coordinate space of item to one in the coordinate space of this window. Does not update reactively.

Equivalent to calling window.contentItem.mapFromItem(item, point)

See also: Item.mapFromItem()

mapFromItem(item: Item, x: real, y: real): point

Maps the given point in the coordinate space of item to one in the coordinate space of this window. Does not update reactively.

Equivalent to calling window.contentItem.mapFromItem(item, x, y)

See also: Item.mapFromItem()

mapFromItem(item: Item, rect: rect): rect

Maps the given rect in the coordinate space of item to one in the coordinate space of this window. Does not update reactively.

Equivalent to calling window.contentItem.mapFromItem(item, rect)

See also: Item.mapFromItem()

mapFromItem(item: Item, x: real, y: real, width: real, height: real): rect

Maps the given rect in the coordinate space of item to one in the coordinate space of this window. Does not update reactively.

Equivalent to calling window.contentItem.mapFromItem(item, x, y, width, height)

See also: Item.mapFromItem()

Signals#

closed()handler: onClosed

This signal is emitted when the window is closed by the user, the display server, or an error. It is not emitted when visible is set to false.

resourcesLost()handler: onResourcesLost

This signal is emitted when resources a window depends on to display are lost, or could not be acquired during window creation. The most common trigger for this signal is a lack of VRAM when creating or resizing a window.

Following this signal, closed(s) will be sent.

windowConnected()handler: onWindowConnected
No upstream description.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

  • itemRect()/itemPosition() don't update reactively; call them when you need the value, or use windowTransform as a binding dependency.
  • Children you write inside a window go to contentItem, which fills the window.

ValueNumberMeaning
ExclusionMode.Normal0

PanelWindow

creatable

Decorationless window attached to screen edges by anchors.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
PanelWindow → QsWindow → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: PanelWindow { … }.

Overview#

A layer-shell window glued to screen edges: bars, docks, sidebars, OSDs, launchers, notifications, overlays, desktop widgets and wallpapers. The most-used Quickshell type. It also has every QsWindow property (size, color, screen, mask…), and the WlrLayershell attached properties set its layer, namespace and keyboard focus.

From the upstream documentation#

Example

The following snippet creates a white bar attached to the bottom of the screen.

PanelWindow {
  anchors {
    left: true
    bottom: true
    right: true
  }

  Text {
    anchors.centerIn: parent
    text: "Hello!"
  }
}

Example: using every property#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    id: bar
    screen: Quickshell.screens[0]

    anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }    // which screen edges
    margins { top: 6; left: 8; right: 8 }             // distance from anchored edges
    implicitHeight: 36

    exclusiveZone: 42                                  // reserve 42 px (sets mode to Normal-with-zone)
    // exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Auto               // default: reserve the window size
    // exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore             // reserve nothing, overlap other panels
    aboveWindows: true                                 // Top layer (false → Bottom layer)
    focusable: false                                   // take keyboard focus when clicked?

    color: "transparent"
    WlrLayershell.namespace: "quickshell:bar"
    WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Top
    WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.None

    Rectangle { anchors.fill: parent; radius: 12; color: "#cc1e1e2e" }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onAnchorsChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
anchorsAnchorsread / write

Anchors attach a shell window to the sides of the screen. By default all anchors are disabled to avoid blocking the entire screen due to a misconfiguration.

When two opposite anchors are attached at the same time, the corresponding dimension

(width or height) will be forced to equal the screen width/height. Margins can be used to create anchored windows that are also disconnected from the monitor sides.

Four booleans: top, bottom, left, right. Anchoring two opposite edges stretches the window in that direction (no need to set that dimension). No anchors at all centers the window.

marginsMarginsread / write

Offsets from the sides of the screen.

Only applies to edges with anchors
exclusiveZoneintread / write

The amount of space reserved for the shell layer relative to its anchors. Setting this property sets exclusionMode to ExclusionMode.Normal.

Note

Either 1 or 3 anchors are required for the zone to take effect.

Setting it switches to manual reservation. 0 reserves nothing. Animate it together with the bar for smooth auto-hide.

exclusionModeExclusionModeread / write

Defaults to ExclusionMode.Auto.

See ExclusionMode. Use Ignore for overlays, fullscreen click-through windows, OSDs and launchers.

aboveWindowsboolread / write

If the panel should render above standard windows. Defaults to true.

Note: On Wayland this property corresponds to WlrLayershell.layer.

focusableboolread / write

If the panel should accept keyboard focus. Defaults to false.

Note: On Wayland this property corresponds to WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus.

A portable shortcut for keyboard focus on demand. For precise control use WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus.

FloatingWindow

creatable

Standard toplevel operating system window that looks like any other application.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
FloatingWindow → QsWindow → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: FloatingWindow { … }.

Overview#

A normal application window, managed by the compositor like any app (tiled, floated, fullscreened). Use it for settings apps, debug panels, or test windows while developing.

Example: using every property#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

FloatingWindow {
    id: win
    title: "My Shell Settings"                   // window title (match it in window rules)
    implicitWidth: 720; implicitHeight: 480
    minimumSize: Qt.size(400, 300)
    maximumSize: Qt.size(1600, 1200)
    color: "#1e1e2e"
    visible: true

    // state (read and request)
    Text {
        anchors.centerIn: parent; color: "white"
        text: `minimized ${win.minimized} · maximized ${win.maximized} · fullscreen ${win.fullscreen}`
    }
    // custom title bar: drag to move, corner to resize
    Rectangle {
        anchors { top: parent.top; left: parent.left; right: parent.right }
        height: 32; color: "#313244"
        DragHandler { target: null; onActiveChanged: if (active) win.startSystemMove() }
        Text { anchors.right: parent.right; text: " □ "; color: "white"; TapHandler { onTapped: win.maximized = !win.maximized } }
    }
    Rectangle {
        anchors { right: parent.right; bottom: parent.bottom }
        width: 16; height: 16; color: "#585b70"
        DragHandler { target: null; onActiveChanged: if (active) win.startSystemResize(Edges.Bottom | Edges.Right) }
    }
    // parentWindow: someOtherWindow    // make it a child/dialog of another window
}
hyprland.confwindowrule = float, title:^(My Shell Settings)$

maskRegionread / write

The clickthrough mask. Defaults to null.

If non null then the clickable areas of the window will be determined by the provided region.

ShellWindow {
  // The mask region is set to `rect`, meaning only `rect` is clickable.
  // All other clicks pass through the window to ones behind it.
  mask: Region { item: rect }

  Rectangle {
    id: rect

    anchors.centerIn: parent
    width: 100
    height: 100
  }
}

If the provided region's intersection mode is Combine (the default), then the region will be used as is. Otherwise it will be applied on top of the window region.

For example, setting the intersection mode to Xor will invert the mask and make everything in the mask region not clickable and pass through clicks inside it through the window.

ShellWindow {
  // The mask region is set to `rect`, but the intersection mode is set to `Xor`.
  // This inverts the mask causing all clicks inside `rect` to be passed to the window
  // behind this one.
  mask: Region { item: rect; intersection: Intersection.Xor }

  Rectangle {
    id: rect

    anchors.centerIn: parent
    width: 100
    height: 100
  }
}

PopupWindow

creatable

Popup window.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
PopupWindow → QsWindow → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: PopupWindow { … }.

Overview#

A window positioned relative to another window or item: dropdowns, calendars, tray menus, tooltips. Its position is controlled by the PopupAnchor in anchor. It starts hidden (visible: false).

From the upstream documentation#

that can display in a position relative to a floating or panel window.

Example

The following snippet creates a panel with a popup centered over it.

PanelWindow {
  id: toplevel

  anchors {
    bottom: true
    left: true
    right: true
  }

  PopupWindow {
    anchor.window: toplevel
    anchor.rect.x: parentWindow.width / 2 - width / 2
    anchor.rect.y: parentWindow.height
    width: 500
    height: 500
    visible: true
  }
}

Example: using every property#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    id: bar
    anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }
    implicitHeight: 34

    Rectangle {
        id: btn
        anchors.centerIn: parent
        width: 120; height: 26; radius: 13; color: "#313244"
        TapHandler { onTapped: pop.visible = !pop.visible }
    }

    PopupWindow {
        id: pop
        anchor.window: bar                       // parent window (implied by anchor.item)
        anchor.item: btn                         // attach to this item
        anchor.edges: Edges.Bottom               // point on the anchor rect
        anchor.gravity: Edges.Bottom             // grow direction
        anchor.margins.top: 8
        anchor.adjustment: PopupAdjustment.Slide | PopupAdjustment.Flip
        grabFocus: true                          // click outside → closes, visible becomes false
        visible: false
        implicitWidth: 260; implicitHeight: 180
        color: "transparent"
        Rectangle { anchors.fill: parent; radius: 14; color: "#1e1e2e"
            Text { anchors.centerIn: parent; color: "white"; text: "on " + (pop.screen?.name ?? "?") } }
    }
}

import Quickshell

How to get one
You create this type in QML: Singleton { … }.

Overview#

The root type for your own singletons. Put pragma Singleton at the top of a file whose root is Singleton { }, place it in an imported folder, and use it by its file name from anywhere.

From the upstream documentation#

All singletons should inherit from this type.

import Quickshell

    id: root
    property int count: 0
    function increment(): void { count++ }
}
import qs.services
Text { text: Counter.count; TapHandler { onTapped: Counter.increment() } }

Quickshell

LazyLoader

creatable

Asynchronous component loader.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
LazyLoader → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: LazyLoader { … }.
Default property
component — children you write inside LazyLoader { } go here

Overview#

Creates its component only when needed and destroys it when not, which saves memory for panels that are usually closed. It works with windows and any other object, and can pre-load in the background so opening is instant.

From the upstream documentation#

The LazyLoader can be used to prepare components that don't need to be created immediately, such as windows that aren't visible until triggered by another action. It works on creating the component in the gaps between frame rendering to prevent blocking the interface thread. It can also be used to preserve memory by loading components only when you need them and unloading them afterward.

Note that when reloading the UI due to changes, lazy loaders will always load synchronously so windows can be reused.

Example

The following example creates a PopupWindow asynchronously as the bar loads. This means the bar can be shown onscreen before the popup is ready, however trying to show the popup before it has finished loading in the background will cause the UI thread to block.

import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls
import Quickshell

ShellRoot {
  PanelWindow {
    id: window
    height: 50

    anchors {
      bottom: true
      left: true
      right: true
    }

    LazyLoader {
      id: popupLoader

      // start loading immediately
      loading: true

      // this window will be loaded in the background during spare
      // frame time unless active is set to true, where it will be
      // loaded in the foreground
      PopupWindow {
        // position the popup above the button
        parentWindow: window
        relativeX: window.width / 2 - width / 2
        relativeY: -height

        // some heavy component here

        width: 200
        height: 200
      }
    }

    Button {
      anchors.centerIn: parent
      text: "show popup"

      // accessing popupLoader.item will force the loader to
      // finish loading on the UI thread if it isn't finished yet.
      onClicked: popupLoader.item.visible = !popupLoader.item.visible
    }
  }
}
Components that internally load other components must explicitly

support asynchronous loading to avoid blocking.

Notably, Variants does not corrently support asynchronous loading, meaning using it inside a LazyLoader will block similarly to not having a loader to start with.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Scope {
    property bool open: false

    LazyLoader {
        id: loader
        // choose ONE way to control it:
        active: open              // true → load synchronously now; false → destroy
        // activeAsync: open      // true → load in the background, then activate
        // loading: true          // pre-load in the background without showing yet

        // what to load: inline (component) or from a file (source)
        component: PanelWindow {
            implicitWidth: 400; implicitHeight: 300
            Text { anchors.centerIn: parent; text: "I exist only while open" }
        }
        // source: "BigPanel.qml"
    }

    // the created object (null when not loaded)
    Timer { interval: 1000; running: true; repeat: true; onTriggered: console.log("item:", loader.item) }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onItemChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
itemQtObjectread-only

The fully loaded item if the loader is loading or active, or null if neither loading nor active.

Note that the item is owned by the LazyLoader, and destroying the LazyLoader will destroy the item.

Watch out

If you access the item of a loader that is currently loading, it will block as if you had set active to true immediately beforehand.

You can instead set loading and listen to activeChanged(s) signal to ensure loading happens asynchronously.

loadingboolread / write

If the loader is actively loading.

If the component is not loaded, setting this property to true will start loading it asynchronously. If the component is already loaded, setting this property has no effect.

See also: activeAsync.

Setting loading: true starts building in the background; when active later becomes true the object is ready immediately. Combine both: loading: true; active: GlobalStates.launcherOpen.

activeboolread / write

If the component is fully loaded.

Setting this property to true will force the component to load to completion, blocking the UI, and setting it to false will destroy the component, requiring it to be loaded again.

See also: activeAsync.

activeAsyncboolread / write

If the component is fully loaded.

Setting this property to true will asynchronously load the component similarly to loading. Reading it or setting it to false will behanve the same as active.

componentComponentread / write

The component to load. Mutually exclusive to source.

sourcestringread / write

The URI to load the component from. Mutually exclusive to component.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

When active becomes false the object is destroyed immediately, so there's no time for a closing animation. Keep it active while animating: active: open || closeAnim.running.

EasingCurve

creatable

Easing curve.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
EasingCurve → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: EasingCurve { … }.

Overview#

Evaluates an easing curve in JavaScript, so you can apply the same curve as your animations to computed values (for example, mapping a scroll position or a progress value through a curve).

From the upstream documentation#

Directly accessible easing curve as used in property animations.

Example#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Item {
    EasingCurve {
        id: curve
        curve.type: Easing.OutCubic               // same options as an animation's `easing`
    }
    property real progress: 0.3                    // 0..1, e.g. from a drag
    readonly property real eased: curve.valueAt(progress)
    readonly property real x2: curve.interpolate(progress, 0, 300)                       // number
    readonly property point p: curve.interpolate(progress, Qt.point(0, 0), Qt.point(100, 50))   // point
    readonly property rect r: curve.interpolate(progress, Qt.rect(0, 0, 10, 10), Qt.rect(50, 50, 200, 100))
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onCurveChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
curveQEasingCurveread / write

Easing curve settings. Works exactly the same as PropertyAnimation.easing.

Functions#

valueAt(x: real): real

Returns the Y value for the given X value on the curve from 0.0 to 1.0.

interpolate(x: real, a: real, b: real): real

Interpolates between two values using the given X coordinate.

interpolate(x: real, a: point, b: point): point

Interpolates between two points using the given X coordinate.

TransformWatcher

creatable

Monitor of all geometry changes between two objects.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
TransformWatcher → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: TransformWatcher { … }.

Overview#

Notifies you whenever the geometry relationship between two items changes, including when any ancestor moves, resizes or transforms. Useful when something must track another item's position across different parts of the tree (e.g. an indicator following a button inside a moving panel).

From the upstream documentation#

The TransformWatcher monitors all properties that affect the geometry of two Item relative to eachother.

The algorithm responsible for determining the relationship

between a and b is biased towards a being a parent of b, or a being closer to the common parent of a and b than b.

Example#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Item {
    TransformWatcher {
        id: watcher
        a: buttonInBar             // item A
        b: overlayRoot             // item B
        commonParent: null         // optional optimization if you know one
    }
    Rectangle {
        // re-evaluates whenever watcher.transform changes
        readonly property point p: { watcher.transform; return buttonInBar.mapToItem(overlayRoot, 0, 0) }
        x: p.x; y: p.y; width: 10; height: 10; color: "red"
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onAChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
aItemread / writeNo upstream description.
bItemread / writeNo upstream description.
commonParentItemread / write

Known common parent of both a and b. Defaults to null.

This property can be used to optimize the algorithm that figures out the relationship between a and b. Setting it to something that is not a common parent of both a and b will prevent the path from being determined correctly, and setting it to null will disable the optimization.

transformQtObjectread-only

This property is updated whenever the geometry of any item in the path from a to b changes.

Its value is undefined, and is intended to trigger an expression update.

BoundComponent

creatable

Component loader that allows setting initial properties.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
BoundComponent → Item
How to get one
You create this type in QML: BoundComponent { … }.

Overview#

Like a Loader, but properties you declare on the BoundComponent are passed to the loaded object and (by default) kept bound. Handy for loading a component from a file and feeding it properties without wiring each one by hand.

From the upstream documentation#

, primarily useful for escaping cyclic dependency errors.

Properties defined on the BoundComponent will be applied to its loaded component, including required properties, and will remain reactive. Functions created with the names of signal handlers will also be attached to signals of the loaded component.

MouseArea {
  required property color color;
  width: 100
  height: 100

  Rectangle {
    anchors.fill: parent
    color: parent.color
  }
}
BoundComponent {
  source: "MyComponent.qml"

  // this is the same as assigning to `color` on MyComponent if loaded normally.
  property color color: "red";

  // this will be triggered when the `clicked` signal from the MouseArea is sent.
  function onClicked() {
    color = "blue";
  }
}

Example#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

BoundComponent {
    source: "Card.qml"                // or sourceComponent: Component { … }
    bindValues: true                  // keep the values below bound (default)
    property string title: "Hello"    // passed to Card's `title`
    property color accent: "#cba6f7"  // passed to Card's `accent`
    onLoaded: console.log("loaded", item, "size", implicitWidth, implicitHeight)
}

ObjectModel

provided by Quickshell

View into a list of objets

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
ObjectModel → QAbstractListModel
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (ObjectModels cannot be created directly.). Quickshell gives you instances through: Bluetooth.adapters, Bluetooth.devices, BluetoothAdapter.devices, DesktopEntries.applications, Hyprland.monitors, Hyprland.toplevels, Hyprland.workspaces, HyprlandWorkspace.toplevels, I3.monitors, I3.workspaces, Mpris.players, NetworkDevice.networks.

Overview#

Quickshell's live list type. Service lists like Hyprland.workspaces, Mpris.players, SystemTray.items, Pipewire.nodes and DesktopEntries.applications are ObjectModels. Give them directly to a Repeater/ListView/Variants, or read .values as a JS array.

From the upstream documentation#

Typed view into a list of objects.

An ObjectModel works as a QML Data Model, allowing efficient interaction with components that act on models. It has a single role named modelData, to match the behavior of lists. The same information contained in the list model is available as a normal list via the values property.

Differences from a list

Unlike with a list, the following property binding will never be updated when model[3] changes.

// will not update reactively
property var foo: model[3]

You can work around this limitation using the values property of the model to view it as a list.

// will update reactively
property var foo: model.values[3]

Example#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Mpris
import QtQuick

Column {
    Repeater {                                    // 1. as a model: delegates get modelData
        model: Mpris.players
        Text { required property MprisPlayer modelData; text: modelData.identity }
    }
    Text {                                        // 2. as an array
        text: "playing: " + Mpris.players.values.filter(p => p.isPlaying).length
    }
    Connections {                                 // 3. per-item change signals
        target: Mpris.players
        function onObjectInsertedPost(obj, index) { console.log("added", obj.identity, "at", index) }
        function onObjectRemovedPre(obj, index) { console.log("removing", obj.identity) }
    }
    Component.onCompleted: console.log("index of first:", Mpris.players.indexOf(Mpris.players.values[0]))
}

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onValuesChanged: …).

valueslist<QtObject>read-only

The content of the object model, as a QML list. The values of this property will always be of the type of the model.

No upstream description.

Sent immediately before an object is inserted into the list.

Sent immediately after an object is inserted into the list.

ElapsedTimer

creatable

Measures time between events

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
ElapsedTimer → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: ElapsedTimer { … }.

Overview#

Measures elapsed time precisely, like a stopwatch. Starts when created.

From the upstream documentation#

The ElapsedTimer measures time since its last restart, and is useful for determining the time between events that don't supply it.

Example: every function#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Item {
    ElapsedTimer { id: sw }
    TapHandler {
        onTapped: {
            console.log("seconds:", sw.elapsed())       // real, nanosecond precision
            console.log("ms:", sw.elapsedMs())
            console.log("ns:", sw.elapsedNs())
            const lap = sw.restart()                     // returns elapsed seconds, then restarts
            // restartMs() / restartNs() return ms / ns
            console.log("lap:", lap)
        }
    }
}

Functions#

elapsed(): real

Return the number of seconds since the timer was last started or restarted, with nanosecond precision.

restart(): real

Restart the timer, returning the number of seconds since the timer was last started or restarted, with nanosecond precision.

elapsedMs(): int

Return the number of milliseconds since the timer was last started or restarted.

restartMs(): int

Restart the timer, returning the number of milliseconds since the timer was last started or restarted.

elapsedNs(): int

Return the number of nanoseconds since the timer was last started or restarted.

restartNs(): int

Restart the timer, returning the number of nanoseconds since the timer was last started or restarted.

DesktopEntry

provided by Quickshell

A desktop entry. See DesktopEntries for details.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
DesktopEntry → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (DesktopEntry instances must be retrieved from DesktopEntries). Quickshell gives you instances through: DesktopEntries.applications, DesktopEntries.byId, DesktopEntries.heuristicLookup.

Overview#

One installed application, read from a .desktop file. Get entries from DesktopEntries: the applications list, byId() or heuristicLookup().

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Widgets
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Layouts

ColumnLayout {
    readonly property DesktopEntry e: DesktopEntries.heuristicLookup("firefox")
    visible: e !== null
    IconImage { implicitSize: 48; source: Quickshell.iconPath(e?.icon ?? "", "application-x-executable") }
    Text { text: "id: " + e?.id }                         // "firefox" (file name without .desktop)
    Text { text: "name: " + e?.name }                     // "Firefox"
    Text { text: "genericName: " + e?.genericName }       // "Web Browser"
    Text { text: "comment: " + e?.comment }
    Text { text: "icon: " + e?.icon }
    Text { text: "startupClass: " + e?.startupClass }     // window class/app id it will use
    Text { text: "noDisplay: " + e?.noDisplay }
    Text { text: "runInTerminal: " + e?.runInTerminal }
    Text { text: "categories: " + e?.categories.join(", ") }
    Text { text: "keywords: " + e?.keywords.join(", ") }
    Text { text: "execString: " + e?.execString }         // raw Exec= line (don't run it directly)
    Text { text: "command: " + JSON.stringify(e?.command) } // parsed argv, safe to run
    Text { text: "workingDirectory: " + e?.workingDirectory }
    Repeater { model: e?.actions ?? []; Text { required property DesktopAction modelData; text: "action: " + modelData.name } }
    Text { text: "[launch]"; TapHandler { onTapped: e.execute() } }
}

If true, this application should not be displayed in menus and launchers.

Note

The Exec line parsed into a list, with field codes (%u, %F…) removed. Run it with Quickshell.execDetached(entry.command) or put a terminal in front when runInTerminal is true.

import Quickshell

    Text { text: "heuristic('Code'): " + (DesktopEntries.heuristicLookup("Code")?.name ?? "none") } // fuzzy: matches window classes
    ListView {
        width: 300; height: 300; clip: true
        model: DesktopEntries.applications
        delegate: Text { required property DesktopEntry modelData; text: modelData.name }

Functions#

byId(id: string): DesktopEntry

Look up a desktop entry by name. Includes NoDisplay entries. May return null.

While this function requires an exact match, heuristicLookup() will correctly find an entry more often and is generally more useful.

heuristicLookup(name: string): DesktopEntry

Look up a desktop entry by name using heuristics. Unlike byId(), if no exact matches are found this function will try to guess - potentially incorrectly. May return null.

Use it to map a window's app id or class to its desktop entry (icons in docks, taskbars and overviews). It tries exact ids, StartupWMClass and case-insensitive matches.

Repeater {
    model: opener.children

        required property QsMenuEntry modelData
        visible: !modelData.isSeparator                       // separators: draw a line instead
        opacity: modelData.enabled ? 1 : 0.4
        Image { source: modelData.icon; width: 16; height: 16; visible: modelData.icon !== "" }
        Text { text: modelData.text.replace(/_/g, "") }
        Text {                                                // checkbox / radio state
            visible: modelData.buttonType !== QsMenuButtonType.None
            text: modelData.checkState === Qt.Checked ? "☑" : "☐"
        }
        Text { visible: modelData.hasChildren; text: "›" }    // submenu: open another QsMenuOpener with menu: modelData
        TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.triggered() }
        // native submenu instead: modelData.display(window, x, y)
    }
}

Retainable

provided by Quickshellhas attached properties

Attached object for types that can have delayed destruction.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
Retainable → QtObject
How to get one
This is an attached type: you use it as Retainable.property on another object.

Overview#

Some objects (notably notifications) can be retained: kept alive briefly after they would normally be destroyed, so you can animate them out. Retainable is attached to such objects: notification.Retainable.lock(). Usually RetainableLock is more convenient.

From the upstream documentation#

Retainable works as an attached property that allows objects to be kept around (retained) after they would normally be destroyed, which is especially useful for things like exit transitions.

An object that is retainable will have Retainable as an attached property. All retainable objects will say that they are retainable on their respective typeinfo pages.

Working directly with Retainable is often overly complicated and

error prone. For this reason RetainableLock should usually be used instead.

Example#

NotificationCard {
    required property Notification notif
    Component.onCompleted: notif.Retainable.lock()                      // keep alive
    Connections {
        target: notif.Retainable
        function onDropped() { fadeOut.start() }                        // it would be destroyed now
        function onAboutToDestroy() { console.log("gone") }
    }
    SequentialAnimation {
        id: fadeOut
        NumberAnimation { target: card; property: "opacity"; to: 0; duration: 200 }
        ScriptAction { script: notif.Retainable.unlock() }              // allow destruction
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onRetainedChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
retainedboolread-only

If the object is currently in a retained state.

Functions#

lock(): void

Hold a lock on the object so it cannot be destroyed.

A counter is used to ensure you can lock the object from multiple places and it will not be unlocked until the same number of unlocks as locks have occurred.

Watch out

It is easy to forget to unlock a locked object. Doing so will create what is effectively a memory leak.

Using RetainableLock is recommended as it will help avoid this scenario and make misuse more obvious.

unlock(): void

Remove a lock on the object. See lock() for more information.

forceUnlock(): void

Forcibly remove all locks, destroying the object.

unlock() should usually be preferred.

Signals#

dropped()handler: onDropped

This signal is sent when the object would normally be destroyed.

If all signal handlers return and no locks are in place, the object will be destroyed. If at least one lock is present the object will be retained until all are removed.

aboutToDestroy()handler: onAboutToDestroy

This signal is sent immediately before the object is destroyed. At this point destruction cannot be interrupted.

Quickshell

RetainableLock

creatable

A helper for easily using Retainable.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
RetainableLock → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: RetainableLock { … }.

Overview#

A declarative way to retain an object: while locked is true, the object isn't destroyed even after it's closed, giving you time for an exit animation.

From the upstream documentation#

A RetainableLock provides extra safety and ease of use for locking Retainable objects. A retainable object can be locked by multiple locks at once, and each lock re-exposes relevant properties of the retained objects.

Example

The code below will keep a retainable object alive for as long as the RetainableLock exists.

RetainableLock {
  object: aRetainableObject
  locked: true
}

Example#

Item {
    id: card
    required property Notification notif
    RetainableLock {
        id: lock
        object: card.notif
        locked: true
        onDropped: exit.start()               // notification closed: animate out
    }
    NumberAnimation { id: exit; target: card; property: "opacity"; to: 0; duration: 250
                      onFinished: lock.locked = false }      // now it may be destroyed
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onObjectChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
objectQtObjectread / write

The object to lock. Must be Retainable.

lockedboolread / write

If the object should be locked.

retainedboolread-only

If the object is currently in a retained state.

Signals#

Rebroadcast of the object's Retainable.dropped(s).

Rebroadcast of the object's Retainable.aboutToDestroy(s).

import Quickshell
Inherits
PopupAnchor → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself. Quickshell gives you instances through: PopupWindow.anchor, QsMenuAnchor.anchor.

Overview#

The positioning group used by PopupWindow.anchor and QsMenuAnchor.anchor. It describes an anchor rectangle (an item, or a rect inside a window), which point of it to attach to (edges), which way to grow (gravity), and how to adjust when the popup doesn't fit.

Example: every property#

PopupWindow {
    id: pop
    anchor.window: bar                         // the parent window
    anchor.item: button                        // the rect becomes the button's geometry (sets window too)
    anchor.rect.x: 0                           // or a manual rect relative to item/window
    anchor.rect.y: 0
    anchor.rect.width: button.width
    anchor.rect.height: button.height
    anchor.margins { top: 6; bottom: 6; left: 0; right: 0 }   // grow/shrink the rect
    anchor.edges: Edges.Bottom | Edges.Left    // attach at the bottom-left corner of the rect
    anchor.gravity: Edges.Bottom | Edges.Right // and extend down and to the right
    anchor.adjustment: PopupAdjustment.Slide | PopupAdjustment.Flip
    anchor.onAnchoring: { /* last chance to tweak anchor.rect before positioning */ }
    implicitWidth: 200; implicitHeight: 100
}
// if the anchor item moved without a property change: pop.anchor.updateAnchor()

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onWindowChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
windowQtObjectread / write

The window to anchor / attach the popup to. Setting this property unsets item.

itemItemread / write

The item to anchor / attach the popup to. Setting this property unsets window.

The popup's position relative to its parent window is only calculated when it is initially shown (directly before anchoring(s) is emitted), meaning its anchor rectangle will be set relative to the item's position in the window at that time. updateAnchor() can be called to update the anchor rectangle if the item's position has changed.

Note

If a more flexible way to position a popup relative to an item is needed, set window to the item's parent window, and handle the anchoring signal to position the popup relative to the window's contentItem.

rectBoxread / write

The anchorpoints the popup will attach to, relative to item or window. Which anchors will be used is determined by the edges, gravity, and adjustment.

If using item, the default anchor rectangle matches the dimensions of the item.

If you leave edges, gravity and adjustment at their default values, setting more than x and y does not matter. The anchor rect cannot be smaller than 1x1 pixels.

marginsMarginsread / write

A margin applied to the anchor rect.

This is most useful when item is used and rect is left at its default value (matching the Item's dimensions).

edgesEdgesread / write

The point on the anchor rectangle the popup should anchor to. Opposing edges suchs as Edges.Left | Edges.Right are not allowed.

Defaults to Edges.Top | Edges.Left.

gravityEdgesread / write

The direction the popup should expand towards, relative to the anchorpoint. Opposing edges suchs as Edges.Left | Edges.Right are not allowed.

Defaults to Edges.Bottom | Edges.Right.

adjustmentPopupAdjustmentread / write

The strategy used to adjust the popup's position if it would otherwise not fit on screen, based on the anchor rect, preferred edges, and gravity.

See the documentation for PopupAdjustment for details.

Functions#

updateAnchor(): void

Update the popup's anchor rect relative to its parent window.

If anchored to an item, popups anchors will not automatically follow the item if its position changes. This function can be called to recalculate the anchors.

Signals#

anchoring()handler: onAnchoring

Emitted when this anchor is about to be used. Mostly useful for modifying the anchor rect using coordinate mapping functions, which are not reactive.

Where this type appears#

  • PopupWindow.anchor (property)
  • QsMenuAnchor.anchor (property)

See also#

Popups, Anchors and Menus · Edges · PopupAdjustment

SystemClock

creatable

System clock accessor.

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
SystemClock → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: SystemClock { … }.

Overview#

A clock that updates exactly on second, minute or hour boundaries, and only as often as you need. It's better than a Timer for any displayed time.

From the upstream documentation#

SystemClock is a view into the system's clock. It updates at hour, minute, or second intervals depending on precision.

Examples

SystemClock {
  id: clock
  precision: SystemClock.Seconds
}

@@QtQuick.Text {
  text: Qt.formatDateTime(clock.date, "hh:mm:ss - yyyy-MM-dd")
}
Watch out

Clock updates will trigger within 50ms of the system clock changing, however this can be either before or after the clock changes (+-50ms). If you need a date object, use date instead of constructing a new one, or the time of the constructed object could be off by up to a second.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Column {
    SystemClock {
        id: clock
        precision: SystemClock.Seconds     // Seconds | Minutes | Hours
        enabled: true                      // false pauses updates
    }
    Text { text: Qt.formatDateTime(clock.date, "dddd d MMMM yyyy, hh:mm:ss") }
    Text { text: `${clock.hours}h ${clock.minutes}m ${clock.seconds}s` }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onEnabledChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
enabledboolread / write

If the clock should update. Defaults to true.

Setting enabled to false pauses the clock.

precisionSystemClockread / write

The precision the clock should measure at. Defaults to SystemClock.Seconds.

Use Minutes unless you display seconds: the shell wakes 60× less often.

datedateread-only

The current date and time.

You can use Qt.formatDateTime() to get the time as a string in

your format of choice.

hoursintread-only

The current hour.

minutesintread-only

The current minute, or 0 if precision is SystemClock.Hours.

0 when precision is Hours.

secondsintread-only

The current second, or 0 if precision is SystemClock.Hours or SystemClock.Minutes.

0 when precision is Minutes or Hours.

SystemClock.Hours1
SystemClock.Minutes2
SystemClock.Seconds3

Timers, Dates and Time

Quickshell

ScriptModel

creatable

QML model reflecting a javascript expression

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
ScriptModel → QAbstractListModel
How to get one
You create this type in QML: ScriptModel { … }.

Overview#

A model built from a JavaScript array that diffs each new array against the previous one, so views keep existing delegates and animate only real insertions and removals. Use it for filtered or sorted lists.

From the upstream documentation#

ScriptModel is a QML Data Model that generates model operations based on changes to a javascript expression attached to values.

When should I use this#

ScriptModel should be used when you would otherwise use a javascript expression as a model, QAbstractItemModel is accepted, and the data is likely to change over the lifetime of the program.

When directly using a javascript expression as a model, types like Repeater or ListView will destroy all created delegates, and re-create the entire list. In the case of ListView this will also prevent animations from working. If you wrap your expression with ScriptModel, only new items will be created, and ListView animations will work as expected.

Example#

// Will cause all delegates to be re-created every time filterText changes.
@@QtQuick.Repeater {
  model: myList.filter(entry => entry.name.startsWith(filterText))
  delegate: // ...
}

// Will add and remove delegates only when required.
@@QtQuick.Repeater {
  model: ScriptModel {
    values: myList.filter(entry => entry.name.startsWith(filterText))
  }

  delegate: // ...
}

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

ListView {
    width: 300; height: 400; clip: true
    model: ScriptModel {
        values: DesktopEntries.applications.values
                    .filter(a => a.name.toLowerCase().includes(search.text.toLowerCase()))
                    .sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name))
        comparisonMode: ObjectComparison.Identity       // objects: same reference = same item (fast)
        // objectProp: "id"                              // plain JS objects: compare by this key
    }
    delegate: Text { required property DesktopEntry modelData; text: modelData.name }
    add: Transition { NumberAnimation { property: "opacity"; from: 0; to: 1; duration: 150 } }
    remove: Transition { NumberAnimation { property: "opacity"; to: 0; duration: 150 } }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onValuesChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
valueslist<var>read / write

The list of values to reflect in the model.

Watch out

ScriptModel currently only works with lists of unique values. There must not be any duplicates in the given list, or behavior of the model is undefined.

Tip

ObjectModel supplied by Quickshell types will only contain unique values, and can be used like so:

ScriptModel {
  values: DesktopEntries.applications.values.filter(...)
}

Note that we are using ObjectModel.values because it will cause ScriptModel.values to receive an update on change.

Most lists exposed by Quickshell are read-only. Some operations like sort()

act on a list in-place and cannot be used directly on a list exposed by Quickshell. You can copy a list using spread syntax: [...variable] instead of variable.

For example:

ScriptModel {
  values: [...DesktopEntries.applications.values].sort(...)
}
objectPropstringread / write

The property that javascript objects passed into the model will be compared with.

For example, if objectProp is "myprop" then { myprop: "a", other: "y" } and { myprop: "a", other: "z" } will be considered equal.

Defaults to "", meaning no key.

comparisonModeObjectComparisonread / write

How values should be compared. Defaults to ObjectComparison.Structure.

Identity based comparison is faster if usable for a given model, and often achievable with objectProp.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

Values must be unique. For lists of plain objects (parsed JSON), set objectProp to a unique key.

See also#

ObjectModel and ScriptModel · ObjectComparison

creatable

Color Quantization Utility

Import
import Quickshell
Inherits
ColorQuantizer
How to get one
You create this type in QML: ColorQuantizer { … }.

Overview#

Extracts the dominant colors of an image, in-process. Use it to tint a media card with album art colors or make accents from a wallpaper without external tools.

From the upstream documentation#

A color quantization utility used for getting prevalent colors in an image, by averaging out the image's color data recursively.

Example

ColorQuantizer {
  id: colorQuantizer
  source: Qt.resolvedUrl("./yourImage.png")
  depth: 3 // Will produce 8 colors (2³)
  rescaleSize: 64 // Rescale to 64x64 for faster processing
}

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import QtQuick

Row {
    ColorQuantizer {
        id: q
        source: "file:///home/me/Pictures/wall.jpg"   // or Media.active.trackArtUrl
        depth: 3                                      // 2^3 = up to 8 colors
        rescaleSize: 64                               // shrink first for speed (0 = no scaling)
        imageRect: Qt.rect(0, 0, 500, 500)            // optional crop; undefined = whole image
    }
    Repeater {
        model: q.colors                               // list<color> results
        Rectangle { required property color modelData; width: 32; height: 32; color: modelData }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onColorsChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
colorslist<color>read-only

Access the colors resulting from the color quantization performed.

The amount of colors returned from the quantization is determined by

the property depth, specifically 2ⁿ where n is the depth.

sourceurlread / write

Path to the image you'd like to run the color quantization on.

depthrealread / write

Max depth for the color quantization. Each level of depth represents another binary split of the color space

imageRectrectread / write

Rectangle that the source image is cropped to.

Can be set to undefined to reset.

rescaleSizerealread / write

The size to rescale the image to, when rescaleSize is 0 then no scaling will be done.

Results from color quantization doesn't suffer much when rescaling, it's

recommended to rescale, otherwise the quantization process will take much longer.

Functions#

operationFinished(result: list<color>): void
No upstream description.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

Results arrive asynchronously; bind to colors and provide a fallback (q.colors[0] ?? Colors.primary).

You create this type in QML: SplitParser { … }.

Overview#

Splits a stream into chunks at a delimiter (default newline) and emits read(chunk) for each. Best for long-running commands that print events line by line.

From the upstream documentation#

DataStreamParser.read(s) is emitted once per delimited chunk of the stream.

Example#

Process {
    command: ["sh", "-c", "for i in 1 2 3; do echo tick $i; sleep 1; done"]
    running: true
    stdout: SplitParser {
        splitMarker: "\n"                 // any string; "" = emit whatever arrives
        onRead: chunk => console.log("got:", chunk)
    }
}

import Quickshell

    connected: true                                   // connect now (set false to disconnect)
    parser: SplitParser { onRead: line => console.log("event:", line) }

SocketServer

creatable

Import
import Quickshell.Io
Inherits
SocketServer → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: SocketServer { … }.

Overview#

Creates a Unix socket server. Each client connection creates a Socket from the handler component.

From the upstream documentation#

Example

SocketServer {
  active: true
  path: "/path/too/socket.sock"
  handler: Socket {
    onConnectedChanged: {
      console.log(connected ? "new connection!" : "connection dropped!")
    }
    parser: SplitParser {
      onRead: message => console.log(`read message from socket: ${message}`)
    }
  }
}

Example#

SocketServer {
    active: true
    path: Quickshell.env("XDG_RUNTIME_DIR") + "/myshell.sock"
    handler: Socket {
        parser: SplitParser {
            onRead: cmd => {
                if (cmd === "toggle") GlobalStates.launcherOpen = !GlobalStates.launcherOpen
            }
        }
    }
}
echo toggle | socat - UNIX-CONNECT:$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/myshell.sock

activeboolread / write

If the socket server is currently active. Defaults to false.

Setting this to false will destroy all active connections and delete the socket file on disk.

If path is empty setting this property will have no effect.

pathstringread / write

The path to create the socket server at.

Setting this property while the server is active will have no effect.

handlerComponentread / write

Connection handler component. Must create a Socket.

The created socket should not set connected or path or the incoming socket connection will be dropped (they will be set by the socket server.) Setting connected to false on the created socket after connection will close and delete it.

Inherited from Reloadable (1 properties)
reloadableIdstringread / write

An additional identifier that can be used to try to match a reloadable object to its previous state.

Simply keeping a stable identifier across config versions (saves) is enough to help the reloader figure out which object in the old revision corresponds to this object in the current revision, and facilitate smoother reloading.

Note that identifiers are scoped, and will try to do the right thing in context. For example if you have a Variants wrapping an object with an identified element inside, a scope is created at the variant level.

Variants {
  // multiple variants of the same object tree
  variants: [ { foo: 1 }, { foo: 2 } ]

  // any non `Reloadable` object
  QtObject {
    FloatingWindow {
      // this FloatingWindow will now be matched to the same one in the previous
      // widget tree for its variant. "myFloatingWindow" refers to both the variant in
      // `foo: 1` and `foo: 2` for each tree.
      reloadableId: "myFloatingWindow"

      // ...
    }
  }
}

Process

creatable
