Import
import Quickshell.Io
Inherits
Process
How to get one
You create this type in QML: Process { … }.

Overview#

Runs an external program asynchronously and gives you its output. It's the way to use any command-line tool from your shell: brightnessctl, nmcli, curl, your own scripts.

From the upstream documentation#

Example

Process {
  running: true
  command: [ "some-command", "arg" ]
  stdout: @@StdioCollector {
    onStreamFinished: console.log(`line read: ${this.text}`)
  }
}

Example: every property, function and signal#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Scope {
    id: root
    property string out: ""

    Process {
        id: proc
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo hello $NAME; echo oops >&2; read line; echo got $line"]
        workingDirectory: Quickshell.env("HOME")           // cwd
        environment: ({ NAME: "rice", LANG: "C" })          // extra vars (null value = unset)
        clearEnvironment: false                             // true = start from an empty env
        stdinEnabled: true                                  // allow write()
        running: false                                      // true starts it

        stdout: SplitParser { onRead: line => console.log("stdout:", line) }
        stderr: StdioCollector { onStreamFinished: console.warn("stderr:", text) }

        onStarted: { console.log("pid", processId); write("from-qml\n") }
        onExited: (code, status) => console.log("exit code", code, "status", status)
    }

    Timer {
        interval: 1000; running: true
        onTriggered: proc.running = true                    // start
    }
    // other functions:
    //   proc.signal(15)                 send SIGTERM (or any signal number)
    //   proc.startDetached()            run a copy that outlives Quickshell
    //   proc.exec(["ls", "-la"])        stop current run and start this command now
    //   proc.running = false            kill it
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onRunningChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
runningboolread / write

If the process is currently running. Defaults to false.

Setting this property to true will start the process if command has at least one element. Setting it to false will send SIGTERM. To immediately kill the process, use signal() with SIGKILL. The process will be killed when quickshell dies.

If you want to run the process in a loop, use the onRunningChanged signal handler to restart the process.

Process {
  running: true
  onRunningChanged: if (!running) running = true
}
See startDetached() to prevent the process from being killed by Quickshell

if Quickshell is killed or the configuration is reloaded.

Becomes false when the program exits. To run the same command again, set it to true again (for example from a Timer).

processIdvarread-only

The process ID of the running process or null if running is false.

commandlist<string>read / write

The command to execute. Each argument is its own string, which means you don't have to deal with quoting anything.

If the process is already running changing this property will affect the next started process. If the property has been changed after starting a process it will return the new value, not the one for the currently running process.

This does not run command in a shell. All arguments to the command

must be in separate values in the list, e.g. ["echo", "hello"] and not ["echo hello"].

Additionally, shell scripts must be run by your shell, e.g. ["sh", "script.sh"] instead of ["script.sh"] unless the script has a shebang.

You can use ["sh", "-c", <your command>] to execute your command with

the system shell.

A list: program first, then each argument. It isn't run through a shell, so no quoting is needed, but pipes and $VARS need ["sh", "-c", "…"].

workingDirectorystringread / write

The working directory of the process. Defaults to quickshell's working directory.

If the process is already running changing this property will affect the next started process. If the property has been changed after starting a process it will return the new value, not the one for the currently running process.

environmentQVariantHashread / write

Environment of the executed process.

This is a javascript object (json). Environment variables can be added by setting them to a string and removed by setting them to null (except when clearEnvironment is true, in which case this behavior is inverted, see clearEnvironment for details).

environment: ({
  ADDED: "value",
  REMOVED: null,
  "i'm different": "value",
})
Note

You need to wrap the returned object in () otherwise it won't parse due to javascript ambiguity.

If the process is already running changing this property will affect the next started process. If the property has been changed after starting a process it will return the new value, not the one for the currently running process.

clearEnvironmentboolread / write

If the process's environment should be cleared prior to applying environment. Defaults to false.

If true, all environment variables will be removed before the environment object is applied, meaning the variables listed will be the only ones visible to the process. This changes the behavior of null to pass in the system value of the variable if present instead of removing it.

clearEnvironment: true
environment: ({
  ADDED: "value",
  PASSED_FROM_SYSTEM: null,
})

If the process is already running changing this property will affect the next started process. If the property has been changed after starting a process it will return the new value, not the one for the currently running process.

stdoutDataStreamParserread / write

The parser for stdout. If the parser is null the process's stdout channel will be closed and no further data will be read, even if a new parser is attached.

stderrDataStreamParserread / write

The parser for stderr. If the parser is null the process's stdout channel will be closed and no further data will be read, even if a new parser is attached.

stdinEnabledboolread / write

If stdin is enabled. Defaults to false. If this property is false the process's stdin channel will be closed and write() will do nothing, even if set back to true.

Functions#

exec(context: ProcessContext): void

Launch a process with the given arguments, stopping any currently running process.

The context parameter can either be a list of command arguments or a JS object with the following fields: - command: A list containing the command and all its arguments. See Process.command. - environment: Changes to make to the process environment. See Process.environment. - clearEnvironment: Removes all variables from the environment if true. - workingDirectory: The working directory the command should run in.

Passed parameters will change the values currently set in the process.

This does not run command in a shell. All arguments to the command

must be in separate values in the list, e.g. ["echo", "hello"] and not ["echo hello"].

Additionally, shell scripts must be run by your shell, e.g. ["sh", "script.sh"] instead of ["script.sh"] unless the script has a shebang.

You can use ["sh", "-c", <your command>] to execute your command with

the system shell.

Calling this function is equivalent to running:

process.running = false;
process.command = ...
process.environment = ...
process.clearEnvironment = ...
process.workingDirectory = ...
process.running = true;

Accepts a command list (or a context object with command, environment, workingDirectory…). Stops any current run first.

signal(signal: int): void

Sends a signal to the process if running is true, otherwise does nothing.

write(data: string): void

Writes to the process's stdin. Does nothing if running is false.

startDetached(): void

Launches an instance of the process detached from Quickshell.

The subprocess will not be tracked, running will be false, and the subprocess will not be killed by Quickshell.

This function is equivalent to Quickshell.execDetached().

Signals#

started()handler: onStarted
No upstream description.
exited(exitCode: int, exitStatus: ExitStatus)handler: onExited
No upstream description.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

  • Wrap output in .trim().
  • Set environment: ({ LC_ALL: "C" }) when parsing output, so other languages don't change it.
  • For files in /proc or /sys, use FileView instead; it's much cheaper.

See also#

Running Commands with Process · StdioCollector · SplitParser · Quickshell.execDetached()

Quickshell.Io

FileViewError

enum
Import
import Quickshell.Io
Inherits
FileViewError → QtObject
How to get one
This is an enum (a fixed list of named values). You never create it; you compare against or assign its values, e.g. FileViewError.Success. Turn a value into readable text with FileViewError.toString(value).

Functions#

toString(value: FileViewError): string
No upstream description.

Enum values#

ValueNumberMeaning
FileViewError.Success0

No error occurred.

FileViewError.Unknown1

An unknown error occurred. Check the logs for details.

FileViewError.FileNotFound2

The file to read does not exist.

FileViewError.PermissionDenied3

Permission to read/write the file was not granted, or permission to create parent directories was not granted when writing the file.

FileViewError.NotAFile4

The specified path to read/write exists and was not a file.

Example#

import Quickshell.Io

// compare a value
if (someObject.someProperty === FileViewError.Unknown) console.log("it is Unknown")

// show a value as text
Text { text: FileViewError.toString(someObject.someProperty) }

Where this type appears#

  • FileView.loadFailed (signal)
  • FileView.saveFailed (signal)
Quickshell.Io

FileView

creatable

Simple accessor for small files.

Import
import Quickshell.Io
Inherits
FileView → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: FileView { … }.
Default property
adapter — children you write inside FileView { } go here

Overview#

Reads, watches and writes a file. Reading is cheap (no process), and with watchChanges you're notified the moment another program edits the file. With an adapter (JsonAdapter) the file's contents become QML properties.

From the upstream documentation#

A reader for small to medium files that don't need seeking/cursor access, suitable for most text files.

Example: Reading a JSON as text

FileView {
  id: jsonFile
  path: Qt.resolvedUrl("./your.json")
  // Forces the file to be loaded by the time we call JSON.parse().
  // see blockLoading's property documentation for details.
  blockLoading: true
}

readonly property var jsonData: JSON.parse(jsonFile.text())

Also see JsonAdapter for an alternative way to handle reading and writing JSON files.

Example: every property, function and signal#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Column {
    FileView {
        id: fv
        path: Quickshell.statePath("demo.txt")    // "" unloads
        preload: true                             // load as soon as path is set (default)
        blockLoading: false                       // true: text() waits for the first load
        blockAllReads: false                      // true: every read waits for loads
        blockWrites: false                        // true: setText() blocks until written
        atomicWrites: true                        // write to temp file then swap (default)
        printErrors: false                        // don't log missing-file errors
        watchChanges: true                        // emit fileChanged on external edits

        onLoaded: console.log("loaded:", text())
        onLoadFailed: err => {
            console.log("load failed:", FileViewError.toString(err))
            if (err === FileViewError.FileNotFound) setText("created at " + new Date())
        }
        onSaved: console.log("saved")
        onSaveFailed: err => console.warn("save failed:", FileViewError.toString(err))
        onFileChanged: reload()                   // re-read after external change
    }

    Text { text: fv.loaded ? fv.text() : "(not loaded)" }    // text() is bindable
    Text { text: "[append]"; TapHandler { onTapped: fv.setText(fv.text() + "\nmore") } }
    // fv.data()        raw bytes (ArrayBuffer)
    // fv.setData(buf)  write raw bytes
    // fv.waitForJob()  block until the current load finishes
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onPathChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
pathstringread / write

The path to the file that should be read, or an empty string to unload the file.

preloadboolread / write

If the file should be loaded in the background immediately when set. Defaults to true.

This may either increase or decrease the amount of time it takes to load the file depending on how large the file is, how fast its storage is, and how you access its data.

blockLoadingboolread / write

If text() and data() should block all operations until the file is loaded. Defaults to false.

If the file is already loaded, no blocking will occur. If a file was loaded, and path was changed to a new file, no blocking will occur.

Blocking operations should be used carefully to avoid stutters and other performance

degradations. Blocking means that your interface WILL NOT FUNCTION during the call.

We recommend you use a blocking load ONLY for files loaded before the windows of your shell are loaded, which happens after Component.onCompleted runs for the root component of your shell.

The most reasonable use case would be to load things like configuration files that the program must have available.

Useful for config files read at startup, so nothing flashes with default values. Don't use it for big files.

blockAllReadsboolread / write

If text() and data() should block all operations while a file loads. Defaults to false.

This is nearly identical to blockLoading, but will additionally block when a file is loaded and path changes.

Watch out

We cannot think of a valid use case for this. You almost definitely want blockLoading.

blockWritesboolread / write

If true (default false), all calls to setText() or setData() will block the UI thread until the write succeeds or fails.

Blocking operations should be used carefully to avoid stutters and other performance

degradations. Blocking means that your interface WILL NOT FUNCTION during the call.

atomicWritesboolread / write

If true (default), all calls to setText() or setData() will be performed atomically, meaning if the write fails for any reason, the file will not be modified.

This works by creating another file with the desired content, and renaming

it over the existing file if successful.

printErrorsboolread / write

If true (default), read or write errors will be printed to the quickshell logs. If false, all known errors will not be printed.

watchChangesboolread / write

If true (defaule false), fileChanged() will be called whenever the content of the file changes on disk, including when setText() or setData() are used.

You can reload the file's content whenever it changes on disk like so:
FileView {
  // ...
  watchChanges: true
  onFileChanged: this.reload()
}

Uses inotify. Some /proc and /sys files never notify; for those call reload() on a Timer.

adapterFileViewAdapterread / write

In addition to directly reading/writing the file as text, adapters can be used to expose a file's content in new ways.

An adapter will automatically be given the loaded file's content. Its state may be saved with writeAdapter().

Currently the only adapter is JsonAdapter.

loadedboolread-only

If a file is currently loaded, which may or may not be the one currently specified by path.

Note

If a file is loaded, path is changed, and a new file is loaded, this property will stay true the whole time. If path is set to an empty string to unload the file it will become false.

Functions#

text(): string

Returns the data of the file specified by path as text.

If blockAllReads is true, all changes to path will cause the program to block when this function is called.

If blockLoading is true, reading this property before the file has been loaded will block, but changing path or calling reload() will return the old data until the load completes.

If neither is true, an empty string will be returned if no file is loaded, otherwise it will behave as in the case above.

Note

Due to technical limitations, text() could not be a property, however you can treat it like a property, it will trigger property updates as a property would, and the signal textChanged() is present.

Although it's a function, you can use it in bindings like a property: they update after each load.

data(): string

Returns the data of the file specified by path as an ArrayBuffer.

If blockAllReads is true, all changes to path will cause the program to block when this function is called.

If blockLoading is true, reading this property before the file has been loaded will block, but changing path or calling reload() will return the old data until the load completes.

If neither is true, an empty buffer will be returned if no file is loaded, otherwise it will behave as in the case above.

Note

Due to technical limitations, data() could not be a property, however you can treat it like a property, it will trigger property updates as a property would, and the signal dataChanged() is present.

waitForJob(): bool

Block all operations until the currently running load completes.

Watch out

See blockLoading for an explanation and warning about blocking.

reload(): void

Unload the loaded file and reload it, usually in response to changes.

This will not block if blockLoading is set, only if blockAllReads is true. It acts the same as changing path to a new file, except loading the same file.

writeAdapter(): void

Write the content of the current adapter to the selected file.

setData(data: string): void

Sets the content of the file specified by path as an [ArrayBuffer].

atomicWrites and blockWrites affect the behavior of this function.

saved(s) or saveFailed(s) will be emitted on completion.

setText(text: string): void

Sets the content of the file specified by path as text.

atomicWrites and blockWrites affect the behavior of this function.

saved(s) or saveFailed(s) will be emitted on completion.

Signals#

loaded()handler: onLoaded

Emitted if the file was loaded successfully.

loadFailed(error: FileViewError)handler: onLoadFailed

Emitted if the file failed to load.

saved()handler: onSaved

Emitted if the file was saved successfully.

saveFailed(error: FileViewError)handler: onSaveFailed

Emitted if the file failed to save.

fileChanged()handler: onFileChanged

Emitted if the file changes on disk and watchChanges is true.

adapterUpdated()handler: onAdapterUpdated

Emitted when the active adapter's data is changed.

See also#

Files, Watching and JSON Config · JsonAdapter · FileViewError

Quickshell.Io

FileViewAdapter

provided by Quickshell

See FileView.adapter.

Import
import Quickshell.Io
Inherits
FileViewAdapter → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself. Quickshell gives you instances through: FileView.adapter.

Overview#

The base type of adapters you put in FileView.adapter. Quickshell's adapter is JsonAdapter. Its adapterUpdated signal is forwarded to the FileView's adapterUpdated, which you connect to writeAdapter().

Signals#

adapterUpdated()handler: onAdapterUpdated

This signal is fired when data in the adapter changes, and triggers FileView.adapterUpdated(s).

Where this type appears#

  • FileView.adapter (property)
Quickshell.Io

JsonObject

creatable

See JsonAdapter.

Import
import Quickshell.Io
Inherits
JsonObject → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: JsonObject { … }.

Overview#

A nested JSON object inside a JsonAdapter. Declare it as a typed property and put properties inside; it maps to { … } in the file.

Example#

JsonAdapter {
    property JsonObject appearance: JsonObject {
        property string font: "Inter"
        property JsonObject animation: JsonObject {       // nesting can go deeper
            property int duration: 250
        }
    }
}
// JSON: { "appearance": { "font": "Inter", "animation": { "duration": 250 } } }
Quickshell.Io

JsonAdapter

creatable

FileView adapter for accessing JSON files.

Import
import Quickshell.Io
Inherits
JsonAdapter
How to get one
You create this type in QML: JsonAdapter { … }.

Overview#

Turns a JSON file into live properties, both ways. Declare properties (with defaults) inside a JsonAdapter placed in a FileView: values load from the file, and changes you make in QML can be written back.

From the upstream documentation#

JsonAdapter is a FileView adapter that exposes a JSON file as a set of QML properties that can be read and written to.

Each property defined in a JsonAdapter corresponds to a key in the JSON file. Supported property types are: - Primitves (int, bool, string, real) - Sub-object adapters (JsonObject) - JSON objects and arrays, as a var type - Lists of any of the above (list<string> etc)

When the FileView's data is loaded, properties of a JsonAdapter or sub-object adapter (JsonObject) are updated if their values have changed.

When properties of a JsonAdapter or sub-object adapter are changed from QML, FileView.adapterUpdated(s) is emitted, which may be used to save the file's new state (see FileView.writeAdapter()$).

Example#

@@FileView {
  path: "/path/to/file"

  // when changes are made on disk, reload the file's content
  watchChanges: true
  onFileChanged: reload()

  // when changes are made to properties in the adapter, save them
  onAdapterUpdated: writeAdapter()

  JsonAdapter {
    property string myStringProperty: "default value"
    onMyStringPropertyChanged: {
      console.log("myStringProperty was changed via qml or on disk")
    }

    property list<string> stringList: [ "default", "value" ]

    property JsonObject subObject: JsonObject {
      property string subObjectProperty: "default value"
      onSubObjectPropertyChanged: console.log("same as above")
    }

    // works the same way as subObject
    property var inlineJson: { "a": "b" }
  }
}

The above snippet produces the JSON document below:

{
   "myStringProperty": "default value",
   "stringList": [
     "default",
     "value"
   ],
   "subObject": {
     "subObjectProperty": "default value"
   },
   "inlineJson": {
     "a": "b"
   }
}

Example: a complete config#

services/Config.qmlpragma Singleton
import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Singleton {
    property alias options: adapter

    FileView {
        path: Quickshell.env("HOME") + "/.config/myshell/config.json"
        watchChanges: true
        onFileChanged: reload()                  // manual edits → reload
        onAdapterUpdated: writeAdapter()         // QML edits → save
        blockLoading: true
        onLoadFailed: err => { if (err === FileViewError.FileNotFound) writeAdapter() }  // create with defaults

        JsonAdapter {
            id: adapter
            property string terminal: "kitty"              // "terminal": "kitty"
            property bool darkMode: true
            property real opacity: 0.85
            property color accent: "#cba6f7"
            property list<string> pinnedApps: ["firefox", "kitty"]
            property var extra: ({})                       // any JSON value
            property JsonObject bar: JsonObject {          // nested object
                property int height: 36
                property bool bottom: false
            }
        }
    }
}
Text { text: Config.options.terminal }
Switch { checked: Config.options.bar.bottom; onToggled: Config.options.bar.bottom = checked }   // saved automatically

Notes, tips and gotchas#

  • Missing keys keep their defaults; unknown keys in the file are ignored.
  • For var/list properties, assign a new value to trigger saving (x = [...x, item]).

See also#

Files, Watching and JSON Config · JsonObject

Quickshell.Io

IpcHandler

creatable

Handler for IPC message calls.

Import
import Quickshell.Io
Inherits
IpcHandler
How to get one
You create this type in QML: IpcHandler { … }.

Overview#

Exposes functions, properties and signals to the outside world via qs ipc. That's how keybinds, scripts and other programs control your shell on any compositor.

From the upstream documentation#

Each IpcHandler is registered into a per-instance map by its unique target. Functions and properties defined on the IpcHandler can be accessed via qs ipc.

Handler Functions

IPC handler functions can be called by qs ipc call as long as they have at most 10 arguments, and all argument types along with the return type are listed below.

Argument and return types must be explicitly specified or they will not be registered.

Arguments
  • string will be passed to the parameter as is.
  • int will only accept parameters that can be parsed as an integer.
  • bool will only accept parameters that are "true", "false", or an integer, where 0 will be converted to false, and anything else to true.
  • real will only accept parameters that can be parsed as a number with or without a decimal.
  • color will accept named colors or hex strings (RGB, RRGGBB, AARRGGBB) with an optional # prefix.
Return Type
  • void will return nothing.
  • string will be returned as is.
  • int will be converted to a string and returned.
  • bool will be converted to "true" or "false" and returned.
  • real will be converted to a string and returned.
  • color will be converted to a hex string in the form #AARRGGBB and returned.

Signals

IPC handler signals can be observed remotely using qs ipc wait (one call) and qs ipc listen (many calls). IPC signals may have zero or one argument, where the argument is one of the types listed above, or no arguments for void.

Example

The following example creates ipc functions to control and retrieve the appearance of a Rectangle.

FloatingWindow {
  Rectangle {
    id: rect
    anchors.centerIn: parent
    width: 100
    height: 100
    color: "red"
  }

  IpcHandler {
    target: "rect"

    function setColor(color: color): void { rect.color = color; }
    function getColor(): color { return rect.color; }

    function setAngle(angle: real): void { rect.rotation = angle; }
    function getAngle(): real { return rect.rotation; }

    function setRadius(radius: int): void {
      rect.radius = radius;
      this.radiusChanged(radius);
    }

    function getRadius(): int { return rect.radius; }

    signal radiusChanged(newRadius: int);
  }
}

The list of registered targets can be inspected using qs ipc show.

$ qs ipc show
target rect
  function setColor(color: color): void
  function getColor(): color
  function setAngle(angle: real): void
  function getAngle(): real
  function setRadius(radius: int): void
  function getRadius(): int
  signal radiusChanged(newRadius: int)

and then invoked using qs ipc call.

$ qs ipc call rect setColor orange
$ qs ipc call rect setAngle 40.5
$ qs ipc call rect setRadius 30
$ qs ipc call rect getColor
#ffffa500
$ qs ipc call rect getAngle
40.5
$ qs ipc call rect getRadius
30

Properties

Properties of an IpcHanlder can be read using qs ipc prop get as long as they are of an IPC compatible type. See the table above for compatible types.

Example: functions, property and signal#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Io
import QtQuick

Scope {
    id: root
    property real volume: 0.5

    IpcHandler {
        id: ipc
        target: "audio"                          // unique name: qs ipc call audio …
        enabled: true

        property real level: root.volume         // qs ipc prop get audio level
        signal levelChanged2(value: real)        // qs ipc listen audio levelChanged2

        function get(): real { return root.volume }
        function set(v: real): void { root.volume = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, v)); levelChanged2(root.volume) }
        function up(step: int): void { set(root.volume + step / 100) }
        function mute(on: bool): void { console.log("mute", on) }
        function tint(c: color): color { return Qt.darker(c, 1.2) }
        function name(): string { return "speakers" }
    }
}
qs ipc show
qs ipc call audio set 0.3
qs ipc call audio up 5
qs ipc call audio mute true
qs ipc call audio get              # → 0.3
qs ipc call audio tint "#ff8800"   # → #ffd46d00
qs ipc prop get audio level
qs ipc listen audio levelChanged2

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onEnabledChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
enabledboolread / write

If the handler should be able to receive calls. Defaults to true.

targetstringread / write

The target this handler should be accessible from. Required and must be unique. May be changed at runtime.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

  • Every parameter and the return type must be annotated (string, int, bool, real, color, void), or the function isn't exposed.
  • Up to 10 arguments. Signals may have zero or one argument.

See also#

IPC, Keybinds and Sockets · GlobalShortcut

Quickshell.Widgets

WrapperManager

creatable

Helper object for creating components with a single visual child.

Import
import Quickshell.Widgets
Inherits
WrapperManager
How to get one
You create this type in QML: WrapperManager { … }.

Overview#

The helper behind the Wrapper types: it picks the wrapper's single visual child (child) and tracks the wrapper. You normally use MarginWrapperManager or the ready-made Wrapper* types instead.

From the upstream documentation#

WrapperManager determines which child of an Item should be its visual child, and exposes it for further operations. See MarginWrapperManager for a subclass that implements automatic sizing and margins.

Using wrapper types#

WrapperManager based types have a single visual child item. You can specify the child item using the default property, or by setting the child property. You must use the child property if the widget has more than one Item based child.

Example using the default property

WrapperWidget { // a widget that uses WrapperManager
  // Putting the item inline uses the default property of WrapperWidget.
  @@QtQuick.Text { text: "Hello" }

  // Scope does not extend Item, so it can be placed in the
  // default property without issue.
  @@Quickshell.Scope {}
}

Example using the child property

WrapperWidget {
  @@QtQuick.Text {
    id: text
    text: "Hello"
  }

  @@QtQuick.Text {
    id: otherText
    text: "Other Text"
  }

  // Both text and otherText extend Item, so one must be specified.
  child: text
}

See child for more details on how the child property can be used.

Implementing wrapper types#

In addition to the bundled wrapper types, you can make your own using WrapperManager. To implement a wrapper, create a WrapperManager inside your wrapper component 's default property, then alias a new property to the WrapperManager's child property.

Example

Item { // your wrapper component
  WrapperManager { id: wrapperManager }

  // Allows consumers of your wrapper component to use the child property.
  property alias child: wrapperManager.child

  // The rest of your component logic. You can use
  // `wrapperManager.child` or `this.child` to refer to the selected child.
}

See also#

  • WrapperItem - A MarginWrapperManager based component that sizes itself to its child.
  • WrapperRectangle - A MarginWrapperManager based component that sizes itself to its child, and provides an option to use its border as an inset.

Example: making your own wrapper type#

MyWrapper.qmlimport Quickshell.Widgets
import QtQuick

Rectangle {
    color: "#313244"; radius: 10
    WrapperManager { id: wm }               // wrapper defaults to this parent
    // wm.child is the single visual child written inside MyWrapper { … }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onChildChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
childItemread / write

The wrapper component's selected child.

Setting this property override's WrapperManager's default selection, and resolve ambiguity when more than one visual child is present. The property can additionally be defined inline or reference a component that is not already a child of the wrapper, in which case it will be reparented to the wrapper. Setting child to null will select no child, and undefined will restore the default child.

When read, child will always return the (potentially null) selected child, and not undefined.

wrapperItemread / write

The wrapper managed by this manager. Defaults to the manager's parent. This property may not be changed after Component.onCompleted.

Enum values#

Enum Flag — values are written WrapperManager.Value.

ValueNumberMeaning
WrapperManager.NoFlags0x0
WrapperManager.NullChild0x1
WrapperManager.HasMultipleChildren0x2
Quickshell.Widgets

MarginWrapperManager

creatable

Helper object for applying sizes and margins to a single child item.

Import
import Quickshell.Widgets
Inherits
MarginWrapperManager → WrapperManager
How to get one
You create this type in QML: MarginWrapperManager { … }.

Overview#

Adds margins and automatic sizing to a wrapper: the wrapper's implicit size becomes the child's implicit size plus margins, and the child is placed inside. All Wrapper* types use it, so these properties appear on them.

From the upstream documentation#

Note

MarginWrapperManager is an extension of WrapperManager. You should read its documentation to understand wrapper types.

MarginWrapperManager can be used to apply margins to a child item, in addition to handling the size / implicit size relationship between the parent and the child. WrapperItem and WrapperRectangle exist for Item and Rectangle implementations respectively.

MarginWrapperManager based types set the child item's

Item.x, Item.y, Item.width, Item.height or Item.anchors properties. Do not set them yourself, instead set Item.implicitWidth and Item.implicitHeight.

Implementing a margin wrapper type#

Follow the directions in WrapperManager's documentation, and or alias the margin property if you wish to expose it.

Margin calculation#

The margin of the content item is calculated based on topMargin, bottomMargin, leftMargin, rightMargin, extraMargin and resizeChild.

If resizeChild is true, each side's margin will be the value of <side>Margin plus extraMargin, and the content item will be stretched to match the given margin if the wrapper is not at its implicit size.

If resizeChild is false, the <side>Margin properties will be interpreted as a ratio and the content item will not be stretched if the wrapper is not at its implicit side.

The implicit size of the wrapper is the implicit size of the content item plus all margins.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell.Widgets
import QtQuick

Rectangle {
    color: "#313244"; radius: 12
    MarginWrapperManager {
        margin: 10                    // default for all sides
        topMargin: 6                  // per-side (falls back to margin)
        bottomMargin: 6
        leftMargin: 14
        rightMargin: 14
        extraMargin: 0                // added to all sides
        resizeChild: true             // stretch child if the wrapper is made bigger
        // implicitWidth / implicitHeight: override the computed size
    }
    Text { text: "auto-sized"; color: "white" }
}

Quickshell.Widgets

IconImage

creatableQML widget

Image component for displaying widget/icon style images.

Import
import Quickshell.Widgets
Inherits
IconImage → Item
How to get one
You create this type in QML: IconImage { … }.

Overview#

An image specialized for icons: always square, sized by one value (implicitSize), and scaled crisply. Use it for app icons, tray icons and notification icons. It accepts any image source, usually from Quickshell.iconPath().

From the upstream documentation#

This is a specialization of Image configured for icon-style images, designed to make it easier to use correctly. If you need more control, use Image directly.

The image's aspect raito is assumed to be 1:1. If it is not 1:1, padding will be added to make it 1:1. This is currently applied before the actual aspect ratio of the image is taken into account, and may change in a future release.

You should use it for: - Icons for custom buttons - Status indicator icons - System tray icons - Things similar to the above.

Do not use it for: - Big images - Images that change size frequently - Anything that doesn't feel like an icon.

More information about many of these properties can be found in

the documentation for Image.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Widgets
import QtQuick

Row {
    spacing: 8
    IconImage {
        id: icon
        implicitSize: 32                                     // width = height = 32 unless overridden
        source: Quickshell.iconPath("firefox", "application-x-executable")
        asynchronous: true                                   // Image properties are available too
        onStatusChanged: if (status === Image.Error) console.warn("icon failed")
    }
    Text { text: "actual: " + icon.actualSize + "px · status " + icon.status }
}

Try enabling this if your image is significantly scaled down and looks bad because of it.

ClippingRectangle

creatableQML widget

Rectangle capable of clipping content inside its border.

Import
import Quickshell.Widgets
Inherits
ClippingRectangle → Item
How to get one
You create this type in QML: ClippingRectangle { … }.

Overview#

A rectangle that clips its children to its rounded corners. That's the easy way to get rounded album art, avatars and thumbnails (plain clip: true ignores radius).

From the upstream documentation#

This type requires at least Qt 6.7.

This is a specialized version of Rectangle that clips content inside of its border, including rounded rectangles. It costs more than Rectangle, so it should not be used unless you need to clip items inside of it to the border.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell.Widgets
import QtQuick

ClippingRectangle {
    width: 160; height: 160
    radius: 32                         // children are clipped to this shape
    color: "#313244"                   // background behind children
    border.width: 4
    border.color: "#cba6f7"
    contentUnderBorder: false          // true: content extends under a (translucent) border
    contentInsideBorder: true          // true: content is resized to fit inside the border

    Image {
        anchors.fill: parent           // fills contentItem (inside the border)
        source: "file:///home/me/.face"
        fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectCrop
        sourceSize: Qt.size(320, 320)
    }
}

Defaults to !contentUnderBorder. Most useful when combined with anchors.fill: parent on an item passed to the ClippingRectangle.

WrapperItem

creatableQML widget

Item that handles sizes and positioning for a single visual child.

Import
import Quickshell.Widgets
Inherits
WrapperItem → Item
How to get one
You create this type in QML: WrapperItem { … }.

Overview#

An Item that sizes itself to exactly one visual child plus margins, and keeps the child positioned inside. It saves you from writing implicitWidth: child.implicitWidth + 2*m by hand. Margin properties come from its MarginWrapperManager.

From the upstream documentation#

This component is useful when you need to wrap a single component in an item, or give a single component a margin. See QtQuick.Layouts for positioning multiple items.

Note

WrapperItem is a MarginWrapperManager based component. See its documentation for information on how margins and sizes are calculated.

Example: Adding a margin to an item#

The snippet below adds a 10px margin to all sides of the Text item.

WrapperItem {
  margin: 10

  @@QtQuick.Text { text: "Hello!" }
}
Note

The child item can be specified by writing it inline in the wrapper, as in the example above, or by using the child property. See WrapperManager.child for details.

Watch out

You should not set Item.x, Item.y, Item.width, Item.height or Item.anchors on the child item, as they are used by WrapperItem to position it. Instead set Item.implicitWidth and Item.implicitHeight.

Example#

import Quickshell.Widgets
import QtQuick

WrapperItem {
    margin: 10                 // all sides
    leftMargin: 16             // override one side
    // child: label            // optional: pick the child explicitly
    Text { id: label; text: "padded" }
}

Quickshell.Wayland

WlrLayershell

creatablehas attached properties

Wlroots layershell window

Import
import Quickshell.Wayland
Inherits
WlrLayershell → PanelWindow → QsWindow → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: WlrLayershell { … }.

Overview#

Layer-shell settings for a PanelWindow, used as attached properties: WlrLayershell.layer, WlrLayershell.namespace, WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus. They decide which stacking layer the window lives on, what name compositor rules see, and whether it receives keyboard input.

From the upstream documentation#

Decorationless window that can be attached to the screen edges using the zwlr_layer_shell_v1 protocol.

Attached object

WlrLayershell works as an attached object of PanelWindow which you should use instead if you can, as it is platform independent.

PanelWindow {
  // When PanelWindow is backed with WlrLayershell this will work
  WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Bottom
}

To maintain platform compatibility you can dynamically set layershell specific properties.

PanelWindow {
  Component.onCompleted: {
    if (this.WlrLayershell != null) {
      this.WlrLayershell.layer = WlrLayer.Bottom;
    }
  }
}

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    implicitWidth: 500; implicitHeight: 60
    color: "#1e1e2e"
    WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay                   // Background | Bottom | Top (default) | Overlay
    WlrLayershell.namespace: "quickshell:search"            // for layerrules; can't change after creation
    WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive // None (default) | Exclusive | OnDemand

    TextInput { anchors.centerIn: parent; focus: true; color: "white"; width: 400; Keys.onEscapePressed: Qt.quit() }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onLayerChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
layerWlrLayerread / write

The shell layer the window sits in. Defaults to WlrLayer.Top.

namespacestringread / write

Similar to the class property of windows. Can be used to identify the window to external tools.

Cannot be set after windowConnected.

Use a consistent scheme such as quickshell:bar and match it in Hyprland with layerrule = blur, quickshell:bar.

keyboardFocusWlrKeyboardFocusread / write

The degree of keyboard focus taken. Defaults to KeyboardFocus.None.

Exclusive takes all keyboard input while the window is mapped, so close it with Esc. OnDemand gets focus when clicked. Bars should stay None.

Inherited from PanelWindow (6 properties)

Anchors attach a shell window to the sides of the screen. By default all anchors are disabled to avoid blocking the entire screen due to a misconfiguration.

When two opposite anchors are attached at the same time, the corresponding dimension

(width or height) will be forced to equal the screen width/height. Margins can be used to create anchored windows that are also disconnected from the monitor sides.

marginsMarginsread / write

Offsets from the sides of the screen.

Only applies to edges with anchors

The amount of space reserved for the shell layer relative to its anchors. Setting this property sets exclusionMode to ExclusionMode.Normal.

Note

Either 1 or 3 anchors are required for the zone to take effect.

Qt's coordinate system works in logical pixels, which equal N monitor pixels depending on scale factor. This property returns the amount of monitor pixels in a logical pixel for the current window.

The clickthrough mask. Defaults to null.

If non null then the clickable areas of the window will be determined by the provided region.

ShellWindow {
  // The mask region is set to `rect`, meaning only `rect` is clickable.
  // All other clicks pass through the window to ones behind it.
  mask: Region { item: rect }

}

If the provided region's intersection mode is Combine (the default), then the region will be used as is. Otherwise it will be applied on top of the window region.

For example, setting the intersection mode to Xor will invert the mask and make everything in the mask region not clickable and pass through clicks inside it through the window.

ShellWindow {
  // The mask region is set to `rect`, but the intersection mode is set to `Xor`.
  // This inverts the mask causing all clicks inside `rect` to be passed to the window
  // behind this one.
  mask: Region { item: rect; intersection: Intersection.Xor }

  Rectangle {
    id: rect

    anchors.centerIn: parent
    width: 100
    height: 100
  }
}
surfaceFormatQsSurfaceFormatread / write

Set the surface format to request from the system.

  • opaque - If the requested surface should be opaque. Opaque windows allow the operating system to avoid drawing things behind them, or blending the window with those behind it, saving power and GPU load. If unset, this property defaults to true if color is opaque, or false if not. You should not need to modify this property unless you create a surface that starts opaque and later becomes transparent.
Note

The surface format cannot be changed after the window is created.

updatesEnabledboolread / write

If the window should receive render updates. Defaults to true.

When set to false, the window will not re-render in response to animations or other visual updates from other windows. This is useful for static windows such as wallpapers that do not need to update frequently, saving GPU cycles.

When set back to true, a new frame is rendered, including any changes made while updates were disabled.

datalist<QtObject>read-onlyNo upstream description.
Inherited from Reloadable (1 properties)
reloadableIdstringread / write

An additional identifier that can be used to try to match a reloadable object to its previous state.

Simply keeping a stable identifier across config versions (saves) is enough to help the reloader figure out which object in the old revision corresponds to this object in the current revision, and facilitate smoother reloading.

Note that identifiers are scoped, and will try to do the right thing in context. For example if you have a Variants wrapping an object with an identified element inside, a scope is created at the variant level.

Variants {
  // multiple variants of the same object tree
  variants: [ { foo: 1 }, { foo: 2 } ]

  // any non `Reloadable` object
  QtObject {
    FloatingWindow {
      // this FloatingWindow will now be matched to the same one in the previous
      // widget tree for its variant. "myFloatingWindow" refers to both the variant in
      // `foo: 1` and `foo: 2` for each tree.
      reloadableId: "myFloatingWindow"

      // ...
    }
  }
}

See also#

Windows: PanelWindow, Layers and Exclusive Zones · WlrLayer · WlrKeyboardFocus

Quickshell.Wayland

WlSessionLock

creatable

Wayland session locker.

Import
import Quickshell.Wayland
Inherits
WlSessionLock → Reloadable
How to get one
You create this type in QML: WlSessionLock { … }.
Default property
surface — children you write inside WlSessionLock { } go here

Overview#

Locks the session with the ext-session-lock protocol: while locked is true, the compositor shows only your lock surfaces and sends input only to them. If your shell crashes, the session stays locked.

From the upstream documentation#

Wayland session lock implemented using the ext_session_lock_v1 protocol.

WlSessionLock will create an instance of its surface component for every screen when locked is set to true. The surface component must create a WlSessionLockSurface which will be displayed on each screen.

The below example will create a session lock that disappears when the button is clicked.

WlSessionLock {
  id: lock

  WlSessionLockSurface {
    Button {
      text: "unlock me"
      onClicked: lock.locked = false
    }
  }
}

// ...
lock.locked = true
If the WlSessionLock is destroyed or quickshell exits without setting locked

to false, conformant compositors will leave the screen locked and painted with a solid color.

This is what makes the session lock secure. The lock dying will not expose your session, but it will render it inoperable.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

Scope {
    WlSessionLock {
        id: lock
        locked: false                                 // set true to lock
        surface: Component {                          // one surface per screen, created automatically
            WlSessionLockSurface {
                color: "black"
                Text { anchors.centerIn: parent; color: "white"; text: "Locked" + (lock.secure ? " (secure)" : "") }
                // unlock ONLY after successful PAM auth (see PamContext)
            }
        }
        onSecureChanged: console.log("compositor confirmed lock:", secure)
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onLockedChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
lockedboolread / write

Controls the lock state.

Only one WlSessionLock may be locked at a time. Attempting to enable a lock while

another lock is enabled will do nothing.

Only one WlSessionLock may be locked at a time. Setting locked = false unlocks.

secureboolread-only

The compositor lock state.

This is set to true once the compositor has confirmed all screens are covered with locks.

True once the compositor confirms every screen is covered. Don't show sensitive UI before then.

surfaceComponentread / write

The surface that will be created for each screen. Must create a WlSessionLockSurface.

Inherited from Reloadable (1 properties)
reloadableIdstringread / write

An additional identifier that can be used to try to match a reloadable object to its previous state.

Simply keeping a stable identifier across config versions (saves) is enough to help the reloader figure out which object in the old revision corresponds to this object in the current revision, and facilitate smoother reloading.

Note that identifiers are scoped, and will try to do the right thing in context. For example if you have a Variants wrapping an object with an identified element inside, a scope is created at the variant level.

Variants {
  // multiple variants of the same object tree
  variants: [ { foo: 1 }, { foo: 2 } ]

  // any non `Reloadable` object
  QtObject {
    FloatingWindow {
      // this FloatingWindow will now be matched to the same one in the previous
      // widget tree for its variant. "myFloatingWindow" refers to both the variant in
      // `foo: 1` and `foo: 2` for each tree.
      reloadableId: "myFloatingWindow"

      // ...

  }
}

Notes, tips and gotchas#

Never unlock without authentication. Keep a safety timer while developing (Project: Lock Screen).

Quickshell.Wayland

Toplevel

provided by Quickshell

Window from another application.

Import
import Quickshell.Wayland
Inherits
Toplevel → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (Toplevels must be acquired from the ToplevelManager.). Quickshell gives you instances through: HyprlandToplevel.wayland, ToplevelManager.activeToplevel, ToplevelManager.toplevels.

Overview#

A window of another application, from the compositor-independent foreign-toplevel protocol. Get them from ToplevelManager or HyprlandToplevel.wayland. Use them for taskbars, docks and live previews.

From the upstream documentation#

A window/toplevel from another application, retrievable from the ToplevelManager.

Example: every property and function#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

Column {
    Repeater {
        model: ToplevelManager.toplevels
        Row {
            required property Toplevel modelData
            spacing: 8
            Text { text: (modelData.activated ? "● " : "  ") + modelData.appId + " — " + modelData.title }
            Text { text: modelData.maximized ? "[max]" : ""; color: "grey" }
            Text { text: modelData.minimized ? "[min]" : ""; color: "grey" }
            Text { text: modelData.fullscreen ? "[full]" : ""; color: "grey" }
            Text { text: modelData.parent ? "dialog of " + modelData.parent.title : "" }
            Text { text: "on " + modelData.screens.map(s => s.name).join(",") }
            Text { text: "[focus]"; TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.activate() } }
            Text { text: "[max]"; TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.maximized = !modelData.maximized } }
            Text { text: "[min]"; TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.minimized = true } }
            Text { text: "[full on 1st screen]"; TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.fullscreenOn(Quickshell.screens[0]) } }
            Text { text: "[close]"; TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.close() } }
            Connections { target: modelData; function onClosed() { console.log("closed:", modelData.title) } }
        }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onAppIdChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
appIdstringread-onlyNo upstream description.
titlestringread-onlyNo upstream description.
parentToplevelread-only

Parent toplevel if this toplevel is a modal/dialog, otherwise null.

activatedboolread-only

If the window is currently activated or focused.

Activation can be requested with the activate() function.

screenslist<ShellScreen>read-only

Screens the toplevel is currently visible on. Screens are listed in the order they have been added by the compositor.

Note

Some compositors only list a single screen, even if a window is visible on multiple.

maximizedboolread / write

If the window is currently maximized.

Maximization can be requested by setting this property, though it may be ignored by the compositor.

minimizedboolread / write

If the window is currently minimized.

Minimization can be requested by setting this property, though it may be ignored by the compositor.

fullscreenboolread / write

If the window is currently fullscreen.

Fullscreen can be requested by setting this property, though it may be ignored by the compositor. Fullscreen can be requested on a specific screen with the fullscreenOn() function.

Functions#

activate(): void

Request that this toplevel is activated. The request may be ignored by the compositor.

close(): void

Request that this toplevel is closed. The request may be ignored by the compositor or the application.

fullscreenOn(screen: ShellScreen): void

Request that this toplevel is fullscreened on a specific screen. The request may be ignored by the compositor.

setRectangle(window: QtObject, rect: rect): void

Provide a hint to the compositor where the visual representation of this toplevel is relative to a quickshell window. This hint can be used visually in operations like minimization.

Tells the compositor where this window's icon is (e.g. in your dock), so minimize animations can fly there: toplevel.setRectangle(dockWindow, dockWindow.itemRect(icon)).

unsetRectangle(): void
No upstream description.

Signals#

closed()handler: onClosed
No upstream description.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

All state changes are requests; the compositor may ignore them.

Where this type appears#

  • HyprlandToplevel.wayland (property)
  • ToplevelManager.activeToplevel (property)
  • ToplevelManager.toplevels (property)

Quickshell.Wayland

ScreencopyView

creatable

Displays a video stream from other windows or a monitor.

Import
import Quickshell.Wayland
Inherits
ScreencopyView → Item
How to get one
You create this type in QML: ScreencopyView { … }.

Overview#

Displays a live video (or a single frame) of a window or a whole monitor. That's how overviews and window switchers show previews.

From the upstream documentation#

ScreencopyView displays live video streams or single captured frames from valid capture sources. See captureSource for details on which objects are accepted.

Example: every property and function#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

Row {
    spacing: 10
    ScreencopyView {                                       // live monitor preview
        id: mon
        width: 320; height: 180
        captureSource: Quickshell.screens[0]               // ShellScreen, Toplevel, or null
        live: true                                         // continuous updates
        paintCursor: true                                  // include the mouse cursor
        constraintSize: Qt.size(320, 180)                  // fit within, keep aspect ratio
        onStopped: console.log("stream ended")
    }
    ScreencopyView {                                       // still frame of the focused window
        id: still
        width: 320; height: 180
        captureSource: ToplevelManager.activeToplevel
        live: false
        Component.onCompleted: captureFrame()              // grab one frame
        Text { visible: !still.hasContent; text: "no content yet"; color: "white" }
        Text { anchors.bottom: parent.bottom; color: "white"
               text: still.hasContent ? still.sourceSize.width + "×" + still.sourceSize.height : "" }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onCaptureSourceChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
captureSourceQtObjectread / write

The object to capture from. Accepts any of the following: - null - Clears the displayed image. - ShellScreen - A monitor. Requires a compositor that supports wlr-screencopy-unstable or both ext-image-copy-capture-v1 and ext-capture-source-v1. - Toplevel - A toplevel window. Requires a compositor that supports hyprland-toplevel-export-v1.

paintCursorboolread / write

If true, the system cursor will be painted on the image. Defaults to false.

liveboolread / write

If true, a live video feed from the capture source will be displayed instead of a still image. Defaults to false.

hasContentboolread-only

If true, the view has content ready to display. Content is not always immediately available, and this property can be used to avoid displaying it until ready.

sourceSizesizeread-only

The size of the source image. Valid when hasContent is true.

constraintSizesizeread / write

If nonzero, the width and height constraints set for this property will constrain those dimensions of the ScreencopyView's implicit size, maintaining the image's aspect ratio.

Functions#

captureFrame(): void

Capture a single frame. Has no effect if live is true.

Signals#

stopped()handler: onStopped

The compositor has ended the video stream. Attempting to restart it may or may not work.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

Live capture costs GPU time. Enable live only while visible.

Quickshell.Wayland

IdleInhibitor

creatable

Prevents a wayland session from idling

Import
import Quickshell.Wayland
Inherits
IdleInhibitor → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: IdleInhibitor { … }.

Overview#

Prevents the session from going idle (screen blanking, auto-lock) while enabled, for "caffeine" toggles or while presenting. It must be associated with a window.

From the upstream documentation#

If an idle daemon is running, it may perform actions such as locking the screen or putting the computer to sleep.

An idle inhibitor prevents a wayland session from being marked as idle, if compositor defined heuristics determine the window the inhibitor is attached to is important.

A compositor will usually consider a PanelWindow or a focused FloatingWindow to be important.

Note

Using an idle inhibitor requires the compositor support the [idle-inhibit-unstable-v1] protocol.

Example#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    id: bar
    anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }
    implicitHeight: 30
    property bool caffeine: false
    IdleInhibitor { window: bar; enabled: bar.caffeine }
    Text { anchors.centerIn: parent; text: bar.caffeine ? "☕ awake" : "💤 normal"
           TapHandler { onTapped: bar.caffeine = !bar.caffeine } }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onEnabledChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
enabledboolread / write

If the idle inhibitor should be enabled. Defaults to false.

windowQtObjectread / write

The window to associate the idle inhibitor with. This may be used by the compositor to determine if the inhibitor should be respected.

Must be set to a non null value to enable the inhibitor.

The compositor may ignore the inhibitor if this window isn't visible.

creatable

Import
import Quickshell.Wayland
Inherits
IdleMonitor
How to get one
You create this type in QML: IdleMonitor { … }.

Overview#

Tells you when the user has been idle for timeout seconds. Use it to lock the screen, dim, or turn displays off, without hypridle.

From the upstream documentation#

An idle monitor detects when the user stops providing input for a period of time.

Note

Using an idle monitor requires the compositor support the [ext-idle-notify-v1] protocol.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

Scope {
    IdleMonitor {
        id: idle
        enabled: true
        timeout: 300                       // seconds
        respectInhibitors: true            // don't report idle while a video/IdleInhibitor blocks it
        onIsIdleChanged: {
            if (isIdle) GlobalStates.locked = true
        }
    }
}

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onEnabledChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
enabledboolread / write

If the idle monitor should be enabled. Defaults to true.

timeoutrealread / write

The amount of time in seconds the idle monitor should wait before reporting an idle state.

Defaults to zero, which reports idle status immediately.

respectInhibitorsboolread / write

When set to true, isIdle will depend on both user interaction and active idle inhibitors. When false, the value will depend solely on user interaction. Defaults to true.

isIdleboolread-only

This property is true if the user has been idle for at least timeout. What is considered to be idle is influenced by respectInhibitors.

Quickshell.Wayland

ShortcutInhibitor

creatable

Prevents compositor keyboard shortcuts from being triggered

Import
import Quickshell.Wayland
Inherits
ShortcutInhibitor → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: ShortcutInhibitor { … }.

Overview#

While enabled and its window has keyboard focus, compositor shortcuts are disabled: every key goes to your window. Useful for key-capture UIs (keybind editors), games or kiosk screens.

From the upstream documentation#

A shortcuts inhibitor prevents the compositor from processing its own keyboard shortcuts for the focused surface. This allows applications to receive key events for shortcuts that would normally be handled by the compositor.

The inhibitor only takes effect when the associated window is focused and the inhibitor is enabled. The compositor may choose to ignore inhibitor requests based on its policy.

Note

Using a shortcuts inhibitor requires the compositor support the [keyboard-shortcuts-inhibit-unstable-v1] protocol.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Wayland
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    id: win
    implicitWidth: 400; implicitHeight: 120
    WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive
    ShortcutInhibitor {
        id: inhib
        window: win
        enabled: true
        onCancelled: console.log("compositor cancelled the inhibitor")
    }
    Text { anchors.centerIn: parent; text: inhib.active ? "Press any key combo…" : "inactive" }
    Item { focus: true; Keys.onPressed: e => console.log("captured", e.key, e.modifiers) }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onEnabledChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
enabledboolread / write

If the shortcuts inhibitor should be enabled. Defaults to false.

windowQtObjectread / write

The window to associate the shortcuts inhibitor with. The inhibitor will only inhibit shortcuts pressed while this window has keyboard focus.

Must be set to a non null value to enable the inhibitor.

activeboolread-only

Whether the inhibitor is currently active. The inhibitor is only active if enabled is true, window has keyboard focus, and the compositor grants the inhibit request.

The compositor may deactivate the inhibitor at any time (for example, if the user requests normal shortcuts to be restored). When deactivated by the compositor, the inhibitor cannot be programmatically reactivated.

Sent if the compositor cancels the inhibitor while it is active.

HyprlandEvent

provided by Quickshell

Live Hyprland IPC event.

Import
import Quickshell.Hyprland
Inherits
HyprlandEvent → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (HyprlandIpcEvents cannot be created.). Quickshell gives you instances through: Hyprland.rawEvent.

Overview#

One event from Hyprland's event socket, delivered by Hyprland's rawEvent signal. name is the event type, data the raw text after >>.

From the upstream documentation#

Holding this object after the signal handler exits is undefined as the event instance is reused.

Emitted by Hyprland.rawEvent(s).

Example#

Connections {
    target: Hyprland
    function onRawEvent(event) {
        if (event.name === "activelayout") {
            const [keyboard, layout] = event.parse(2)      // split into exactly 2 fields
            console.log(keyboard, "uses", layout)
        } else if (event.name === "urgent") {
            console.log("urgent window", event.data)
        }
    }
}

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onNameChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription

The name of the event.

See Hyprland Wiki: IPC for a list of events.

datastringconstant

The unparsed data of the event.

Functions#

parse(argumentCount: int): list<string>

Parse this event with a known number of arguments.

Argument count is required as some events can contain commas in the last argument, which can be ignored as long as the count is known.

Some events contain commas inside their last field (window titles), so you pass the expected field count and the rest stays together.

Example: every property#

Text {
    readonly property HyprlandMonitor m: Hyprland.monitorFor(screen)
    text: `#${m?.id} ${m?.name} "${m?.description}" ${m?.width}x${m?.height}@(${m?.x},${m?.y}) scale ${m?.scale}`
        + ` · focused ${m?.focused} · active ws ${m?.activeWorkspace?.id}`
        + ` · refresh ${m?.lastIpcObject?.refreshRate ?? "?"}Hz`
}

import Quickshell.Hyprland

How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (HyprlandWorkspaces must be retrieved from the HyprlandIpc object.). Quickshell gives you instances through: Hyprland.focusedWorkspace, Hyprland.workspaces, HyprlandMonitor.activeWorkspace, HyprlandToplevel.workspace.

Overview#

A Hyprland workspace, from Hyprland.workspaces, Hyprland.focusedWorkspace or HyprlandMonitor.activeWorkspace.

Example: every property and function#

Repeater {
    model: Hyprland.workspaces
    Text {
        required property HyprlandWorkspace modelData
        text: `${modelData.id} "${modelData.name}" @${modelData.address}`
            + (modelData.active ? " active" : "") + (modelData.focused ? " FOCUSED" : "")
            + (modelData.urgent ? " urgent" : "") + (modelData.hasFullscreen ? " fullscreen" : "")
            + ` · ${modelData.toplevels.values.length} windows on ${modelData.monitor?.name}`
            + ` · ${modelData.lastIpcObject?.windows ?? "?"} (ipc)`
        TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.activate() }
    }
}

Import
import Quickshell.Hyprland
Inherits

How to get one
This is an attached type: you use it as HyprlandToplevel.property on another object.

Overview#

A window as Hyprland sees it. From Hyprland.toplevels, HyprlandWorkspace.toplevels or Hyprland.activeToplevel. Its wayland property gives the generic Toplevel (for previews and activation).

From the upstream documentation#

Can also be used as an attached object of a Toplevel, to resolve a handle to an Hyprland toplevel.

Example: every property#

Repeater {
    model: Hyprland.toplevels
    Text {
        required property HyprlandToplevel modelData
        readonly property var ipc: modelData.lastIpcObject
        text: `0x${modelData.address} "${modelData.title}" class=${ipc?.class}`
            + ` ws=${modelData.workspace?.id} mon=${modelData.monitor?.name}`
            + (modelData.activated ? " ACTIVE" : "") + (modelData.urgent ? " urgent" : "")
            + ` at ${ipc?.at} size ${ipc?.size} floating ${ipc?.floating}`
        TapHandler { onTapped: Hyprland.dispatch("focuswindow address:0x" + modelData.address) }
    }
}
Component.onCompleted: Hyprland.refreshToplevels()     // fill lastIpcObject

Quickshell.Hyprland

Hyprland

singleton
Import
import Quickshell.Hyprland
Inherits
Hyprland → QtObject
How to get one
This is a singleton: exactly one exists, created by Quickshell. Use it from anywhere by its name, e.g. Hyprland.usingLua. Never write Hyprland { }.

Overview#

Everything about Hyprland: monitors, workspaces, windows, the focused ones, raw events, and running dispatchers. Data updates live from Hyprland's event socket.

Example: every property, function and signal#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Hyprland
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Layouts

FloatingWindow {
    implicitWidth: 600; implicitHeight: 500
    color: "#1e1e2e"
    ColumnLayout {
        anchors { fill: parent; margins: 14 }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "Lua config: " + Hyprland.usingLua }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "sockets: " + Hyprland.requestSocketPath + " | " + Hyprland.eventSocketPath }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "focused monitor: " + (Hyprland.focusedMonitor?.name ?? "-") }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "focused workspace: " + (Hyprland.focusedWorkspace?.name ?? "-") }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "active window: " + (Hyprland.activeToplevel?.title ?? "-") }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "monitors: " + Hyprland.monitors.values.map(m => m.name).join(", ") }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "workspaces: " + Hyprland.workspaces.values.map(w => w.id).join(", ") }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "windows: " + Hyprland.toplevels.values.length }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "this screen's monitor: " + (Hyprland.monitorFor(Quickshell.screens[0])?.description ?? "") }
        Text { color: "#89b4fa"; text: "[go to workspace 2]"; TapHandler { onTapped: Hyprland.dispatch("workspace 2") } }
        Text { color: "#89b4fa"; text: "[refresh all]"
               TapHandler { onTapped: { Hyprland.refreshMonitors(); Hyprland.refreshWorkspaces(); Hyprland.refreshToplevels() } } }
    }
    Connections {
        target: Hyprland
        function onRawEvent(event) { console.log(event.name, "→", event.data) }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onUsingLuaChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription

True if Hyprland is running in lua mode. Dispatcher syntax changes when using lua.

This property will be false until the Hyprland module is initialized.

Path to the request socket (.socket.sock)

Path to the event socket (.socket2.sock)

The currently focused hyprland monitor. May be null.

Sorted by id. Named and special workspaces have negative ids and come first; filter with w.id > 0. Only existing workspaces are listed.

All hyprland toplevels

Functions#

dispatch(request: string): void

Execute a hyprland dispatcher.

Runs any dispatcher, same syntax as hyprctl dispatch (e.g. "exec kitty", "movetoworkspace 3"). In Lua mode (usingLua) the syntax differs (e.g. hl.dsp.focus({ workspace = "3" })); prefer helper methods like HyprlandWorkspace.activate() which handle both.

monitorFor(screen: ShellScreen): HyprlandMonitor

Get the HyprlandMonitor object that corresponds to a quickshell screen.

refreshMonitors(): void

Refresh monitor information.

Many actions that will invalidate monitor state don't send events, so this function is available if required.

refreshWorkspaces(): void

Refresh workspace information.

Many actions that will invalidate workspace state don't send events, so this function is available if required.

refreshToplevels(): void

Refresh toplevel information.

Many actions that will invalidate workspace state don't send events, so this function is available if required.

Updates every window's lastIpcObject (position, size, class, floating…). Call it when you need fresh geometry, e.g. when opening an overview.

Signals#

rawEvent(event: HyprlandEvent)handler: onRawEvent

Emitted for every event that comes in through the hyprland event socket (socket2).

See Hyprland Wiki: IPC for a list of events.
