Talking to Your Compositor · HyprlandWorkspace · HyprlandMonitor · HyprlandToplevel

Quickshell.Hyprland

HyprlandFocusGrab

creatable

Input focus grabber

Import
import Quickshell.Hyprland
Inherits
HyprlandFocusGrab
How to get one
You create this type in QML: HyprlandFocusGrab { … }.

Overview#

Detects when the user clicks or focuses outside a set of your windows: the standard "click outside to close" for panels on Hyprland.

From the upstream documentation#

Object for managing input focus grabs via the hyprland_focus_grab_v1 wayland protocol.

When enabled, all of the windows listed in the windows property will receive input normally, and will retain keyboard focus even if the mouse is moved off of them. When areas of the screen that are not part of a listed window are clicked or touched, the grab will become inactive and emit the cleared signal.

This is useful for implementing dismissal of popup type windows.

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Hyprland
import QtQuick.Controls

ShellRoot {
  FloatingWindow {
    id: window

    Button {
      anchors.centerIn: parent
      text: grab.active ? "Remove exclusive focus" : "Take exclusive focus"
      onClicked: grab.active = !grab.active
    }

    HyprlandFocusGrab {
      id: grab
      windows: [ window ]
    }
  }
}

Example: every property and signal#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Hyprland
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    id: panel
    implicitWidth: 300; implicitHeight: 200
    visible: open
    property bool open: true
    HyprlandFocusGrab {
        windows: [panel]                   // clicks inside these are allowed (add your bar too)
        active: panel.open                 // grab only while open
        onCleared: panel.open = false      // user clicked elsewhere
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onActiveChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
activeboolread / write

If the focus grab is active. Defaults to false.

When set to true, an input grab will be created for the listed windows.

This property will change to false once the grab is dismissed. It will not change to true until the grab begins, which requires at least one visible window.

windowslist<QtObject>read / write

The list of windows to whitelist for input.

Signals#

cleared()handler: onCleared

Sent whenever the compositor clears the focus grab.

This may be in response to all windows being removed from the list or simultaneously hidden, in addition to a normal clear.

Quickshell.Hyprland

GlobalShortcut

creatable

Hyprland global shortcut.

Import
import Quickshell.Hyprland
Inherits
GlobalShortcut
How to get one
You create this type in QML: GlobalShortcut { … }.

Overview#

Registers a Hyprland global shortcut. You bind keys to it in Hyprland's config; pressing them notifies your shell instantly, with both press and release events.

From the upstream documentation#

Global shortcut implemented with hyprland_global_shortcuts_v1.

You can use this within hyprland as a global shortcut:

bind = <modifiers>, <key>, global, <appid>:<name>

See the wiki for details.

Watch out

The shortcuts protocol does not allow duplicate appid + name pairs. Within a single instance of quickshell this is handled internally, and both users will be notified, but multiple instances of quickshell or XDPH may collide.

If that happens, whichever client that tries to register the shortcuts last will crash.

Note

This type does not use the xdg-desktop-portal global shortcuts protocol, as it is not fully functional without flatpak and would cause a considerably worse user experience from other limitations. It will only work with Hyprland. Note that, as this type bypasses xdg-desktop-portal, XDPH is not required.

Example: every property and signal#

import Quickshell.Hyprland
import QtQuick

Scope {
    GlobalShortcut {
        id: sc
        appid: "myshell"                     // default "quickshell"
        name: "cheatsheet"                   // bind = SUPER, slash, global, myshell:cheatsheet
        description: "Show the cheatsheet while held"   // visible in `hyprctl globalshortcuts`
        triggerDescription: ""               // rarely used
        onPressed: console.log("down")
        onReleased: console.log("up")
    }
    Text { text: sc.pressed ? "held" : "not held" }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onPressedChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
pressedboolread-only

If the keybind is currently pressed.

appidstringread / write

The appid of the shortcut. Defaults to quickshell. You cannot change this at runtime.

If you have more than one shortcut we recommend subclassing GlobalShortcut to set this.

namestringread / write

The name of the shortcut. You cannot change this at runtime.

descriptionstringread / write

The description of the shortcut that appears in hyprctl globalshortcuts. You cannot change this at runtime.

triggerDescriptionstringread / write

Have not seen this used ever, but included for completeness. Safe to ignore.

Signals#

pressed()handler: onPressed

Fired when the keybind is pressed.

released()handler: onReleased

Fired when the keybind is released.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

appid and name can't change at runtime, and the pair must be unique across all running clients.

See also#

IPC, Keybinds and Sockets
Quickshell.Hyprland

HyprlandWindow

provided by Quickshellhas attached properties

Hyprland specific QsWindow properties.

Import
import Quickshell.Hyprland
Inherits
HyprlandWindow → QtObject
How to get one
This is an attached type: you use it as HyprlandWindow.property on another object.

Overview#

Hyprland-specific settings for your own windows, used as attached properties on a Quickshell window: overall opacity and a visible-region hint.

From the upstream documentation#

Allows setting hyprland specific window properties on a QsWindow or subclass, as an attached object.

Example

@@Quickshell.PopupWindow {
  // ...
  HyprlandWindow.opacity: 0.6 // any number or binding
}
Note

Requires at least hyprland 0.47.0, or [hyprland-surface-v1] support.

Example#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Hyprland
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    anchors { top: true; bottom: true; left: true; right: true }
    color: "transparent"
    HyprlandWindow.opacity: 0.95                          // multiplies the whole window
    HyprlandWindow.visibleMask: Region { item: panel }    // compositor may skip the rest
    mask: Region { item: panel }
    Rectangle { id: panel; width: 400; height: 300; anchors.centerIn: parent; color: "#1e1e2e" }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onOpacityChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
opacityrealread / write

A multiplier for the window's overall opacity, ranging from 1.0 to 0.0. Overall opacity includes the opacity of both the window content and visual effects such as blur that apply to it.

Default: 1.0

visibleMaskRegionread / write

A hint to the compositor that only certain regions of the surface should be rendered. This can be used to avoid rendering large empty regions of a window which can increase performance, especially if the window is blurred. The mask should include all pixels of the window that do not have an alpha value of 0.

I3IpcListener {
  subscriptions: ["input"]
  onIpcEvent: function (event) {
    handleInputEvent(event.data)
  }
}

Example#

I3IpcListener {
    subscriptions: ["window", "mode", "binding"]
    onIpcEvent: e => {
        const d = JSON.parse(e.data)
        if (e.type === "window" && d.change === "focus") console.log("focus →", d.container.name)
    }
}

How to get one

niri integration (noctalia-qs fork only): outputs, workspaces, windows, keyboard layouts, the overview state, raw events and actions.

Example: every property, function and signal#

import Quickshell.Niri
import QtQuick

Column {
    Text { text: "socket: " + Niri.socketPath }
    Text { text: "focused: " + (Niri.focusedWindow?.title ?? "-") }
    Text { text: "overview open: " + Niri.overviewActive }
    Text { text: "layout: " + Niri.currentKeyboardLayoutName + " (" + Niri.currentKeyboardLayoutIndex + " of " + Niri.keyboardLayoutNames.length + ")" }
    Text { text: "outputs: " + Niri.outputs.values.map(o => o.name).join(", ") }
    Text { text: "workspaces: " + Niri.workspaces.values.map(w => w.idx).join(" ") }
    Text { text: "windows: " + Niri.windows.values.length }
    Text { text: "[ws 2]"; TapHandler { onTapped: Niri.dispatch(["focus-workspace", "2"]) } }
    Text { text: "[overview]"; TapHandler { onTapped: Niri.dispatch(["toggle-overview"]) } }
    Text { text: "[refresh]"; TapHandler { onTapped: { Niri.refreshOutputs(); Niri.refreshWorkspaces(); Niri.refreshWindows() } } }
    Connections {
        target: Niri
        function onRawEvent(e) { console.log(e.type) }
        function onWorkspacesUpdated() { console.log("workspaces changed") }
        function onWindowsUpdated() {}
        function onOutputsUpdated() {}
        function onKeyboardLayoutSwitched() { console.log("layout →", Niri.currentKeyboardLayoutName) }
    }
}

Quickshell.WindowManager

WindowManager

singleton

Window management interfaces exposed by the window manager.

Import
import Quickshell.WindowManager
Inherits
WindowManager → QtObject
How to get one
This is a singleton: exactly one exists, created by Quickshell. Use it from anywhere by its name, e.g. WindowManager.windowsets. Never write WindowManager { }.

Overview#

A compositor-independent workspace API using the ext-workspace-v1 Wayland protocol. Workspaces (or tags) are Windowsets, grouped by the screens they cover (WindowsetProjection). Support depends on your compositor.

Example#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.WindowManager
import QtQuick

Row {
    spacing: 6
    Repeater {
        model: WindowManager.screenProjection(Quickshell.screens[0])?.windowsets ?? []
        Text {
            required property Windowset modelData
            visible: modelData.shouldDisplay
            text: modelData.name
            color: modelData.active ? "#cba6f7" : modelData.urgent ? "#f38ba8" : "white"
            TapHandler { enabled: modelData.canActivate; onTapped: modelData.activate() }
        }
    }
    Component.onCompleted: console.log("all windowsets:", WindowManager.windowsets.length,
                                       "projections:", WindowManager.windowsetProjections.length)
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onWindowsetsChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
windowsetslist<Windowset>read-only

All windowsets tracked by the WM across all projections.

windowsetProjectionslist<WindowsetProjection>read-only

All windowset projections tracked by the WM. Does not include internal projections from screenProjection().

Functions#

screenProjection(screen: ShellScreen): ScreenProjection

Returns an internal WindowsetProjection that covers a single screen and contains all windowsets on that screen, regardless of the WM-specified projection. Depending on how the WM lays out its actual projections, multiple ScreenProjections may contain the same Windowsets.

Quickshell.WindowManager

Windowset

provided by Quickshell

A group of windows worked with by a user, usually known as a Workspace or Tag.

Import
import Quickshell.WindowManager
Inherits
Windowset → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself. Quickshell gives you instances through: WindowManager.windowsets, WindowsetProjection.windowsets.

Overview#

A workspace or tag from WindowManager.

From the upstream documentation#

A Windowset is a generic type that encompasses both "Workspaces" and "Tags" in window managers. Because the definition encompasses both you may not necessarily need all features.

Example: every member#

Text {
    required property Windowset ws
    text: `${ws.name} [${ws.coordinates}] id=${ws.id} active=${ws.active} urgent=${ws.urgent}`
        + ` display=${ws.shouldDisplay} canActivate=${ws.canActivate} canDeactivate=${ws.canDeactivate}`
        + ` canRemove=${ws.canRemove} canSetProjection=${ws.canSetProjection}`
    TapHandler { onTapped: ws.activate() }                     // also: deactivate(), remove(), setProjection(p)
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onIdChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
idstringread-only

A persistent internal identifier for the windowset. This property should be identical across restarts and destruction/recreation of a windowset.

namestringread-only

Human readable name of the windowset.

coordinateslist<int>read-only

Coordinates of the workspace, represented as an N-dimensional array. Most WMs will only expose one coordinate. If more than one is exposed, the first is conventionally X, the second Y, and the third Z.

activeboolread-only

True if the windowset is currently active. In a workspace based WM, this means the represented workspace is current. In a tag based WM, this means the represented tag is active.

projectionWindowsetProjectionread-only

The projection this windowset is a member of. A projection is the set of screens covered by a windowset.

shouldDisplayboolread-only

If false, this windowset should generally be hidden from workspace pickers.

urgentboolread-only

If true, a window in this windowset has been marked as urgent.

canActivateboolread-only

If true, the windowset can be activated. In a workspace based WM, this will make the workspace current, in a tag based wm, the tag will be activated.

canDeactivateboolread-only

If true, the windowset can be deactivated. In a workspace based WM, deactivation is usually implicit and based on activation of another workspace.

canRemoveboolread-only

If true, the windowset can be removed. This may be done implicitly by the WM as well.

canSetProjectionboolread-only

If true, the windowset can be moved to a different projection.

Functions#

activate(): void

Activate the windowset, making it the current workspace on a workspace based WM, or activating the tag on a tag based WM. Requires canActivate.

deactivate(): void

Deactivate the windowset, hiding it. Requires canDeactivate.

remove(): void

Remove or destroy the windowset. Requires canRemove.

setProjection(projection: WindowsetProjection): void

Move the windowset to a different projection. A projection represents the set of screens a workspace spans. Requires canSetProjection.

Where this type appears#

  • WindowManager.windowsets (property)
  • WindowsetProjection.windowsets (property)

Quickshell.Services.Pipewire

Pipewire

singleton

Contains links to all pipewire objects.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
Inherits
Pipewire → QtObject
How to get one
This is a singleton: exactly one exists, created by Quickshell. Use it from anywhere by its name, e.g. Pipewire.nodes. Never write Pipewire { }.

Overview#

Access to the PipeWire audio graph: every node (speakers, microphones, app streams), the links between them, and the default input and output. It updates live; no polling.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Layouts

FloatingWindow {
    implicitWidth: 560; implicitHeight: 520
    color: "#1e1e2e"
    PwObjectTracker { objects: [Pipewire.defaultAudioSink, Pipewire.defaultAudioSource] }

    ColumnLayout {
        anchors { fill: parent; margins: 14 }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "ready: " + Pipewire.ready }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "default output: " + (Pipewire.defaultAudioSink?.description ?? "none") }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "default input: " + (Pipewire.defaultAudioSource?.description ?? "none") }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "nodes: " + Pipewire.nodes.values.length + " · links: " + Pipewire.links.values.length
                                   + " · link groups: " + Pipewire.linkGroups.values.length }
        Text { color: "#a6adc8"; text: "Outputs (click to make default):" }
        Repeater {
            model: Pipewire.nodes.values.filter(n => n.isSink && !n.isStream && n.audio)
            Text {
                required property PwNode modelData
                color: modelData === Pipewire.defaultAudioSink ? "#cba6f7" : "white"
                text: "  " + (modelData.description || modelData.name)
                TapHandler { onTapped: Pipewire.preferredDefaultAudioSink = modelData }
            }
        }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onNodesChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
nodesObjectModel<PwNode>constant

All nodes present in pipewire.

This list contains every node on the system. To find a useful subset, filtering with the following properties may be helpful: - PwNode.isStream - if the node is an application or hardware device. - PwNode.isSink - if the node is a sink or source. - PwNode.audio - if non null the node is an audio node.

Every node in the graph, including video and internal ones. Filter: isSink (accepts audio), isStream (an application, not hardware), audio !== null (has audio).

linksObjectModel<PwLink>constant

All links present in pipewire.

Links connect pipewire nodes to each other, and can be used to determine their relationship.

If you already have a node you want to check for connections to, use PwNodeLinkTracker instead of filtering this list.

Multiple links may exist between the same nodes. See linkGroups

for a deduplicated list containing only one entry per link between nodes.

linkGroupsObjectModel<PwLinkGroup>constant

All link groups present in pipewire.

The same as links but deduplicated.

If you already have a node you want to check for connections to, use PwNodeLinkTracker instead of filtering this list.

defaultAudioSinkPwNoderead-only

The default audio sink (output) or null.

This is the default sink currently in use by pipewire, and the one applications are currently using.

To set the default sink, use preferredDefaultAudioSink.

Note

When the default sink changes, this property may breifly become null. This depends on your hardware.

The output currently in use. To change it, set preferredDefaultAudioSink; this property then follows.

defaultAudioSourcePwNoderead-only

The default audio source (input) or null.

This is the default source currently in use by pipewire, and the one applications are currently using.

To set the default source, use preferredDefaultAudioSource.

Note

When the default source changes, this property may breifly become null. This depends on your hardware.

preferredDefaultAudioSinkPwNoderead / write

The preferred default audio sink (output) or null.

This is a hint to pipewire telling it which sink should be the default when possible. defaultAudioSink may differ when it is not possible for pipewire to pick this node.

See defaultAudioSink for the current default sink, regardless of preference.

preferredDefaultAudioSourcePwNoderead / write

The preferred default audio source (input) or null.

This is a hint to pipewire telling it which source should be the default when possible. defaultAudioSource may differ when it is not possible for pipewire to pick this node.

See defaultAudioSource for the current default source, regardless of preference.

readyboolread-only

This property is true if quickshell has completed its initial sync with the pipewire server. If true, nodes, links and sync/source preferences will be in a good state.

You can use the pipewire object before it is ready, but some nodes/links

may be missing, and preference metadata may be null.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

Remember PwObjectTracker: a node's audio properties are only valid while the node is tracked.

See also#

A Tour of the System Services · PwNode · PwNodeAudio

Quickshell.Services.Pipewire

PwNodeLinkTracker

creatable

Tracks non-monitor link connections to a given node.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
Inherits
PwNodeLinkTracker → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: PwNodeLinkTracker { … }.

Overview#

Tracks the link groups connected to one node, excluding monitor links. For a sink, that's the streams playing into it; for a source, the streams recording from it.

Example: apps playing on the default output#

import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
import QtQuick

Column {
    PwNodeLinkTracker { id: tracker; node: Pipewire.defaultAudioSink }
    Repeater {
        model: tracker.linkGroups
        Text {
            required property PwLinkGroup modelData
            text: modelData.source?.properties["application.name"] ?? modelData.source?.name ?? "?"
        }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onNodeChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
nodePwNoderead / write

The node to track connections to.

linkGroupslist<PwLinkGroup>read-only

Link groups connected to the given node, excluding monitors.

If the node is a sink, links which target the node will be tracked. If the node is a source, links which source the node will be tracked.

Quickshell.Services.Pipewire

PwNodeAudio

provided by Quickshell

Audio specific properties of pipewire nodes.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
Inherits
PwNodeAudio → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (PwNodeAudio cannot be created directly). Quickshell gives you instances through: PwNode.audio.

Overview#

The audio part of a PwNode (node.audio): volume and mute, overall and per channel.

From the upstream documentation#

Extra properties of a PwNode if the node is an audio node.

See PwNode.audio.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls

Column {
    readonly property PwNode sink: Pipewire.defaultAudioSink
    PwObjectTracker { objects: [sink] }

    Slider { from: 0; to: 1.5; value: sink?.audio?.volume ?? 0; onMoved: sink.audio.volume = value }   // average of all channels
    CheckBox { text: "muted"; checked: sink?.audio?.muted ?? false; onToggled: sink.audio.muted = checked }
    Repeater {                                                                // per-channel volumes
        model: sink?.audio?.channels ?? []
        Row {
            required property int index
            required property var modelData                                   // PwAudioChannel value
            Text { text: PwAudioChannel.toString(modelData) }
            Slider {
                from: 0; to: 1
                value: sink.audio.volumes[index]
                onMoved: { const v = [...sink.audio.volumes]; v[index] = value; sink.audio.volumes = v }  // assign a new list
            }
        }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onMutedChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
mutedboolread / write

If the node is currently muted. Setting this property changes the mute state.

Watch out

This property is invalid unless the node is bound using PwObjectTracker.

volumerealread / write

The average volume over all channels of the node. Setting this property modifies the volume of all channels proportionately.

Watch out

This property is invalid unless the node is bound using PwObjectTracker.

Can be set above 1.0 (amplification). Clamp it in your UI, e.g. to 1.5.

channelslist<PwAudioChannel>read-only

The audio channels present on the node.

Watch out

This property is invalid unless the node is bound using PwObjectTracker.

volumeslist<real>read / write

The volumes of each audio channel individually. Each entry corresponds to the volume of the channel at the same index in channels. volumes and channels will always be the same length.

Watch out

This property is invalid unless the node is bound using PwObjectTracker.

Where this type appears#

  • PwNode.audio (property)
Quickshell.Services.Pipewire

PwNode

provided by Quickshell

A node in the pipewire connection graph.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
Inherits
PwNode → PwObjectIface
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (PwNodes cannot be created directly). Quickshell gives you instances through: Pipewire.defaultAudioSink, Pipewire.defaultAudioSource, Pipewire.nodes, Pipewire.preferredDefaultAudioSink, Pipewire.preferredDefaultAudioSource, PwLink.source, PwLink.target, PwLinkGroup.source, PwLinkGroup.target, PwNodeLinkTracker.node, PwNodePeakMonitor.node.

Overview#

One node in the PipeWire graph: a device (speakers, headphones, microphone) or an application stream (Firefox playing sound). Get them from Pipewire.nodes, Pipewire.defaultAudioSink and friends.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
import QtQuick

Column {
    readonly property PwNode n: Pipewire.defaultAudioSink
    PwObjectTracker { objects: [n] }
    Text { text: "id " + n?.id + " · name " + n?.name }                // name = node.name (machine id)
    Text { text: "description: " + n?.description }                    // human readable
    Text { text: "nickname: " + n?.nickname }
    Text { text: "isSink " + n?.isSink + " · isStream " + n?.isStream + " · ready " + n?.ready }
    Text { text: "type: " + PwNodeType.toString(n?.type) }
    Text { text: "volume: " + Math.round((n?.audio?.volume ?? 0) * 100) + "%  muted " + n?.audio?.muted }
    Text { text: "app: " + (n?.properties["application.name"] ?? "-") }   // any PipeWire property
    Text { text: "media.class: " + (n?.properties["media.class"] ?? "-") }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onIdChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
idintconstant

The pipewire object id of the node.

Mainly useful for debugging. You can inspect the node directly with pw-cli i <id>.

namestringconstant

The node's name, corresponding to the object's node.name property.

descriptionstringconstant

The node's description, corresponding to the object's node.description property.

May be empty. Generally more human readable than name.

nicknamestringconstant

The node's nickname, corresponding to the object's node.nickname property.

May be empty. Generally but not always more human readable than description.

isSinkboolconstant

If true, then the node accepts audio input from other nodes, if false the node outputs audio to other nodes.

isStreamboolconstant

If true then the node is likely to be a program, if false it is likely to be a hardware device.

typePwNodeTypeconstant

The type of this node. Reflects Pipewire's media.class.

propertiesobjectread-only

The property set present on the node, as an object containing key-value pairs. You can inspect this directly with pw-cli i <id>.

A few properties of note, which may or may not be present: - application.name - A suggested human readable name for the node. - application.icon-name - The name of an icon recommended to display for the node. - media.name - A description of the currently playing media. (more likely to be present than media.title and media.artist) - media.title - The title of the currently playing media. - media.artist - The artist of the currently playing media.

Watch out

This property is invalid unless the node is bound using PwObjectTracker.

All PipeWire properties as an object, e.g. application.name, application.icon-name, media.name, node.nick. Inspect them with pw-cli info <id>.

audioPwNodeAudioconstant

Extra information present only if the node sends or receives audio.

The presence or absence of this property can be used to determine if a node manages audio, regardless of if it is bound. If non null, the node is an audio node.

null for nodes without audio. Its values are only valid while the node is bound with PwObjectTracker.

readyboolread-only

True if the node is fully bound and ready to use.

The node may be used before it is fully bound, but some data

may be missing or incorrect.

PwLink

provided by Quickshell

A connection between pipewire nodes.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
Inherits
PwLink → PwObjectIface
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (PwLinks cannot be created directly). Quickshell gives you instances through: Pipewire.links.

Overview#

A single connection between two nodes (one channel). source sends audio, target receives. From Pipewire.links. Usually PwLinkGroup is more useful.

From the upstream documentation#

Note that there is one link per channel of a connection between nodes. You usually want PwLinkGroup.

Example#

Repeater {
    model: Pipewire.links
    Text {
        required property PwLink modelData
        text: `${modelData.id}: ${modelData.source?.name} → ${modelData.target?.name} (${PwLinkState.toString(modelData.state)})`
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onIdChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
idintconstant

The pipewire object id of the link.

Mainly useful for debugging. you can inspect the link directly with pw-cli i <id>.

targetPwNodeconstant

The node that is receiving information. (the sink)

sourcePwNodeconstant

The node that is sending information. (the source)

statePwLinkStateread-only

The current state of the link.

Watch out

This property is invalid unless the node is bound using PwObjectTracker.

PwLinkGroup

provided by Quickshell

A group of connections between pipewire nodes.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
Inherits
PwLinkGroup
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (PwLinkGroups cannot be created directly). Quickshell gives you instances through: Pipewire.linkGroups, PwNodeLinkTracker.linkGroups.

Overview#

All channels between two nodes, merged into one connection. From Pipewire.linkGroups or PwNodeLinkTracker.linkGroups. Use it to answer questions like "which apps are playing into my headphones?" or "is any app recording from my microphone?".

From the upstream documentation#

, one per source->target pair.

Example: microphone-in-use indicator#

import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
import QtQuick

Text {
    readonly property var recorders: Pipewire.linkGroups.values
        .filter(g => g.source === Pipewire.defaultAudioSource && g.target?.isStream)
        .map(g => g.target.properties["application.name"] ?? g.target.name)
    visible: recorders.length > 0
    text: "🎙 " + recorders.join(", ")
    color: "#f38ba8"
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onTargetChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
targetPwNodeconstant

The node that is receiving information. (the sink)

sourcePwNodeconstant

The node that is sending information. (the source)

statePwLinkStateread-only

The current state of the link group.

Watch out

This property is invalid unless the node is bound using PwObjectTracker.

Where this type appears#

  • Pipewire.linkGroups (property)
  • PwNodeLinkTracker.linkGroups (property)
Quickshell.Services.Pipewire

PwObjectTracker

creatable

Binds pipewire objects.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
Inherits
PwObjectTracker → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: PwObjectTracker { … }.

Overview#

Binds PipeWire objects so their detailed properties (a node's audio, a link's state) become valid and live. Without it, node.audio.volume reads 0 and writes do nothing. Put every node you read or control into objects.

From the upstream documentation#

PwObjectTracker binds every node given in its objects list.

Object Binding

By default, pipewire objects are unbound. Unbound objects only have a subset of information available for use or modification. Binding an object makes all of its properties available for use or modification if applicable.

Properties that require their object be bound to use are clearly marked. You do not need to bind the object unless mentioned in the description of the property you want to use.

Example#

import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
import QtQuick

Item {
    readonly property var streams: Pipewire.nodes.values.filter(n => n.isStream && n.audio)
    PwObjectTracker { objects: [Pipewire.defaultAudioSink, Pipewire.defaultAudioSource, ...streams] }   // nulls are fine
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onObjectsChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
objectslist<QtObject>read / write

The list of objects to bind. May contain nulls.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

Tracking is cheap. A tracker anywhere in your shell (e.g. in your Audio service) is enough for all users of those nodes.

Quickshell.Services.Pipewire

PwNodePeakMonitor

creatable

Monitors peak levels of an audio node.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
Inherits
PwNodePeakMonitor → QtObject
How to get one
You create this type in QML: PwNodePeakMonitor { … }.

Overview#

Measures the live peak level of an audio node, per channel, from 0.0 to 1.0. That's a VU meter with no external program (unlike cava).

From the upstream documentation#

Tracks volume peaks for a node across all its channels.

The peak monitor binds nodes similarly to PwObjectTracker when enabled.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell.Services.Pipewire
import QtQuick

Row {
    spacing: 3
    PwNodePeakMonitor {
        id: peak
        node: Pipewire.defaultAudioSink      // must be an audio node
        enabled: parent.visible              // stop capturing when hidden
    }
    Repeater {
        model: peak.peaks                    // one value per channel (volume doesn't affect it)
        Rectangle {
            required property real modelData
            required property int index
            width: 8; height: 60 * modelData; anchors.bottom: parent.bottom
            color: "#a6e3a1"
            Text { anchors.top: parent.bottom; text: PwAudioChannel.toString(peak.channels[index]); font.pixelSize: 8 }
        }
    }
    Text { text: "max " + peak.peak.toFixed(2) }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onNodeChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
nodePwNoderead / write

The node to monitor. Must be an audio node.

enabledboolread / write

If true, the monitor is actively capturing and computing peaks. Defaults to true.

peakslist<real>read-only

Per-channel peak noise levels (0.0-1.0). Length matches channels.

The channel's volume does not affect this property.

peakrealread-only

Maximum value of peaks.

channelslist<PwAudioChannel>read-only

Channel positions for the captured format. Length matches peaks.

MprisPlayer

provided by Quickshell

A media player exposed over MPRIS.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Mpris
Inherits
MprisPlayer → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (MprisPlayers can only be acquired from Mpris). Quickshell gives you instances through: Mpris.players.

Overview#

One media player. Read the current track's metadata and playback state, and control playback. Get players from Mpris.players.

From the upstream documentation#

Support for various functionality and general compliance to

the MPRIS specification varies wildly by player. Always check the associated canXyz and xyzSupported properties if available.

The TrackList and Playlist interfaces were not implemented as we could not

find any media players using them to test against.

Example: every property and function#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Mpris
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls
import QtQuick.Layouts

FloatingWindow {
    implicitWidth: 560; implicitHeight: 640
    color: "#1e1e2e"
    readonly property MprisPlayer p: Mpris.players.values[0] ?? null

    // position isn't pushed continuously: refresh it while playing
    Timer { running: p?.isPlaying ?? false; interval: 1000; repeat: true; onTriggered: p.positionChanged() }

    ColumnLayout {
        anchors { fill: parent; margins: 14 }
        visible: p !== null
        spacing: 3
        // ---- identity ----
        Text { color: "white"; text: "identity: " + p?.identity + " · desktopEntry: " + p?.desktopEntry + " · dbus: " + p?.dbusName }
        // ---- track ----
        Image { source: p?.trackArtUrl ?? ""; Layout.preferredWidth: 120; Layout.preferredHeight: 120; fillMode: Image.PreserveAspectCrop }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "title: " + (p?.trackTitle || "Unknown title") }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "artist: " + (p?.trackArtist || "Unknown artist") }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "album: " + p?.trackAlbum + " · album artist: " + p?.trackAlbumArtist }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "uniqueId: " + p?.uniqueId + " · metadata keys: " + Object.keys(p?.metadata ?? {}).join(", ") }
        // ---- position ----
        Slider {
            Layout.fillWidth: true
            enabled: (p?.canSeek ?? false) && (p?.positionSupported ?? false)
            from: 0; to: p?.lengthSupported ? p.length : 1
            value: p?.position ?? 0
            onMoved: p.position = value                     // seconds
        }
        Text { color: "white"; text: `position ${p?.position?.toFixed(1)}s / length ${p?.length?.toFixed(1)}s` }
        // ---- state ----
        Text { color: "white"; text: "state: " + MprisPlaybackState.toString(p?.playbackState) + " · isPlaying " + p?.isPlaying }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "loop: " + MprisLoopState.toString(p?.loopState) + " (supported " + p?.loopSupported + ")" }
        Text { color: "white"; text: "shuffle: " + p?.shuffle + " (supported " + p?.shuffleSupported + ")" }
        Text { color: "white"; text: `rate ${p?.rate} (min ${p?.minRate}, max ${p?.maxRate}) · fullscreen ${p?.fullscreen}` }
        Slider { from: 0; to: 1; enabled: p?.volumeSupported ?? false; value: p?.volume ?? 1; onMoved: p.volume = value }
        // ---- capabilities ----
        Text { color: "#a6adc8"; text: `canControl ${p?.canControl} canPlay ${p?.canPlay} canPause ${p?.canPause} canTogglePlaying ${p?.canTogglePlaying}` }
        Text { color: "#a6adc8"; text: `canSeek ${p?.canSeek} canGoNext ${p?.canGoNext} canGoPrevious ${p?.canGoPrevious} canQuit ${p?.canQuit} canRaise ${p?.canRaise} canSetFullscreen ${p?.canSetFullscreen}` }
        Text { color: "#a6adc8"; text: "uri schemes: " + p?.supportedUriSchemes.join(",") + " · mime: " + p?.supportedMimeTypes.length }
        // ---- controls ----
        RowLayout {
            Button { text: "⏮"; enabled: p?.canGoPrevious ?? false; onClicked: p.previous() }
            Button { text: "-10s"; onClicked: p.seek(-10) }
            Button { text: p?.isPlaying ? "⏸" : "▶"; onClicked: p.togglePlaying() }   // or play() / pause()
            Button { text: "⏹"; onClicked: p.stop() }
            Button { text: "+10s"; onClicked: p.seek(10) }
            Button { text: "⏭"; enabled: p?.canGoNext ?? false; onClicked: p.next() }
            Button { text: "raise"; enabled: p?.canRaise ?? false; onClicked: p.raise() }
            Button { text: "quit"; enabled: p?.canQuit ?? false; onClicked: p.quit() }
        }
    }
    Connections { target: p; function onTrackChanged() { console.log("new track:", p.trackTitle) } }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onCanControlChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
canControlboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
canPlayboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
canPauseboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
canTogglePlayingboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
canSeekboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
canGoNextboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
canGoPreviousboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
canQuitboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
canRaiseboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
canSetFullscreenboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
identitystringread-only

The human readable name of the media player.

desktopEntrystringread-only

The name of the desktop entry for the media player, or an empty string if not provided.

dbusNamestringconstant

The DBus service name of the player.

positionrealread / write

The current position in the playing track, as seconds, with millisecond precision, or 0 if positionSupported is false.

May only be written to if canSeek and positionSupported are true.

To avoid excessive property updates wasting CPU while position is not

actively monitored, position usually will not update reactively, unless a nonlinear change in position occurs, however reading it will always return the current position.

If you want to actively monitor the position, the simplest way it to emit the positionChanged(s) signal manually for the duration you are monitoring it, Using a FrameAnimation if you need the value to update smoothly, such as on a slider, or a Timer if not, as shown below.

FrameAnimation {
  // only emit the signal when the position is actually changing.
  running: player.playbackState == MprisPlaybackState.Playing
  // emit the positionChanged signal every frame.
  onTriggered: player.positionChanged()
}
Timer {
  // only emit the signal when the position is actually changing.
  running: player.playbackState == MprisPlaybackState.Playing
  // Make sure the position updates at least once per second.
  interval: 1000
  repeat: true
  // emit the positionChanged signal every second.
  onTriggered: player.positionChanged()
}

In seconds. Not updated continuously (for efficiency): call positionChanged() on a Timer while playing to make bindings refresh. Setting it seeks (if canSeek).

positionSupportedboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
lengthrealread-only

The length of the playing track, as seconds, with millisecond precision, or the value of position if lengthSupported is false.

lengthSupportedboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
volumerealread / write

The volume of the playing track from 0.0 to 1.0, or 1.0 if volumeSupported is false.

May only be written to if canControl and volumeSupported are true.

volumeSupportedboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
metadataobjectread-only

Metadata of the current track.

A map of common properties is available here. Do not count on any of them actually being present.

Note that the trackTitle, trackAlbum, trackAlbumArtist, trackArtist and trackArtUrl properties have extra logic to guard against bad players sending weird metadata, and should be used over grabbing the properties directly from the metadata.

uniqueIdintread-only

An opaque identifier for the current track unique within the current player.

This is NOT mpris:trackid as that is sometimes missing or nonunique

in some players.

trackTitlestringread-only

The title of the current track, or "" if none was provided.

Use player.trackTitle || "Unknown Title" to provide a message

when no title is available.

Empty string if the player didn't provide one: p.trackTitle || "Unknown title".

trackArtiststringread-only

The current track's artist, or an "" if none was provided.

Use player.trackArtist || "Unknown Artist" to provide a message

when no artist is available.

trackArtistsstringread-only

[!ERROR] deprecated in favor of trackArtist.

trackAlbumstringread-only

The current track's album, or "" if none was provided.

Use player.trackAlbum || "Unknown Album" to provide a message

when no album is available.

trackAlbumArtiststringread-only

The current track's album artist, or "" if none was provided.

Use player.trackAlbumArtist || "Unknown Album" to provide a message

when no album artist is available.

trackArtUrlstringread-only

The current track's art url, or "" if none was provided.

Can be file://, http(s):// or empty. Images load asynchronously; show a placeholder.

playbackStateMprisPlaybackStateread / write

The playback state of the media player.

  • If canPlay is false, you cannot assign the Playing state.
  • If canPause is false, you cannot assign the Paused state.
  • If canControl is false, you cannot assign the Stopped state. (or any of the others, though their repsective properties will also be false)
isPlayingboolread / write

True if playbackState == MprisPlaybackState.Playing.

Setting this property is equivalent to calling play() or pause(). You cannot set this property if canTogglePlaying is false.

loopStateMprisLoopStateread / write

The loop state of the media player, or None if loopSupported is false.

May only be written to if canControl and loopSupported are true.

loopSupportedboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
raterealread / write

The speed the song is playing at, as a multiplier.

Only values between minRate and maxRate (inclusive) may be written to the property. Additionally, It is recommended that you only write common values such as 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0 to the property, as media players are free to ignore the value, and are more likely to accept common ones.

minRaterealread-onlyNo upstream description.
maxRaterealread-onlyNo upstream description.
shuffleboolread / write

If the play queue is currently being shuffled, or false if shuffleSupported is false.

May only be written if canControl and shuffleSupported are true.

shuffleSupportedboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
fullscreenboolread / write

If the player is currently shown in fullscreen.

May only be written to if canSetFullscreen is true.

supportedUriSchemeslist<string>read-only

Uri schemes supported by openUri().

supportedMimeTypeslist<string>read-only

Mime types supported by openUri().

Functions#

raise(): void

Bring the media player to the front of the window stack.

May only be called if canRaise is true.

quit(): void

Quit the media player.

May only be called if canQuit is true.

openUri(uri: string): void

Open the given URI in the media player.

Many players will silently ignore this, especially if the uri does not match supportedUriSchemes and supportedMimeTypes.

next(): void

Play the next song.

May only be called if canGoNext is true.

previous(): void

Play the previous song, or go back to the beginning of the current one.

May only be called if canGoPrevious is true.

seek(offset: real): void

Change position by an offset.

Even if positionSupported is false and you cannot set position, this function may work.

May only be called if canSeek is true.

play(): void

Equivalent to setting playbackState to Playing.

pause(): void

Equivalent to setting playbackState to Paused.

stop(): void

Equivalent to setting playbackState to Stopped.

togglePlaying(): void

Equivalent to calling play() if not playing or pause() if playing.

May only be called if canTogglePlaying is true, which is equivalent to canPlay or canPause depending on the current playback state.

Signals#

trackChanged()handler: onTrackChanged

The track has changed.

All track information properties that were sent by the player will be updated immediately following this signal. postTrackChanged will be sent after they update.

Track information properties: uniqueId, metadata, trackTitle, trackArtist, trackAlbum, trackAlbumArtist, trackArtUrl

Some particularly poorly behaved players will update metadata

before indicating the track has changed.

Emitted when the track changes; postTrackChanged comes after all track properties are updated.

postTrackChanged()handler: onPostTrackChanged

Sent after track info related properties have been updated, following trackChanged.

It is not safe to assume all track information is up to date after

this signal is emitted. A large number of players will update track information, particularly trackArtUrl, slightly after this signal.

Where this type appears#

  • Mpris.players (property)

See also#

Project: Media Player · MprisPlaybackState · MprisLoopState

Quickshell.Services.Mpris

Mpris

singleton
Import
import Quickshell.Services.Mpris
Inherits
Mpris → QtObject
How to get one
This is a singleton: exactly one exists, created by Quickshell. Use it from anywhere by its name, e.g. Mpris.players. Never write Mpris { }.

Overview#

Lists every media player that speaks MPRIS: Spotify, Firefox and Chromium tabs, mpv, VLC, music players. Each is an MprisPlayer.

Example#

import Quickshell.Services.Mpris
import QtQuick

Column {
    Text { text: Mpris.players.values.length + " players" }
    Repeater {
        model: Mpris.players
        Text { required property MprisPlayer modelData; text: modelData.identity + (modelData.isPlaying ? " ▶" : "") }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onPlayersChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
playersObjectModel<MprisPlayer>constant

All connected MPRIS players.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

Pick the "active" player with Mpris.players.values.find(p => p.isPlaying) ?? Mpris.players.values[0].

Quickshell.Services.UPower

UPower

singleton

Provides access to the UPower service.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.UPower
Inherits
UPower → QtObject
How to get one
This is a singleton: exactly one exists, created by Quickshell. Use it from anywhere by its name, e.g. UPower.displayDevice. Never write UPower { }.

Overview#

Access to the UPower service: your combined battery (displayDevice), every power device (devices), and whether you're on battery.

From the upstream documentation#

An interface to the UPower daemon, which can be used to view battery and power statistics for your computer and connected devices.

The UPower daemon must be installed to use this service.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell.Services.UPower
import QtQuick

Column {
    Text { text: "on battery: " + UPower.onBattery }
    Text { text: "battery: " + Math.round(UPower.displayDevice.percentage * 100) + "% (" + UPowerDeviceState.toString(UPower.displayDevice.state) + ")" }
    Repeater {
        model: UPower.devices
        Text { required property UPowerDevice modelData; text: UPowerDeviceType.toString(modelData.type) + " " + modelData.model }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onDisplayDeviceChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
displayDeviceUPowerDeviceconstant

UPower's DisplayDevice for your system. Cannot be null, but might not be initialized (check UPowerDevice.ready if you need to know).

This is an aggregate device and not a physical one, meaning you will not find it in devices. It is typically the device that is used for displaying information in desktop environments.

devicesObjectModel<UPowerDevice>constant

All connected UPower devices.

onBatteryboolread-only

If the system is currently running on battery power, or discharging.

See also#

UPowerDevice · PowerProfiles

Quickshell.Services.UPower

UPowerDevice

provided by Quickshell

A device exposed through the UPower system service.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.UPower
Inherits
UPowerDevice → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (UPowerDevices can only be acquired from UPower). Quickshell gives you instances through: UPower.devices, UPower.displayDevice.

Overview#

A UPowerDevice is one thing that has a battery or supplies power: your laptop battery, the AC adapter, a wireless mouse, a Bluetooth headset, a game controller, a UPS. Quickshell reads these from the UPower system service over D-Bus, so you get live updates without running any command or polling anything.

You never create a UPowerDevice yourself. You get them from the UPower singleton:

Where What you get
UPower.displayDevice One combined "virtual" battery for your whole system. Use this for a bar battery icon. On laptops with two batteries it combines them.
UPower.devices Every real device UPower knows: each battery, the AC adapter, mice, keyboards, headsets…

Everything on this page is read-only. You can read the numbers and react to changes, but you can't change them (you can't "set" a battery to 100%).

Requirements

The upower daemon must be running (systemctl status upower). It ships with almost every desktop distro. Install it with sudo pacman -S upower if it's missing.

Example: a battery widget that uses every property#

This complete file shows every property of UPowerDevice in a small dashboard card. Save it as ~/.config/quickshell/battery-test/shell.qml and run qs -c battery-test.

~/.config/quickshell/battery-test/shell.qmlimport Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.UPower
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Layouts

FloatingWindow {
    implicitWidth: 520
    implicitHeight: 640
    color: "#1e1e2e"

    // The combined system battery. Swap this for any entry of UPower.devices.
    readonly property UPowerDevice bat: UPower.displayDevice

    // helper: seconds -> "1 h 23 min"
    function duration(sec: real): string {
        if (sec <= 0) return "—"
        const h = Math.floor(sec / 3600), m = Math.round((sec % 3600) / 60)
        return h > 0 ? `${h} h ${m} min` : `${m} min`
    }

    ColumnLayout {
        anchors.fill: parent
        anchors.margins: 20
        spacing: 6

        component Row2: RowLayout {
            property string label
            property string value
            Text { text: parent.label; color: "#a6adc8"; Layout.preferredWidth: 190 }
            Text { text: parent.value; color: "#cdd6f4"; font.bold: true; Layout.fillWidth: true; elide: Text.ElideRight }
        }

        // --- is it real and ready? ----------------------------------------
        Row2 { label: "ready";            value: bat.ready }             // statistics loaded yet?
        Row2 { label: "isLaptopBattery";  value: bat.isLaptopBattery }   // true on laptops, false on desktops
        Row2 { label: "isPresent";        value: bat.isPresent }         // battery physically inserted?
        Row2 { label: "powerSupply";      value: bat.powerSupply }       // powers the computer itself?

        // --- what kind of device ------------------------------------------
        Row2 { label: "type";             value: UPowerDeviceType.toString(bat.type) }
        Row2 { label: "model";            value: bat.model || "(none)" }
        Row2 { label: "nativePath";       value: bat.nativePath || "(virtual)" }
        Row2 { label: "iconName";         value: bat.iconName }

        // --- charge level ---------------------------------------------------
        Row2 { label: "percentage";       value: Math.round(bat.percentage * 100) + " %" }
        Row2 { label: "energy";           value: bat.energy.toFixed(1) + " Wh" }
        Row2 { label: "energyCapacity";   value: bat.energyCapacity.toFixed(1) + " Wh" }
        Row2 { label: "changeRate";       value: bat.changeRate.toFixed(1) + " W" }

        // --- state and time -------------------------------------------------
        Row2 { label: "state";            value: UPowerDeviceState.toString(bat.state) }
        Row2 { label: "timeToEmpty";      value: duration(bat.timeToEmpty) }
        Row2 { label: "timeToFull";       value: duration(bat.timeToFull) }

        // --- health -----------------------------------------------------------
        Row2 { label: "healthSupported";  value: bat.healthSupported }
        Row2 { label: "healthPercentage"; value: bat.healthSupported ? Math.round(bat.healthPercentage) + " %" : "n/a" }

        // --- a visual bar driven by the same data ---------------------------
        Rectangle {
            Layout.fillWidth: true
            Layout.topMargin: 14
            implicitHeight: 26
            radius: 13
            color: "#313244"
            Rectangle {
                width: parent.width * bat.percentage
                height: parent.height
                radius: 13
                color: bat.state === UPowerDeviceState.Charging ? "#a6e3a1"
                     : bat.percentage < 0.15 ? "#f38ba8" : "#89b4fa"
                Behavior on width { NumberAnimation { duration: 400 } }
            }
        }
    }

    // React to a change (every property has an xxxChanged signal):
    Connections {
        target: bat
        function onStateChanged() {
            console.log("battery state is now", UPowerDeviceState.toString(bat.state))
        }
    }
}

How it works, line by line:

  • import Quickshell.Services.UPower makes UPower, UPowerDevice, UPowerDeviceState and UPowerDeviceType available.
  • readonly property UPowerDevice bat: UPower.displayDevice stores the device in a typed property, so the rest of the file can say bat.percentage instead of UPower.displayDevice.percentage.
  • bat.percentage is a number from 0.0 to 1.0, so multiply by 100 to display it.
  • bat.state is an enum number. UPowerDeviceState.toString() turns it into text like "Charging". Compare with UPowerDeviceState.Charging in conditions.
  • Every Text uses a binding: when UPower reports a new value, only that text updates. There's no timer anywhere.

Example: the bar battery icon you will actually use#

modules/bar/BatteryIndicator.qmlimport QtQuick
import Quickshell.Services.UPower

Row {
    id: root
    readonly property UPowerDevice bat: UPower.displayDevice
    readonly property bool charging: bat.state === UPowerDeviceState.Charging
                                  || bat.state === UPowerDeviceState.PendingCharge
    readonly property bool full: bat.state === UPowerDeviceState.FullyCharged
    readonly property int pct: Math.round(bat.percentage * 100)

    visible: bat.isLaptopBattery          // hide completely on desktops
    spacing: 4

    Text {
        // Material Symbols icon names: battery_0_bar … battery_6_bar, battery_full, battery_charging_full
        font.family: "Material Symbols Rounded"
        font.pixelSize: 18
        text: root.charging ? "battery_charging_full"
            : root.full ? "battery_full"
            : "battery_" + Math.min(6, Math.floor(root.pct / 15)) + "_bar"
        color: root.pct <= 15 && !root.charging ? "#f38ba8" : "#cdd6f4"
    }
    Text {
        text: root.pct + "%"
        color: "#cdd6f4"
        anchors.verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter
    }
}

Example: list every device (mouse, headset, controller batteries)#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.UPower
import QtQuick

Column {
    spacing: 4
    Repeater {
        // UPower.devices is an ObjectModel: pass it straight to a Repeater
        model: UPower.devices
        Text {
            required property UPowerDevice modelData
            // skip the AC adapter (LinePower) because it has no percentage
            visible: modelData.type !== UPowerDeviceType.LinePower
            text: `${UPowerDeviceType.toString(modelData.type)} ${modelData.model}: ${Math.round(modelData.percentage * 100)}%`
            color: "white"
        }
    }
}

Example: low-battery notification#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.UPower
import QtQuick

Scope {
    readonly property UPowerDevice bat: UPower.displayDevice
    property bool warned: false

    Connections {
        target: bat
        function onPercentageChanged() {
            const discharging = bat.state === UPowerDeviceState.Discharging
            if (discharging && bat.percentage <= 0.10 && !warned) {
                warned = true
                Quickshell.execDetached(["notify-send", "-u", "critical", "Battery low",
                                         Math.round(bat.percentage * 100) + "% remaining"])
            }
            if (bat.percentage > 0.15) warned = false     // re-arm after charging
        }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onTypeChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
typeUPowerDeviceTyperead-only

The type of device.

Compare against UPowerDeviceType values, e.g. UPowerDeviceType.Battery, UPowerDeviceType.Mouse, UPowerDeviceType.Headset.

powerSupplyboolread-only

If the device is a power supply for your computer and can provide charge.

energyrealread-only

Current energy level of the device in watt-hours.

energyCapacityrealread-only

Maximum energy capacity of the device in watt-hours

changeRaterealread-only

Rate of energy change in watts (positive when charging, negative when discharging).

timeToEmptyrealread-only

Estimated time until the device is fully discharged, in seconds.

Will be set to 0 if charging.

In seconds. 0 means "unknown" or "currently charging".

timeToFullrealread-only

Estimated time until the device is fully charged, in seconds.

Will be set to 0 if discharging.

In seconds. 0 means "unknown" or "currently discharging".

percentagerealread-only

Current charge level as a percentage.

This would be equivalent to energy / energyCapacity.

Range 0.0 – 1.0 (not 0–100). Show it with Math.round(bat.percentage * 100) + "%".

isPresentboolread-only

If the power source is present in the bay or slot, useful for hot-removable batteries.

If the device type is not Battery, then the property will be invalid.

stateUPowerDeviceStateread-only

Current state of the device.

Compare against UPowerDeviceState values: bat.state === UPowerDeviceState.Charging. Show text with UPowerDeviceState.toString(bat.state).

healthPercentagerealread-only

Health of the device as a percentage of its original health.

healthSupportedboolread-onlyNo upstream description.
iconNamestringread-only

Name of the icon representing the current state of the device, or an empty string if not provided.

A freedesktop icon name such as battery-good-charging-symbolic. Show it with IconImage: source: Quickshell.iconPath(bat.iconName).

isLaptopBatteryboolread-only

If the device is a laptop battery or not. Use this to check if your device is a valid battery.

This will be equivalent to type == Battery && powerSupply == true.

The safest single check for "should I show a battery icon at all?". It's false on desktop PCs.

nativePathstringread-only

Native path of the device specific to your OS.

modelstringread-only

Model name of the device. Unlikely to be useful for internal devices.

readyboolread-only

If device statistics have been queried for this device yet. This will be true for all devices returned from UPower.devices, but not the default device, which may be returned before it is ready to avoid returning null.

UPower.displayDevice is returned immediately (never null), but its numbers may still be zero for a split second at startup. Check ready if a flash of "0%" bothers you.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

  • Desktop PCs: UPower.displayDevice still exists but isLaptopBattery is false and percentage is 0. Always gate your UI on isLaptopBattery.
  • The AC adapter is a separate device of type LinePower. To know if you're plugged in, check UPower.onBattery instead.
  • Wireless peripherals (Logitech mice, many Bluetooth headsets, Xbox/PlayStation controllers) show up in UPower.devices only if their driver reports battery to the kernel.
  • Values update at the rate UPower polls the hardware, usually every 30–120 seconds for batteries. That's normal and very cheap.

Where this type appears#

  • UPower.devices (property)
  • UPower.displayDevice (property)

See also#

  • UPower, the singleton that gives you devices
  • UPowerDeviceState, UPowerDeviceType, the enums used by state and type
  • PowerProfiles, for power-saver/balanced/performance switching
  • Chapter 41: A Tour of the System Services

PowerProfile

How to get one
This is an enum (a fixed list of named values). You never create it; you compare against or assign its values, e.g. PowerProfile.PowerSaver. Turn a value into readable text with PowerProfile.toString(value).

Overview#

See PowerProfiles.

Functions#

toString(profile: PowerProfile): string
No upstream description.

Enum values#

ValueNumberMeaning
PowerProfile.PowerSaver0

This profile will limit system performance in order to save power.

PowerProfile.Balanced1

This profile is the default, and will attempt to strike a balance between performance and power consumption.

PowerProfile.Performance2

This profile will maximize performance at the cost of power consumption.

Example#

import Quickshell.Services.UPower

// compare a value
if (PowerProfiles.profile === PowerProfile.Balanced) console.log("it is Balanced")

// show a value as text
Text { text: PowerProfile.toString(PowerProfiles.profile) }

// used by: PowerProfiles.profile

Where this type appears#

Quickshell.Services.UPower

PowerProfiles

singleton

Provides access to the Power Profiles service.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.UPower
Inherits
PowerProfiles → QtObject
How to get one
This is a singleton: exactly one exists, created by Quickshell. Use it from anywhere by its name, e.g. PowerProfiles.profile. Never write PowerProfiles { }.

Overview#

Read and switch the system power profile (power-profiles-daemon): Power Saver, Balanced, Performance.

From the upstream documentation#

An interface to the UPower power profiles daemon, which can be used to view and manage power profiles.

Note

The power profiles daemon must be installed to use this service. Installing UPower does not necessarily install the power profiles daemon.

Example: every property#

import Quickshell.Services.UPower
import QtQuick

Column {
    Text { text: "profile: " + PowerProfile.toString(PowerProfiles.profile) }
    Text { text: "has performance: " + PowerProfiles.hasPerformanceProfile }
    Text { text: "degraded: " + PerformanceDegradationReason.toString(PowerProfiles.degradationReason) }   // e.g. LapDetected
    Text { text: "holds: " + PowerProfiles.holds.length }               // other apps requesting a profile
    Row {
        Repeater {
            model: [PowerProfile.PowerSaver, PowerProfile.Balanced, PowerProfile.Performance]
            Text {
                required property int modelData
                visible: modelData !== PowerProfile.Performance || PowerProfiles.hasPerformanceProfile
                text: "[" + PowerProfile.toString(modelData) + "] "
                font.bold: PowerProfiles.profile === modelData
                TapHandler { onTapped: PowerProfiles.profile = modelData }
            }
        }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onProfileChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
profilePowerProfileread / write

The current power profile.

This property may be set to change the system's power profile, however it cannot be set to Performance unless hasPerformanceProfile is true.

Setting Performance fails if hasPerformanceProfile is false.

hasPerformanceProfileboolread-only

If the system has a performance profile.

If this property is false, your system does not have a performance profile known to power-profiles-daemon.

degradationReasonPerformanceDegradationReasonread-only

If power-profiles-daemon detects degraded system performance, the reason for the degradation will be present here.

holdslist<PowerProfileHold>read-only

Power profile holds created by other applications.

This property returns a powerProfileHold object, which has the following properties. - profile - The PowerProfile held by the application. - applicationId - A string identifying the application - reason - The reason the application has given for holding the profile.

Applications may "hold" a power profile in place for their lifetime, such as a game holding Performance mode or a system daemon holding Power Saver mode when reaching a battery threshold. If the user selects a different profile explicitly (e.g. by setting profile) all holds will be removed.

Multiple applications may hold a power profile, however if multiple applications request profiles than PowerSaver will win over Performance. Only Performance and PowerSaver profiles may be held.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

Requires power-profiles-daemon (or tuned-ppd) running.

Quickshell.Services.SystemTray

SystemTrayItem

provided by Quickshell

An item in the system tray.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.SystemTray
Inherits
SystemTrayItem → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (SystemTrayItems can only be acquired from SystemTray). Quickshell gives you instances through: SystemTray.items.

Overview#

One tray icon. Show its icon, react to clicks with activate()/secondaryActivate()/scroll(), and show its menu.

From the upstream documentation#

A system tray item, roughly conforming to the kde/freedesktop spec (there is no real spec, we just implemented whatever seemed to actually be used).

Example: every property and function#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.SystemTray
import Quickshell.Widgets
import QtQuick

PanelWindow {
    id: bar
    anchors { top: true; left: true; right: true }
    implicitHeight: 32
    Row {
        anchors.centerIn: parent
        spacing: 8
        Repeater {
            model: SystemTray.items
            IconImage {
                id: icon
                required property SystemTrayItem modelData
                implicitSize: 20
                source: modelData.icon                                 // image source string
                opacity: modelData.status === Status.Passive ? 0.5 : 1 // Passive | Active | NeedsAttention
                Component.onCompleted: console.log(modelData.id, modelData.title, "category", modelData.category,
                                                   "tooltip:", modelData.tooltipTitle, modelData.tooltipDescription,
                                                   "hasMenu", modelData.hasMenu, "onlyMenu", modelData.onlyMenu)
                MouseArea {
                    anchors.fill: parent
                    acceptedButtons: Qt.LeftButton | Qt.MiddleButton | Qt.RightButton
                    onClicked: m => {
                        if (m.button === Qt.LeftButton && !icon.modelData.onlyMenu) icon.modelData.activate()
                        else if (m.button === Qt.MiddleButton) icon.modelData.secondaryActivate()
                        else if (icon.modelData.hasMenu) {
                            const p = bar.itemPosition(icon)
                            icon.modelData.display(bar, p.x, p.y + icon.height)      // quick native menu
                        }
                    }
                    onWheel: w => icon.modelData.scroll(w.angleDelta.y / 120, false)  // horizontal = false
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onIdChanged: …).

A name unique to the application, such as its name.

Text that describes the application.

Icon source string, usable as an Image source.

Usually an image:// URL usable directly as an image source. Some apps send name?path=/dir; see Project: System Tray with Custom Menus for a fix.

tooltipTitlestringread-onlyNo upstream description.
tooltipDescriptionstringread-onlyNo upstream description.

If this tray item has an associated menu accessible via display() or menu.

menuDBusMenuHandleread-only

A handle to the menu associated with this tray item, if any.

Can be displayed with QsMenuAnchor or QsMenuOpener.

Pass it to QsMenuAnchor (native) or QsMenuOpener (custom-drawn menu).

onlyMenuboolread-only

If this tray item only offers a menu and activation will do nothing.

If true, activate() does nothing: open the menu on left click instead.

Primary activation action, generally triggered via a left click.

secondaryActivate(): void

Secondary activation action, generally triggered via a middle click.

Scroll action, such as changing volume on a mixer.

Display a platform menu at the given location relative to the parent window.

No upstream description.

Quickshell.Services.Notifications

NotificationServer

creatable

Desktop Notifications Server.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Notifications
Inherits
NotificationServer
How to get one
You create this type in QML: NotificationServer { … }.

Overview#

Makes your shell the notification daemon. Create one (only one daemon can run on the system), declare which features you support, and handle notification to receive them.

From the upstream documentation#

An implementation of the Desktop Notifications Specification for receiving notifications from external applications.

The server does not advertise most capabilities by default. See the individual properties for details.

Example: every property and signal#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Notifications
import QtQuick

Scope {
    NotificationServer {
        id: server
        keepOnReload: true                 // re-emit existing notifications after a hot reload (default)
        persistenceSupported: true         // you keep notifications after they leave the screen
        bodySupported: true                // default true
        bodyMarkupSupported: true          // <b>, <i>, <u>
        bodyHyperlinksSupported: true      // <a href>
        bodyImagesSupported: false         // <img> in body
        actionsSupported: true             // buttons
        actionIconsSupported: false        // action identifiers are icon names
        imageSupported: true               // image / avatar
        inlineReplySupported: true         // reply text field
        extraHints: []                     // extra hint names to advertise

        onNotification: n => {
            n.tracked = true               // REQUIRED: keep it in trackedNotifications
            console.log(n.appName, n.summary)
        }
    }
    // history: server.trackedNotifications (ObjectModel<Notification>)
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onKeepOnReloadChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
keepOnReloadboolread / write

If notifications should be re-emitted when quickshell reloads. Defaults to true.

The Notification.lastGeneration flag will be set on notifications from the prior generation for further filtering/handling.

Re-emitted notifications have lastGeneration true. Skip showing popups for those.

persistenceSupportedboolread / write

If the notification server should advertise that it can persist notifications in the background after going offscreen. Defaults to false.

bodySupportedboolread / write

If notification body text should be advertised as supported by the notification server. Defaults to true.

Note that returned notifications are likely to return body text even if this property is false, as it is only a hint.

bodyMarkupSupportedboolread / write

If notification body text should be advertised as supporting markup as described in [the specification] Defaults to false.

Note that returned notifications may still contain markup if this property is false, as it is only a hint. By default Text objects will try to render markup. To avoid this if any is sent, change Text.textFormat to PlainText.

bodyHyperlinksSupportedboolread / write

If notification body text should be advertised as supporting hyperlinks as described in the specification Defaults to false.

Note that returned notifications may still contain hyperlinks if this property is false, as it is only a hint.

bodyImagesSupportedboolread / write

If notification body text should be advertised as supporting images as described in the specification Defaults to false.

Note that returned notifications may still contain images if this property is false, as it is only a hint.

actionsSupportedboolread / write

If notification actions should be advertised as supported by the notification server. Defaults to false.

actionIconsSupportedboolread / write

If notification actions should be advertised as supporting the display of icons. Defaults to false.

imageSupportedboolread / write

If the notification server should advertise that it supports images. Defaults to false.

inlineReplySupportedboolread / write

If the notification server should advertise that it supports inline replies. Defaults to false.

trackedNotificationsObjectModel<Notification>read-only

All notifications currently tracked by the server.

extraHintslist<string>read / write

Extra hints to expose to notification clients.

Signals#

notification(notification: Notification)handler: onNotification

Sent when a notification is received by the server.

If this notification should not be discarded, set its tracked property to true.

Notes, tips and gotchas#

  • Stop dunst, mako or swaync first.
  • Advertising a feature tells apps they may use it; only enable what your UI shows.

See also#

Project: Notification Daemon · Notification
