Quickshell.Services.Notifications

Notification

provided by Quickshell

A notification emitted by a NotificationServer.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Notifications
Inherits
Notification
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (Notifications must be acquired from a NotificationServer). Quickshell gives you instances through: NotificationServer.notification, NotificationServer.trackedNotifications.

Overview#

One notification received by a NotificationServer. Show its content, run its actions, and close it.

From the upstream documentation#

This type is Retainable. It

can be retained after destruction if necessary.

Example: every property and function#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Notifications
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls
import QtQuick.Layouts

ColumnLayout {
    required property Notification n
    Text { text: `#${n.id} from ${n.appName} (${n.desktopEntry}) icon ${n.appIcon}` }
    Text { text: n.summary; font.bold: true }
    Text { text: n.body; textFormat: Text.StyledText; wrapMode: Text.Wrap }
    Image { source: n.image; visible: n.image !== ""; sourceSize: Qt.size(64, 64) }
    Text { text: "urgency: " + NotificationUrgency.toString(n.urgency) }
    Text { text: "expire after: " + n.expireTimeout + " s" }                    // ≤ 0 means "you decide"
    Text { text: `resident ${n.resident} transient ${n.transient} tracked ${n.tracked} lastGeneration ${n.lastGeneration}` }
    Text { text: "hints: " + JSON.stringify(n.hints) }
    Row {
        Repeater {
            model: n.actions
            Button { required property NotificationAction modelData; text: modelData.text; onClicked: modelData.invoke() }
        }
    }
    TextField {
        visible: n.hasInlineReply
        placeholderText: n.inlineReplyPlaceholder
        onAccepted: n.sendInlineReply(text)
    }
    Row {
        Button { text: "Dismiss"; onClicked: n.dismiss() }   // user closed it
        Button { text: "Expire"; onClicked: n.expire() }     // timed out
    }
    Connections { target: n; function onClosed(reason) { console.log("closed:", NotificationCloseReason.toString(reason)) } }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onIdChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
idintconstant

Id of the notification as given to the client.

trackedboolread / write

If the notification is tracked by the notification server.

Setting this property to false is equivalent to calling dismiss().

Set to true in onNotification to keep it. Setting it to false is like dismissing it.

lastGenerationboolconstant

If this notification was carried over from the last generation when quickshell reloaded.

Notifications from the last generation will only be emitted if NotificationServer.keepOnReload is true.

expireTimeoutrealread-only

Time in seconds the notification should be valid for

In seconds. 0 or negative means the server decides (typically 5 s; critical: never).

appNamestringread-only

The sending application's name.

appIconstringread-only

The sending application's icon. If none was provided, then the icon from an associated desktop entry will be retrieved. If none was found then "".

summarystringread-only

The image associated with this notification, or "" if none.

bodystringread-onlyNo upstream description.
urgencyNotificationUrgencyread-onlyNo upstream description.
actionslist<NotificationAction>read-only

Actions that can be taken for this notification.

hasActionIconsboolread-only

If actions associated with this notification have icons available.

See NotificationAction.identifier for details.

residentboolread-only

If true, the notification will not be destroyed after an action is invoked.

If true, invoking an action doesn't close the notification.

transientboolread-only

If true, the notification should skip any kind of persistence function like a notification area.

If true, don't keep it in a history/notification center.

desktopEntrystringread-only

The name of the sender's desktop entry or "" if none was supplied.

imagestringread-only

An image associated with the notification.

This image is often something like a profile picture in instant messaging applications.

hasInlineReplyboolread-only

If true, the notification has an inline reply action.

A quick reply text field should be displayed and the reply can be sent using sendInlineReply().

inlineReplyPlaceholderstringread-only

The placeholder text/button caption for the inline reply.

hintsobjectread-only

All hints sent by the client application as a javascript object. Many common hints are exposed via other properties.

Functions#

expire(): void

Destroy the notification and hint to the remote application that it has timed out an expired.

dismiss(): void

Destroy the notification and hint to the remote application that it was explicitly closed by the user.

sendInlineReply(replyText: string): void

Send an inline reply to the notification with an inline reply action.

This method can only be called if

hasInlineReply is true and the server has NotificationServer.inlineReplySupported set to true.

Signals#

closed(reason: NotificationCloseReason)handler: onClosed

Sent when a notification has been closed.

The notification object will be destroyed as soon as all signal handlers exit.

Where this type appears#

  • NotificationServer.notification (signal)
  • NotificationServer.trackedNotifications (property)

    Text { text: `${a?.name} (${a?.adapterId}) at ${a?.dbusPath}` }
    Text { text: "state: " + BluetoothAdapterState.toString(a?.state) }   // Enabling, Blocked (rfkill)…
    Switch { text: "enabled"; checked: a?.enabled ?? false; onToggled: a.enabled = checked }
    Switch { text: "scanning"; checked: a?.discovering ?? false; onToggled: a.discovering = checked }
    Switch { text: "discoverable"; checked: a?.discoverable ?? false; onToggled: a.discoverable = checked }
    SpinBox { from: 0; to: 600; value: a?.discoverableTimeout ?? 0; onValueModified: a.discoverableTimeout = value }   // 0 = forever
    Switch { text: "pairable"; checked: a?.pairable ?? false; onToggled: a.pairable = checked }
    SpinBox { from: 0; to: 600; value: a?.pairableTimeout ?? 0; onValueModified: a.pairableTimeout = value }
    Text { text: (a?.devices.values.length ?? 0) + " known devices" }
}

Timeout in seconds for how long the adapter stays discoverable after discoverable is set to true. A value of 0 means the adapter stays discoverable forever.

Quickshell.Bluetooth

BluetoothDevice

provided by Quickshell

A tracked Bluetooth device.

Import
import Quickshell.Bluetooth
Inherits
BluetoothDevice → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself. Quickshell gives you instances through: Bluetooth.devices, BluetoothAdapter.devices.

Overview#

A Bluetooth device known to an adapter. Connect, pair, trust, forget, rename, and read its battery.

Example: every property and function#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Bluetooth
import Quickshell.Widgets
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls

Repeater {
    model: Bluetooth.defaultAdapter?.devices ?? []
    Row {
        required property BluetoothDevice modelData
        readonly property BluetoothDevice d: modelData
        spacing: 6
        IconImage { implicitSize: 20; source: Quickshell.iconPath(d.icon, "bluetooth") }
        Text { text: `${d.name} [${d.deviceName}] ${d.address}` }
        Text { text: BluetoothDeviceState.toString(d.state) }          // Connecting / Connected …
        Text { text: d.batteryAvailable ? Math.round(d.battery * 100) + "%" : "" }
        Text { text: `paired ${d.paired} bonded ${d.bonded} pairing ${d.pairing} trusted ${d.trusted} blocked ${d.blocked} wake ${d.wakeAllowed}` }
        Button { text: d.connected ? "Disconnect" : "Connect"; onClicked: d.connected ? d.disconnect() : d.connect() }   // or d.connected = !d.connected
        Button { text: d.pairing ? "Cancel" : "Pair"; visible: !d.paired; onClicked: d.pairing ? d.cancelPair() : d.pair() }
        Button { text: d.trusted ? "Untrust" : "Trust"; onClicked: d.trusted = !d.trusted }
        Button { text: "Forget"; onClicked: d.forget() }
        TextField { placeholderText: "rename"; onAccepted: d.name = text }   // "" resets the alias
        Text { text: "via " + d.adapter?.name + " " + d.dbusPath; color: "grey" }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onAddressChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
addressstringread-only

MAC address of the device.

namestringread / write

The name of the Bluetooth device. This property may be written to create an alias, or set to an empty string to fall back to the device provided name.

See deviceName for the name provided by the device.

deviceNamestringread-only

The name of the Bluetooth device, ignoring user provided aliases. See also name which returns a user provided alias if set.

iconstringread-only

System icon representing the device type. Use Quickshell.iconPath() to display this in an image.

stateBluetoothDeviceStateread-only

Connection state of the device.

connectedboolread / write

True if the device is currently connected to the computer.

Setting this property is equivalent to calling connect() and disconnect().

state provides more detailed information if required.
pairedboolread-only

True if the device is paired to the computer.

Note

pair() can be used to pair a device, however you must forget() the device to unpair it.

bondedboolread-only

True if pairing information is stored for future connections.

pairingboolread-only

True if the device is currently being paired.

cancelPair() can be used to cancel the pairing process.
trustedboolread / write

True if the device is considered to be trusted by the system. Trusted devices are allowed to reconnect themselves to the system without intervention.

blockedboolread / write

True if the device is blocked from connecting. If a device is blocked, any connection attempts will be immediately rejected by the system.

wakeAllowedboolread / write

True if the device is allowed to wake up the host system from suspend.

batteryAvailableboolread-only

True if the connected device reports its battery level. Battery level can be accessed via battery.

batteryrealread-only

Battery level of the connected device, from 0.0 to 1.0. Only valid if batteryAvailable is true.

0.0–1.0, valid only when batteryAvailable is true.

adapterBluetoothAdapterread-only

The Bluetooth adapter this device belongs to.

dbusPathstringconstant

DBus path of the device under the org.bluez system service.

Functions#

connect(): void

Attempt to connect to the device.

disconnect(): void

Disconnect from the device.

pair(): void

Attempt to pair the device.

Note

paired and pairing return the current pairing status of the device.

Pairing that needs a PIN or confirmation requires a BlueZ agent; many devices (headphones, mice) pair without one.

cancelPair(): void

Cancel an active pairing attempt.

forget(): void

Forget the device.

  • Bluetooth.devices (property)
  • BluetoothAdapter.devices (property)

Networking

singleton

The Network service.

Import
import Quickshell.Networking
Inherits
Networking → QtObject
How to get one
This is a singleton: exactly one exists, created by Quickshell. Use it from anywhere by its name, e.g. Networking.devices. Never write Networking { }.

Overview#

Network management (currently through NetworkManager): devices, Wi-Fi on/off, and internet connectivity. Networks are found on each device.

From the upstream documentation#

An interface to a network backend (currently only NetworkManager), which can be used to view, configure, and connect to various networks.

Example: every property and function#

import Quickshell.Networking
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls

Column {
    Text { text: "backend: " + NetworkBackendType.toString(Networking.backend) }
    Switch { text: "Wi-Fi"; checked: Networking.wifiEnabled; onToggled: Networking.wifiEnabled = checked }
    Text { text: "hardware switch on: " + Networking.wifiHardwareEnabled }
    Text { text: "connectivity: " + NetworkConnectivity.toString(Networking.connectivity) }   // None/Portal/Limited/Full
    Text { text: "can check: " + Networking.canCheckConnectivity + " · enabled " + Networking.connectivityCheckEnabled }
    Button { text: "check now"; onClicked: Networking.checkConnectivity() }
    Repeater {
        model: Networking.devices
        Text { required property NetworkDevice modelData; text: DeviceType.toString(modelData.type) + " " + modelData.name + (modelData.connected ? " ✓" : "") }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onDevicesChanged: …).

A list of all network devices. Networks are exposed through their respective devices.

backendNetworkBackendTypeconstant

The backend being used to power the Network service.

wifiEnabledboolread / write

Switch for the rfkill software block of all wireless devices.

wifiHardwareEnabledboolread-only

State of the rfkill hardware block of all wireless devices.

canCheckConnectivityboolread-only

True if the backend supports connectivity checks.

connectivityCheckEnabledboolread / write

True if connectivity checking is enabled.

connectivityNetworkConnectivityread-only

The result of the last connectivity check.

Connectivity checks may require additional configuration depending on your distro.

This property can be used to determine if network access is restricted

or gated behind a captive portal.

If checking for captive portals, checkConnectivity() should be called after the portal is dismissed to update this property.

Portal means a captive portal (hotel Wi-Fi login page): you can open a browser to log in.

Functions#

checkConnectivity(): void

Re-check the network connectivity state immediately.

Note

This should be invoked after a user dismisses a web browser that was opened to authenticate via a captive portal.

NetworkDevice · WifiDevice · WifiNetwork · Project: Control Center

A network you can connect to (a Wi-Fi network, or a wired connection). Wi-Fi networks are the subtype WifiNetwork.

From the upstream documentation#

Networks derived from a WifiDevice are WifiNetwork instances.

Example: every property, function and signal#

Repeater {
    model: device.networks
    Row {
        required property Network modelData
        readonly property Network n: modelData
        spacing: 6
        Text { text: n.name + " · " + ConnectionState.toString(n.state) + (n.stateChanging ? "…" : "") }
        Text { text: n.known ? "saved" : "new" }
        Text { text: "[" + (n.connected ? "disconnect" : "connect") + "]"
               TapHandler { onTapped: n.connected ? n.disconnect() : n.connect() } }
        Text { text: "[forget]"; visible: n.known; TapHandler { onTapped: n.forget() } }
        Text { text: n.nmSettings.length + " profiles" }      // NetworkManager only
        Connections { target: n; function onConnectionFailed(r) { console.warn("failed:", ConnectionFailReason.toString(r)) } }
    }
}

connect(): void

Attempt to connect to the network.

If the network is a WifiNetwork and requires secrets, a connectionFailed(s)

Attempt to connect to the network with a specific nmSettings entry.

Only valid for the NetworkManager backend.
disconnect(): void

Disconnect from the network.

forget(): void

Forget all connection settings for this network.

Functions#

connectWithPsk(psk: string): void

Attempt to connect to the network with the given PSK. If the PSK is wrong, a Network.connectionFailed(s) signal will be emitted with NoSecrets.

The networking backend may store the PSK for future use with Network.connect(). As such, calling that function first is recommended to avoid having to show a prompt if not required.

PSKs should only be provided when the security is one of

WpaPsk, Wpa2Psk, or Sae.

NetworkConnectivity

enum

The degree to which the host can reach the internet.

Import
import Quickshell.Networking
Inherits
NetworkConnectivity → QtObject
How to get one
This is an enum (a fixed list of named values). You never create it; you compare against or assign its values, e.g. NetworkConnectivity.Unknown. Turn a value into readable text with NetworkConnectivity.toString(value).

Functions#

toString(conn: NetworkConnectivity): string
No upstream description.

Enum values#

ValueNumberMeaning
NetworkConnectivity.Unknown0

Network connectivity is unknown. This means the connectivity checks are disabled or have not run yet.

NetworkConnectivity.None1

The host is not connected to any network.

NetworkConnectivity.Portal2

The internet connection is hijacked by a captive portal gateway. This indicates the shell should open a sandboxed web browser window for the purpose of authenticating to a gateway.

NetworkConnectivity.Limited3

The host is connected to a network but does not appear to be able to reach the full internet.

NetworkConnectivity.Full4

The host is connected to a network and appears to be able to reach the full internet.

Example#

import Quickshell.Networking

// compare a value
if (Networking.connectivity === NetworkConnectivity.None) console.log("it is None")

// show a value as text

NMSettings

provided by Quickshell

A NetworkManager connection settings profile.

Import
import Quickshell.Networking
Inherits
NMSettings → QtObject
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself. Quickshell gives you instances through: Network.connectWithSettings, Network.nmSettings.

Overview#

A saved NetworkManager connection profile for a network, from Network.nmSettings. Read or update its settings, clear saved secrets, or delete it.

Example#

Repeater {
    model: network.nmSettings
    Row {
        required property NMSettings modelData
        Text { text: modelData.id + " (" + modelData.uuid + ")" }
        Text { text: "[dump]"; TapHandler { onTapped: console.log(JSON.stringify(modelData.read(), null, 2)) } }   // secrets excluded
        Text { text: "[no autoconnect]"; TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.write({ connection: { autoconnect: false } }) } }
        Text { text: "[clear password]"; TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.clearSecrets() } }
        Text { text: "[delete]"; TapHandler { onTapped: modelData.forget() } }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onIdChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
idstringread-only

The human-readable unique identifier for the connection.

uuidstringread-only

A universally unique identifier for the connection.

Functions#

clearSecrets(): void

Clear all of the secrets belonging to the settings.

forget(): void

Delete the settings.

write(settings: object): void

Update the connection with new settings and save the connection to disk. Only changed fields need to be included. Writing a setting to null will remove the setting or reset it to its default.

Note

Secrets may be part of the update request, and will be either stored in persistent storage or sent to a Secret Agent for storage, depending on the flags associated with each secret.

read(): object

Get the settings map describing this network configuration.

Note

This will never include any secrets required for connection to the network, as those are often protected.

Signals#

loaded()handler: onLoaded
No upstream description.

Quickshell.Services.Pam

PamContext

creatable

Connection to pam.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Pam
Inherits
PamContext
How to get one
You create this type in QML: PamContext { … }.

Overview#

Runs a PAM authentication conversation: check a password (or fingerprint, or anything your PAM config allows) for a user. Used by lock screens.

From the upstream documentation#

See the module documentation for pam configuration advice.

Example: every property, function and signal#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Pam
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls
import QtQuick.Layouts

FloatingWindow {
    implicitWidth: 400; implicitHeight: 260
    color: "#1e1e2e"

    PamContext {
        id: pam
        config: "login"                          // file in configDirectory
        configDirectory: "/etc/pam.d"            // default
        user: ""                                 // "" = current user; can't change while active

        onPamMessage: {                          // after message/responseRequired/… update
            console.log("PAM says:", message, "error?", messageIsError)
            if (responseRequired) respond(pw.text)           // responseVisible: echo or hide?
        }
        onCompleted: result => status.text = result === PamResult.Success ? "✓ success" : "✗ " + PamResult.toString(result)
        onError: err => status.text = "error: " + PamError.toString(err)
    }

    ColumnLayout {
        anchors { fill: parent; margins: 20 }
        TextField { id: pw; echoMode: TextInput.Password; placeholderText: "password"; onAccepted: pam.start(); enabled: !pam.active }
        Button { text: pam.active ? "Cancel" : "Check"; onClicked: pam.active ? pam.abort() : pam.start() }   // start() returns bool
        Text { id: status; color: "white" }
        Text { color: "#a6adc8"; text: `active ${pam.active} · needs response ${pam.responseRequired} · visible ${pam.responseVisible}` }
        Text { color: pam.messageIsError ? "#f38ba8" : "#a6adc8"; text: pam.message }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onActiveChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
activeboolread / write

If the pam context is actively performing an authentication.

Setting this value behaves exactly the same as calling start() and abort().

configstringread / write

The pam configuration to use. Defaults to "login".

The configuration should name a file inside configDirectory.

This property may not be set while active is true.

Only the auth stack is used. Write your own config (e.g. fingerprint OR password) in a folder and point configDirectory to it. The module overview explains PAM config syntax.

configDirectorystringread / write

The pam configuration directory to use. Defaults to "/etc/pam.d".

The configuration directory is resolved relative to the current file if not an absolute path.

On FreeBSD this property is ignored as the pam configuration directory cannot be changed.

This property may not be set while active is true.

userstringread / write

The user to authenticate as. If unset the current user will be used.

This property may not be set while active is true.

messagestringread-only

The last message sent by pam.

messageIsErrorboolread-only

If the last message should be shown as an error.

responseRequiredboolread-only

If pam currently wants a response.

Responses can be returned with the respond() function.

responseVisibleboolread-only

If the user's response should be visible. Only valid when responseRequired is true.

Functions#

start(): bool

Start an authentication session. Returns if the session was started successfully.

abort(): void

Abort a running authentication session.

respond(response: string): void

Respond to pam.

May not be called unless responseRequired is true.

Signals#

completed(result: PamResult)handler: onCompleted

Emitted whenever authentication completes.

error(error: PamError)handler: onError

Emitted if pam fails to perform authentication normally.

A completed(PamResult.Error) will be emitted after this event.

pamMessage()handler: onPamMessage

Emitted whenever pam sends a new message, after the change signals for message, messageIsError, and responseRequired.

See also#

Project: Lock Screen · PamResult · PamError

Quickshell.Services.Polkit

AuthFlow

provided by Quickshell
Import
import Quickshell.Services.Polkit
Inherits
AuthFlow
How to get one
You cannot create this type yourself (AuthFlow can only be obtained from PolkitAgent.). Quickshell gives you instances through: PolkitAgent.flow.

Overview#

One polkit authentication request, available as PolkitAgent.flow while active. Display its message, collect the password, submit() it, or cancel.

Example: every property, function and signal#

ColumnLayout {
    required property AuthFlow flow
    Image { source: Quickshell.iconPath(flow.iconName || "dialog-password") }
    Text { text: flow.message }                                   // e.g. "Authentication is required to mount the disk"
    Text { text: "action: " + flow.actionId + " · cookie: " + flow.cookie; color: "grey" }
    ComboBox {                                                    // users/groups allowed to authenticate
        model: flow.identities.map(i => String(i))
        onActivated: i => flow.selectedIdentity = flow.identities[i]   // restarts the conversation
    }
    TextField {
        enabled: flow.isResponseRequired
        placeholderText: flow.inputPrompt                         // e.g. "Password:"
        echoMode: flow.responseVisible ? TextInput.Normal : TextInput.Password
        onAccepted: flow.submit(text)
    }
    Text { text: flow.supplementaryMessage; color: flow.supplementaryIsError ? "red" : "grey" }
    Text { text: `completed ${flow.isCompleted} success ${flow.isSuccessful} cancelled ${flow.isCancelled} failed-once ${flow.failed}` }
    Button { text: "Cancel"; onClicked: flow.cancelAuthenticationRequest() }
    Connections {
        target: flow
        function onAuthenticationSucceeded() { console.log("ok") }
        function onAuthenticationFailed() { console.log("wrong password; a new attempt starts automatically") }
        function onAuthenticationRequestCancelled() { console.log("cancelled by polkit") }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onMessageChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
messagestringconstant

The main message to present to the user.

iconNamestringconstant

The icon to present to the user in association with the message.

The icon name follows the FreeDesktop icon naming specification. Use Quickshell.iconPath() to resolve the icon name to an actual file path for display.

actionIdstringconstant

The action ID represents the action that is being authorized.

This is a machine-readable identifier.

cookiestringconstant

A cookie that identifies this authentication request.

This is an internal identifier and not recommended to show to users.

identitieslist<Identity>constant

The list of identities that may be used to authenticate.

Each identity may be a user or a group. You may select any of them to authenticate by setting selectedIdentity. By default, the first identity in the list is selected.

selectedIdentityIdentityread / write

The identity that will be used to authenticate.

Changing this will abort any ongoing authentication conversations and start a new one.

isResponseRequiredboolread-only

Indicates that a response from the user is required from the user, typically a password.

inputPromptstringread-only

This message is used to prompt the user for required input.

responseVisibleboolread-only

Indicates whether the user's response should be visible. (e.g. for passwords this should be false)

supplementaryMessagestringread-only

An additional message to present to the user.

This may be used to show errors or supplementary information. See supplementaryIsError to determine if this is an error message.

supplementaryIsErrorboolread-only

Indicates whether the supplementary message is an error.

isCompletedboolread-only

Has the authentication request been completed.

isSuccessfulboolread-only

Indicates whether the authentication request was successful.

isCancelledboolread-only

Indicates whether the current authentication request was cancelled.

failedboolread-only

Indicates whether an authentication attempt has failed at least once during this authentication flow.

Functions#

submit(value: string): void

Submit a response to a request that was previously emitted. Typically the password.

cancelAuthenticationRequest(): void

Cancel the ongoing authentication request from the user side.

Signals#

authenticationSucceeded()handler: onAuthenticationSucceeded

Emitted whenever an authentication request completes successfully.

authenticationFailed()handler: onAuthenticationFailed

Emitted whenever an authentication request completes unsuccessfully.

This may be because the user entered the wrong password or otherwise failed to authenticate. This signal is not emitted when the user canceled the request or it was cancelled by the PolKit daemon.

After this signal, a new session is automatically started for the same identity.

authenticationRequestCancelled()handler: onAuthenticationRequestCancelled

Emitted when an ongoing authentication request is cancelled by the PolKit daemon.

Where this type appears#

  • PolkitAgent.flow (property)

PolkitAgent

creatable
Import
import Quickshell.Services.Polkit
Inherits
PolkitAgent
How to get one
You create this type in QML: PolkitAgent { … }.

Overview#

Registers your shell as the polkit authentication agent, the program that shows "Authentication required" dialogs. When a request arrives, flow holds an AuthFlow describing it.

Example#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Polkit
import QtQuick

Scope {
    PolkitAgent {
        id: agent
        path: ""                                         // D-Bus path; default /org/quickshell/Polkit
        onAuthenticationRequestStarted: console.log("request:", flow.message, "action:", flow.actionId)
    }
    // agent.isRegistered: did registration succeed (another agent may already be running)
    // agent.isActive: a request is in progress → show your dialog bound to agent.flow
}

isRegisteredboolread-only

Indicates whether the agent registered successfully and is in use.

Indicates an ongoing authentication request.

If this is true, other properties such as message and iconName will also be populated with relevant information.

The current authentication state if an authentication request is active.

Null when no authentication request is active.

Quickshell.Services.Greetd

Greetd

singleton

This object provides access to a running greetd instance if present.

Import
import Quickshell.Services.Greetd
Inherits
Greetd → QtObject
How to get one
This is a singleton: exactly one exists, created by Quickshell. Use it from anywhere by its name, e.g. Greetd.available. Never write Greetd { }.

Overview#

Talks to greetd so a Quickshell config can be a graphical login screen. Create a session for a user, answer authentication messages, then launch their desktop.

From the upstream documentation#

With it you can authenticate a user and launch a session.

See the greetd wiki for instructions on how to set up a graphical greeter.

Example: every property, function and signal#

import Quickshell
import Quickshell.Services.Greetd
import QtQuick
import QtQuick.Controls
import QtQuick.Layouts

FloatingWindow {
    color: "#11111b"
    ColumnLayout {
        anchors.centerIn: parent
        Text { color: "white"; text: "greetd available: " + Greetd.available + " · state: " + GreetdState.toString(Greetd.state)
                                     + " · user: " + Greetd.user }
        TextField { id: user; placeholderText: "user" }
        TextField { id: pw; placeholderText: "password"; echoMode: TextInput.Password; onAccepted: Greetd.createSession(user.text) }
        Button { text: "Log in"; onClicked: Greetd.createSession(user.text) }
        Button { text: "Cancel"; onClicked: Greetd.cancelSession() }
        Text { id: msg; color: "#f38ba8" }
    }
    Connections {
        target: Greetd
        function onAuthMessage(message, error, responseRequired, echoResponse) {
            if (error) msg.text = message                    // recoverable error (e.g. fingerprint misread)
            if (responseRequired) Greetd.respond(pw.text)    // echoResponse: show input in clear text?
        }
        function onAuthFailure(message) { msg.text = message || "Login failed" }
        function onReadyToLaunch() {
            Greetd.launch(["Hyprland"])                      // also: launch(cmd, ["VAR=value"]), launch(cmd, env, quit)
        }
        function onLaunched() { console.log("greetd accepted the session") }
        function onError(err) { msg.text = err }
    }
}

Properties#

Every property also emits a <name>Changed signal; handle it with on<Name>Changed (e.g. onAvailableChanged: …).

NameTypeAccessDescription
availableboolconstant

If the greetd socket is available.

stateGreetdStateread-only

The current state of the greetd connection.

userstringread-only

The currently authenticating user.

Functions#

createSession(user: string): void

Create a greetd session for the given user.

cancelSession(): void

Cancel the active greetd session.

respond(response: string): void

Respond to an authentication message.

May only be called in response to an authMessage(s) with responseRequired set to true.

launch(command: list<string>): void

Launch the session, exiting quickshell. state must be GreetdState.ReadyToLaunch to call this function.

Quickshell exits after launching (unless quit is false). Run animations before calling launch, because greetd expects the greeter to exit quickly.

launch(command: list<string>, environment: list<string>): void

Launch the session, exiting quickshell. state must be GreetdState.ReadyToLaunch to call this function.

Quickshell exits after launching (unless quit is false). Run animations before calling launch, because greetd expects the greeter to exit quickly.

launch(command: list<string>, environment: list<string>, quit: bool): void

Launch the session, exiting quickshell if quit is true. state must be GreetdState.ReadyToLaunch to call this function.

The launched signal can be used to perform an action after greetd has acknowledged the desired session.

Note that greetd expects the greeter to terminate as soon as possible

after setting a target session, and waiting too long may lead to unexpected behavior such as the greeter restarting.

Performing animations and such should be done before calling launch.

Quickshell exits after launching (unless quit is false). Run animations before calling launch, because greetd expects the greeter to exit quickly.

Signals#

authMessage(message: string, error: bool, responseRequired: bool, echoResponse: bool)handler: onAuthMessage

An authentication message has been sent by greetd. - message - the text of the message - error - if the message should be displayed as an error - responseRequired - if a response via respond() is required for this message - echoResponse - if the response should be displayed in clear text to the user

Note that error and responseRequired are mutually exclusive.

Errors are sent through authMessage when they are recoverable, such as a fingerprint scanner not being able to read a finger correctly, while definite failures such as a bad password are sent through authFailure.

authFailure(message: string)handler: onAuthFailure

Authentication has failed an the session has terminated.

Usually this is something like a timeout or a failed password entry.

readyToLaunch()handler: onReadyToLaunch

Authentication has finished successfully and greetd can now launch a session.

launched()handler: onLaunched

Greetd has acknowledged the launch request and the greeter should quit as soon as possible.

This signal is sent right before quickshell exits automatically if the launch was not specifically requested not to exit. You usually don't need to use this signal.

error(error: string)handler: onError

Greetd has encountered an error.

See also#

Project: Login Greeter

You cannot create this type yourself (DBusMenus can only be acquired from a DBusMenuHandle). Quickshell gives you instances through: DBusMenuHandle.menu.

Overview#

A menu item exported by another program (a tray app). It's a QsMenuEntry with extras: menuHandle and updateLayout() to refresh the contents when an app builds its menu lazily.

From the upstream documentation#

via the DBusMenu specification.

Example#

QsMenuOpener {
    id: opener
    menu: trayItem.menu
    onMenuChanged: if (menu && menu.updateLayout) menu.updateLayout()   // some apps need a refresh
}
